items.statement: MUFG to invest ~US$4.4bn for 20% stake via preferential allotment; boards approved, EGM notice sent
items.quote: The proposed partnership with MUFG will be with a 20% stake , in the sense, the professional allotment given to them. So fresh capital would be coming in with approximately US$4.4 billion.

items.statement: Target AUM growth of 18-20% vs current 16-17%
items.quote: We have been growing around 16%-17%. We would like to grow another 3%-4% more, that is anywhere between 18%-20%.

items.statement: ROA to expand from 2.8% to 3.6% over 4-5 years
items.quote: The ROA part of it, because the capital and lower cost, the ROA will expand from current 2.8 to around 3.6 over the period.

items.statement: ROE to dip to ~13.5% next year then recover to current levels in ~5 years
items.quote: the ROE which will come down in next year because of the additional capital to around 13.5 will start growing year after , and we would be able to go back to the current ROE by 31, that is around 5 years from now.

items.statement: NIM likely to expand as 100bps borrowing cost reduction benefits entire book; new vehicle lending limited to ~5% of customers
items.quote: In fact, my net interest margin is likely to expand from here. Exact numbers I will not be able to give you immediately. Sanjay will be able to help you out of that. But you can imagine 100 basis point coming down for the entire book over the two years and very few customers I will be able to offer new vehicle lending rate

items.statement: Expect ~100bps reduction in blended cost of funds over 2-3 years from rating upgrades, MUFG backing and RBI rate cuts
items.quote: overall we believe the 100 basis point advantage will get over the next two years on our borrowing cost.

items.statement: Credit cost may improve 10-20bps from retaining top-paying customers longer
items.quote: around 10 to 20 basis point improvement in credit cost is a possibility , because we would be able t o retain our top customers, our best paying customers for a longer term.

items.statement: New vehicle market share ~3% currently; aim to double in 3 years primarily by lending to existing customers
items.quote: our new vehicle market share is very low. It's around 3% , including the passenger vehicle among the overall new vehicle sales, which we would like to double it in the next three years.

items.statement: ~30% of customers leave as they grow and seek newer/larger vehicles; retention focus to drive growth
items.quote: around 30% of my customers over the period move out because they grow their business and they want a newer vehicle -- new vehicle or larger ticket.

items.statement: Vehicle (incl. 2W, CE, farm) ~80%, SME ~15%, gold/personal ~5%; mix stable, gold may rise ~2%
items.quote: including two-wheeler and construction equipment and farm equipment, it is 80-20. That is, 15% is SME and another 5% is gold and personal loans. So, overall, that proportion will continue to remain. But maybe, yes, we will be a little more aggressive in the gold financing because we have a reach which we need to take an advantage. There will be a certain push for gold finance that will increase ma

items.statement: Will stay in semi-urban/rural; expand reach in north, central, east by converting rural centres to branches
items.quote: We would prefer to be in the semi -urban rural market. And as I was telling, that we would prefer to retain my existing customer and definitely I will create more rea ch in the north, central and east where our footprints are a little less. We would be expanding. We have a rural center there. We would be converting those into branches.

items.statement: No M&A or inordinate growth planned; capital sufficient for organic growth
items.quote: No. So we'll not be looking into any kind of inordinate growth.

items.statement: MUFG may second up to 3 personnel (non-KMP, non-senior management) for up to 6 months post-completion; focus on reporting, digital, learning
items.quote: none of the second is -- would be either KMPs or senior management. They will be number two or number three level only. So none of the KMPs and senior management change is envisaged at this level or discussed.

items.statement: Transaction needs RBI and CCI approval; EGM on 14th; expect completion in 2-3 months, latest by April
items.quote: Basically, the 14th is the EGM date and after that we need to apply for RBI approval, a formal approval from RBI and CCI. We expect it to take two to three months, but it can be faster also. It all depends on how these things move. And we would be happy to get it in this financial year, but at the max it can be April.

items.statement: Target steady-state debt-to-equity of 4-5x (ideal 4.5x); may take 5-6 years to reach 4x
items.quote: we always feel the sweet spot for us is anywhere between four to five times. Maximum five and four is ideal. And for reaching that four times leverage it may take maybe five to six years, but we are happy in this. I think the sweet spot is four to five and we should or I shoul d say 4.5, should be the exact.

items.statement: Cost-of-fund benefit to come from capital market borrowings (~23% of liabilities) and retail deposits (~26-27%); bank borrowing spread AAA vs AA minimal
items.quote: I don't think there is much of a differential when it comes to the bank borrowing between AAA and AA. There is definitely a lot of differential between the capital market borrowing what we have and also the retail deposit. Retail deposit is, for us, is around 26 %, 27%. So, as and when we reduce rate there and the capital market, which is close to around 23% of our liabilities, both this will have

items.statement: Gearing to improve from ~4.3x to ~2.6x immediately post-infusion
items.quote: The immediate impact of the capital infusion will be our gearing increase around 4.3, that is leveraging will come down to 2 .6

items.statement: Management changes (new MD & CEO Parag Sharma) were normal succession, not deal-related; no further changes expected
items.quote: No, the management changes were the normal management changes. There is nothing surprising here. So as the term came to end of the earlier Managing Dir ector, the new Managing Director and CEO has come, Mr. Parag Sharma. And he will continue for a longer time. And there is nothing in anticipation of this deal we have done.

items.statement: Will not enter large-ticket SME or LAP lending; remain cash-flow based, secured, 5-7 year tenor
items.quote: We will not go into large ticket SME lending. We will never get into lab lending. We will do only the SME business lending. We are very clear. However, yes, we will have additional security of property, either commercial property or residential property that will continue. But we will not get into large ticket and will not get into LAP.

items.statement: MUFG brings digital platform experience from Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia; potential digital synergy
items.quote: They have a very strong digital play that we should be able to take certain advantage of the platform what they have built in these countries.

items.statement: Conservative stance: no aggressive new customer acquisition, no new geographies, no unrelated businesses
items.quote: We do not wish to play for a long term lending. LA P, moment you call it as a LA P, it goes into 12 t o 15 years longer lending, which you would like to restrict to five to seven years only, and only for a term loan and for the business purpose and based on the cash flow.

items.statement: Non-compete payment of ~$200m to SOT (promoter group) paid directly by investor; no discount to SEBI preferential price
items.quote: No, it is paid directly by the investor. Parag Sharma: And there is no price which is reduced because of this investment. As per the SEBI determined pricing, whatever was the preferential issue rate is what is paid, which is not discounted at all. So that full money comes into Shriram Finance

items.statement: Interim ROA may spike to ~3.8% on capital inflow before settling at 3.6% in 5 years
items.quote: When the capital comes in, the ROA will go up significantly. It may go up to 3.8. But it will slowly, as we expand our business, it will come down to 3.6.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain current EBITDA per ton levels going forward
items.quote: Yes, our endeavor is of course to maintain these kind of EBITDA per ton figures now.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR 97 crore allocated for Supa and Chakan capex and rooftop solar; equipment deliveries over next 15 months
items.quote: The second primary u se of the fresh proceeds was INR97 crores which was towards capital expenditure in Supa and Chakan plants as well as installation of the rooftop solar power plant at Supa

items.statement: Phase I Supa expansion of 12,000 tons operational from Oct 1; Phase II to take total capacity to 59,045 tons by FY27
items.quote: Once Phase II of our Supa expansion is completed in FY '27, we would have an installed capacity of 59,045 metric tons in place.

items.statement: 80-85% of business is repeat contracts; one-third of CTC volume now goes to largest transformer class (765 kV/HVDC) up from single digits two years ago
items.quote: 80% to 85% of our businesses normally always repeat, you know, the same customers will be repeated, it's gone as high as 90% also.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA per ton INR 65,500, up 42% YoY from INR 46,000; driven by higher voltage transformers, exports, utilization
items.quote: Thus, for second quarter FY '26 EBITDA per ton was approximately INR65,500 per metric ton on a consolidated basis and increased to 42.1% from INR46,000 per metric ton last year.

items.statement: Structural long-term demand cycle in T&D driven by renewables, grid modernization, urbanization, AI data centers globally
items.quote: Coming back to the T&D sector, it is experiencing a structural long -term cycle driven by renewable energy, grid modernization, urbanization, and growing power demand for AI data centers.

items.statement: Specialized winding wires 77% of revenue in Q2 FY26; CTC ~75% of specialized; standard wires 23%; EBITDA per ton ratio specialized:standard = 3:1
items.quote: Specialized winding wires represented 77% of our total revenue, excluding other operating revenue during second quarter of FY '26.

items.statement: ~120 OEM customers; top 10 ~50% revenue; 5 of top 10 >10 years tenure; 90%+ revenue from repeat customers
items.quote: We are a B2B company, servicing approximately 120 leading domestic and global OEM customers, and maintain long -term relations with these customers, resulting in more than 90% of our revenue being from repeat customers.

items.statement: Exports 29.5% of revenue in Q2 FY26, up 21.7% YoY; supply to 24 countries; rupee depreciation benefits value addition; US tariffs passed through by customers
items.quote: Revenue from exports grew 21.7% compared to Q2 of FY '25 and represented 29.5% of the total revenue, excluding other operating revenue during the period.

items.statement: Working capital days ~75, higher than peers; targeting reduction in 1-2 years via higher payable days (shifting copper purchases from advance to credit)
items.quote: Yes, so rightly pointed out, our working capital days are around 75 days and as compared to peers a little more. We are actively engaging and undertaking steps to bring down the working capital days consistently in the next one or two years at all fronts, may it be receivable days, inventory days or increasing the payable days.

items.statement: INR 225.9 crore of IPO proceeds used to repay term debt and working capital lines; balance sheet strengthened
items.quote: I am pleased to let you know that the company has already paid INR225.9 crores towards reducing its term debt as well as certain working capital lines.

items.statement: Copper price and FX fully passed through; EBITDA per ton unaffected by copper price; value addition agreed with customers independent of copper
items.quote: No, copper prices has got no role to play in the EBITDA per ton. But, you know, once again, just to be clear, that what's contributing to the increase in EBITDA per ton is of course, the product mix that is there.

items.statement: Chinese competitors exited US market post-COVID; KSH benefits from China+1 in Europe/Middle East/Japan; difficult in SE Asia due to Chinese FTAs
items.quote: So, once upon a time, the Chinese were quite predominantly there in the US market. But as of right now, I mean, that's absolutely the US market is something that the Chinese vacated, post COVID.

items.statement: Only Indian supplier qualified for HVDC 400 kV; utility approvals (PowerGrid, NTPC) require field track record creating high entry barriers
items.quote: And we are the only ones right now in India who are qualified, the Indian supplier qualified to supply for the HVDC 400.

items.statement: Transformer manufacturers backward integrating into CTC seen as low risk due to complexity, volume needs, and utility approval requirements
items.quote: And we've not seen this trend anywhere else. In fact, anywhere else in the world that we have seen, most of the transformer manufacturers are not doing, and there is a certain degree of complexity also that is involved in manufacturing CTC.

items.statement: Rohit Hegde (Joint MD) moving to Whole Time Director role in other group companies; remains Non-Executive Director on board
items.quote: So Rohit Hegde, who's the other, Joint Managing Director, who's my brother, he is going to take up a more, active role in some of the other group companies as a Whole Time Director.

items.statement: Copper sourcing from long-term suppliers (Hindalco, Adani, Vedanta, HCL); 15-20 days raw material inventory; 2-day order-to-delivery cycle
items.quote: Around 15 to 20 days.

items.statement: Exclusive license from HPW (Europe) for PEEK wire technology for 800V EV traction motors; indigenization underway; meaningful volumes expected post FY27
items.quote: And what we are trying to do is, we are trying to indigenize this technology, like we have taken up a license, because this is a patent technology. And we'll use this technology, this technology and set up lines for indigenizing this, you know, product to be supplied to the local manufacturers here of traction motors.

items.statement: Targeting product mix of 75% pipe and 25% value-added products over time
items.quote: We are targeting to achieve a product mix of 75:25, which means 75% will be pipe and 25% will be these miscellaneous products.

items.statement: Transmission line towers have EBITDA margins 3-4% higher than pipe; poles 2-3% higher; monopoles 8-10%+
items.quote: For transmission line tower the product is quite profitable. The EBITDA margins as opposed to pipe is significantly higher by 3% to 4% in some cases

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin expected to improve by ~2% once value-added product lines gain foothold
items.quote: So it is definitely going to be more than the EBITDA levels right now but as future is difficult to say but even still I can totally say that it is going to be higher by 2% or so with all of these lines coming in.

items.statement: Inventory gains from Rs 3,000/t steel price rise on 25,000+ tons inventory will reflect in Q4 numbers
items.quote: It is evident if we are sitting on an inventory a certain inventory like upwards of 25,000 tons and there is a Rs. 3,000 jump in that inventory it will reflect in your numbers, it will definitely reflect in anyone's number

items.statement: Capex of Rs 45 cr CWIP and fixed assets up to Rs 110 cr for crash barrier, transmission towers, poles and pipe inventory infrastructure
items.quote: So, the pipe is already installed. Highway crash barrier is getting installed. We thought one line would be sufficient but the requirement is more so we have to invest more in highway crash barrier.

items.statement: Total installed capacity now 377,000 metric tons across three plants after Orissa commissioning
items.quote: With Orissa coming in, our installed capacity has improved. Now, we stand at 3,77,000 metric tons that we can produce.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capacity utilization ~50% due to Orissa plant ramping up; Bombay and Hyderabad galvanizing at full capacity
items.quote: that Orissa has not reached 50% yet. Orissa we have only done 2000, our installed capacity here is quite more than this. So, we yet have to achieve our capacity utilization in Orissa to a certain level

items.statement: Targeting 30% capacity utilization at Orissa plant in Q4 FY26
items.quote: For Orissa hopefully we will be able to achieve 30% in the quarter four not the entire year because we only started now.

items.statement: Current order book: Orissa 800t pipe + 600t crash barrier + 600t transmission towers in talks; Bombay 2,600t; Hyderabad ~1,000t after renewals
items.quote: Right now we have an order booking of 800 tons in Orissa right now for pipe for upward of 600 in a highway crash barrier and there are products for transmission line tower we are in talks with a couple of companies of around 600 tons.

items.statement: Steel price rally (safeguard duty, anti-dumping, rising iron ore/coal) driving strong domestic demand pickup in Q3
items.quote: The market has really significantly picked up just this month itself due to which, although this is a quarter three number we will talk about it in one month's time we will have this conversation again there is a lot of sale that we have seen in quarter three

items.statement: Orissa pipe dispatches accelerating: 2,000t last month, now 100-120t/day
items.quote: just last month we have 2000 tons dispatched and this month our dispatch it is early to say but every day I am seeing the dispatch is u pward of 100 tons sometime 120 tons

items.statement: Exports steady at 3-5% of pipe sales to 11 countries (Europe, UK); targeting export growth from Orissa plant
items.quote: Our export is very steady. It has been constant for our pipe. We do a lot of export from Mumbai plant, Nagothane plant. It is very steady between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Export inquiries rising from Europe/UK; Orissa capacity to serve export if domestic demand allows
items.quote: Now we are entertaining more and more inquiries. So, if more inquiries are coming, we shall be able to have more orders so those extra orders we will be able to give from Orissa.

items.statement: Crash barrier galvanizing line at Hyderabad running at full capacity; similar line may be needed at Orissa
items.quote: I am glad to a nnounce that the galvanizing plant, which we have installed for crash barrier alone, is running at full capacity in Hyderabad. Now, from this month, we are seeing similar order flow of crash barrier or highway guardrail in Orissa as well

items.statement: Transmission line tower approvals progressing: Gujarat, Sikkim, Meghalaya state approvals secured; Power Grid first inspection completed
items.quote: We have got oursel ves approved in Gujarat and also in Sikkim, Meghalaya, and also power grid, power PGCL, we call it power grid. They have carried out the first inspection

items.statement: Monopole prototype for 132 kVA under development; testing and approvals will take time
items.quote: For 132 kVA we are making a prototype and that prototype we will send for testing so that will take some time

items.statement: Safeguard duty on China and anti-dumping duties on steel products implemented, boosting domestic steel prices
items.quote: There is a safeguard duty that has come in for China, there is an anti-dumping also for some of the steel products. So that has really taken the market in India up

items.statement: Working capital cycle at ~70 days expected to remain healthy or improve given strong demand and rising prices
items.quote: Looks like the markets are staying strong and the demand is very steady and prices are going high. In a situation like that if history has to be considered we have always seen that the working capital cycles remain very healthy.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue up 19% YoY, PAT up 60% YoY, EBITDA margin steady at 3.83% vs 3.85% in FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA levels are very healthy at a steady 3.85% versus the 3.85% was in 2025, and now we are at 3.85% in FY'25, and FY'26 is 3.83% in the first half.

items.statement: Achieved 51% of full-year revenue target in H1 FY26, indicating strong momentum
items.quote: We have already achieved 51% of our revenue in the first half, which is a strong signal that there is a momentum, there is a sustainability in the market.

items.statement: Strong dealer network for pipe and crash barrier; transmission towers sold via EPC contractors; not participating in tenders directly
items.quote: Our line of work is distribution. We have certain dealers we give it to the dealers dealer participate on te nders. We are not ourselves participating in tenders in pipes steel pipes galvanized pipe even in highway guardrails it is a dealer

items.statement: Orissa plant strategically located near SAIL, JSW, Tata, JSP steel plants; raw material logistics cost advantage
items.quote: We are very close to all the steel plant where all the raw materials come from. Steel authority is also under 100 kilometers. JSW is in the same city as us. Tata and JSP are also not far away.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs 72.17 cr at Rs 75/share; current valuation ~Rs 135/share
items.quote: Okay with this Rs. 72.17 crore from IPO t hrough IPO and at that time valuation of only Rs. 75 per share and presently company's valuation is around Rs. 135 per share

items.statement: Margin outlook dependent on steel price trajectory; inventory gains may reverse if prices fall
items.quote: who knows but at but at this point in time in January we can definitely say there is an increase of 3000 wh ich has been passed on so it will definitely show in the numbers, the balance sheet

items.statement: Targets 15% revenue CAGR and 20% PAT/EPS growth for next 3-4 years
items.quote: we are on track to deliver 15% CAGR, 15% revenue growth and 20% PAT or EPS growth for next three to four years.

items.statement: Reiterates 15% revenue growth and 20% PAT/EPS growth target through FY29
items.quote: our endeavor is about 20% PAT or EPS growth year-on-year for next 4 years. We have a plan in place till FY '29.

items.statement: New hormonal API plant at La Chandra to start commercial production by end of Q2 or early Q3 FY27
items.quote: We are now, you know, going to kick start the commercial by Q2, end of Q2 or early of Q3 of FY '27.

items.statement: Invested in La Chandra Pharma Lab for backward integration of hormonal API
items.quote: the company has also invested in La Chandra Pharma Lab which operates an EU GMP and WHO GMP certified hormonal API manufacturing facility

items.statement: Added 400 million tablets/capsules capacity at Gujarat facility in December 2025
items.quote: This includes capacity of around 400 million tablets and capsules which was recently commissioned at our Gujarat facility in December 2025.

items.statement: Total installed capacity of 1.65 billion tablets/capsules, 20 million sachets, 10 million bottles across two facilities
items.value: 1.65 billion tablets or capsules, 20 million sachets and 10 million bottles
items.quote: We have a total installed annual capacity of 1.65 billion tablets or capsules, 20 million sachets and 10 million bottles across both facilities.

items.statement: Acquired seven brand trademarks from Bayer Zydus Pharma in July 2025 for infertility and women's healthcare
items.quote: In the month of July 2025, CORONA had acquired seven brand trademarks from Bayer Zydus Pharma.

items.statement: In-licensed brands in women's healthcare and urology from Ferring Pharmaceuticals
items.quote: Apart from the brand acquisition, we also have in-licensing some brands in women's healthcare and urology therapies from Swiss giant Ferring Pharmaceuticals

items.statement: Growing at 1.5x IPM; ranked #1 fastest growing among top 30 pharma companies per MAT September 2025
items.quote: As per PharmaTrac data, CORONA is number one fastest growing pharmaceutical company amongst top 30 pharma companies as per MAT September '25 data.

items.statement: Chronic and semi-chronic segments contribute ~70% of revenues driving healthy volume growth
items.quote: CORONA's healthy volume growth trajectory is on the back of our focus on the chronic and semi-chronic segment which contributes approximately 70% of our total revenues.

items.statement: Launching infertility portfolio (Fostine, Menodac, Ovidac, Luprofact) with dedicated <50 person team in 3-4 months
items.quote: we are going to launch a separate team for infertility and entering into the infertility market with these products, a specialized team of about less than 50 people across the nation

items.statement: Plans to unlock 6-7 new therapies (infertility, spine, rheumatoid, CNS, dermatology, GI) over 3-5 years
items.quote: We are working to develop six, seven therapies today like infertility, spine, rheumatoid, CNS, dermatology, gastrointestinal. And what we have decided, we will unlock each therapy at the right time

items.statement: Focus on specialist/super-specialist doctors in urban/semi-urban markets (middle of pyramid strategy)
items.quote: our specialist and super specialist, which is the biggest chunk of IPM, we have been super focused over there. And whatever therapies we are entering from today to tomorrow, or day after, our focus will remain strong on the specialist and super specialist.

items.statement: Holds ~1.9% market share in covered therapies growing at ~10% (25% above IPM)
items.quote: today, as far as our covered market is concerned, wherever therapies we are, we are about 1.9% market share and that market is growing by 10%, which is about 25% more than the IPM.

items.statement: MR productivity ~INR 4 lakh/month; varies 2.5-8 lakh by tenure; plans 5-7% annual MR headcount growth
items.quote: CORONA's PCPM per capita per month is about 3.9 lakhs, about 4 lakhs rupees. But if you dissect this PCPM from the people who have joined for zero to three years, three to six years and six to nine years. The productivity varies from 2.5 lakhs to 8 lakhs.

items.statement: ~2,600+ medical representatives currently; adding 5-7% annually for new therapy launches
items.quote: today we are on a critical mark of around 2,600 plus medical representatives. And by launching our new super specialty therapies like infertility, spine rheumatoid, etcetera, we require that 5% to 7% people.

items.statement: Annualized ROE 31.1% and ROCE 49.7% for H1 FY26
items.quote: our annualized ROE for H1 FY '26 stood at 31.1% whereas our annualized ROCE for H1 FY '26 stood at 49.7%.

items.statement: Boards of Devyani International and Sapphire Foods approved merger on 1 Jan 2026 to create one of India's largest F&B platforms with 3,000+ stores and ~INR 8,000 crore annualised turnover.
items.quote: The proposed merger is about far more than combining 2 businesses - it is about creating one of the largest F&B platforms in India, that is positioned to seize the vast, long-term opportunity in India's F&B economy.

items.statement: Merged entity expected to cross $1 billion USD in annual revenues by the time merger is consummated.
items.quote: By this time, the merger gets consummated, the merged entity is likely to cross $1 billion USD in annual revenues.

items.statement: Cost synergies of INR 2.1-2.25 billion net of costs expected; 60% in first year post-merger, 100% within two years.
items.quote: We are expecting in the first year post-merger approval, we will be able to realize a substantial part of the synergy. Our estimate is that number will be close to 60%. And in the second year, we will be able to realize the balance amount of synergies.

items.statement: Targeting low double-digit brand contribution margin for Pizza Hut in first year post-merger, up from current 7-8% pre-IND-AS margins.
items.quote: In the first year, we will be able to kind of get to a positive brand contribution margin on Pizza Hut. Our endeavor will be to be at a low double digit given what we have as part of the deal and negotiation with Yum! and as part of our revival strategy.

items.statement: No net new Pizza Hut unit openings required; flexibility to close and relocate stores while keeping net count non-negative.
items.quote: We will not be under stress to open net new units from where we are today. What we have negotiated is a small number that can be easily achieved. We will have the full flexibility to shut the stores and turn around the stores and put new stores in place.

items.statement: Will take over marketing, innovation, technology and supply chain for Pizza Hut; only technology and SCM for KFC.
items.quote: For Pizza Hut, we will be taking over marketing and innovation, and we will be taking over technology and supply chain function as well. Whereas for KFC, as of now, it is going to be only technology and SCM.

items.statement: Functional leadership hiring for marketing, technology and supply chain already underway; some offers closed, others in pipeline; ready by June 2026.
items.quote: We have already gone and hired some positions, and some of them are in pipeline. So rather than waiting for the merger approval, we have already started working on these areas, recognizing what we have and what we do not have.

items.statement: Shortlisted a large global technology vendor for unified tech stack across all brands; internal approvals pending.
items.quote: You will also be happy to know that we have also already shortlisted a technology partner who will help us and create the new technology assets in terms of web and app.

items.statement: Share swap ratio of 177 Devyani shares for 100 Sapphire shares; promoter entity RJ Corp to buy 18.5% of Sapphire Mauritius stake bilaterally at floor INR 280/share over 3-15 months.
items.quote: The pricing, there has been a floor price set between the two parties of INR 280 which is driven by both the fairness valuation, which was around that level and the 90-day average as well.

items.statement: One-time fee of INR 320 crore payable to Yum! Brands for merger approvals; will be capitalised.
items.quote: INR320 crore, the fee that we are going to be paying to Yum, that is a onetime payment, whereas synergies will accrue year after year for the entire whatever lifespan of the business.

items.statement: Pizza Hut incentives from Yum! secured for 10-year period to support turnaround.
items.quote: So, Gaurav, we have incentives for a period of 10 years. And I think in your model beyond 10 years, the NPV, I guess, will be zero. So therefore, I mean, these are long-term.

items.statement: Unified franchisee model with national rights seen as competitive advantage to capture QSR growth vs fragmented approach.
items.quote: A single, well-capitalized franchisee with national rights is much better positioned to capture this growth potential.

items.statement: India QSR market estimated at >$25 billion and growing; structural tailwinds from rising incomes, urbanisation, changing preferences.
items.quote: India's food and beverage market is large, getting formalised and expanding rapidly with independent estimates placing the broader food services market at more than $100 billion and the QSR segment alone at more than $25 billion and growing.

items.statement: KFC same-store sales growth weak for both companies (~45% home delivery); unified technology strategy expected to drive SSSG recovery.
items.quote: Today, let us say, if you look at KFC for both the businesses, close to 45% of the business gets home consumed or home delivered. And there technology has a huge role to play.

items.statement: Combined balance sheet will be stronger post-merger; Devyani standalone debt not a concern.
items.quote: If at all, let us say, when we merge, the balance sheet will become even stronger versus where we are today. And even from a Devyani standalone perspective, the debt is a small number.

items.statement: Merger approval process expected to take 9-15 months; deep integration planning to occur after CCI approval.
items.quote: As you know that the entire merger approval process is going to take about 12 months' time, so it could be anywhere from 9 months to 15 months.

items.statement: Boards of Devyani International and Sapphire Foods approved merger on 1 Jan 2026 creating entity with 3,000+ stores and ~INR 8,000 crore annualised turnover
items.quote: The proposed merger is about far more than combining 2 businesses - it is about creating one of the largest F&B platforms in India, that is positioned to seize the vast , long-term opportunity in India's F&B economy. The merged entity will have more than 3,000 stores globally and a turnover of approximately INR 8,000 crore on an annualised basis

items.statement: Merged entity likely to cross $1 billion USD annual revenues by merger consummation
items.quote: By this time, the merger gets consummated, the merged entity is likely to cross $1 billion USD in annual revenues.

items.statement: Cost synergies of INR 2.1-2.25 billion net of costs; 60% in year 1 post-merger, 100% within 2 years
items.quote: We feel confident that we will be able to deliver these synergies by way of G&A, by way of additional Yum! incentives, by way of additional negotiations on the procurement costs and so on and so forth. items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance: FY26 ~20%, FY27 ~21%, FY28 ~22%
items.quote: Next year margin is around 21% to 22%. Maybe next year, it is 21%. And next to next in 2028, it should be 22%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin ~20.5% driven by strong execution, OEM demand, stable exports
items.quote: See, benefited from strong execution, healthy OEM demand and stable export orders. While we may not see the same growth rate every quarter, we believe the current run rate is sustainable.

items.statement: Brakes segment EBITDA margin currently 12-13%, expected to reach 18% next year as utilisation improves
items.quote: So far as Brakes is concerned, it is less because we have just started and recovery that is in process as soon as we increase the volumes, what we foresee what we have given for the next year is comparatively a conservative figure. But from about 12% to 13%, it may go up to 18% next year.

items.statement: Raw material volatility (copper, steel) being mitigated via partial pass-through contracts, monthly renegotiation, yield improvement, process efficiency
items.quote: Our contracts typically allow for partial pass-through. We are in the process of passing the increased raw material cost to the customers, and that is a process maybe depending upon three months contract, six months contract for revision of rates. So that is a continuous process that we are following.

items.statement: Management targeting monthly price revisions instead of 3-6 month cycles due to extreme volatility; customers responsive so far
items.quote: Considering the volatility in the prices, we cannot avoid by the contract that we have already entered with them. We are already talking with them that it will be on a monthly basis instead of three months or six months.

items.statement: Proactive measures to reduce raw material cost burden by ₹55-60 lakh/month this month, ₹75-80 lakh/month from next month via process and yield improvements
items.quote: A number of actions have been already taken by the management, which will definitely result in reduction in the raw material cost by about ₹60 lakhs to ₹70 lakhs per month which will be actually the burden of raw material prices per month will be around ₹70 lakhs, but this month, we will be able to reduce it due to process improvement by about ₹55 lakh to ₹60 lakh. And from the next month, it will

items.statement: FY26 CapEx incurred ~₹15 cr; FY27-28 planned CapEx ~₹20 cr over two years (₹7 cr Alkop, ₹7 cr Bearings, ₹6 cr Brakes)
items.quote: So far as this year is concerned, we have already completed CapEx of around ₹15 crores. Additionally, for next two years what we have envisaged is around ₹20 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 CapEx ~₹3 cr; remaining ₹17 cr over next two years
items.quote: Maybe in the remaining period in this quarter, we may be incurring expenditure to the tune of around ₹3 crores and rest ₹17 crores consolidated basis, we have to incur during next two years.

items.statement: Capacity utilisation: Bearings ~90%, Alkop ~65%, Brakes ~60-65%; sufficient headroom for growth without major new capacity
items.quote: In Menon Bearings, bushing and washers, we are around 90% and in aluminium, aluminium castings we are around 65%. And Brakes, we are around at 60%, 65%. So there is still a lot of room for future expansion.

items.statement: Alkop capacity doubling from 1,440 to 2,880 MT over next two years to fulfil export-driven growth
items.quote: In the PPT, we've mentioned that we're planning to double the Alkop capacity from around 1,440 to 2,880 in the next two years.

items.statement: Alkop incremental revenue target ₹50-60 cr over two years from wallet share gains and new customers
items.quote: We have already increased our wallet share with the existing customers as well. Then addition of new customers, what we discussed just now, that is in the pipeline. And we are sure that we will be able to grab that business as well so that there will be addition of ₹50 crores, ₹60 crores during the next two years, 100%.

items.statement: Export growth driven by new business with Allison Transmission (>₹2.5 cr/month), Federal-Mogul DRiV, and other new customers; tariff impact minimal
items.quote: we have already started additional business with one of the major customers from U.S.A., that is Allison Transmission, and that alone business has added value of more than ₹2.5 crores a month. Apart from that, Federal-Mogul DRiV is also there, and other customers also added in the fold of our company so

items.statement: Alkop: John Deere (India, Europe, USA, South America) driving export growth; new customers Concentric Pumps, Eaton, Brakes India, GPP, Allison, Miyakawa in pipeline
items.quote: We are doing John Deere USA, John Deere Europe, John Deere South America. So that's one place. At the same time, we are doing continuous efforts to get new customers also.

items.statement: Brakes: ~₹1 cr/month run-rate; two OEMs in advanced talks; auto giant visit by Feb 15 may add ₹1-1.5 cr/month; railway dynamometer in 4-5 months
items.quote: One of the auto giants have already contacted us. So we had a detailed meeting with them. And probably, they will visit to our establishment in the next month by 15th of February, wherein we expect -- we are not very sure, but we may expect that additional business of at least ₹1 crore will start with them per month.

items.statement: Aftermarket competitor opportunity: 800 parts offered; selecting high-value parts; ~₹1 cr/month from April/May after testing approval
items.quote: Partly, we have gone forward and probably after having report from them so far as the testing is concerned, we may start a business so far as out of 800 parts, some of the parts have been already developed and samples have been approved. And we are likely to get another business of ₹1 crores per month from April or May onwards.

items.statement: Exports 36% of Q3 revenue; 60-65% to USA, rest EU, South Africa (~₹6-7 cr/yr via Dubai); shifting to ex-works terms to mitigate tariff/FX risk
items.quote: Exports accounted for over 36%, underscoring the strength of our international customer base and diversification benefits.

items.statement: Moving US exports to ex-works from DDP: cash conversion 180→30 days, 90% of exports targeted; may lose 15% top-line but margins improve ~5%
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the cash conversion, whatever you are telling you, it will drop down from 180 days to almost 30 days. That is amazing we can save much -- so far as interest is concerned on working capital.

items.statement: Ex-works shift reduces cash conversion cycle from 180 to 30 days, saving significant working capital interest
items.quote: Prices from 180 days, it will come down to 30 days. There is a great amount of saving on account of interest as well as the total turnover of inventory.

items.statement: Revenue mix FY26: Bimetal ~74%, Alkop ~22%, Brakes ~3%; FY27 expected: Bimetal 65-68%, Alkop 25-28%, Brakes remainder
items.quote: For this year, it will remain more or less constant. But next year, it will change. Maybe it can be about 65% to 68% in Bimetal, about 25% to 28% in Alkop and remaining in Brakes.

items.statement: Asset turnover target 2.0-2.5x at peak utilisation with current capacity and planned CapEx
items.quote: It will be almost 2.5.

items.statement: Solar installation (3.8 MW) saves ₹2.25 cr/yr electricity; process/yield improvements save ₹8-9 cr/yr; automation to reduce manpower/rejection long-term
items.quote: See, one thing is electricity charges or power charges for one year, we are 100% sure that we should be able to curtail the expenditure on electricity by ₹2.25 crores per year. Apart from that, due to the process improvements improved yield in the raw material, we should be able to save at least ₹8 crores per year.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility (copper ₹900→₹1,200/kg) may dent margins; partial pass-through and monthly renegotiation in progress
items.quote: Before it used to be like from ₹900 to ₹950, but now it's from ₹900 to ₹1,200 a kilo. So that's a lot of cost which we are bearing.

items.statement: Railway brakes delayed by dynamometer procurement (4-5 months); registration complete, in-house dyno required by railways
items.quote: We have now given to another manufacturer and he has given the assurance that it will be completed within a period of four months from now.

items.statement: US tariff on HCV/LCV reduced from 50% to 25%; customers share remaining tariff burden; China+1 policy benefiting India sourcing
items.quote: Earlier the tariff was 50%, now it has reduced to 25%. Aditya Menon: And on that 25% also because of good relation and we have supported them during tough times, they share the burden with

items.statement: Loan growth guidance maintained at 12% and above for FY26
items.quote: So, what we said the last time around was that we want to be 12% and over. So, we are still sticking to that.

items.statement: ROA expected to reach 1.15-1.2% in 12 months
items.quote: So, if I were to hazard a guess, in a 12-month period, we should end the 12 months at about 1.15% to 1.2% or thereabouts.

items.statement: Credit cost expected at 7-8 basis points near term
items.quote: So, 7, 8 basis points would be the credit cost in the near term.

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilize at current level this quarter despite 25 bps repo cut
items.quote: we think that we should remain stabl e at the level that we are. There may be some marginal movements, but we do not think that is going to be very significant

items.statement: Cost of deposits fell 7 bps to 5.34% in Q3
items.quote: Cost of deposits have been coming off; they came off 7 basis points in the last quarter from 5.41% to 5.34%.

items.statement: GNPA fell to 2.67% YoY, partly due to Rs.900 cr write-off
items.quote: Overall gross NPA reduced by 163 basis points from 4.3% to 2.67% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Slippage ratio at 16 bps for quarter, annualized 64 bps
items.quote: Our NPA slippage rate is at 16 basis points for the quarter, not annualized. So, on an annualized basis, we are at 64 basis points.

items.statement: MSME disbursements grew 45% YoY, retail including gold grew 60% YoY
items.quote: On a YOY basis, MSME, in this case, including LAP, disbursements grew by 45% year-on-year, and retail loans, including gold disbursements, grew by 60%.

items.statement: Targeting one-third corporate, two-thirds retail/MSME/Agri in medium term
items.quote: In the medium term, I think we would near, I mean, head towards 33%, one-third corporate and the rest being retail, MSME and Agri.

items.statement: Home loan growth negative QoQ due to pricing discipline vs peers at 7.1%
items.quote: Yields on housing finance, especially prime housing finance have dropped to a very, very low level with nationalized banks now operating at 7.1% and some of them are even sub-7%.

items.statement: 16 export customers inquired about RBI trade relief measures
items.quote: As of this moment, I think about 16 of our customers have asked us to take a look at whether they can access this funding source.

items.statement: Price competition in gold loans exists but trust and processes are differentiators
items.quote: Pricing competition is there. I am not saying it is not there, but it is not insurmountable.

items.statement: Plan to add 10-12 branches in core southern states near term
items.quote: In the near-term, there may be 10 or 12 branches that are built up.

items.statement: CD ratio at ~82%, headroom to 85-86%, exploring non-reserve funding
items.quote: We are at approximately 82% or so in the last quarter. We think that there is still some headroom available there. We can get to 85%, 86%.

items.statement: CASA grew 15% YoY to Rs.37,640 cr
items.quote: CASA balances grew by 15% year-on-year to Rs.37,640 crores versus the earlier figure of Rs.32,830 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan book grew 26% annualized, avg LTV 55%, ticket Rs.2.46 lakh
items.quote: We continue to grow our gold loan business, which now stands at Rs.21,303 crores with an average LTV of approximately 55%. This includes portfolios that may have been acquired by the Bank and an average ticket size of approximately Rs.2.46 lakhs. The gold loan book grew on an annualized basis by 26%.

items.statement: MSME loans at Rs.14,019 cr, 12% growth excluding write-off
items.quote: MSME business loans now stand at Rs.14,019 crores, which is a growth of 12% excluding the write-off done during March 2025.

items.statement: Retail segment grew 23% YoY
items.quote: Retail segment continues to grow for us; it has grown YOY at 23%.

items.statement: Co-lending/partnership book at ~Rs.1,900 cr ex-credit cards, mostly gold
items.quote: Our current balances on these partnerships is approximately Rs.1,900 crores or thereabouts, ex-credit cards.

items.statement: Export portfolio monitoring for tariff impact; no material deterioration yet
items.quote: We are looking at it very closely. And as of this juncture, as I said earlier, we do not see any material deterioration in our portfolio.

items.statement: Credit card issuance stopped since March 2024; working on alternate strategy
items.quote: From March of 2024 onwards, fresh issuances have been stopped. We had engaged with both the counterparty as well as the regulator to try and have it restarted, but we have not had any success on that front.

items.statement: Investment book grew significantly, driving highest investment income in 8-12 quarters
items.quote: That is because the investment book itself has grown quite significantly. So, if you see the investment book, last quarter it grew by what, Rs.7,000 crores or so.

items.statement: Staff retraining via external classroom sessions for MSME lending
items.quote: We have been sending our folks for intensive classroom sessions outside of our offices in third-party locations so that they can learn more about MSME businesses.

items.statement: Expect better loan growth in Q4 FY26 than Q3 FY26 and aim to reach industry-level growth Y-o-Y soon
items.quote: So, I think this is what we start with. So, we expect better than this in this quarter. And yes, the ma rket which is having the growth is certainly is our aspiration , and we will be moving in that line only

items.quote: So, still we will say that we would like to defend to 2.76, but then we hope for a better, I think.

items.statement: Expect NIMs to improve in FY27 as deposit repricing lags loan repricing
items.quote: Actually, what we see that the NIM s will further impr ove because whatever the deposit was taken, that is going to be repriced in this quarter or next financial

items.statement: Credit cost guidance around 26 bps for coming quarters, similar to 9-month run rate
items.quote: Yes, if you look at our 9-month credit cost is about 26 bps, right, so what sir is indicating is, we would like to try and achieve that kind of a number going forward.

items.statement: NIM declined from 2.91% in Dec'24 to 2.76% in Dec'25 despite 125 bps repo cut, but improved sequentially from Q2
items.quote: In December '24, our NIM was around 2.91%. And though there is a rate cut of 125 basis point, since then, till 31st of December '25. But then, if you see from 2.91%, we stand at 2.76%.

items.statement: MCLR book at 32%, rest linked to external benchmarks; deposit repricing lag expected to boost NIM
items.quote: Our book MCLR is around 38%. The other remaining is the EBLR, that is repo linked rate, benchmark rate.

items.statement: Corporate sanctions pending disbursement of INR 24,000-26,000 crores; good pipeline in various stages
items.quote: Even right now in the Corporate only, I am saying, around INR 24,000 crores to INR 26,000 crores is sanctioned and disbursement pending. And we further have a good pipeline in various stages of sanction.

items.statement: RAM segment grew 11.50% Y-o-Y; Retail 21.67%, Agri 19.75%
items.quote: And the growth in the RAM sector certainly increased by 11.50%, 21.67% growth in Retail and 19.75% in Agri, so the robust growth is coming into the RAM segment.

items.statement: GNPA and NNPA reduced to comfortable range; SMA2 at INR 4,285 crores (above INR 5 cr); PCR >95%
items.quote: And coming to SMA2, we are again at the very lowest level of INR 4,285 crores, above INR 5 crores. I think this also gives a good color that the first time bank has crossed INR 10 lakh crores of advances as a bank.

items.statement: ECL transition impact estimated at INR 4,200-4,300 crores net of existing provisions; bank can absorb in first year without 5-year dispensation
items.quote: If we take the total requirement for the ECL, keeping in view our book, and the provisions which we are already holding, if we come to the netting position, it is hardly 4200 to 4300 range.

items.statement: Shed INR 38,000-40,000 crores high-cost bulk deposits; contracted treasury by INR 15,000 crores; IBPC reduced to zero
items.quote: The first thing is that we already had the funds inside. So, around INR 38,000 crores to INR 40,000 crores, we have shed off the bulk deposits, which was at the higher cost.

items.statement: CASA increased 140 bps QoQ (~INR 9,000 crores); Retail term deposits up INR 15,000-16,000 crores
items.quote: the Union Bank of India January 14, 2026 CASA of the bank is increased by 140 basis point. Now, if you take the CASA, around INR 9,000 crore CASA is increased. items.statement: Technology capex budget of INR 1,600 crores for FY26, higher than previous year; focused on infrastructure, cybersecurity, digital platform
items.quote: we have for this year around 1,600 crores of capital budget for the tec hnology, and it is higher than the previous year's level also. And that is going on the strengthening the infrastructure network, as well as strengthening our cybersecurity

items.statement: Plan to open 75 branches in FY26 and 200 more going forward; digital platform handles 80% of liability account openings
items.quote: We have a plan of opening some 75 branches this year itself, and going forward, we want to further open 200 branches.

items.statement: Gold loan yield at 8.85-9% for 9M FY26; LTV 75% non-Agri, 85% Agri
items.quote: coming Union Bank of India January 14, 2026 around, up till now, I can take, not exactly with the quarter, but the 9 months, it is coming around 8.85%-9% levels

items.quote: Yes, actually, the total, till date we have sanctioned around 78 of the proposals around INR 500 crores. And within which 61 proposals of INR 216.64 crores have already been disbursed.

items.statement: ROA at 1.35% (highest); RoE at highest; CD ratio domestic <81%, global 80-83%; LCR, NSFR within range
items.quote: The Return on Assets is exactly 1.35 %, which is again the highest one. The R oE is again the highest one

items.statement: Recovery outlook FY26: expect similar quarterly average (~INR 3,000 crores); FY27 regular recoveries may improve, large resolutions uncertain
items.quote: You can expect more or less the same average, what we have done in the last 3 quarters, it will be there.

items.statement: Bank well capitalized (14-15% capital); adequate profit to absorb ECL transition in first year without using 5-year dispensation
items.quote: Bank is well capitalized and profit is adequate to take care of ECL provision requirement in the first year itself.

items.statement: Project MUSKAAN simplifying 300+ processes for staff efficiency; 32,000 of 74,000 staff are FRM, Engineers, CAs
items.quote: Under project Muskan, we have currently identified around 300 odd processes, which we are trying to simplify, so that our employees can serve their customers in a better way.

items.quote: For existing portfolio, there won't be any additional impact because either COD has been achieved or COD has been extended. For only new cases where COD is getting extended, this will have some impact.

items.statement: Treasury income INR 900 crores includes mutual fund sales, HTM sales, forex, swaps; contracted treasury book by INR 15,000 crores to shift to higher-yielding loans
items.quote: This includes mutual fund income also. There is a part that is HTM sale also is there. Then exchange income also, because of this fluctuation, we could garner more exchange income. All these have led to this INR 900 crores treasury income.

items.statement: Volume guidance for FY2026 maintained at 20 million tonnes
items.quote: So, we are not changing any guidance on the volume numbers for FY 2026.

items.statement: Expects double-digit volume growth for FY2027 and FY2028, targeting 22.5-23 million tonnes in FY2027 and 25.5 million tonnes thereafter
items.quote: And we are seeing maybe early teens maybe closer to 23 million tonnes, 22.5 million tonnes to 23 million tonnes, and 25.5 -- as we go up and it should be anything ranging between 12% to 15% growth.

items.statement: FY2026 capex INR 2,500-2,800 crores including INR 600 crores for Jaisalmer and INR 50-60 crores for Nathdwara wall putty
items.quote: CAPEX number in this year should be INR 2,500 crores to INR 2,800 crores and out of that Jaisalmer would be INR 600 crores.

items.statement: FY2027 capex around INR 3,500 crores including INR 3,000 crores for 7 million tonne expansion
items.quote: And next year CAPEX would be around INR 3,500 crores, which would include around INR 3,000 crores of the CAPEX on the 7 billion tonne expansion.

items.statement: FY2028 spillover capex INR 1,000-1,200 crores
items.quote: 2028 will be the spillover CAPEX in the range of INR 1,000 crores - INR 1,200 crores.

items.statement: Buxar grinding unit to be commissioned within 30 days; all remaining Panna work by end of February
items.quote: The Buxar Greenfield grinding is the advanced stage of completion, and we feel that within the next 30 days this should get commissioned. With this, we are confident that all the remaining work of the project at Panna like OLBC, etc. would also get commissioned within February.

items.statement: Jaisalmer integrated plant and Punjab/Rajasthan grinding units targeting commissioning by September 2027
items.quote: We are hopeful that by September 2027, this should get commissioned. We are soon going to start work at both the grinding locations in Punjab and Rajasthan, so that also we are confident that by September 2027 we should be able to commission the same.

items.statement: Rajasthan wall putty plant (4 lakh tonnes) expected commissioning by September 2026
items.quote: We have also taken up a Greenfield wall putty plant in Rajasthan and the work on the same has already been started and we expect that by September 2026 we should be able to commission these 4 lakhs tonnes additional wall putty plant.

items.statement: Panna Line 2 clinker capacity 3.3 million tonnes; potential to reach 4 million tonnes by end of FY2027 after 6 months optimal run
items.quote: So, maybe in the next fiscal it is end of next fiscal that we will see the possibility , how we accelerate it to higher capacity to about 4 million tonnes.

items.statement: March quarter could be one of the best ever; industry growth 7-8% but year-on-year Q4 growth may be 6-7% due to high base
items.quote: So, the March quarter, I think it could be one of the best quarters what we have ever seen. So, it looks like March. And then definitely, as the cycle goes with the March hangover, though it is a good construction period, but marginally in April, the volume does, because there is a lot of inventory of March, which is there in the market.

items.statement: Non-trade demand expected to grow in tandem with cement consumption going forward
items.quote: So, I think the non-trade demand going forward should be good. It should go in tandem with the cement consumption growth.

items.statement: Premium product share increased to 17.3% in Q3 from 14.9% in Q2 and 15.8% year-ago

items.statement: North capacity additions may cause quarterly pricing pressure if capacities bunch up, but no major concerns seen
items.quote: So, yes, depending on the capacity, which is coming up, it takes time. I think there should not be much pressure unless one or two capacities bunching up, come up one time. At a time, it may have some pressure for a quarter or two, not beyond that.

items.quote: Q3 number of incentives is lower on account of the GST rate cut and the impact is around INR 25 crores. So, last quarter number was INR 86 crores and this quarter it is INR 60 crores.

items.quote: As of 31st December, we are at 1.41. And I think by March, it could be around 1.6 or something. And next year, also, FY 2027, it should be closer to 2 or reach 2, I think.

items.statement: Expect to grow higher than peer average by end of FY27 while progressing towards 15% EBIT margin for FY27

items.quote: Our deal wins this quarter stand at $1096 million, including the large deals shared earlier. This represents a robust 48% year -on-year growth on an LTM basis.

items.quote: Operating margins expanded by 290 basis points year -on-year to 13.1%, underscoring the progress enabled by our improved operating disciplines and the quality of our revenue growth.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 120 bps QoQ driven by fixed price productivity program and volume growth

items.statement: Headcount reduction driven by productivity gains in fixed-price portfolio and better bench visibility; redeploying existing talent instead of backfilling

items.statement: Return on capital employed strengthened to 26.9% reflecting efficient growth
items.quote: Through disciplined capital allocation and sharper execution, we have strengthened our return on capital employed to 26.9%, reflecting the business that is not just growing, but growing efficiently.

items.statement: New wage code notification led to one-time provision of $30 million exceptional item; studying implications for wage hike cycle timing

items.statement: Unique comprehensive portfolio in Comms (IT, BPO, Network Services, Software) driving market share gains through vendor consolidation

items.statement: AI increasingly embedded across large enterprise engagements driving business experience, process and operations transformation, IT build and change, and IT operations

items.statement: Credit card interest rate cap proposal in India; exposure largely to payment networks not issuers, no near-term impact expected

items.statement: Annual new business TCV target of $3.5-4 billion sounds reasonable based on past 4 quarters trajectory; LTM already at $3.5 billion

items.quote: Headcount remained flat at 23,639 in Q3 compared to 23,678 in Q2. Attrition came in at 14.6%, slightly better compared to Q2.
