items.statement: HNI segment (RESERVE) grew from <Rs 500 crores to Rs 3,000+ crores AUM; 58 RMs; net new flows ~Rs 2,000-2,200 crores YTD; retention 100-110 bps; breakeven expected in 3-6 months.
items.quote: Happy to say that the business which started off with less than Rs 400-500 crores of AUM at the beginning of the current financial year in a very steady format has grown to Rs 3,000 crores plus.

items.statement: UHNI RM count grown to ~191 from 155-160; target 300-350 RMs over 3-4 years adding 40-50 annually.
items.quote: The RMs on the UHNI segment have grown to around about 191 odd RMs, plus a few teams will get added over the next 3-6 months where the offers have kind of already been given.

items.statement: Attrition in H1 offset by strong hiring; added fresh teams in Delhi and Bangalore; deep talent bench gives confidence to invest and grow.
items.quote: As we faced a little bit of attrition over the last 12 to 24 months, our own ability to add a fresh set of legs and an equally enthusiastic and capable set of legs in all our locations including Delhi and Bangalore has really given us a lot of confidence.

items.statement: SEBI introduced co-investment vehicles, reduced large value fund threshold from Rs 75 crores to Rs 25 crores, and allowed AI investors in AIFs, providing additional ammunition for alternates growth.
items.quote: SEBI has taken a lot of proactive steps where we've seen at least three excellent kinds of new initiatives on the AIF side. One, clearly, is the introduction of the co-investment vehicles. Second is the introduction of a large value funds being reduced from Rs 75 crores to Rs 25 crores. And thirdly, the introduction of AI investors on the AIF side.

items.statement: TBR revenue quality improved with diversification across 6-7 asset classes; equity brokerage ~Rs 60-65 crores quarterly; remaining Rs 115-120 crores from unlisted, fixed income, real estate, real assets.
items.quote: The first line, which is obviously there is the secondary brokerage coming on stocks, right. So there, obviously, now we're kind of covering two segments. We're covering the institutional segment and the family office segment through the B&K transaction. And we are covering the HNI on the secondary side. So, I think those three things put together today aggregate to about a Rs 60-65 crores equity

items.statement: TBR revenue not expected to grow dramatically over next 2-3 years; healthy inflation-linked growth; growth to shift more to ARR AUM.
items.quote: I don't see it dramatically increasing over the next 2-3 years, a healthy inflation linked growth. But obviously, I think a part of that resultant growth will show up in the ARR AUM growth because it kind of gives us the ability to continuously add more to the ARR as compared to the TBR.

items.statement: HNI business expected to breakeven in 3-6 months; ET Money targeting run-rate breakeven by end of next financial year.
items.quote: Definitely HNI business will be breaking even next year, or middle half of next year. And ET Money, hopefully, on a run rate basis, being close to breakeven next, towards the end of next financial year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income improvement of 200 bps from new businesses (HNI, ET Money) and 100-150 bps from core productivity gains targeted; overall target 45-46% next year.
items.quote: So, we would definitely, as a team, want to target 45 to 46 next year. Hopefully, we can get to 45 aspirationally. But, otherwise, 46 for sure compared to the 48.2 we are at now.

items.statement: First global institution mandate secured in private equity vertical in Q3; strong pipeline of institutional mandates and fund launches in AIF/SIF segments.
items.quote: we are happy to state that we have o ur first mandate from a global institution in the private equity vertical in Q3. Leveraging our established alternative investment capabilities, we are well positioned to capitalize on such opportunities in the future

items.statement: Healthy product pipeline across private side, mutual fund/SIF, real asset, REIT, and GIFT City funds; multiple asset classes and formats adding up.
items.quote: We've got something on the private side, we've got something on the Mutual Fund, SIF side, we've got something happening on the real asset side, we've also got a product happening on the REIT side. So, we've got 4-5 things happening through the quarter.

items.statement: Building inward platform from GIFT City; global institutions and family offices interested in accessing India through GIFT City; launched couple of funds via GIFT City.
items.quote: Outside of these two, obviously, there's a fair degree of excitement in the ability of building the right inward platform from Gift City. I think there are a lot of institutions across the world interested in being able to understand institutions as well a s family offices and in the ability to understand how to access India through the Gift City

items.statement: Geographic expansion planned: Phase 1 covered 6 metros, Phase 2 added 10 cities; next phase targets 10 more cities including Dubai and Singapore.
items.quote: I think today, honestly, if I can think of another 10 cities, including places like Dubai, Singapore, it's a big market. So, fourth, obviously, we have to ensure that we're able to build a much more significant geographical presence.

items.statement: NIM expected to range 7.9-8% for coming quarters
items.quote: We expect again that to be range bound at least for the coming few quarters in the range of 5 to 10 bps, not a lot more variance from there. So we should be able to hold on to our NIMs in the region of 8 as we had mentioned.

items.statement: Book growth target nominal GDP plus 6-7% over medium term
items.quote: In terms of 18% to 20%, the way we've always looked at it, Viral, is the nominal GDP plus 6 to 7. And overall, the thought process does not change.

items.statement: Credit cost target 10-20 bps lower than current 2.5% over longer term
items.quote: The longer term, we'd like to operate, at least 10 to 15 bps or at least 20 bps lower than where we are today. Overall, that is where we would want to operate in the longer term.

items.statement: Consumption growth strong during festive season, positive for quarter
items.quote: Briefly on the macros, consumption growth remains strong during the festive season and positive for the quarter.

items.statement: Festive season surge, pent-up demand and GST cuts fuelled Consumer Finance growth
items.quote: Festive season surge, pent-up demand and market response to GST cuts fuelled growth.

items.statement: NIM improved to 8.09% in Q3FY26 from 7.95% in Q2FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin, NIM, for Q3FY26 improved to 8.09% vs. 7.95% for Q2FY26 and 7.46% in Q3FY25

items.statement: Disbursements at all-time high of ₹17,917 crores, up 15% Q-o-Q
items.quote: Disbursement for Q3, which is the October to December period, clocked in at an all -time high of ₹17,917 crores. It grew by 15% Q-o-Q, led by the Consumer Finance segment followed by the asset-backed businesses.

items.statement: Gross loan book ₹1,14,577 crores, up 2.8% Q-o-Q and 12.2% Y-o-Y
items.quote: The total gross loan book, as on December 31, 2025, stood at ₹ 1,14,577 crores, growing 2.8% sequentially and 12.2% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Gold loans book grew 17.8% Q-o-Q
items.quote: Gold loans book grew by 17.8% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Consumer Finance book grew 17.3% Q-o-Q led by Auto, 2-wheeler and Consumer Durables
items.quote: Book for this segment grew by 17.3% Q-o-Q. This was led by Auto, 2-wheeler and Consumer Durables.

items.statement: CV and CE book showed moderate growth in Q3
items.quote: CV and CE book showed moderate growth in Q3.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 at 2.81%, similar to September 30, 2025
items.quote: Gross Stage 3 as at December 31, 2025 was 2.81%, similar to the number that we had as at September 30, 2025

items.statement: Stage 1 asset quality improved to 95.22%
items.quote: Our asset quality at stage 1 has improved to 95.22%.

items.statement: Stage 3 provision coverage at 55.59%
items.quote: Provision for coverage as on December 31, 2025 for Stage 3 stood at 55.59%

items.statement: Credit cost ₹712 crores vs ₹748 crores prior quarter
items.quote: Credit cost for the quarter was ₹712 crores as compared to ₹748 crores for the prior quarter

items.statement: Unsecured SME book health improved, book reduced ~1% but quality better
items.quote: With the unsecured SME pain that was there for the last five to six quarters, if I can put it that way, that has clearly started easing off. The book, as you would have seen in the investor deck, has actually reduced slightly by almost 1%. But there, the health of the book has actually improved.

items.statement: CV/CE asset quality challenges showed improvement in early buckets in Q3
items.quote: Asset quality challenges that we had called out in H1 showed signs of improvement in Q3 in the early buckets.

items.statement: Vehicle Finance average ticket size reduced ~5% due to GST cuts and manufacturer price cuts
items.quote: In terms of vehicle financing value vs average ticket size, as you put it, there has been a slight reduction in the ticket size of approximately 5%, if I can put it that way.

items.statement: Auto and 2-wheeler ticket size down ~5% due to vehicle price reductions from GST cuts
items.quote: So within 2-wheelers and auto loans, we have seen about a 5% reduction in our average ticket size because the vehicle prices itself have come down.

items.statement: Labour code BAU impact uncertain, awaiting final rules and clarifications
items.quote: Let this space develop over the coming months. And let us get finality. Then it would be better for us to comment on this.

items.statement: Technology investment continuous, no budget constraints even during COVID
items.quote: Over the years, that is one area where while we obviously look at pricing everything that we acquir e and spend very reasonably, if I can use that word reasonably, there has never been a question mark if our CTO comes along and says, this is what we need to invest for future growth. I think we have not even stopped during COVID

items.statement: Customer franchise grew to 22 million, up 4.8% Q-o-Q and 19.3% Y-o-Y
items.quote: Customer franchise grew to 22 million, which is an increase of 4.8% sequentially and 19.3% Y-o-Y

items.statement: ECB book fully hedged, zero impact from INR depreciation
items.quote: On cost of borrowing, our entire ECB book is fully hedged. So there is zero impact. We treat it as a fixed product kind of a thing.

items.statement: RoA annualized 2.35% for Q3, 2.15% for nine months; RoE annualized 13.99% for Q3
items.quote: RoA (annualized) for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 stood at 2.35% and for the nine months was at 2.15% RoE (annualized) for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 stood at 13.99%

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio for lending business reduced to 39.5% in Q3FY26 from 40.7% in Q2FY26
items.quote: Cost-to-income ratio for our lending business reduced to 39.5% in Q3FY26 as compared to 40.7% in Q2FY26 and 42.5% in Q3FY25.

items.statement: State Street partnership in AMC business to bring global practices, credibility, and global access for Indian and foreign investors
items.quote: State Street being one of the world's largest brings a lot of global practices that helps us build the business in India. It's very early stage in our asset management also. We have launched almost 2, 2.5 years back and we've seen very good growth in terms of new customers coming in.

items.statement: Fisdom acquisition consolidated in October, integration ongoing, wealth business scaling from both Groww and Fisdom customers
items.quote: We just recently, October is when we consolidated the acquisition. So there's a lot of work going on the wealth side from a strategy point of view, how we build it, how we are building both for the existing Groww customers and for a lot of affluent customers who want to come in for these services.

items.statement: No dividend expected in near future as company is in high growth phase post IPO and investing in new businesses
items.quote: Sir, we have just got listed three months back and we are still in a very high growth phase. We are still building new businesses where we have raised money in the IPO also to invest in those businesses. And once our growth is probably letting us give dividend also, we will start giving dividend, but we are not expecting to give dividend in the near future.

items.statement: Commodity derivatives active users at 0.26 million end of December 2025, contributing 4% of revenue
items.quote: As reported in our Q3 FY26 KPI Handbook, we had 0.26 million Commodity Derivatives Active Users on our platform at the end of December 2025.

items.statement: Provisioning of INR 2.5-3 crores taken for new labor laws impact on gratuity
items.quote: So there is, I think, already roughly INR2.5 crores to INR3 crores of provisioning that we have already taken for that from a gratuity perspective.

items.statement: Employee count reduced from ~1,450 to ~1,350 QoQ excluding Fisdom employees
items.quote: So previous quarter, we had 1,450* approximate employees. This quarter, we had 1,350. So we've reduced it by 100. So it doesn't include the employees on the Fisdom, which is just October onwards is when the consolidation has happened.

items.statement: Variable cost ~10% of revenue, fixed costs (people, marketing) growing 10-20% annually, EBITDA margin expansion driven by revenue growth
items.quote: The EBITDA margin, if you look at it, is expanding because the revenue has grown significantly. And our variable cost is roughly like - 10% is roughly the variable cost. Rest all is more on the fixed nature.

items.statement: 80-90% of Groww users make profits, derivative-only loss-making customers <0.3%
items.quote: But when we look at the user as a whole, we see majority, or when I say majority, like 80%-90% of them actually make profits. There are very few customers who make losses. And derivatives as a like a derivative only customers are probably very similar as industry where probably similar ratios as what SEBI is also publishing in terms of losses. But that number is like less than 0.3% today and that

items.statement: MTF book growing ~INR 600 crores per quarter, momentum continuing, growth depends on stock volatility and market breadth
items.quote: So, the way I think historically it has grown is roughly INR600 crores we are adding almost every quarter. I think this momentum is continuing from last three quarters and I think we see that momentum to continue in the future as well.

items.statement: Not hitting 15% open interest limit on NSE/BSE, currently at ~50% of limit at contract level
items.quote: I think we'll be probably half of it.

items.statement: Gaining market share across all metrics, no significant competitive change requiring reaction
items.quote: And we've been able to gain market share across all matrices in the last quarter as well as earlier, I think probably last few years. And we think if we can continue in the future as well. We don't see any - like there is a lot of competition already there, but there is no significant change that is happening in competition as such that will warrant any kind of reaction.

items.statement: 915 platform in early stage with limited users, cross-usage with main app makes attribution difficult
items.quote: So, 915 is as of now in a very early stage, so we have very limited set of users. And there is a like a cross also. So, a lot of people who use 915 also use Groww. So, there is a -- it's very difficult for us to attribute at this scale what is the delta that is getting created.

items.statement: Wealth products include mutual fund regular plans, PMS, AIF, private unlisted products, insurance; early traction in mutual funds, AIF, PMS
items.quote: So there is a mutual fund regular plan itself that they already have good AUM, which is a monetized mutual fund, which is already existing. And then there are PMS, AIF. There are distribution of some private unlisted products and also insurance.

items.statement: No plans for payment for order flow, crypto, prediction markets, securities lending as not legal/regulated; SLBM under watch
items.quote: So I think all the products that you just talked about are not really legal or not in the regulated space as of now. And hence, we have taken a conscious call not to do all of these products with the exception of SLBM, which we think is currently in a very nascent stage.

items.statement: Launched Groww Lite for reliability during tech glitches, allowing position viewing and squaring off
items.quote: So for which we have launched Groww Lite using which all our customers can, as the name suggests, it's a very lighter version of Groww. You can't do many other things, but you can see your positions and you can square them off.

items.statement: Broking transacting user to active user ratio improved from ~60% to ~67-68% driven by gold/silver, IPOs, and user acquisition
items.quote: So roughly this number was more closer to 60% earlier. Now it's close to like 67%, 68% now. And that is primarily because last quarter, we talked about like gold, silver was doing well. So some of the customers got activated because of that.

items.statement: F&O active customers 1.47 million, ~80% acquired before 2024, top cohort (>10L turnover) increased significantly post regulation
items.quote: Today we have 1.47. Large part of that is actually existing customers. There is a roughly you can say probably 20% of them would have been acquired in the last year or so.

items.statement: AMC business to use State Street proceeds for organic growth and potential inorganic opportunities
items.quote: See the business right now is in a growth state and it is needing cash. And we've spent some investments we've already made in the last two years. So the cash that we generate will be requiring to scale the business itself. So that's the primary use case of that.

items.statement: Parent company continuing primary investment in AMC, secondary stake sale to State Street leaves enough capital for AMC growth
items.quote: We are also doing primary from our parent company in the asset management. Then the transaction, proposed transaction once upon approval from the regulators will have primary and secondary, will leave enough capital in the AMC for it to grow and scale.

items.statement: CAC calculated on annual basis using total marketing spend divided by new transacting users (one transaction in any product)
items.quote: So, CAC, Yes, sorry. Yes, CAC is, sir, overall spends that we do for marketing across the different functions, whether it's a brand or performance or content. That is the total cost and the new customers that we acquired on our platform.

items.statement: Marketing spend seasonal and opportunistic, annual CAC consistent YoY despite quarterly fluctuations
items.quote: Our acquisition and marketing spends are seasonal across the year spread out and we are a little opportunist in when the time is right, then we spend more. And that is always worked for us to reduce and keep the CAC within the guardrails at the annual basis.

items.statement: Fisdom broking revenue still reported separately, will be integrated post integration completion
items.quote: This broking revenue from Fisdom as of now is part of Fisdom only. So we haven't clubbed yet when we are showing the split that will probably once the integration is done, we'll be able to probably do that.

items.statement: No significant impact from HFT competition as Groww not in HFT/MFT space, meeting current customer speed expectations
items.quote: We are not into, I think you talked about HFT. We are not into HFT and all. As of today, the speed that customers are expecting, we are meeting those expectations. And since none of our customers are into HFT or MFT space, I think that is not required.

items.statement: No specific EBITDA margin target, marketing spend driven by LTV/CAC not EBITDA level, focus on product launches and cross-sell
items.quote: So again, we don't look at EBITDA as like a metric that we want to drive. This is more of an output. The way we look at is basically that if marketing is giving us enough like LTV from the customer, then with the kind of a reasonable CAC, we will probably start spending more.

items.statement: DCR module pricing at 24-24.5 cents per watt on bulk orders; no downward change seen so far
items.quote: DCR price realizations today are about 24 – 24.5 cents per watt when we're looking at on like you know significantly decent size of orders like you know not I'm not talking about like retail spot orders that will be on a much higher price realization This is on a bulk order basis it's about 24-24.5 cents and when we look at and that pricing that we have not seen so far change downwards

items.statement: EBITDA per watt peak maintained for both DCR and non-DCR; absolute margins strong, percentage margins not comparable due to price changes
items.quote: We don't see any pressure in that EBITDA per watt even going forward. The company has achieved so far, we continue to achieve that number sir.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA spread around 8.5 cents per watt at gross level, maintainable subject to DCR/non-DCR mix
items.quote: You're looking at a blended EBITDA so subject to our DCR and non DCR ratios we can maintain.

items.statement: Order book 9.3 GW as of 31 Dec 2025 including 4.5 GW multi-year TopCon cell order
items.quote: We ended the quarter with an order book of 9.3 GW as on 31st December 2025 including a 4.5 GW of multi-year TopCon Cell order.

items.statement: Commissioned 2.5 GW module line at Sulibele; total module capacity 10.3 GW, cell capacity 2.94 GW
items.quote: We commissioned 2.5 GWof model line at Sulibele, taking our aggregate model capacity city of 10.3 GW.

items.statement: Land acquired and financial closure done for 6 GW integrated cell and module facility at Devanahalli; project work in progress
items.quote: We also completed the land payment and also acquired the land which is planned for 6 GW of integrated cell and module facility at Devanahalli and the Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd | Q3FY26 Earnings Conference Call January 16, 2026 project work is progress in line with our plan and all our financial also has been closed for this purpose

items.statement: Module utilization ~43%, cell utilization ~76% in Q3; effective cell capacity 2.155 GW vs installed 2.94 GW due to wafer size difference
items.quote: Q3 production was about 737 MW of modules and about 412 MW of cells with utilization of approximately 43% for modules and 76% for cells reflecting ramp up and product mix.

items.statement: DCR demand driven by Suryaghar (30 GW, 5-6 GW done), Kusum (30 GW, phase 2 from April), C&I (15-16 GW/year growing); utility DCR demand in 9-12 months
items.quote: We are looking at firstly like the current ones if I want to talk one is the Suryaghar Yojna which is about 30 GW. Out of that we have seen about 5-6 GW only completed so far and we are looking at Kusum that's another 30 GW you know that the fresh there is a lot of discussion that Kusum 2 is going to start from April onwards

items.statement: Silver paste consumption halved since line start; targeting further 40% reduction; cost impact minimal due to tech improvements and pass-through contracts
items.quote: Because of improved technology, design and process R&D the consumption of silver paste has come down drastically and the targeted consumption of silver paste, there is an opportunity to bring it down another 40%, this is what we have seen even in China.

items.statement: Aluminium frame ~3 kg per module
items.quote: Aluminium frames are usually about 3 kg per module we usually use.

items.statement: Module capacity intentionally higher than cell (16.3 GW vs 8.9 GW by FY28) due to lower module utilization (60-65%) vs cell (85-90%); production broadly matched
items.quote: Module capacities have a tendency of peak utilization to be at 60 to 65% whereas cell will be about 85 to 90%. The reason is what happens is in module it's an inline production whereas cell is a batch production.

items.statement: ALMM List 2 mandate from June 2026 unchanged; ministry released plan for wafer ALMM showing intent to deepen domestic content
items.quote: There was sufficient time that was given by the ministry, and the ministry's intention is quite clear. In fact, I think what is more reassuring is they have released a plan to further give you know the ALMM for wafers.

items.statement: ALMM cell capacity approved 1.6 GW vs effective 2.155 GW; approval based on running capacity at audit; can reapply as utilization improves
items.quote: The way ALMM works is on the day they come for inspection whatever is the running capacity on that day is the capacity that they approve right and so when you can see this particular capacity of 1,600 MW is as per our utilization rate at that at that time

items.statement: Export markets evaluated; Europe mandating 10% non-China content (Italy, Germany); US team in place; focus remains domestic
items.quote: In Europe there are regulations that mandate about 10% of their capacities to be used from non-China cell and module that probably that also includes the non-China Chinese ownership also for example Italy is the country that started it and ratified that bill and that is further going to get extended to Germany also

items.statement: All key account contracts in US cents; FX passed through at execution billing in INR
items.quote: all key account contracts everything is done in US cents so at only at the time of execution we change it to INR we bill it in INR but orders are all taken in US cents so whatever exchange rate is all passed on to the customer

items.statement: Wafer/ingot capacity planned next; timeline pending clarity on wafer ALMM implementation and demand
items.quote: Wafer is the next transition that we are looking at doing and that is something that you know we are looking as I think we have also announced that we want to do ingot and wafer capacity quite soon. But the only thing is that we don't want to commit on a timeline right now.

items.statement: Key accounts: Hero, CleanMax, Ayana, Bluepine, KPI Green; premium segment, strong customer preference
items.quote: For example, if you look at our client list, it is all you know Hero, CleanMax, Ayana, Bluepine, KPI like you know very key accounts class A accounts that are there.

items.statement: Chinese export rebate cut from 18% to 0% over time; narrows price gap but Chinese pricing independent; Indian pass-through contracts mitigate impact
items.quote: Initially it was about 18% rebate was there that had come down to 13%. Then it came down to 9%, today they're saying zero. So, the market adaptability will happen based on that and of course like in an overall sense perspective it can be treated as an advantage to Indian manufacturers

items.statement: No abnormal project delays seen; order book reflects confirmed orders with advances and PPAs; some normal cascading delays possible
items.quote: We have not seen any abnormal delay lately because of one particular reason. There are always some delays that could happen and there is always a cascading you know one order gets delayed the previous order will come for this thing.

items.statement: Cell efficiency improved from 24.5% to 25.2%; zero MonoPERC, 100% TopCon in FY26 vs 70/30 in FY25
items.quote: If you see we started off with 24.5% efficiency today we're at 25.2% efficiency and that is a growth that we have seen. Next is and then you know moving to your next question which is about the gap between module and cell.

items.statement: Orders taken only with advances and confirmed PPAs; avoid overbooking beyond 12-18 month execution visibility
items.quote: We don't want to take up more orders than what we can execute in the next 12 to 18 months when it comes to modules. The reason the difference between modules and cells what happen the people who I sell module to are developers and these developers can only get bank financing after they sign their PPA and after they get the land.

items.statement: Finance cost 33 crores, lower QoQ due to loan repayment
items.quote: Finance Cost was 33 crores and that was lower than the previous quarter which is subsequent to the loan repayment.

items.statement: Management team: Manjunatha DV (Chairman & MD), Suhas Donthi (President & CEO), Pawan Kumar Jain (CFO)
items.quote: We have from the management side today, Mr. Manjunatha D V, Chairman and Managing Director, Mr. Suhas Donthi Manjunatha, President and CEO and Mr. Pawan Kumar Jain, Chief Financial Officer.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 35-40% for FY26
items.quote: But I would probably hold that broad approach directionally to be 35% - 40% is what I would like in today's economy.

items.statement: AUM grew 77.6% YoY and 15.3% QoQ to ₹55,017 crores as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: Our AUM, as all of you are well aware, is growing at around 77.6% year-on-year, 15.3% quarter-on-quarter, standing at around ₹55,017 crores as of December 31st, 2025.

items.statement: Total disbursements grew 84% YoY and 6.5% QoQ in Q3FY26
items.quote: Total disbursements in Q3FY26 grew by 84% year-on-year and 6.5% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: New product disbursements reached monthly run rate of ~₹950 crores in Dec 2025
items.quote: Our new product disbursements have reached a monthly run rate of approximately ₹950 crores in the month of December.

items.statement: New products contributed 20% of Q3FY26 disbursements vs 17% in Q2FY26
items.quote: Yes, the new product contribution to disbursements in Q3FY26 stands at 20% as compared to 17% in comparison to the previous quarter.

items.statement: NIM including fee and other income increased 22 bps QoQ to 8.62% in Q3FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin, including fee and other income, stands at around 8.62% in Q3FY26 versus 8.4% in Q2FY26. So, it has increased by around 22 basis points from Q2 to Q3.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing reduced 39 bps over three quarters to 7.65% in Q3FY26
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing has reduced from 8.04% in Q1FY26 to 7.65% in Q3FY26, i.e. around 39 bps in three quarters.

items.statement: Disbursement yield for new originations in Q3FY26 is approximately 15.5%
items.quote: The present disbursement yield, pricing of new originations for Q3FY26, is approximately 15.5%, reflecting the impact of new product launches and disciplined risk calibration across originations.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 1.51% in Q3FY26 from 1.59% in Q2FY26
items.quote: Our GNPA for Q3FY26 stands now at 1.51% versus a 1.59% in Q2FY26. It is a drop of another eight basis points here.

items.statement: Stage-1 assets rose to 97.4% in Q3FY26 from 97.1% in Q2FY26
items.quote: Our Stage-1 assets, which I think is an important indicator for any finance Company, rose to 97.4% for Q3FY26 as compared to 97.1% in Q2FY26.

items.statement: Quarterly credit cost improved to 2.62% in Q3FY26 from 2.67% in Q2FY26
items.quote: The quarterly credit cost has improved to 2.62% for Q3FY26 versus 2.67% for Q2FY26.

items.statement: Credit cost for all products except instant consumer loans range-bound at 1.4-1.5% in Q3FY26
items.quote: For all products other than the instant consumer loans, the quarterly credit cost has been a range bound around 1.4% to 1.5% for Q3FY26.

items.statement: 6-MOB 30+ delinquency for instant consumer loans improved 70% YoY in Q3FY26
items.quote: We are pleased to report that this metric has shown consistent improvement on quarter-on-quarter basis, with Q3FY26 reflecting a 70% improvement compared to Q3FY25.

items.statement: LAP portfolio LTV at 45-50% of market value; 70% exposures against self-occupied properties
items.quote: Loan against property book has a portfolio LTV of around 45% - 50% of the market value, providing higher margin against outstanding principal. 70% of our exposures are extended against self-occupied residential or self-occupied commercial properties.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio has zero accounts crossing 30 DPD as of Q3FY26
items.quote: As of Q3FY26, there are no accounts that have crossed 30 DPD.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 320 branches as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: We have expanded our branch network to 320 branches as on date and increased employee strength to 5,264 as on 31st of December 2025.

items.statement: Consumer durable business on track to reach 12,000 retail outlets by FY26 end across 190+ locations
items.quote: Our next product, consumer durable business, continues to scale efficiently, on track to reach 12,000 retail outlets by the year end across 190 -plus locations.

items.statement: NCD share in borrowings increased to 33% as of Dec 2025 from 7% in Mar 2025; target 30-35%
items.quote: The share of NCD in our borrowing stands at 33% as of December 31 st 2025, vis-à-vis 7% as of March 31 st 2025. This increase in NCD borrowings has also contributed to a significant diversification of our investor

items.statement: Raised over ₹4,500 crores via secured NCDs in Q3FY26 and ~₹12,330 crores in 9M FY26
items.quote: In line with the guidance provided during our last investor call, we have successfully raised over ₹4,500 crores by way of secured NCDs during Q3FY26 and a subset of around ₹12,330 crores during the nine months.

items.statement: Long-term borrowing share increased to 84% from 80%; variable-rate borrowing at ~50%
items.quote: The share of long-term borrowing has gone up by about 4% from 80% to 84% in an overall borrowing. The share of variable-rate borrowing stood at approximately 50%.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 4.25x; capital adequacy at 18.17% (Tier-1 at 17.15%)
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio stood at 4.25 times, which gives us headroom for growth. The capital adequacy ratio continues to remain healthy and comfortably above the regulatory requirement at 18.17%, of which the Tier 1 capital is at 17.15%.

items.statement: Liquidity coverage ratio at 156% with surplus liquidity of ₹6,488 crores as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: The liquidity coverage ratio at 156% as on December 31 st, 2025, is well above the regulatory requirement of 100%. • On the liquidity front, we remain comfortable at a surplus liquidity of ₹6,488 crores as of December 31st, 2025

items.statement: Board approved 12-month enabling resolution for ₹5,500 crores equity raise; no specific timeline
items.quote: I think we have taken a 12-months enabling approval, but I think you are well aware of our growth rates.

items.statement: On-book secured mix at ~56%; target 50-60% from gold loans, education loans, salaried PL, LAP
items.quote: Our on-book secured mix stands at around 56%.

items.statement: Prime personal loan: 70%+ customers with bureau score >750, salaried at Category A corporates, income >₹75k
items.quote: Over 70% of customers have bureau scores above 750, are salaried with 'category A' corporates and earn net monthly income exceeding ₹75,000.

items.statement: Gold loan monthly disbursements nearly doubled from ₹110 crores (Sep) to ₹207 crores (Dec 2025)
items.quote: In gold loans, monthly disbursements have nearly doubled from ₹110 crores in September to ₹207 crores in December 2025, driven by strong branch productivity.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle business: avg monthly disbursement ₹100 crores in Q3FY26, 35% QoQ growth
items.quote: Our next product, commercial vehicle business, delivered average monthly disbursement of ₹100 crores in Quarter 3 financial year 2026, representing 35% quarter-on-quarter growth.

items.statement: Education loan: 16,000+ files in 9 months; Dec disbursement ₹118 crores; 300+ instant sanctions worth ₹150 crores YTD
items.quote: Our disbursement in the month of December has reached ₹118 crores. Our instant sanction journey in education loan has crossed 300 sanctions, valued at ₹150 crores year till date.

items.statement: Commercial business AUM ~₹33,700 crores; LAP ₹15,100 crores; unsecured BL/professional/shopkeeper ₹8,000 crores
items.quote: Commercial business AUM stands approximately at ₹33,700 crores, exhibiting a very robust growth year-on-year. Our LAP AUM stands at approximately ₹15,100 crores and is the major contributor to the commercial business AUM. Our unsecured business loan, loans to professionals, and shopkeeper loan AUM stands at approximately ₹8,000 crores, growing substantially year-on-year.

items.statement: Direct non-DSA channel contributes ~22% of commercial retail disbursements; target 40-50% over time
items.quote: I am happy to announce that this non-DSA channel has started contributing approximately 22% of the overall commercial retail loan disbursements. We are on track to achieve 40% - 50% of the total commercial retail disbursement through the direct channel over a period of time.

items.statement: Opex-to-AUM reduced 40 bps QoQ to 4.41% in Q3FY26 despite new business investments
items.quote: Opex-to-AUM for the quarter was at 4.41%, a reduction of 40 basis points quarter-on-quarter, primarily on account of improved productivity and efficiency. Further, this reduction is despite continuous investment in new businesses and distribution.

items.statement: PAT grew 102% QoQ and 702% YoY to ₹150 crores in Q3FY26
items.quote: Our profit after tax stood at ₹150 crores for the quarter, representing a 102% growth quarter-on-quarter and 702% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Annualized revenue run rate at INR 48 crores based on nine-month FY26 performance; expects to surpass FY26 revenue guidance of INR 20-22 crores
items.quote: Based on our nine-month FY26 performance, our annualized revenue run rate now stands at INR 48 crores, although heavy equipment hiring business remains the core growth engine operating at 100% utilization.

items.statement: Current order book at INR 55-56 crores as of today, up from INR 48 crores at December 31
items.quote: We have received around INR 48 crores worth of orders on the nine-month balance sheet, but on same P&L point of view. So, till December 31, our net order book signed at INR 48 crores. Recently, in the past one or two weeks -- in the past two weeks, we have received a few more contracts as well. So, we are currently -- as of if you're talking about today, then we are at around INR 55 to INR 56 cror

items.statement: INR 400 crore CapEx program through FY28 with INR 200 crores already spent; FY26 target was INR 100 crores but INR 154 crores deployed year-to-date
items.quote: During this quarter, we have made exceptional progress on our INR 400-crore CapEx program planned through FY28 with INR 200 crores already spent. Our FY26 CapEx target was INR 100 crores and we are delighted to announce that we have already deployed INR 154 crores worth of machines year to date.

items.statement: Fleet size at 117 machines operating at 100% utilization; last machines started around January 10
items.quote: With fleet size now standing at 117 machines and marquee clients including Larsen and Toubro, Reliance, Jindal Group, KEC International and ITD Cementation anchoring our order book.

items.statement: All machines at 100% utilization as of now; last set of 110-ton and 150-ton machines started around January 10
items.quote: So, for this particular order book, we have already started the execution. All the machines are at 100% utilization as of now. Our last set of machines, which will be 110-ton machines and the 150-ton machines have also been started around January 10.

items.statement: Demand skyrocketing in renewable energy segment (solar and BESS plants); also won bullet train project order via L&T
items.quote: So in the las t six months itself, we have seen that in the renewable energy segment, the demand is skyrocketing like anything. So be it in the solar part and the BESS plants as well. So recently, we have got a lot of orders related to the BESS industry battery storage

items.statement: EBITDA margins at 65-70% due to zero maintenance cost for first 3 years covered by OEMs; expects 60-65% after maintenance kicks in
items.quote: The major, major reason is that, we don't have to pay for any maintenance for the first three years because it's covered by the OEMs of late. So, that is the reason why we don't take an additional 5% hit, which most of our competitors are taking. So, this is the major reason why we are clocking the 65% to 70% range.

items.statement: PAT margin expected to stabilize at 25-30% for next 3-4 years due to depreciation benefits from new machines
items.quote: It will be anywhere between 25% to 30% because in the first two years, we get good amount of depreciation because the machines are absolutely brand new. But eventually, in the next three years to four years, when we do have to pay taxes on the income tax side, then this PAT margin will slightly go down, but it's not a big thing because we will be churning our machines and we will be buying more ma

items.statement: Order book consists of 6-12 month contracts with projects surveyed for minimum 2-year duration; current signed order book at INR 55-56 crores
items.quote: It's a contractual business. We get six months' orders to twelve months' orders. But generally, before we actually take an order from a client, we have a full survey on the site where we make sure that the project should at least go on for the next two years or so.

items.statement: Marquee clients include L&T, Reliance, Jindal Group, KEC International, ITD Cementation; concentration in blue-chip companies but diversified over 12 months
items.quote: With fleet size now standing at 117 machines and marquee clients including Larsen and Toubro, Reliance, Jindal Group, KEC International and ITD Cementation anchoring our order book. These relationships provide us with resilient revenue visibility and a sustainable growth runway.

items.statement: Client concentration can be 30-40% from one company in short term but blends over 12 months; avoids local subcontractors for better cash management
items.quote: So, we have to make sure that whichever company is doing CapEx, we are actually behind them and working with them. So, maybe on a three-month basis or a six-month basis, maybe our order book can come from, like, 30% to 40% -- 40% of our order book can come from one company also.

items.statement: Receivables high due to V-shaped demand cycle and 1.5 month lead time for machines to generate revenue; expected to stabilize as top line grows
items.quote: It is expected to stabilize. It is that this financial year has been like a V-shaped demand cycle for us. So, the whole point is that since we are adding so many machines, like, our projections were just, as I told you, on INR 400-crore CapEx side, even though one and a half years is left, we are already done with more than half of the CapEx cycle.

items.statement: Machines purchased at 100% LTV through 3-4 year funding; raised two equity rounds in past 1.5 years; payback cycle 3-3.5 years
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust, supported by a prudent financial management and an efficient payback cycle of around 3 years to 3.5 years for our equipment investments.

items.statement: Raised two equity rounds in past 1.5 years to fund CapEx; internal accruals now growing with deployed machines
items.quote: We have raised two equity rounds as well in the past one and a half years because, with these cash flows, we are able to buy even more machines.

items.statement: Monthly yield 2.5-3.5% on asset value (30-42% annualized); higher tonnage machines 2.5% monthly, lower tonnage up to 3.5% monthly
items.quote: So, to be on the safer side, on a lower tonnage machines, we can generate up to 3% or 2.8%, 3%. With over time, we can also go to 3.5% of net revenue. But in the higher tonnage machines, our net revenue will be 2.5% only.

items.statement: H2 sees massive overtime adding 10-20% more yield; 30% annual yield can go to 36-48% in strong years
items.quote: And, see, in H2, we get a lot of overtimes, like, massive amount of overtime. So, we can generate 10% to 20% more yields as well. Like, if our yields are 30% per annum, and in some years, we can generate 36% also like being on a hypothetical situation, I'm saying. If the yield of 40%, then it's gonna go up to 48% also.

items.statement: No maintenance cost for first 3 years covered by OEMs; saves 5% vs competitors who bear maintenance
items.quote: The major, major reason is that, we don't have to pay for any maintenance for the first three years because it's covered by the OEMs of late. So, that is the reason why we don't take an additional 5% hit, which most of our competitors are taking.

items.statement: 45% exposure to renewable energy (solar and BESS); no wind exposure due to poor yields and regulatory changes; also serve metro, steel, bullet train projects
items.quote: Now, if you technically see, we -- like, on the renewable energy side, if you see on a pie chart basis, right now, we are at 45% exposure to the renewable energy side.

items.statement: No wind energy exposure; government raised windmill height requirements making 750-ton machines unusable; yields not great in wind segment
items.quote: We don't have any exposure in the wind energy segment. Because for wind energy, you need more than 750 ton-plus and 900 ton-plus machines. So right now, we feel that, that market, that particular market segment does not have good yields because the number of machines in those industries is going up significantly.

items.statement: Government increased average windmill height from 10m to 11-12m, making 750-ton machines unusable for wind energy
items.quote: And recently, the government had also raise d a new rule that the average height of the windmill has been like, suppose if it was 10 meters, then it has been moved to around 11 or 12 meters. So because of that, most of the 750-ton machines are now not usable for the wind energy segment

items.statement: Customer de-hire risk mitigated by 30-day grace period plus one-way mobilization cost (INR 20-25 lakhs for 260-ton machine)
items.quote: So, technically, this is a huge chunk of money because, for example, if I'm renting out a 260- ton machine, so hypothetically I'm sa ying, that if I'm generating INR 15 lakhs of income on a monthly basis from a 260-ton machine then if the contract during the tenure is de-hired -- if we get de-hired, then first of all, we'll be needing a 30-day grace

items.statement: CapEx guidance maintained at INR 400-500 crores as genuine organic target; INR 1000 crore would need further approvals and bank limits
items.quote: So because of that, INR 400 crore to INR 500 crore is a genuine number we feel that with the current internal approvals, we can easily reach there. Now, in order to go to INR 1,000 crores, then we'll be needing further internal approvals and the demand should also be like that.

items.statement: Confident of surpassing FY27 revenue guidance of INR 60-65 crores; current order book supports INR 55 crores revenue
items.quote: So because of that, we are currently at our current pace, we are very confident that we can't surpass that number as well. Because this financial year, if you've seen the first three quarters itself, we have done almost INR 19 crores of revenue, and our guided revenue was INR 20 to INR 22 crores. And now we are at peak capacity. So this year, we will be surpassing by a good percentage

items.statement: FY28 revenue target INR 100 crores achievable if demand continues; currently 55-60% there with two years remaining
items.quote: Yes. We generally feel that there is a very high time because of the kind of demand we are seeing right now. But we don't want to commit to anything. But with our current order book, we are already 55%, 60% there, and it's literally two years.

items.statement: Non-current liability spike due to machine purchases with short moratorium; temporary and will balance out in coming quarters
items.quote: So, the noncurrent liability is actually the machines we purchased. So, we have a very short moratorium period for that. Right? So because of that, we purchased the machines with that particular logic behind it. So, that is the reason why there is a spike in the noncurrent liabilities.

items.statement: Segmental 'others' revenue negative due to accounting entry for free-of-cost spares credit notes received with machine purchases
items.quote: When we buy a lot of machines for the FOC part, the free of cost side, we do get a lot of credit notes as well. So, this is jus t accounting entry of those credit notes entry

items.statement: Family separation in FY24 led to restructuring; company transformed into pure infrastructure equipment hiring play
items.quote: we had given a press release last year regarding this thing, and we had a family separation where our side of the family had taken over this whole company in FY24. So, then we had restructured the whole company, and now we are only focusing on this business, which is our core revenue-generating business

items.statement: Targets INR8,500 crores real estate sales for FY26, a 35% increase over last year
items.quote: if they come through in time, we should be able to surpass our annual plan of 35% increase over last year at about INR8,500 crores.

items.statement: Expects INR750 crores revenue from non-real estate businesses for FY26
items.quote: we achieved about INR575 crores in the first 9 months and hope to do about INR750 crores for the year.

items.statement: Civil contracts segment to degrow by INR150-175 crores from next financial year
items.quote: Since we are not undertaking any new projects in civil contracts, there would be a degrowth in this segment to the extent of about INR150 crores to INR175 crores from next financial year.

items.statement: Plans to complete 5.2-5.3 million sq ft in FY26, a 15-17% increase over last year
items.quote: We plan to complete another 1.5 million to 1.7 million this quarter and take it to a total of 5.2 million to 5.3 million square feet, a growth of about 15% to 17% over last year completions of 4.54 million square feet.

items.statement: Blended net margin on unrecognized revenue of INR18,600 crores is ~30% after project interest
items.quote: The blended net margin at project level after accounting for project interest is about 30% for this unrecognized revenue.

items.statement: Margin on projects completing in next 12-15 months is 18-19%, rising to ~34% for projects beyond 15 months
items.quote: Projects that we have completed and we are going to recognize in the next few quarters and going to complete in the next 12 to 15 months, the margin of the same would be in the range of about 18% to 19%.

items.statement: Expects significant margin improvement from Q3 FY27 as completions ramp up and sales marketing spend normalizes
items.quote: So I think from Q3, it should be significantly better. But first 2 quarters also should be okay, mainly apart from the fact that it is the, there would be an impact on higher sales and marketing.

items.statement: Achieved INR6,097 crores real estate sales in 9M FY26, an all-time high for a 9-month period
items.quote: The first 9 months of FY '26 have been truly exceptional for Sobha with our real estate sales reaching an all-time high of INR6,097 crores in a 9-month period.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 real estate sales of INR2,115 crores, highest ever quarterly sales
items.quote: In Q3, we have surpassed our earlier highest sales with INR2,115 crores.

items.statement: Average price realization of INR14,500/sq ft in 9M FY26, up 8% YoY
items.quote: We have achieved an average price realization of about INR14,500 in the first 9 months versus last year's of about INR13,400, an increase of about 8%.

items.statement: Bangalore achieved highest ever quarterly sales of over INR1,500 crores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: This quarter, Bangalore achieved our highest ever quarterly sales of over INR1,500 crores, thanks to the launch of SOBHA Magnus on Bannerghatta Road.

items.statement: Launched 2.58 million sq ft in 9M FY26; plans 3-4 projects in Q4 totaling ~5.5 million sq ft
items.quote: Overall, we have launched 2.58 million square feet in the first 9 months of this year. Some of the planned launches in this year got delayed due to a combination of factors. We are working towards launching 3 to 4 projects in Q4.

items.statement: Hoskote project (48 acres, 5.4 million sq ft first phase) to launch in Q1 FY27
items.quote: First phase, we are planning to launch it — launch about 5.4 million square feet. That should happen in the first quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: Pipeline of 16.51 million sq ft forthcoming projects to be launched over next 6-8 quarters
items.quote: Additionally, we expect to generate INR7,300 crores of marginal cash flow from forthcoming projects of 16.51 million square feet, which shall be launched over next 6 to 8 quarters.

items.statement: Net land payments of INR872 crores in 9M FY26, up 38% YoY, strengthening growth pipeline
items.quote: During the 9 months, net land payments were INR872 crores, up nearly by 38%, reflecting a strengthening of our growth pipeline.

items.statement: Q3 land payments of INR240 crores mainly for settlement of old dues on existing land for FY27 launches
items.quote: majority is towards settlement of old dues for some of the existing lands, which we are planning to launch in the next financial year and very little component towards any new projects.

items.statement: Estimated INR1,000 crores investment needed for forthcoming and subsequent project launches
items.quote: all put together, we have an estimate of about INR1,000 crores that need to be spent for, or let's say, invested towards this, towards both this, forthcoming, very minimal, but a part of it is forthcoming and part of it is subsequent.

items.statement: Q3 operational cash inflow INR1,985 crores (34% YoY); 9M inflow INR5,809 crores (32% YoY)
items.quote: Q3 was another strong quarter with total operational cash inflow of INR1,985 crores, representing a 34% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Q3 net operational cash flow INR362 crores (78% YoY); 9M net operational cash flow INR1,270 crores, exceeding full FY25
items.quote: For the first 9 months, net operational cash flow stood at INR1,270 crores, already surpassing the full year FY '25.

items.statement: Gross debt INR997 crores, cash balance INR1,790 crores, net negative debt position
items.quote: We closed the quarter with a gross debt of INR997 crores and cash balance of INR1,790 crores, underscoring high solvency and strong financial footing.

items.statement: Raised INR2,000 crores via rights issue last financial year to fund growth
items.quote: As you are aware, we have actually raised INR2,000 crores as part of rights issue last financial year. So hence, we have already addressed that question of funding growth.

items.statement: Bangalore demand steady; Gurgaon end-user demand robust in INR4-5 cr ticket size despite reduced short-term investor demand
items.quote: Bangalore seems to be steady in nature. And Gur gaon, while there are pockets of concern, but like I was always mentioning in the previous calls, the sweet spot of about — between INR4 crores to INR5 crores is still — l a good market for Gurgaon

items.statement: NCR/Noida demand structurally robust due to job creation; long-term investor and end-user base remains strong
items.quote: NCR as an overall market is -- for us, it is a very long-term play. And immediate and in the next few quarters or a year, a couple of years, the demand side seems to be still very robust the — for the whole of NCR.

items.statement: Pricing stabilized in Gurgaon and Noida; no rationalization planned, will not sacrifice margins for volume
items.quote: I think the pricing is largely stabilized in both these locations. We have not come across or not seen any rationalization of pricing. So hence, I, and our, the projects are of long-term in nature. We are not chasing only the short-term sales or growth, are, from a, we are here changing both the growth and also I would not like to sacrifice our margins as well.

items.statement: GST reforms have limited impact on margins as Sobha consumes RMC (B2B) not cement directly
items.quote: Basically, it should be reduced prices. But since we are in B2B segment, so we are not getting any benefit of GST reduction. So hence, there is no impact on margins.

items.statement: New labor codes not yet notified by states; Sobha already fully compliant on gratuity and leave encashment, no impact expected
items.quote: We have to see impact. But gratuity and leave encashment perspective, we are already fully compliant. So we don't have any impact from that perspective.

items.statement: Corporate overheads estimated at INR320-330 crores for FY26
items.quote: That's roughly about, for this financial year, it would be about INR320 crores to INR330 crores.

items.statement: Unrecognized real estate revenue of INR18,600 crores from sold units as of date
items.quote: We have unrecognized revenue from sold units of approximately INR18,600 crores as on date.

items.statement: Expects INR9,000 crores marginal cash flow from ongoing projects and INR7,300 crores from forthcoming projects over next 4-5 years
items.quote: From all ongoing projects, we expect to generate marginal cash flow of close to INR9,000 crores at project level post sales and marketing spend. We should be able to realize this over the next 4 to 5 years. Additionally, we expect to generate INR7,300 crores of marginal cash flow from forthcoming projects.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels net EBITDA expected at Rs 850 crore in FY27 and Rs 1,000+ crore by FY28
items.quote: We are very sure we will do Rs. 850 crore or more in FY27, net EBITDA, and we are very sure we will cross very, very sure we will cross Rs. 1,000-plus crore by FY28.

items.statement: Lemon Tree standalone EBITDA margin expected north of 80% by FY28
items.quote: We expect that our underwriting is that within 2 years, which is by FY28, our EBITDA margin should be North of 80%.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels net EBITDA margin expected north of 48% after renovations complete by H1 next year
items.quote: The renovations will only be over by H1 next year, after which the EBITDA margins of Fleur will be north of 48%.

items.statement: Lemon Tree targets 30,000-40,000 rooms (including pipeline) in 3-4 years, with 20,000-25,000 operational
items.quote: In the next 3 -4 years, we would certainly like to be 30,000 - 40,000 rooms, a large , in fact, the largest operator in this space with very significant fee income.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels gross EBITDA margin expected at 60% by FY28 before fees and incremental costs
items.quote: Our expectation is Fleur on a gross EBITDA before fees and everything else, would have an EBITDA margin of 60%. This is what our expectation is for FY28.

items.statement: Fleur has Rs 300-350 crore equity cash available in next 1.5 years plus Rs 960 crore Warburg commitment for growth
items.quote: Fleur itself will have a few hundred crores of cash available, maybe Rs. 300 crore - Rs. 350 crores of equity cash available in the next 1.5 years to deploy.

items.statement: Fleur plans to deploy up to Rs 3,000 crore (1:1 debt-equity) for acquisitions and development before listing
items.quote: We have potentially about Rs. 3,000 crores available to deploy in this growth before we list.

items.statement: Fleur in active discussions for 2,500+ rooms across operating and development assets
items.quote: We are in active conversations for 2,500 rooms. A lot of them are operating assets and a lot of them are going to be development assets.

items.statement: Lemon Tree signed ~7,000 rooms under third-party management contracts over last 2 years
items.quote: Securing a marquee 500 -plus room hotel Aurika Hotel at Nehru Place in New Delhi and signing about 7,000 rooms under third -party management contracts.

items.statement: Incremental one-off costs (renovations, labour code, ex-gratia, property tax, digital) to impact EBITDA margins by 5% of revenue in FY26 and FY27, reverting to normal by FY28
items.quote: If we put all this together, the incremental impact on our EBITDA margins will be 5% of revenue for FY26 and FY27. And then it will revert to norm by FY28.

items.statement: Fleur FY26/FY27 EBITDA margins 5% below normal due to one-offs; normal run-rate costs 3-4% of revenue
items.quote: Our all these costs, excluding the one -offs, put together should be 3% -4% of revenue. But this year, it will be 9% of revenue.

items.statement: GST input credit loss on rooms below Rs 7,500: 40% of revenue currently below threshold, impact ~Rs 35-40 crore last year, reducing to 1.5-2% of revenue
items.quote: If 40% of our revenue, these rooms, which are selling at below Rs. 7,500 then the GST input credit we get is only 60% of the total, which means we lose 40%.

items.statement: Labour code one-off hit of Rs 16-20 crore this quarter, ongoing impact just a couple of crores annually
items.quote: Labour code will hit us one -off quite significantly. I think it will be close to Rs. 16 crores to Rs. 20 crore this quarter.

items.statement: GST rule change: no input credit for rooms below Rs 7,500; Labour Code implementation impacting costs
items.quote: There were two regulatory interventions , one in GST and second in Labour Code. GST meant that any hotel where we do not charge Rs. 7,500, we no longer were entitled to input credit.

items.statement: Fleur to hold all group debt (~Rs 1,300 crore post-demerger) with target debt-EBITDA management; may borrow additional Rs 1,300 crore against Rs 900 crore EBITDA
items.quote: have 100% of our debt and Lemon Tree will have zero debt. Okay. So, what will Fleur's debt be on an ongoing basis by end of next year, by the time of this demerger would be around Rs. 1,300

items.statement: Warburg Pincus committing Rs 960 crore primary equity into Fleur pre-listing at fair valuation (not QIP)
items.quote: In addition, the primary capital commitment of about Rs. 960 crores by Warburg significantly strengthens Fleur's balance sheet and provides flexibility to pursue growth at scale.

items.statement: Lemon Tree Board to define dividend/shareholder reward policy in next few months as it becomes ~100% asset-light
items.quote: And that would require, in fact, the Board to define a dividend policy or a shareholder reward policy, which I have no doubt we will be coming out with in the next few months.

items.statement: Transitioned to independent professionally led management teams with separate MDs for Lemon Tree and Fleur
items.quote: We have also strengthened our organizational foundation by transitioning to independent professionally led management teams for both Lemon Tree Hotels and Fleur Hotels, including separate Managing Directors for the 2 entities.

items.statement: Lemon Tree fee income growing ~20% annually; variable fee component 30% of total fees tied to hotel EBITDA thresholds
items.quote: I think if I look at our fee income growth, every year, it is about 20%.

items.statement: Lemon Tree management fee structure: ~65-70% fixed, 30% variable based on hotel EBITDA performance thresholds
items.quote: Typically for every Rs. 100 in fees that we charge, about 65 , two-third maybe 70% is fixed and 30% is variable.

items.statement: Fleur portfolio skewed to Lemon Tree and Aurika brands; Keys/Red Fox to drive asset-light economy/mid segments
items.quote: It will be more Lemon Tree and Aurika. The asset -light side of our business, especially in the economy and lower mid segments will be driven by Keys or Red Fox.

items.statement: Lemon Tree aims to control supply in micro-markets (e.g., 3,000 of 4,000 rooms in Gurgaon) to prevent disintermediation by OTAs/tech platforms
