items.quote: Maintenance capex is routine, which will be around $90 million to $100 million for Q4, and the whole year should be $400 million.

items.statement: 250 ktpa integrated zinc smelter at Debari and tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha to be completed by Q2 FY29 and Q4 FY28 respectively
items.quote: With respect to 2 x growth projects of 250,000 tons per annum integrated zinc smelter at Debari and tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha, we have locked in key EPC partners and groundwork has started. Both the projects are set to be completed by second quarter of FY '29 and fourth quarter of FY '28, respectively.

items.statement: Debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba smelters added 21,000 tons refined metal capacity; 160 ktpa roaster commissioned at Debari
items.quote: With the successful completion of debottlenecking at Chanderiya smelter and the earlier commissioned debottlenecking at Dariba smelter, we added 21,000 tons to the overall refined metal capacity. Earlier this year, we completed the commissioning of 160,000 tons per annum roaster at Debari, which has improved the overall plant availability.

items.statement: Record quarterly EBITDA of INR 6,087 crores at 55% margin; 9-month EBITDA INR 14,415 crores
items.quote: We achieved record quarterly EBITDA of INR6,087 crores, up 36% quarter-on-quarter and 34% Y-o-Y, while maintaining our industry-leading EBITDA margin of 55%.

items.statement: Zinc cost of production excluding royalty at 5-year low of $940/t in Q3 and $980/t for 9 months
items.quote: During the quarter, we achieved 5-year lowest zinc cost of production, excluding royalty, of $940 per ton, better by 10% year-on-year and 5% sequentially.

items.statement: India manufacturing PMI above 56; RBI projects FY26 GDP growth at 7.4%
items.quote: India continues to stand out as one of the brightest spots globally with manufacturing PMI firmly above 56 throughout the quarter. The nation's GDP growth for FY 2026 is projected at around 7.4% by the Reserve Bank of India.

items.statement: Zinc prices surged to ~$3,350/t; silver prices rallied ~75% YoY to all-time high over $93/oz
items.quote: Zinc prices surged to around $3,350 per ton, the highest level since early 2023, driven by tight physical supply. Silver prices, in particular, witnessed strong rally of around 75% year-on-year, even reaching an all-time high of over $93 per troy ounce in January.

items.statement: Record Q3 mined metal production of 276 kt; 9-month production of 799 kt; refined metal production of 270 kt in Q3 and 766 kt for 9 months
items.quote: We delivered mined metal production of 276,000 tons, our best ever third quarter since the underground transition, taking 9-month production to a record 799,000 tons. We achieved highest ever third quarter refined metal production of 270,000 tons with second highest 9-month production of 766,000 tons.

items.statement: Silver production 158 tons in Q3 (up 10% QoQ); 451 tons in 9 months; precious metals contribute 44% of profits
items.quote: Our saleable silver production stood at 158 tons, up 10% sequentially. The contribution of the precious metal portfolio has increased to 44% of the profits, making it uniquely placed to ride the silver wave and unlock full potential.

items.statement: Free cash flow before growth capex and RE investment: INR 3,413 crores in Q3; INR 7,225 crores for 9 months
items.quote: Our free cash flow before growth capex and renewable energy investment for the quarter stood at INR3,413 crores, taking the 9-month free cash flow generation before capex and RE investment to INR7,225 crores.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 329 crores at December 2025 vs net debt of INR 2,547 crores at September 2025; Q4 debt maturity of INR 1,300 crores
items.quote: We achieved net cash position of INR329 crores at the end of December '25 in comparison to net debt position at the September end of INR2,547 crores.

items.statement: Domestic coal usage at 58% in Q3; imported coal prices softened; RE power share at 20% in Q3, targeting 25% by FY26 exit, 35-40% in FY27, 70% thereafter
items.quote: This quarter, we were 20% for the RE power, and we should be exiting at 25% as the wind power capacity getting installed. For the next year, we should be between 35% to 40%. And after the next year, 70%.

items.statement: Mined metal grade 7.3% in Q3 vs 7.4% YoY; 9-month average grade 7.4%
items.quote: So, this quarter, the grade was 7.3%, and last quarter similar period was 7.4%. So grade overall for the 9 months, it has been 7.4%.

items.statement: Delivered 35% shareholder returns over 9 months, outperforming Nifty 100 and Nifty Metal indices
items.quote: Consistent with our track record, the company continues to deliver strong shareholder returns of 35% over 9 months, outperforming the Nifty 100 and Nifty Metal indices.

items.statement: Contributed over INR 13,000 crores to national exchequer in 9 months, including INR 4,000 crores to Rajasthan
items.quote: It is prudent to note that in the last 9 months, we contributed over INR13,000 crores to the national exchequer, of which INR4,000 crores was contributed to the state of Rajasthan.

items.statement: Ranked #1 globally in S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment 2025 for third consecutive year with score of 90/100
items.quote: Advancing our sustainability journey, we flagged off 10 EV bulker trucks at our Debari smelter in collaboration with Enviiiro Wheels Mobility Private Limited, which plans to scale the fleet to 40 vehicles. Further reinforcing our sustainability leadership, the company achieved a global milestone by securing number one ranking in the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment 2025 for the third

items.statement: Overall consumption trends remain modest with some pickup during festive season; heating products saw healthy uptick due to good winter; cooling products faced challenging environment but channel inventory is normalizing
items.quote: While overall consumption trends remain modest, we did see some pickup during this festive season. Also, there was a healthy uptick in demand for heating products supported by a good winter. As regards to the cooling products, we saw a challenging environment in the last couple of quarters. However, now the channel inventory is normalizing.

items.statement: Revenue grew 14% and EBITDA up 21% YoY in Q3; exceptional item impact of INR 45 crores for additional provisioning due to new labour codes
items.quote: Overall, revenue growth in Q3 backed with disciplined spends translated into operating leverage as the revenue grew by 14% and EBITDA was up 21% Y-o-Y. During the quarter, there was an exceptional item impact of INR45 crores on account of additional provisioning pursuant to the new labour codes.

items.statement: Calibrated price hikes being taken to offset commodity inflation, BEE changes, e-waste costs; enhancing operational efficiency
items.quote: We are in the process of taking calibrated price hikes and en hancing operational efficiency.

items.statement: Industry may need 5-10% price increase in Q4 for ACs due to BEE rating, copper prices, INR depreciation; GST reduction may offset consumer price impact
items.quote: But if you take that out, I think overall, there could be a 5% to 10% increase in this quarter.

items.statement: Wires and cables volume growth over 20% in Q3; sharp raw material price increases boosted revenue growth; decent channel stock build-up in wires
items.quote: So volume growth has been a good healthy double digit, over 20%. So -- but there has been a sharp increase in raw material prices, as you mentioned, which actually has given a sharp increase in revenue growth for both cables and wires.

items.statement: Channel inventory normalization may impact volumes if sudden price movements occur; no strategy change to move more B2B heavy; price increases/decreases more predictable in cables and wires over mid-term
items.quote: There were continuous price increases in the third quarter and going into the fourth quarter as well. So if there will be sudden price movements, yes, there will be some amount of channel normalization, which can impact the volumes for some time.

items.statement: Capex of INR 1,200 crores in 9M FY26; continued capex in cables and wires in FY27; Lloyd capex largely done in FY26; new R&D center capex in FY27; total FY27 capex around INR 1,000 crores
items.quote: Yes. I think as far as cables and wires are concerned, there will be continued capex in the coming year. So Lloyd pretty much is done in this present year. But there will be a higher capex spend for the new R&D center, which will come up. So overall, it should be in the range of another INR1,000 crores in the coming year.

items.statement: Wire capacity utilization at 65-70%; cable capacity running at 90-100% with capacity building ongoing
items.quote: As far as wires is concerned, we are fairly comfortable with our capacity. It's operating usually around 65% - 70%. As far as cables are concerned, we are -- as I told you in some time back, we are building capacity. So usually, cable capacity is running at almost 90% to 100%.

items.statement: ECD growth led by winter products (OFR, water heaters) - volume driven; fans still facing summer challenges; solar growing faster in 'other' segment with modules outpacing inverters
items.quote: ECD, largely the growth has been led by also the winter products. Winter has been pretty decent. So there is a good growth in our OFR segment. We continue to be the number 1 player in the country now in this segment. There has been a decent growth there as well as water heaters.

items.statement: A&P spends lower YoY across board, not category-specific; margin outlook: tactical balancing between growth and margins continues; focus on margin improvement via calibrated price hikes, cost rationalization, productivity improvement
items.quote: As far as the margins are concerned, Latika, these fluctuations in the commodity prices definitely will have some degree of effect. And I think this, this tactical balancing between growth and margins will continue to play out.

items.statement: Solar margins currently early double digit to high single digit depending on project; positive outlook for revenue growth and margin expansion in solar; ECD margins impacted by raw material prices, aspiration for continuous improvement
items.value: early double digit to high single digit
items.quote: Yes, I will say early double digit to high single digit depending upon the project. I think this quarter, I don't think we should read too much into this. As I just commented, we see good growth and a good opportunity even for profit.

items.statement: Maintained market shares in most categories; gained share in lighting and small domestic appliances/water heaters; cables/wires: domestic wires share intact, cable growth lower due to capacity build-up vs competitors focused on industrial c
items.quote: Yes. I think pretty much we would say that we would have maintained market shares in most of the categories. I would argue that we may have gained certain market shares in lighting because we do see that our growth or lack of it has been better than the competition.

items.statement: Cables present good export opportunity as hedge against domestic slowdown; export growth was good last year but hit by US tariffs this year; continuing efforts for more export markets including underground cables; RAC exports primarily dome
items.quote: I think cables presents a very good opportunity for exports as well. And as you rightly said, it can provide us a good hedge against some sort of demand neutralization within the country in the coming years. So we are on that process. We are tracking well. Our cable growth was very good last year in terms of exports.

items.statement: Invested INR 600 crores in Goldi Solar for strategic module supply; Goldi backward integrating into cells; no plans to manufacture modules in-house; Havells plays broader renewable ecosystem (inverters, modules, switchgear, cables, wires, s
items.quote: So Goldi, we have already disclosed, we invested around INR600 crores. And I think on the cell side, we will come back. I think this is still being implemented by them.

items.statement: Senior leadership hired for solar and other businesses; created separate business unit for solar/renewables; built talent pipeline over last 5 years investing before growth
items.quote: We have always maintained that over the last 5 years or so, Havells has built a good talent pipeline and has invested before growth. So there will be, I would say, operating leverage coming out in the coming years.

items.statement: Industry headwinds: commodity inflation, BEE changes, e-waste regulations; channel inventory normalization risk if sudden price movements; competitive pressure from regional brands gaining ground in hyperinflationary environment
items.quote: We remain optimistic about a gradual recovery in demand. However, we are cognizant of the industry headwinds such as cost increases on account of commodity inflation, BEE changes, e-waste, etc.

items.statement: BEE norm transition: residual inventory of old norms in ACs and fans to be sold in coming months; trade mature about transition; GST reduction may offset consumer price impact of 5-10% hike requirement
items.quote: Yes, I think we should be able to sell in the next couple of months. In fact, it's not only in air conditioners, but also in fans . So there is some amount of residual inventory of the old BEE norms, which get passed on during the season in the coming time.

items.statement: Cables and wires volume growth over 20% in Q3; ECD growth volume-driven led by winter products; solar module growth outpacing inverter growth
items.quote: So volume growth has been a good healthy double digit, over 20%.

items.statement: NIM was 4.30% in Q3-2026, flat sequentially from Q2-2026
items.quote: Net interest margin was 4.30% in Q3-2026 compared to 4.30% in Q2-2026

items.statement: Domestic loan portfolio grew 11.5% YoY to Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: The domestic loan portfolio grew by 11.5% year-on-year at December 31, 2025

items.statement: Retail loan portfolio grew 7.2% YoY, mortgage 11.1%, business banking 22.8%, domestic corporate 5.6%
items.quote: The retail loan portfolio grew by 7.2% year -on-year. Including non -fund outstanding, the retail loan portfolio was 42.2% of the total portfolio. The mortgage portfolio grew by 11.1% year -on-year. The business banking portfolio grew by 22.8% year -on-year. G rowth in the domestic corporate portfolio was 5.6% year-on-year at December 31, 2025

items.statement: Net NPA ratio improved to 0.37% at Dec 31, 2025 from 0.39% at Sep 30, 2025
items.quote: Net NPA ratio was 0.37% at December 31, 2025 compared to 0.39% at September 30, 2025

items.statement: Gross NPA additions were ₹5,356 crore in Q3-2026, down from ₹6,085 crore in Q3-2025
items.quote: The gross additions in the current quarter were ₹5,356 crore as against ₹6,085 crore

items.statement: Provisioning coverage ratio on non-performing loans was 75.4% at Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: Provisioning coverage ratio on non-performing loans was 75.4% at December 31, 2025

items.statement: Contingency provisions of ₹13,100 crore held at Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: The Bank continues to hold contingency provisions of ₹13,100 crore at December 31, 2025

items.statement: RBI directed additional standard asset provision of ₹1,283 crore for agri PSL portfolio of ~₹20,000-25,000 crore due to classification non-compliance
items.quote: RBI has directed the Bank to make a standard asset provision of ₹1,283 crore in respect of a portfolio of agricultural priority sector credit facilities wherein the terms of the facilities were found to be not fully compliant with the regulatory requirements for classification as agricultural priority sector lending

items.statement: Additional standard asset provisions will continue until loans are repaid or renewed in conformity with PSL guidelines
items.quote: This additional standard asset provision will continue until the loans are repaid or renewed in conformity with the PSL classification guidelines

items.statement: Provisions can be written back if loans are brought into conformity with PSL classification
items.quote: As I already mentioned, we would be working towards repayment or renewal of these loans to make them in conformity with PSL classifications, and our endeavour, as I said, is to minimise the impact of this provision

items.statement: CET-1 ratio 16.46% and total capital adequacy 17.34% including 9M-2026 profits at Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: Including profits for 9M -2026, CET -1 ratio was 16.46% and total capital adequacy ratio was 17.34%

items.statement: Capital adequacy of 17.3% including Q3 profits is very comfortable and adequate for growth
items.quote: Actually, including profits for the quarter, we are at a total capital adequacy of about 17.3%, which is including profits for April to December. We are at a total capital adequacy of 17.3%, which is very comfortable.

items.statement: NIMs expected to remain range-bound reflecting repricing of external benchmarks and competition, offset by retail term repricing
items.quote: Looking ahead, we do expect NIMs to remain more or less range bound, reflecting the repricing of the external benchmarks on loans and investments, as you rightly pointed out. And of course, competition intensity. This would get offset by retail term repricing

items.statement: No specific loan growth targets given; focus on maximizing PBT in risk-calibrated fashion
items.quote: We do not give any specific targets of what we are going to be growing. Our focus is to maximize PBT in a risk calibrated fashion, and that is what we will continue to do.

items.statement: Expect better profit growth once interest rate cycle impact settles; repo rate cut 125 bps over last year
items.quote: Once this settles in, we should be back to a better growth of profits, but as I said, we are focused on ensuring few things —one, we have a customer -centric approach ; two, ensuring that we are fair to our customers and fair to the Bank—and within that framework, we will grow our profits.

items.statement: Opened 402 branches during 9M-2026; network of 7,385 branches and 11,983 ATMs/CRMs at Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: The Bank opened 402 branches during 9M -2026 and had a network of 7,385 branches and 11,983 ATMs and cash recycling machines at December 31, 2025

items.statement: Acquired pension fund business from step-down subsidiary to synergize with banking customers
items.quote: It was a step-down subsidiary. We explained this, I think, about two quarters back when we made the decision. We do believe that the synergy with the Bank will be better and the business will be able to expand in a much better fashion.

items.statement: CEO Sandeep Bakhshi reappointed for two-year term from Oct 2026 to Oct 2028 (nearly three years from now)
items.quote: the Board along with the MD, and it was felt appropriate that a two-year term is what it is at. But just wanted to clarify, it is nearly three years from today. It is starting from October of '26 and goes on till October '28

items.statement: Assessed US tariff impact on MSME portfolio; comfortable with book quality given domestic focus and strong customer balance sheets
items.quote: We continue to assess our portfolio. As you are aware, India is largely a domestically focused economy, and we made an assessment of the impact of US tariffs. Of course, when we are assessing our customers, we prioriti se resilience through strong balance sheet from a customer perspective, and we continue to leverage these … we continue to believe that the quality of book that we have built is ver

items.statement: ECL implementation assessment pending; will comply when regulations finalized
items.quote: ECL is still an internal assessment. Whenever the regulations come into place, we will be compliant with that. So, that is something the future.

items.statement: ROA over 2%; 2.11% in Q3-2026 and 2.29% in 9M-2026 adjusting for one-off provision
items.quote: We have got a healthy ROA. It is over 2%. Even after adjusting for this, we are going to report 2.11% ROA, in Q3-2026. Taking this one-off, it will move to about 2.29% in 9M-2026.

items.statement: Credit-deposit gap widened due to CRR reduction; comfortably funded with healthy retail deposit growth
items.quote: In the current quarter, as you are aware, there was a reduction in the CRR requirement. So, you would have seen the credit-deposit ratio go up across the system, and for most banks, for whose numbers are available , barring maybe one or two. So, that is a very natural thing to happen. From our perspective, I think we are comfortably funded with healthy retail deposit growth.

items.statement: Conducted over 250 senior citizen awareness programmes in Q3; digital services for Form 15H, Life Certificates, Interest Certificates
items.quote: In Q3 alone, we conducted over 250 awareness programmes in housing societies nationwide, helping them recognise prevalent frauds and safeguard their accounts. We also provide them the convenience of digital banking services, including online submission of Form 15H, Life Cer tificates, and digital Interest Certificates.

items.statement: Loan Against Securities customers can now increase overdraft limits and pledge shares fully online
items.quote: Existing Loan Against Securities customers can now increase overdraft limits entirely online and pledge shares seamlessly through the Bank's digital channels.

items.statement: Operating expenses increased 13.2% YoY to ₹11,944 crore in Q3-2026, including ₹145 crore for new Labour Codes provisions
items.quote: Operating expenses increased by 13.2% year -on-year to ₹11,944 crore in Q3 -2026. This includes the impact of additional operating expenses of ₹145 crore provisions on an estimated basis pursuant to the new Labour Codes

items.statement: NIM expected to remain range-bound going forward
items.quote: So, overall, we would stay with our view that the NIM should be range-bound from here on.

items.statement: NIM stable at 4.30% QoQ; cost of deposits fell to 4.55%
items.quote: The net interest margin was 4.30% in this quarter compared to 4.30% in the previous quarter and 4.25% in Q3 of last year. The cost of deposits was 4.55% in this quarter compared to 4.64% in the previous quarter and 4.91% in Q3 of last year.

items.statement: Domestic loan portfolio grew 11.5% YoY and 4.0% QoQ to Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: The domestic loan portfolio grew by 11.5% year -on-year and 4.0% sequentially at December 31, 2025 compared to 10.6% and 3.3% at September 30, 2025.

items.statement: Business banking portfolio grew 22.8% YoY and 4.7% QoQ
items.quote: The business banking portfolio grew by 22.8% year -on-year and 4.7% sequentially.

items.statement: Corporate portfolio grew 5.6% YoY and 6.5% QoQ
items.quote: The domestic corporate portfolio grew by 5.6% year-on-year and 6.5% sequentially.

items.statement: Contingency provisions held at Rs 131 bn (0.9% of advances)
items.quote: In addition, the Bank continues to hold contingency provisions of 131.00 billion Rupees or about 0.9% of total advances at December 31, 2025.

items.statement: Branch count increased by 402 in 9M FY26 to 7,385 branches
items.quote: Our branch count has increased by 402 in 9M of the current year. We had 7,385 branches as of December 31, 2025.

items.statement: Average deposits grew 8.7% YoY and 1.8% QoQ; CASA grew 8.9% YoY and 1.5% QoQ
items.quote: Average deposits grew by 8.7% year-on-year and 1.8% sequentially and average current and savings account deposits grew by 8.9% year -on-year and 1.5% sequentially in this quarter.

items.statement: CET-1 ratio 16.46%, total CAR 17.34% at Dec 31, 2025 including 9M profits
items.quote: The capital position of the Bank continued to be strong with a CET -1 ratio of 16.46% and total capital adequacy ratio of 17.34% at December 31, 2025, including profits for 9M-2026.

items.statement: Operating expenses grew 13.2% YoY and 1.2% QoQ; employee expenses up 12.5% YoY including Rs 1.45 bn Labour Code provision
items.quote: The Bank's operating expenses increased by 13.2% year-on-year and 1.2% sequentially in this quarter. Employee expenses increased by 12.5% year -on-year and 1.8% sequentially in this quarter, including the impact of 1.45 billion Rupees of provisions on an estimated basis pursuant to the new Labour Codes.

items.statement: Sequential cost growth moderated; expect cost growth to slow from recent pace
items.quote: We will see whatever is necessary to maximize kind of the overall PPOP. I don't expect, cost to go up at the pace at which they had gone up maybe till a couple of quarters ago. If you would see, sequentially this quarter, other than the impact of the Labour Code, costs would have come down marginally on an absolute basis.

items.statement: Loan growth momentum picked up in Q3 and expected to sustain in Q4
items.quote: So, clearly we have seen a pickup in the sequential growth rate in the fourth quarter vis -à-vis the third quarter, despite the rundown in cards, which I will come to separately, certainly there has been a pickup in moment um. And we see that momentum sustaining into the fourth quarter as well

items.statement: Retail, rural and business banking fees constitute 78% of total fees
items.quote: Fees from retail, rural and business banking customers constituted about 78% of the total fees in this quarter.

items.statement: Core operating profit grew 6.0% YoY and 2.5% QoQ to Rs 175.13 bn
items.quote: The core operating profit increased by 6.0% year -on-year and 2.5% quarter -on-quarter to 175.13 billion Rupees in this quarter.

items.statement: ICICI Life VNB margin improved to 24.4% in 9M FY26 from 22.8%
items.quote: The value of new business margin was 24.4% in nine months ended December 31, 2025 compared to 22.8% in FY2025 and in nine months of last year.

items.statement: ICICI General combined ratio 104.5% in Q3 FY26 vs 102.7% YoY
items.quote: The combined ratio stood at 104.5% in this quarter compared to 102.7% in Q3 of last year.

items.statement: MD & CEO Sandeep Bakhshi reappointed for two-year term ending Oct 2028
items.quote: So, I think the Board in consultation with the CEO have decided on a two -year appointment. As you know the current term itself ends in October 2026. So, from now till the end of the renewed term is almost three years.

items.statement: KCC portfolio shows seasonal NPA additions in Q1 and Q3; Rs 7.36 bn gross additions this quarter
items.quote: There were gross NPA additions of about 7.36 billion Rupees from the kisan credit card portfolio in the current quarter compared to 7.14 billion Rupees in Q3 of last year. We typically see higher NPA additions from the kisan credit card portfolio in the first and third quarter of a fiscal year.

items.statement: 56% of domestic loans linked to repo/external benchmarks, 13% to MCLR, 31% fixed rate
items.quote: Of the total domestic loans, interest rates on about 56% of the loans are linked to the repo rate and other external benchmarks, 13% to MCLR and other older benchmarks and the remaining 31% of loans have fixed interest rates.

items.statement: Targets full-year FY27 ROA of 1% and mid-term ROA of 1.5% with loan growth in line or marginally higher than industry
items.quote: Looking ahead, YES BANK remains committed to its strategic road map of profitable growth, targeting full year 1% ROA for FY '27 and 1.5% in mid-term, with growth outlook which will be in line or marginally higher than the industry.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 sequential loan growth above 3% taking FY26 loan growth to around 8%
items.quote: We are very confident that we would be sequentially be able to grow more than 3% in the current quarter, which will take our Credit growth to around 8% okay.

items.statement: Targets FY27 loan growth in line with market excluding Prime Home Loan and Car Loan
items.quote: I would be saying the high-risk corporate loans have already been rep aid, I think we would be definitely targeting a loan growth, which would be more or less in line with the market, barring, I think if we need to exclude the growth, especially on the products like Prime Home Loan and the Car

items.statement: Guides FY26 Security Receipt recovery of INR 1,200 crores, already achieved INR 1,113 crores in 9 months
items.quote: We have given a guidance for this year in terms of having a recovery of INR 1,200 crores for the entire year. We have already achieved INR 1,113 crores, okay.

items.statement: Expects Security Receipt recoveries of around INR 800 crores next year
items.quote: But I think next year onwards also we would be seeing maybe recoveries in the range of INR 800 crores.

items.statement: Targets RIDF reduction to below 5% of Total Assets by FY27
items.quote: Bank remains well on track to further reduce it to below 5% of Total Assets by FY '27 in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Q3 NIM expanded 12 bps QoQ and 24 bps YoY to 2.6% driven by RIDF rundown, CASA improvement and deposit pricing actions
items.quote: The NIM for quarter 3 have come in at 2.6%, which is a 12 basis point expansion on quarter-on-quarter basis and 24 basis points on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Cost of Deposits reduced to 5.6% from 6.1% YoY; Cost of Funds reduced 60 bps to 5.9% from 6.5% YoY
items.quote: Bank has also maintained a strong focus on sustained reduction in its Cost of Deposits which has reduced to 5.6% from 6.1% last year, driven by higher deposit-rate cuts relative to the rate cuts undertaken by RBI and competitors.

items.statement: Adjusted Cost-to-Income ratio improved to 66.1% in Q3 from 67.1% in Q2 and 71.1% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: As a result, the Cost-to-Income ratio for the Bank adjusted for gratuity impact for Q3 was 66.1% against 67.1% in Quarter 2 and 71.1% in Quarter 3 last year.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 1.5% from 1.6% QoQ; Net NPA stable at 0.3%; PCR improved to 83.3% from 81% QoQ
items.quote: Our growth calibration, and proactive risk management efforts of last 4-6 quarters, which included tightening of sourcing, underwriting, scorecards and improving our collections infrastructure, including early intervention have yielded a marked improvement in our Asset Quality outcome with headline Gross NPAs improving to 1.5% from 1.6%.

items.statement: Fresh slippages declined to INR 1,050 crores in Q3 from INR 1,248 crores in Q2 and INR 1,458 crores in Q1; slippage ratio improved to 1.6% from 2.0% QoQ
items.quote: Similarly, the Quarter 3 was the second consecutive quarter of improvement in overall Fresh Slippages, which were contained at INR 1,050 crores against INR 1,248 crores in Quarter 2 and INR 1,458 crores in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Retail slippages improved across secured and unsecured; PL slippages INR 180 crores vs INR 250 crores YoY; Credit Card slippages INR 140 crores vs INR 190-200 crores YoY
items.quote: So PL, the Gross Slippage number is about INR 180 crores and credit cards would be about INR 140 crores.

items.statement: Card entry rates (check bounce) improved from 20% to around 12%; Retail Assets entry rates down to 8.7% from 10.7%
items.quote: Entry rates in cards from 20% is down to around 12% which gives us significant confidence on the way things are panning out.

items.statement: Guides full-year Net Credit Cost (Non-tax Provisions to Assets) below 50 bps
items.quote: We've always said that we had guided last year that our Net Credit Cost, Non-tax Provisions to Assets should be below 50 basis points for the full year. I think we're happy to state that I think that's something we should be able to continue regardless of the volatility that will happen during different quarters.

items.statement: Total Advances INR 2.57 lakh crores, up 2.9% QoQ and 5.2% YoY; Retail 47%, Commercial 26%, CIB 27%

items.quote: As regarding the Non Interest Income, the Core Fees are up by 9.8% Y-o-Y, driven by strong traction in fee income streams, which includes the Processing Fee, the Third-Party Distribution and General Banking.

items.statement: Received Ministry of Finance approval to increase foreign investment limit from 49% to 74%
items.quote: During the quarter, the Bank received approval from the Ministry of Finance, Government of India for an increase in the foreign investment limit in the Bank from 49% to a maximum permissible limit of 74%.

items.statement: Borrowings increased Rs 2,000 cr QoQ, mostly refinance; CD ratio excl. refinance at 80%
items.quote: this borrowing book has also increased by Rs. 2,000 crores quarter-on-quarter. That is mostly refinance

items.statement: Wealth franchise serves 2.5 lakh customers with Rs 1,900 cr AUM; AD1 cross-border trade forex revenue up ~50% YoY
items.quote: Our wealth franchise now serving 2.5 lakh customers and managing Rs. 1,900 crores of AUM. Our AD1 business continues to scale well, with steady growth in volumes and transactions and cross-border trade in FOREX revenues growing nearly 50% year-on-year.

items.statement: 90,000 new CASA accounts from retail asset base in Q3 with Rs 160 cr balances; Rs 2,500 cr liability-to-asset cross-sell portfolio
items.quote: We are seeing encouraging progress, including 90,000 new CASA accounts opened from our retail asset base in Q3, with balances of Rs. 160 crores and a Rs. 2,500 crores liability-to-asset cross-sell portfolio by end of the quarter.

items.statement: MFI recovery broad-based across states/districts per MFIN data; minimal overlap with gold loan book; credit culture improving due to MFIN guardrails
items.quote: the MFI recovery is a very broad based recovery. And it is not in the one lender's book. If you look at the MFIN data, it would reveal that it is across the industry. The overlap between AU Small Finance Bank January 20, 2026 the gold loan and MFI book would be very minimal. And it is an independent asset class, right? So, the

items.statement: Digital banking (credit cards) still loss-making; will take ~1 more year to stabilize; PL/BL re-engineered, expect better numbers in Q4
items.quote: Obviously, digital banking still continues to be loss-making or haven't really broken even and that's what Sanjayji indicated that we will take about one more year to stabilize that business.

items.statement: Expect Q4 to build on Q3 momentum with growth in FY27 supported by protection and savings demand
items.quote: We expect Q4 to build on the momentum seen in the last quarter, with growth in FY27 supported by continued strength in protection and sustained demand across savings segments.

items.statement: Aspiration to double VNB every 4-4.5 years remains despite recent regulatory changes
items.quote: Our aspiration to double VNB every 4-4.5 years remains the way it is.

items.statement: Target to neutralize GST impact completely by Q1 FY27 and return to FY25 margin trajectory
items.quote: We said that FY27, we would like to start on a clean slate, having digested the GST impact completely.

items.statement: VNB margin expanded 110 bps to 24.4% for 9M FY26 despite GST impact
items.quote: While a better product profile helped us expand margins by 110 basis points, there was an offset largely on account of GST impact. Our margins ended at 24.4%.

items.statement: Adjusted VNB growth excluding GST and surrender regulation impact was 13% for 9M FY26 and 11% for Q3 FY26
items.quote: On an adjusted basis, VNB growth, excluding the impact of GST and surrender regulation change, would have been 13% for 9M FY26 and 11% for Q3 FY26.

items.statement: GST impact contained to less than 200 bps in Q3 vs initial estimate of 300 bps; expect further reduction in Q4
items.quote: The GST impact for the quarter was contained to less than 200 basis points, lower than the initial estimate impact of 300 basis points.

items.statement: Life insurance sector grew ~10% YoY on individual WRP; HDFC Life grew 11% with volume-driven acceleration in Q3
items.quote: The industry reported year-on-year growth of around 10%, with HDFC Life growing faster at 11% on individual WRP.

items.statement: Retail protection grew 42% YoY for 9M FY26 and 70% in Q3, significantly outpacing company growth
items.quote: Retail protection delivered strong year-on-year growth of 42% for the period nine months ended FY26 and 70% in Quarter 3, significantly outpacing overall company growth.

items.statement: Product mix for 9M FY26: ULIPs 43%, par 27%, non-par savings 19%, term 7%, annuity 4%; protection share rose to ~9% in Q3
items.quote: Our product mix in 9-month FY26 reflected evolving customer preferences and market trends, with ULIPs contributing 43%, participating products at 27%, non-par savings at 19%, term at 7%, and annuity at 4%.

items.statement: Non-par savings mix improved to ~20% in Q3 from ~17% in H1; expect further pickup in Q4
items.quote: In Q3, I think the non-par mix is in the 20% range. We had close d H1 at about 17-odd percent. So that has been a meaningful shift that has started to happen, and we expect more of that to happen in the coming quarter as well

items.statement: High sum assured ULIPs now >25% of ULIP mix with margin profile converging towards par business
items.quote: Yes, the highest sum assured ULIP, like you rightly said, is about a little more than a fourth of our unit-linked business now, and the margin profile of that is a lot stronger than the base ULIP.

items.statement: Branch network crossed 700 branches; focus shifting to scaling productivity and branch-level profitability
items.quote: Our branch network has now crossed 700 branches, reflecting the culmination of a multi-year expansion effort. As this network matures, our focus has shifted towards scaling productivity, improving activation, and enhancing branch-level profitability.

items.statement: Project Inspire phase 1 live on group platforms showing STP and claims benefits; retail phase in couple of quarters
items.quote: The first phase of Inspire, as we went, we have started going live on our group platforms, and we are already seeing efficiency getting built on the Credit Protect side of the business. The next phase around retail will be at least, I think, a couple of quarters away.

items.statement: Individual APE grew 11% YoY with 17% two-year CAGR; market share expanded 20 bps to 10.9% on individual WRP
items.quote: Individual APE grew 11% year-on-year, translating into a healthy two-year CAGR of 17%. Our overall market share based on individual WRP expanded by around 20 basis points to 10.9% for the nine-month period.

items.statement: Over 70% of new customers in 9M FY26 were first-time buyers; >80% in protection segment
items.quote: We also sustained strong momentum in customer acquisition, with over 70% of customers acquired during the period being first-time buyers of HDFC Life's policies.

items.statement: Retail sum assured grew 33% for 9M and 55% in Q3 driven by higher rider attachment and ULIP sum assured multiples
items.quote: Retail sum assured grew 33% over the nine-month period and 55% in Q3. This growth was supported by higher rider attachment and increased sum assured multiples in ULIP business.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 749 crores subordinated debt in Q3; solvency ratio strong at 180%; no further capital needed for organic growth under risk-based solvency
items.quote: The solvency ratio remained strong at 180%, supported by the Rs. 749 crores of subordinated debt raised in Q3. In light of the expected implementation of the risk-based solvency regime over the coming quarters, we do not anticipate any requirement for further capital to support organic growth.

items.statement: FDI limit increase in budget encouraging; distribution framework discussions consultative aiming for balanced ecosystem
items.quote: On the regulatory front, recent policy signals, including the increase in the FDI limit announced in the budget, are encouraging. Ongoing discussions around distribution-related frameworks are consultative in nature.

items.statement: Labor Code impact of Rs. 98 crores one-time hit to EV and PAT; no ongoing impact expected
items.quote: The impact of the new Labor Codes amounts to Rs. 98 crores and has been reflected in embedded value relating to services rendered up to 31st December 2025.

items.statement: Distributor negotiations on GST completed; revised commercials implemented from January 1
items.quote: Yes, short answer, negotiations were completed. And it's moved on in terms of what we said that we would do.

items.statement: Competitive pricing pressure in non-par savings; company maintaining calibrated approach at sensible pricing
items.quote: We do see the intensity of competition in terms of aggressive pricing still there on the ground. We are fairly calibrated, like Vibha mentioned in her initial comments about the kind of business that we are happy to take on board.

items.statement: Embedded value at Rs. 61,565 crores with operating RoEV of 15.6% on rolling 12-month basis
items.quote: Embedded value stood at Rs. 61,565 crores, with an operating return on embedded value of 15.6% on a rolling 12-month basis.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 7% to Rs. 1,414 crores; underlying PAT growth excluding Labor Code impact was 15%
items.quote: Profit after tax grew by 7% to Rs. 1,414 crores. Excluding one-time Labor Code impact, underlying PAT growth for both nine months and quarter would have been 15%.

items.statement: 13-month persistency drop mainly from specific cohorts in last 2-3 months; measures taken to address
items.quote: We do see a further drop from the last quarter, and this is mainly coming from the business written in the last two to three months of last year. And we are seeing some lower collection, and that is why there is a negative operating variance.

items.statement: Operating variance negative Rs. 70 crores primarily due to persistency gap; VNB expense variance Rs. 60 crores from capacity investments
items.quote: So, to start with on operating variances, while we are not really giving specific breakouts, but like Eshwari mentioned, primarily it is on account of persistency gap that we are seeing, and we are trying to close down on.

items.statement: Over 80,000 gross agent additions in 9M FY26; agency channel targeting >25% share of company business
items.quote: Gross agent additions remained strong, with over 80,000 agents onboarded during 9M FY26.

items.statement: Variable annuity product launch expected in next couple of months following recent regulatory change
items.quote: Variable Annuity, yes, it is a very recent change, a very important regulatory change that has happened, which allows us to offer this kind of a proposition. We look forward to launching that sometime in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Board approved redesignation of Bharat Jaisinghani and Nikhil Jaisinghani from Executive Directors to Joint Managing Directors with immediate effect, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: It gives me immense pleasure to inform you that the Board of Directors at its meeting held today has approved the redesignation of Mr. Bharat Jaisinghani and Mr. Nikhil Jaisinghani from Executive Directors to Joint Managing Directors of the company with immediate effect, subject to approval of the shareholders.

items.statement: Project Spring guidance: annual capex of ₹12-16 billion through FY30.
items.quote: Capital expenditure for the quarter was ₹ 3.4 billion, taking the 9M FY26 total to ₹ 10.9 billion, in-line with our Project Spring guidance of investing ₹ 12 billion to ₹ 16 billion annually through FY30.

items.statement: FMEG segment targets 1.5x-2x industry growth and EBITDA margins of 8-10% by FY30.
items.quote: we are confident in the long -term potential of the FMEG segment and remain on track to achieve our Project Spring targets of 1.5x - 2x industry growth and EBITDA margins in the range of 8% to 10% by FY30, positioning the business for sustai ned growth and value

items.statement: EPC annual sustainable operating margin expected in high single digits over mid-to-long term.
items.quote: Looking ahead, the annual sustainable operating margin is expected to remain in the high single digits over mid- to long term.

items.statement: A&P spend guidance of 3-5% of B2C top-line annually.
items.quote: We've given a guidance that we want to spend around 3% to 5% of B2C top-line every year on A&P.

items.statement: W&C long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 11-13% under Project Spring.
items.quote: To refer to our Project Spring guidance, we've given a long-term guidance of 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Domestic consumption revival with 2-wheeler sales up 18.1% YoY and passenger vehicle sales up 7.3% YoY in Sep-Nov period.
items.quote: 2-wheeler sales also increased by 18.1% YoY over the September- November period, while passenger vehicle sales rose by 7.3% during the same time frame, reflecting improving confidence among consumers and businesses alike.

items.statement: Government capex surged 28.2% YoY to ₹6.6 trillion in first 8 months of FY26; ₹1.25 trillion loan released to states for capex.
items.quote: Government capex surged nearly 28.2% YoY in the first 8 months of FY26 reaching ₹ 6.6 trillion versus ₹ 5.1 trillion last year, also 12.4% higher than in the 8 -month period in F Y24. Additionally, the government of India released a loan of ₹ 1.25 trillion to states for capital expenditure during the same period

items.statement: Real estate sector healthy with launches and sales in top 7 cities tracking previous decade high; affordable housing momentum renewed.
items.quote: The real estate sector remains healthy with launches and sales across the top 7 cities closely tracking the previous decade high. The affordable housing segment is also witnessing renewed momentum supported by lower borrowing costs and rising household incomes.

items.statement: Domestic W&C volume growth ~40% YoY in Q3 FY26; wires and cables volumes grew at similar pace.
items.quote: For both domestic cables and wires, our volume growth is about 40%.

items.statement: Institutional sales grew faster than distribution sales, improving mix by ~200 bps; distribution:institutional mix typically ~90:10.
items.quote: Generally, our mix of distribution versus institutional sales is around 90:10. But this time around institutional sales had grown faster than distribution sales, hence, it would have improved by about a couple of hundred basis points.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 5% YoY in Q3 FY26, contributing 6% of consolidated revenue; healthy order book supports continued growth.
items.quote: Our international business maintained its steady momentum, recording a 5% YoY growth during the quarter, despite a high base and contributing 6% to the consolidated revenues. Backed by a healthy order book, we remain confident that this growth trajectory will continue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: US export weakness due to tariff overhang; strong performance in Middle East and Latin America.
items.quote: Yes, it is tariff related. This remains a global overhang and is impacting players worldwide, not just in India. We are currently awaiting a final resolution on this matter.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.7% (ex-gratuity ~13%); PAT margin 8.3%; 9M FY26 EBITDA margin 14.2%, PAT margin 9.6%.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter grew by 34% YoY with EBITDA margins at 12.7%. Excluding the one-off impact of ~₹ 219 million on account of gratuity provisioning due to the implementation of the new labour code, the EBITDA margins would have been ~13%.

items.statement: W&C segment margin pressure from commodity inflation (copper +21%, aluminium +11% QoQ in rupee terms) and staggered price pass-through; gross margin impact primary driver.
items.quote: Between September 2025 and December 2025, copper and aluminium prices, in rupe e terms, increased sequentially by approximately 21% and 11%, respectively, which represents an unusually sharp escalation over a short period of time. In order to avoid demand disruption, arising from elevated input costs, the Company took a strategic decision to pass on the increase in raw material prices in a stagger

items.statement: FMEG profitable for 4th consecutive quarter; solar margin in high single digits; segment profitability to expand toward 8-10% by FY30.
items.quote: Importantly, the FMEG segment remained profitable for the fourth consecutive quarter, even while strategically ramping up our A&P investments to strengthen brand presence and drive long-term growth. As we continue to scale, we expect profitability to expand further, reflecting the leverage in our business model.

items.statement: EPC segment margin 6.7% in Q3 FY26; sustainable operating margin expected in high single digits mid-to-long term.
items.quote: Segment profitability stood at ₹ 272 million, translating to a margin of 6.7%. Looking ahead, the annual sustainable operating margin is expected to remain in the high single digits over mid- to long term.

items.statement: Export EBITDA margins historically ~15%; domestic cables 9-12%, wires 15-16% EBITDA margins.
items.quote: margins in exports are definitely much higher as compared to domestic margins. When we export cables, obviously, it again depends a lot on the geography that we are exporting. But generally, historically, we've been making at least around 15% of EBITDA margins in our exports. If you look at th e domestic sales for us, cables versus wires, in cables, generally, we make anywhere between 9% to 12% of

items.statement: Passed on 75-80% of commodity inflation in Q3 FY26; remaining pass-through in Q4 FY26; price hikes taken month-on-month.
items.quote: The total price hikes that we would have taken within this quarter will be almost 75% to 80% of whatever commodity inflation was there.

items.statement: Copper prices up ~50% YoY and ~22% QoQ in rupee terms (Jan 2025-Jan 2026); aluminium up ~25% YoY and ~11% QoQ.
items.quote: From January 2025 till January 2026, the copper, in rupee terms, has risen almost 50% and aluminium almost 25%. And in this quarter itself, the 22% inflation has happened in copper price compared to previous quarter.

items.statement: Fan price hikes of 2-4% expected in Jan-Feb 2026 due to BEE transition from 1 Jan 2026.
items.quote: Definitely, because the new BEE norms are getting implemented from 1 st of January, there will be a bit of price hike that everybody will be taking. items.statement: EPC commenced BharatNet execution: ₹4.5 billion over 3 years for project execution + ₹3.5 billion for 10-year O&M.
items.quote: This quarter, we commenced execution of our existing orders under BharatNet scheme, which is expected to generate ₹ 4.5 billion over the next 3 years for project execution and an additi onal ₹ 3.5 billion for 10 years for project O&M

items.statement: Export order book healthy, expected to translate into revenue in coming quarters.
items.quote: Backed by a healthy order book, we remain confident that this growth trajectory will continue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Capacity utilization in early 80% range in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: So, our capacity utilization in the quarter was in the early 80% range.

items.quote: On working capital front, same as last quarter, inventory days continue to be higher as we built up inventory in anticipation of strong demand i n Q4 FY26. items.statement: Net cash position of ₹30.3 billion at end Q3 FY26.
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet, closing the quarter with a net cash position of ₹ 30.3 billion.

items.statement: Wires growth outpaced cables in Q3 FY26 due to channel pre-stocking amid elevated copper prices; wires revenue growth 70% vs cables 50% (volume similar ~40%).
items.quote: During the quarter, wires growth outperformed cables, driven by pre-stocking by channel partners amid elevated copper prices. Within the cable segment, institutional sales growth outpaced the channel sales, reflecting strong traction in project-led demand.

items.statement: Solar business grew >2x YoY, now largest FMEG category; switches/switchgears, conduit pipes also performing well.
items.quote: Within the segment, the solar business has been a standout performer, growing more than 2x compared to the same quarter last year, driven by strong uptake under the central and state rooftop solar incentive scheme.

items.statement: Targets 40-45% consolidated PAT margin for FY26
items.quote: this year, we are expecting 40% to 45% PAT margin, considering all four quarters put together.

items.statement: Expects to reach 40-50% PAT margin level in Q4 FY26
items.quote: we will be able to reach this quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 22.4%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 22.4%, underscoring the inherent operating leverage and disciplined cost structure of the business.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA margin at 23.6%
items.quote: EBITDA for nine-month FY '26 was INR34.2 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 23.6%, indicating consistency in operating performance over the year.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin band of 20-22% historically
items.quote: we will have 20% to 22% average for last two, three years.

items.quote: On the IPO front, we cu rrently have 20 active IPOs under execution, comprising 14 SME IPOs on NSE Emerge and BSE platforms and six mainboard IPO mandates, providing healthy visibility across market segments

items.statement: 26 active market-making mandates: 14 SME and 12 institutional
items.quote: In addition, our market-maki ng business remains with 26 active market-making mandates. Of these, 14 mandates are on the NSE Emerge and BSE SME platforms, while 12 mandates are from institutional clients, reflecting the growing scale and depth of our market-making operations

items.statement: No significant capex planned for broking technology upgrades
items.quote: there is no as such big capex going to be there in broking. There is nothing like that.

items.quote: the company has proposed an investment in a CATEGORY II AIF to be spons ored and managed through Bahutex Ventures LLP, in which Gretex Corporate Services Limite d will hold a 50% partnership interest as a designated partner. items.quote: We are committing only the 2.5% as a capital commitment of the overall fund that we are raising. That is INR2.5 crores overall.

items.statement: SEBI inspection concluded with INR15 lakh penalty, no ban imposed
items.quote: this is the final, I mean this is the last inspection which we had and this final conclusion order has been there now. So, nothing is pending. After this, nothing is pending.

items.quote: this is a very good step which SEBI has taken. It's not like that I'm asking for myself. It is about this entire industr y. So, it is always important to have such people only who has th e knowledge, who has that capabilities to do the right, I mean, disclosure has to happen

items.quote: we will be reducing the, I mean, SME IPOs gradually. We will be transforming our entire business model to the Main Board focused. items.statement: India IPO market raised INR1.46 lakh cr up to Nov 2025 (Main Board INR1.38 lakh cr, SME INR8,033 cr)
items.quote: The primary equity market remained active in FY '26 with a INR1.46 lakh crores raised through IPOs up to November 2025, of which Main Board IPOs accounted for INR1.38 lakh crores and SME platform issuances contributed INR8,033 cr ores, reflecting sustained demand for growth capital from corporates

items.statement: 9M FY26 total income INR144.8 cr, EBITDA INR34.2 cr, PAT INR20.7 cr
items.quote: On a nine-month basis, performance remained steady with total income of INR144.8 crores and income from operation of INR143.7 crores. items.statement: AIF focus on pre-IPO investments outside Gretex merchant banking mandates
items.quote: yes. First of all, we are not going to invest only in such pre-IPO where Gretex is involved. This fund is going to invest in some other transition where Gretex is not involved

items.statement: Separate dedicated teams for SME and mainboard IPO execution
items.quote: today we have two set of, I mean, manpower in the entire ecosystem within Gretex. One is for SME, one is for Main Board. So, technically, definitely we need to have, I mean, more strength, I mean, having the proper due diligence for Main Board company.

items.statement: Gretex Share Broking Limited listing preparation ongoing
items.quote: Our subsidiary, Gretex Share Broking Limited, continues to progress towards its proposed listing. items.statement: AIF investment of INR2.5 cr not expected to impact dividend distribution
items.quote: this INR2.5 crores is not going to stop this dividend distribution. So, hopefully, this dividend distribution can be there. This is not going to impact our AIF investment as well.

items.statement: Targeting 7-8% industry demand growth in Q4 FY26; aiming for 10% volume CAGR over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: If you remember my previous call in Q3 I mentioned that the demand for industry should be anywhere between 7% to 8% kind of a number. So, we hope to kind of hit that number or cross that number certainly going forward. That is on the demand side, basis side but I guess Q4 overall the cement industry also peaks and then we will certainly write the demand working up.

items.statement: Gujarat sales target: 1M tons FY26, 2M FY27, 3M FY28, 4M FY29.
items.quote: So, as I mentioned before, our overall scale-up is 1-2-3-4. That's the kind of number which we had in mind. 1 million in FY'26, which is we will exit the year at a million kind of annualized million sale in Gujarat. Next year, by end of the year, we should get into 2 million sale and FY'28 will be 3 million and FY'29 will be 4 million.

items.statement: EBITDA rose ~50% YoY to INR 386 cr in Q3 FY26 despite price moderation; premium products at 44% of trade volumes.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter rose approximately 50% year-on-year to INR 386 crores, even as price moderated more than the benefits passed through, following the revised GST rates coupled with macro headwinds. items.statement: Premiumization at 44% of trade volumes in Q3 FY26; 9M FY26 at 43%, up ~300 bps vs FY25; targeting +200 bps annually for next 2-3 years.
items.quote: We are pleased to report that the premium products sustained their share of trade volumes at a historic high of 44%, marking the consecutive quarter at this elevated level. items.statement: FY26 capex INR 620-670 cr (INR 320 cr spent in 9M, INR 200 cr in Q4); FY27 INR 1,000-1,100 cr; FY28 INR 650-700 cr.

items.statement: Vadraj plant phased commissioning: Surat grinding & Kutch clinker in FY27, Kutch grinding in H1 FY28; East expansion 4MTPA on track; total capacity to reach 35 MTPA.
