items.statement: Expects reasonably healthy Q4 FY26 performance with market support
items.quote: For the upcoming quarter the refinery is focused on maintaining its operational performance and we expect the market to continue to support us and we should be onoc Ik ltr7 ITIRPL able to post a reasonably healthy Q4 25-26 also

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA Rs 2,824 crores vs Rs 1,064 crores YoY; MBN 67 (best ever); fuel & loss 10.06% (among best)
items.quote: The EBITDA earned by the company was Rs.2,824 crores versus Rs.1,064 crore for the last year Quarter Q3. Healthy market prices, optimum energy consumption and throughput led to published bottom-line numbers. MRPL posted MBN of 67. MBN is a measure for energy efficiency for its capacity and its complexity. So this was the best number posted in any quarter.

items.statement: Cumulative GRM still around double of Q1 level; loss of Russian crude offset by higher product cracks
items.quote: However, we had given an indicative figure that it is double of what was the Quarter 1 margin. It is still in a similar range, at a cumulative level.

items.statement: HSD cracks: Q2 ~$15/bbl, Q3 ~$21/bbl, currently moderated to $14-15/bbl
items.quote: Currently, it is not as high as 21 and 13 that I told you. It has come down, and it has moderated to around 14-15. This is what, the current published cracks are.

items.statement: LNG under term contract with BPCL at competitive price; exploring CGD and parent company sources
items.quote: we already have a term contract with BPCL and it is at a significantly competitive price, it is not way above, and in fact, the newer LNG may, in fact be higher than that

items.statement: Freight rates spiked in Q3 but have come down significantly from peak; still slightly above Q1 levels
items.quote: We did see a spike in freight rates earlier in Q3. But the freight rates have gradually come down to the normal levels. They're still higher than the averages but it has come down significantly from its peak.

items.statement: Crude sourcing: ~40% committed to Middle East (Saudi Aramco); balance via tenders, domestic (ONGC, Mangala), and term arrangements (TOTSA, ADNOC)
items.quote: About 40% of our crudes, we have collectively, together with Government of India, we are committed to Middle East crudes led by Saudi Aramco.

items.statement: Heavier crude processing at 70-72% for 9 months; refinery can process up to 15-16 API but depends on economics
items.quote: Currently for the 9 months, I can mention that it is around 70-72%.

items.statement: Actively evaluating Venezuelan crude; decision depends on commercial terms and freight costs
items.quote: Yes so we are actively looking at it. We've not decided, but we are looking at it. Moreover, it depends on the commercial terms.

items.statement: Exports ~40% of products on a running basis; may change quarter to quarter
items.quote: We export almost 40% of our products in exports right now that is the percentage. It may change quarter on quarter, but I'm giving you the figure on a running basis.last year.

items.statement: No Russian crude imports; compliant with sanctions; no expected stop to product exports to Europe
items.quote: We are in strict compliance with all sanctions in place and currently there are no Russian crude which is being imported and we will continue to comply with any of these international sanctions regime or government guidelines. So in near future we do not expect anything to stop our export of finished products.

items.statement: ATF well placed with Shell tie-up; CORSIA compliance expected to protect market share
items.quote: ATF we are very well placed and technically as I mentioned we would be one of the first to be compliant with that CORSIA Standards, and based on our tie-up with Shell, affiliate company, we expect this particular business to keep growing and we expect this market share to be completely with us.

items.statement: Current debt Rs 9,290 crores; debt-equity 0.63; NCDs Rs 3,260 crores (due 2028); ECB $500M (~Rs 4,500 crores)
items.quote: current debt stands at Rs. 9,290 crores and debt equity stands at 0.63.

items.statement: Debt may come down modestly by year-end if market favorable; ECB repayment evaluated against forex loss
items.quote: Right now, it is 9.3 and it could come down, not very significantly, but it might come down if the market remains favorable.

items.statement: Dividend possibility for FY26 if Q4 profitable; board to decide considering capex, debt, and profitability
items.quote: And if Q4 remains profitable that we might... that is the... not me personally, the board might actually look at a dividend also. So that, I will leave to the decision of the board. But that is definitely on the anvil

items.statement: Retail outlet throughput ~120 KL per month per outlet
items.quote: the retail outlet sale is around 120KL per month per outlet.

items.statement: Refinery throughput 4.7 MMT (net crude) in Q3; nameplate 15 MMTPA, running ~120% utilization (18 MMT annualized)
items.quote: the 4.7 Million Metric Ton that we reported in our financials that was the net crude percentage. So our revenue and the rest of the things and the bottom line is driven by the net crude

items.statement: No longer publishing GRM as computation not standardized across industry; aligned with other PSUs
items.quote: we had taken a policy step that GRM computations and depictions and publications are not standardized by the different companies or in any of the forums itself. So we had discontinued publishing that and it is also in line with some of the other major PSUs and other companies also.

items.statement: Float limited: ~88% held by ONGC and HPCL; examining with parents to address float issue
items.quote: Almost 88% is with ONGC and HPCL and only balance 12% approximately is in the open market even in that 12% about 1% would be locked up in those non-participants. So the float is also an issue and we are examining it together with our parent companies to address that float issue.

items.statement: Expect loan growth faster than system in FY27; system growth assumed at 12-13%
items.value: 12-13% system, couple of hundred bps above
items.quote: So our understanding as of now is next year, we expect system growth to be between 12% to 13%, when you look at nominal GDP and the credit growth that's required to support nominal GDP. So if we're talking about 12% to 13%, we are talking about a couple of percentage points above that going into the next year.

items.statement: Target LDR 90-96% for FY26 and 85-90% for FY27
items.quote: We said we will try and be in a range of somewhere between 90% to 96% in the year FY '26, which is what we will be is what we are very confident about. And then maybe by FY '27, by the natural growth and even with the growth in the way we are expecting in terms of faster growth rate, I think we should land somewhere around the 85% to 90% for FY '27.

items.statement: Expect LDR to reach 90s or low 90s over next 1-2 years
items.quote: So given that, we do expect that over the next 1 year to 2 years, we would be getting down further into the levels that we had previously been there, call it, the 90s or low 90s and so on.

items.statement: NIM line of sight via cost of funds levers: time deposit repricing, borrowing mix, CASA improvement
items.quote: Yes, there is a line of sight, and these are some of those elements we work towards.

items.statement: Credit growth buildup encouraging; balanced across segments; CRR release enabled deployment ahead of expectations
items.quote: Looking back, I think the credit growth buildup has been extremely encouraging. We set our sights on a very balanced credit across customer segments. The easing rate cycle and the benign credit has provided catalysts for the credit growth. The CRR release enabled credit deployment slightly ahead of our expectations.

items.statement: Discretionary card spends up 21% YoY; non-discretionary up 13% YoY; overall card spend up 15% YoY, 3.4% QoQ
items.quote: If you look at the recent time period for card spend, which is important for you to look at, the overall card spend up 15%, 3.4% sequentially. Within the card spend, when we look at the discretionary category of card spends, the discretionary category spends have grown 21% year-on-year. The non-discretionary, which is the bread and butter normal activity is about 13% up.

items.statement: Crop cycle improved; healthy reservoir levels; manufacturing PMI expansionary; services consumption strong; auto and tractor sales exceed expectations
items.quote: In the economy, the growth momentum, yes, if you look at some of those indicators that we have seen - take the crop cycle itself, very improved. The sowing cycle has improved over prior year, very healthy water reservoir levels have aided that. The manufacturing PMI continues to be in the expansionary zone with many programs that are coming in. Services sector doing very well on the consumption de

items.statement: Asset quality pristine; lowest gross NPA accretion at decadal lows; no segment showing stress; agri slippages seasonal, ex-agri slippages 24 bps
items.quote: Across segments and even first at the sectoral, you're well aware that the banking industry right now to borrow a term is going through a Cinderella phase where you've got very strong balance sheets when I refer to that from an asset quality point of view. We have the lowest accretion of gross NPAs and net NPAs are at decadal lows.

items.statement: Net credit cost ~37 bps after recoveries; slippages steady ~25 bps; write-offs ~INR3,200 cr/quarter
items.quote: And net of recoveries, if you see, we are at about 37 basis points or thereabouts. And when you look at, again, last quarter, last year, order of magnitude, very similar within a few basis points, 5 basis points.

items.statement: Agri portfolio regulatory inspection complete; ~INR5 bn provision taken in December quarter; recalibration of scale of finance ongoing
items.quote: Our regulatory inspection is also complete. And whatever required according to the regulatory requirement, there was about 5 billion or so thereabouts, which have been taken. In the overall context of our book and our results, if you see, they have been absorbed within that, and there is no special and we have had certain other things that were there.

items.statement: Labour code impact estimated at ~INR8 bn via actuarial valuation; assumptions pending rule-making; recurring impact not determinable yet
items.quote: One, it is an estimate given whatever information that we have. And that estimate is driven through an actuarial process, right? So you go through the normal process of how you do and there is an actuarial valuation and determination of how do you do.

items.statement: Branch additions: 250 (2020), 350 (2021), 750 (2022), 1,500 (2023), 900 (2024), 700 (2025); near-term additions modest, not 5-7% annually
items.quote: We opened about 250 branches in 2020, 350 in '21, 750 in '22. 1,500 in '23, 900 in '24, 700 in '25. So if you look at this, 250, 350, 750, 1,500, 900, the opportunity space that it provided, we took that and accelerated all within the overall returns framework, right?

items.statement: Per branch productivity rose from INR237 cr to INR305 cr despite accelerated additions; 43% branches <5 years vintage
items.quote: If you look at the per branch productivity, we are now at about INR305 crores or thereabouts on a per branch at an aggregate level. Despite all of these additions that I talked to you about, if you go back where I just mentioned to you about how we were doing per branch, if you go to '23 or '19 to '23, that time Classification - Internal Classification - Internal period by time period, about INR23

items.statement: Card strategy shifted to transactors; revolvers at ~2/3 of pre-2020 levels; cards drive 20-25% of deposit momentum
items.quote: Today, 20% to 25%, maybe in the mid of 20% to 25%, I can say, is the range at which, out of the total deposit basket, the kind of momentum that you're seeing, whether it's on the healthy balances and what it contributes to total, it's somewhere around that 20, 25.

items.statement: Auto loans >80% self-funded via customer liability balances; mortgage not leading on pricing but as relationship fulcrum
items.quote: Same with auto. I do want to let you know that our auto loans are almost a little more than 80% self-funded, which means the customers when they take auto loan, we want their liability accounts, we want them to have balances in that and the loan self-funds itself for the most part within the balance sheet.

items.statement: Irrational pricing seen in home loans and auto from PSU banks; expected to play out in couple of quarters
items.quote: Yes. We've seen it not only in auto, but also in the home loan product. So these are two products where we have certainly seen some amount of, if I may say, a bit of irrational pricing, but irrational pricing has never sustained. It will play itself out and bury itself in a couple of quarters on the outer side, if not earlier.

items.statement: Retail individual deposits growing solid double-digits; institutional and non-individual retail in single digits; bulk deposits not chased due to rate discipline
items.quote: If you look at the institutional types, they were in the mid-single digits, right. The institutional type of deposits, mid-single digits. That's what we see. And within the retail branch, the non-individuals were much more modest. I think it was again a little more higher single digit. And the individual individual within the branches were in the solid double-digit growth.

items.statement: Borrowings at ~13% of funding mix QoQ, down from ~7% YoY; industry at 6-7%; opportunity to reduce further
items.quote: Quarter-to-quarter has remained static at about 13%. But again, more than a quarter, if you look at the year, we were at about 7%. Broadly, the industry is at about 6%, 7%. So there is an opportunity space to be that to keep coming down.

items.statement: CASA growth positive; core individual retail segments strong; granular mobilisation focus
items.quote: CASA growth has been positive. Cost has been under control as productivity improvements have brought in efficiencies. Credit, which has always been our USP, remains best-in-class, allowing us to deliver stable returns as we pivot to the next stage of growth.

items.statement: Labour code provision based on actuarial valuation with assumptions on wage definition pending rule-making; varies by staff tenure
items.quote: When you look at these variables, the definition of what is wage, what are determined to be wage inclusion, exclusion, the rule-making on that is pending. You know that, right? So there are some assumptions that go for one of the variables that go into those assumptions and that is not based on determined rules, that is based on some assumed things.

items.statement: CD ratio not a regulatory requirement; glide path committed for sustainable profitability; confident of meeting committed metrics by March 2026 and 2027
items.quote: There's been a lot of talk on the CD ratio. We did sort of drop our CD ratio significantly since the merger to March '25. As you know, the kind of indicator is not necessarily on the radar from a regulatory perspective. Having said that, we believe that our glide path to lowering of CD ratio will continue. It's an important focus for sustainable profitability.

items.statement: Total pipe order book reached 19.64 lakh metric tons in December 2025, up from 19.25 lakh metric tons in September 2025
items.quote: The Pipes business reported a rise in its total order book volume, reaching 19.64 lakh metric tons in December '25 as compared to 19.25 lakh metric tons in September '25.

items.statement: DI pipe order book is approximately 40% of total pipe order book, roughly 700,000 to 750,000 tons, valued at $560-570 million with $45 million export orders
items.quote: Out of the total order backlog -- total order book of pipes aggregating to approximately 19.64 lakh metric tons, DI pipe order book is approximately 40%, which includes exports and supplies under Jal Jeevan Mission as well.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary holds order book valued at approximately $235 million for 215,000 tons, ensuring operational stability for 9-12 months
items.quote: As of 31st December '25, the subsidiary holds a robust order book valued at approximately $235 million, which is for 215,000 tons.

items.statement: Combined order book of parent and UAE subsidiary is around $1.7 billion
items.quote: The backlog is independent of the parent company's stand-alone order book, which stands at approximately USD 1.48 billion. So if you add, it would be somewhere around $1.7 billion.

items.statement: New seamless plant piercing mill started production in Q3 FY26, enabling capacity increase to approximately 4 lakh tons per annum
items.quote: Q3 of FY '26 saw the start of production for our new seamless plant piercing mill. We are now stabilizing the production on this line. This enables a capacity increase to approximately 4 lakh tons per annum.

items.statement: New projects in GCC region including seamless pipe plant in Abu Dhabi, HSAW pipe unit and ductile iron pipe facility in Saudi Arabia expected to be commissioned in next 24 months by February 2028, financial impact from FY29
items.quote: All these p rojects are expected to be commissioned in next 24 months approximately, that is by February 28. And we can expect the impact on the financials from FY '29

items.statement: Seamless pipe plant in Abu Dhabi KEZAD Zone through step-down subsidiary Jindal Seamless Pipe Manufacturing LLC with initial USD 20 million equity infusion, land secured, long lead equipment orders initiated
items.quote: The company -- Jindal Saw is expanding its Middle East footprint with a new seamless facility in Abu Dhabi, KEZAD Zone, establishing through a step-down subsidiary named Jindal Seamless Pipe Manufacturing LLC with initial USD 20 million equity infusion.

items.statement: Saw pipe plant in Saudi Arabia JV with Buhur (51% step-down subsidiary), lease agreements identified and finalized, JV partners infused initial equity
items.quote: Jindal Saw Limited has established a joint venture with Buhur in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to develop a state-of-the-art saw pipe manufacturing facility. It is a 51% step-down subsidiary.

items.statement: Ductile pipe facility in KSA JV agreement signed by partner, other corporate actions in process
items.quote: For ductile pipe facility in KSA, JV agreement has been signed by the partner. Other corporate actions are in process.

items.statement: Pipe sector continued to see strong demand signals across both domestic and international markets
items.quote: The pipe sector continued to see strong demand signals across both domestic and international markets.

items.statement: Water pipe business impacted by protracted payment timelines in Indian water sector, lengthy receivables days pose major challenge for supply chain stability
items.quote: While market demand remains strong, business related to water pipes has been impacted significantly by protracted payment time lines in the Indian water sector.

items.statement: Q2 marked bottom of cycle, green shoots emerging in domestic and export markets, positive outlook on government initiatives including upcoming union budget
items.quote: Q3 demonstrated an improvement over Q2 of FY '26. With green shoots emerging in both domestic and export markets, it appears Q2 marked the bottom of the cycle.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA dropped from 19-20% in Dec 2024 to 12.7% in Dec 2025, uptick of ~300 bps in Q3 FY26, recovery will be slow journey
items.quote: So in summarized form, we dropped from 19.5% to, let's say, 10% in September '25. And there is an uptick of almost 300 basis points in the current quarter.

items.statement: Company capable of producing 2.2 million tons without additional capacity, productivity improvements and cost cutting measures underway
items.quote: We can -- without increasing additional capacity. So I'm not saying debottlenecking. Let's say, I'm not -- let's say, if I'm not putting any new plant of any of the product, we can easily go to, let's say, 2.2 million tons, okay?

items.statement: Q4 FY26 expected to be better than Q3 FY26 but not a return to 20% EBITDA margins
items.quote: What we expect in fou rth quarter, in any case, is always better than the third quarter, but fourth quarter is likely to be comparatively better than the third quarter

items.statement: Overdue receivables from EPC customers under Jal Jeevan Mission approximately INR 350 crores, majority backed by adequate security
items.quote: Importantly, our overdue receivables from EPC customers working under Jal Jeevan Mission are approximately INR350 crores only, and majority of these are backed by adequate security.

items.statement: Receivables improvement in Q3 due to receipt of retention monies and stuck money as usual process, ductile business not being done optimally
items.quote: We have received the retention monies or money which was stuck as a usual process. So that is -- and if you remember -- if you see that we have said in our preface that trade finance is an integral part of the pipe business.

items.statement: Standalone net debt narrowed to INR 3,154 crores as of Dec 31 2025 vs INR 3,310 crores as of Sep 30 2025, long-term debt only INR 534 crores
items.quote: on debt side, as on 31st December 2025, the stand -alone net debt narrowed to INR3,154 crores versus INR3,310 crores as on 30 September 2025, which includes the long -term debt of INR534 crores only

items.statement: Consolidated net institutional debt reduced to INR 3,346 crores vs INR 3,856 crores at Sep 30 2025, long-term institutional debt only INR 690 crores
items.quote: On the consolidation side, the net institutional debt has reduced to INR3,346 crores as compared to INR3,856 crores as at 30th September 2025. The long-term institutional debt is only INR690 crores.

items.statement: Standalone long-term debt exposure approximately INR 533 crores, INR 500 crores attributable to LIC-backed entity with staggered redemption 2028-2030
items.quote: Our long-term debt structure remains highly sustainable, featuring a stand-alone exposure of approximately INR533 crores only notably, INR500 crores is attributable to the LIC-backed entity with a well-staggered redemption schedule between 2028 and 2030.

items.statement: Export revenue share is 30% of total
items.quote: In totality, it is 30%.

items.statement: Still exporting seamless pipes to US despite tariffs, exploring other export markets and opportunities to supply to MENA region from upcoming Abu Dhabi seamless mill
items.quote: We are still supplying to U.S. despite the tariffs, means that India is competitive, and we are still exporting to U.S. Now it has to be seen that how much U.S. will budge -- and our people are now trying to, let's say, explore other export markets as well.

items.statement: Strategy to increase export component in DI sector from less than 5% to larger portfolio to reduce domestic market dependence
items.quote: Yes. That is our strategy that we should increase the export component in DI sector. Earlier, it was very minimal, less than 5%. Now it is increasing. And our focus would be to maintain that export portfolio a little bit large so that we are not depending on domestic market.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission fund release delayed, INR 17,000 crores likely to be disbursed in couple of months, awaiting budget announcement on Feb 1 for scheme extension and allocation
items.quote: They have -- even though they have done INR67,000 crores to INR17,000 crores, but at least INR17,000 crores is likely to be disbursed in some time, a couple of months.

items.statement: Jindal ITF vs NTPC case initial arguments in Jan 2026, next hearing fixed for Feb 2 for NTPC arguments
items.quote: The initial arguments by Jindal ITF took place in January '26. in front of the double bench of Delhi High Court. The hearing has now been fixed for 2nd February, where NTPC will make the arguments.

items.statement: UAE ductile iron pipe plant delivered approximately 52,000 metric tons in Q3 FY26 vs 58,000 metric tons in Q2 FY26
items.quote: In UAE entity, which is Abu Dhabi ductile pipe production plant, the entity maintained steady operations in Q3 of FY '26, delivering approximately 52,000 metric tons of corrosion-resistant ductile iron pipes compared to 58,000 metric tons in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Jindal Hunting JV (51% stake) generated INR 137.9 crores revenue and INR 44 crores PAT in 9 months ended FY25, up from INR 130.7 crores revenue and INR 38 crores PAT previous year
items.value: INR 137.9 crores revenue, INR 44 crores PAT
items.quote: This entity generated INR137.9 crores revenue and INR44 crores of PAT in 9 months period ended FY '25, which is an increase from INR130.7 crores of revenue and INR38 crores PAT in the previous year.

items.statement: Targets double-digit annual revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA growth for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: Our goal for 2026 and 2027 continues to remain the same, which is to consistently deliver double-digit annual revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA growth year-on-year.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA margin at 13.9%, ahead of 11-12% target
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has also come in much ahead , at 13.9% for the first nine months. Last year, when I spoke about double -digit EBITDA, we were expecting around 11–12%, but we are well ahead

items.statement: Budgeting 12% EBITDA margin for FY26, considers it sustainable
items.quote: Very honestly, for us, 11% to 12% was the goal for this year. So yes, 12% is what we are budgeting very well for, and that’s sustainable.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR 411.8 crore, 11.7% YoY growth
items.quote: We delivered INR 411.8 crores in revenue, representing 11.7% growth on an annual basis, very much in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Upgraded infrastructure in Pune, Chennai, Bangalore, Hyderabad; Pune and Hyderabad at full capacity
items.quote: We upgraded our infrastructure in Pune, Chennai, Bangalore, and Hyderabad. Pune and Hyderabad are now running at full capacity, and with the addition of Chennai, we’ve opened up a few hundred addition al seats

items.statement: Majority of new offshore headcount addition in 2026 will be in Chennai
items.quote: So, going into 2026 , the majority of our new offshore headcount addition will be in

items.statement: Focus on scaling 40+ relationships in IEHM vertical and expanding into Europe
items.quote: The key opportunity is to build an execution engine how to scale these 40 plus relationships. And second, is to expand big into Europe, which is a completely new territory for us in this vertical.

items.statement: T&M vertical adding leader with US/Europe experience to build team and transition relationships globally
items.quote: we’ve added a leader with U.S. and European experience who is building his team across Europe and the U.S. The first focus is to build a very strong organization, transition our existing relationships into global markets

items.statement: HCLS vertical won good client engagements, focus on deepening relationships over 1-3 years
items.quote: We’ve won some good client engagements, and now it’s about how fast we can deepen and grow those relationships. Over the next one to three years, I believe this will be a very exciting vertical for us.

items.statement: Committed to 90% T&M revenue mix until INR 1,000 crore revenue
items.quote: Our goal continues to remain at 90% T&M, at least until we get to $100 million or INR 1,000 crores of revenue.

items.statement: DSO improved to 70 days at end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: From a financial perspective, our DSO continues to improve and now stands at 70 days at the end of Q3 FY26.

items.statement: Dividend increased to INR 5/share two years ago; aim to sustain or grow, not one-off special
items.quote: I think we increased it to INR 5 a share two years ago. My job is to make sure I sustain that, if not grow it. So, we’re not looking at anything one-off.

items.statement: Buyback option under consideration by Board
items.quote: the option is under consideration and as I said, we are progressively always looking at the best options for Onward Tech and all our shareholders.

items.statement: Hedging only 50% offshore revenue (US, Germany); conservative approach
items.quote: Not much, We are only hedging the balance 50%. As a company, we are conservative. Predominantly, we are hedging our offshore revenue from the U.S. and Germany.

items.statement: Offshore billing rates double digits vs on-site low single digits; margin expansion from offshore shift
items.quote: On -site billing rates are traditionally low single digits, and offshore rates are double digits, at least for us today.

items.statement: Qualified supplier process takes 3 months to 3 years based on in-house delivery capability
items.quote: To become a qualified supplier to the largest companies in each vertical we operate in, we have to do a lot of capability presentations, client references, pilot projects, POC work, financial check, credit ratings, etc ranging anywhere from three months to three years.

items.statement: Fastest growing organic ER&D company over last 3-4 years per consultants
items.quote: On the engineering side, we’ve had some of the best consultants come and tell us that we are the fastest -growing organic company over the last three to four years.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance maintained at 12-15% for FY26
items.quote: In fact, I would still maintain the guidance of 12% to 15%, especially owing to the fact that there is a stress on the deposit growth.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance 10% for FY26
items.quote: Market guidance for financial year '25, '26 credit growth 12%, deposit growth 10%, CASA 45%, NIM 3.65% to 3.7%, Return on Assets 1.2% to 1.25%, Return on Equity 15% to 16%, Gross NPA below 3%.

items.statement: GNPA guidance below 3% for March 2026
items.quote: We are pleased to inform that we are on the brink of achieving our GNPA guidance of below 3% for March 2026, a quarter ahead of schedule with GNPA as on December 31, 2025, recorded at 3%.

items.statement: Net NPA improved to 0.68% from 0.94% a year ago
items.quote: Our net NPA has also recorded a substantial improvement , recorded at 0.68% as on December 31, 2025, versus 0.94% a year a go, with the bank continuing to maintain adequate provisions with PCR above 90%.

items.statement: Annualized gross slippage ratio at 0.83% for 9 months, zero credit cost
items.quote: Gross slippages also continu e to be under control with annualized gross slippage ratio at 0.83% for the 9-month period and no credit costs for the 9-month period.

items.statement: NIM improved sequentially to 3.62% in Q3, 3.64% for 9 months
items.quote: We have been able to improve our NIMs on a sequential basis despite a 25 bps rate cut , with NIM for Q3 recorded at 3.62% and that of 9 months at 3.64%, broadly in line with the expectations sp elled out in our previous call.

items.statement: Cost of deposits declined to 4.69% in Q3
items.quote: We have Jammu & also recorded a decline in Cost of Deposits and the same has been recorde d at 4.69% for this quarter

items.statement: NIM expected to reach 3.7% by Q4 FY26 if no further rate cuts
items.quote: Definitely, if you look at my guidance it is 3.7%.

items.statement: Full deposit repricing expected by March 2026
items.quote: Basing this, I think by March the entire thing will be re-priced.

items.statement: Board approved raising equity up to INR750 cr and Tier 2 capital up to INR500 cr
items.value: INR750 cr equity, INR500 cr Tier 2
items.quote: the Board of the bank during this quarter has accorded their approval for raising equity capital up to INR750 crores and Tier 2 capital up to INR500 crores.

items.statement: Targeting QIP completion by March 31 2026, may spillover based on market conditions
items.quote: We are also targeting QIP to be completed by 31st March. H owever, it may spillover a little bit based on the conducive marketing conditions.

items.statement: RIDF maturities of ~INR3,000 cr starting next year, no fresh RIDF investment needed next year
items.quote: Starting from next year, I think around INR3,000 crores is getting matured, followed by around same amount in the following year. And if we look at our priority sector and the sub-targets, I believe unless, of course, we get the final figures for the year -end, I believe that we will not be required to invest anymore on RIDF for the next year.

items.statement: CD ratio target 77-78% in medium term, currently at 72%
items.quote: my target would in the mediu m term will be to take it to around 77%, 78%.

items.statement: Credit growth 7.7% Q-o-Q and 17.3% Y-o-Y, outpacing system growth of ~11.7-12%

items.statement: South Africa order worth USD147 million for 240 MW turnkey project; fourth project in South Africa; contracts in USD, no forex risk

items.statement: Module price risk transferred to client until NTP date; post-NTP, company ties up supply quickly; all new contracts have this protection

items.statement: Nearly 6-7 GW of orders likely to be bid out in India in Q4 FY26; confident of further wins; FY27 third-party EPC pipeline building, market bids may surpass 30 GW
items.quote: We have nearly 6 to 7 gigawatt of orders that are likely to be bid out this quarter in India alone. And we are fairly confident of making further headway in so me of these bids. We also have some interesting projects lining up in the international side, where as I mentioned earlier, we are beginning to find work along with terms that we prefer and find equitable.

items.statement: Active dialogue with Reliance for large multi-year multi-GW RE rollout; orders would be over and above current FY26 guidance; traction expected by end of Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: Last but not least, our new order inflow guidance does not capture any potential order inflow from Reliance, where we continue to remain in active dialogue on the ir large multiyear multi-gigawatt RE rollout. Those will be over and above our current guidance for this fiscal. For financial year 2027, we are already beginning to see a strong third-party EPC pipeline continue to build and expect the

items.statement: DCR/ALMC policy from Sep 2025 mandates domestic modules for Indian bids; domestic module manufacturing capacity ~125 GW, cell ~60 GW sufficient for ~40 GW annual Indian demand
items.quote: Now under this scheme, so today, our module manufacturing capacity would be around 125 gigawatt, right? And the cell would be around 60 gigawatts, something like this, right? And in the value chain, the wafers are also coming up. So I am expecting that at least for the large players like Adani, Reliance, the Waaree, Vikrams, all those domestic capacity would be sufficient to cater to the requireme

items.statement: Recurring overheads flat at ~INR93 crores/quarter; cost rationalization underway but conservative run rate ~INR90 crores/quarter expected
items.quote: So we are in the process of rationalizing our costs though, but on a conservative basis, we can consider the similar kind of run rate to go ahead.

items.statement: No operational deficiencies or client claims foreseen; US court cases relate to bank guarantee encashment, cash outgo ~INR750 crores covered under indemnity
items.quote: So our cash outgo at this point in time is around INR750 crores towards legal cases, which is covered under indemnity.

items.statement: India BESS capacity at 0.5 GWh as of June 2025; CEA estimates 34.7+ GW needed by FY27; company sees significant opportunity
items.quote: CEA estimates India will need 34.7 gigawatts and above of BESS capacities by the end of financial year 2027. This widening gap between current capacity and future requirements is now driving a significant reallocation of capital across the power value chain where we hope to play an active role in the coming years.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 order inflow expected ~INR4,000 crores; already L1 on large PSU project, advanced negotiations with private IPPs and international
items.quote: So basically, we are already L1 in one of the very important PSU for the large size project, right? And then we are at the advanced stage of closing few orders with the private IPPs, also international. So with all those things, we are pretty confident that we'll be crossing or we'll be achieving this INR4,000 crores mark.

items.statement: International projects at better margins with conducive terms; international revenue share guided at 15-20% of overall revenue/order book
items.quote: And in terms of guidance, we can say around 15%, 20% of our overall revenue or order book would be international. Otherwise, our focus primarily would be domestic market.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 12%-13% for next year unless B2C business changes
items.quote: at least for the balance part of this year and the next year, until the EO supply situation comes through by Q3, we would hazard that our margins would be in this similar range between 12%-13% unless we take, what I talked about on the B2C business.

items.statement: Core B2B EBITDA margin at ~14% in Q3 FY26, below normalized 15%-16% band
items.quote: Excluding the institutional and B2C business, our core B2B operations delivered an EBITDA of Rs. 72 crore with a margin of approximately 14%, which is marginally lower than our normalized margin band of 15%-16%.

items.statement: Total capex capitalized by end of FY26 expected around Rs. 200 crore across group
items.quote: By the end of FY26, we would have capitalized total close to, I think, about Rs. 200 crore. I do not have the exact number, but it will be around that number across the group.

items.statement: Unitop Ethoxylation facility at 10%-15% utilization in Q3 FY26, targeting 90% by end of FY27
items.quote: Currently, if you ask me in this quarter, the utilization would be at a low of between 10%-15%. But as the plant gets stabilized and as the product continuous process starts going through, I think the capacities will slowly see a ramp-up. We expect an optimal utilization happening over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Second phase of Ethoxylation capacity expected onstream in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The part of the Ethoxylation capacity came up in the last quarter. And the balance second phase is expected to come onstream in this quarter, which is Q4.

items.statement: Ethylene Oxide supply constrained near-term; additional supplier volumes expected by Q3 FY27
items.quote: the expansion on the side of the supplier is going onstream We have been told that the additional volumes should come up by Q3 FY27. Hopefully, post that, then there should not be any issues on EO availability.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 26% YoY in 9M FY26, now ~30% of turnover
items.quote: If you see in these 9 months, export has grown almost 26% v/s last year while domestic has grown only 10%. And today, in these 9 months, the export piece is close to 30% of our turnover, maybe 3-4 years back, this number used to be less than 20%.

items.statement: Domestic demand soft in textiles and HPPC; December saw pickup after weak Oct-Nov
items.quote: If you see our months of October and part of November were really very soft for us. The demand was very low, especially in the HPPC. But then again in the month of December we saw the demand picking back and lot of the subdued demand actually came up in December.

items.statement: New product sales now 20%+ of revenue; bio-surfactants approved by 2 global MNCs
items.quote: the new R&D products which are developed, if you see our sales of new products now is 20%-plus. We are planning to sell part of our consumer businesses, we are expecting even about Rs. 150 crore coming into the company for sale of this.

items.statement: Evaluating sale of consumer business; expecting ~Rs. 150 crore proceeds
items.quote: We are planning to sell part of our consumer businesses, we are expecting even about Rs. 150 crore coming into the company for sale of this. We are expecting a good valuation for the same.

items.statement: KSA greenfield project in evaluation phase; $8M equity infusion approved for groundwork, not capex
items.quote: That $8 million was just an approval taken for doing any kind of equity infusion for us to do the evaluation process. The capex will be substantially higher than that. That was only an initial approval we have taken to start, as I said, now in-principle approval has come and we will need to start doing a lot of groundwork there.

items.statement: Working capital improved sequentially in Q3 with better collections; moving toward normalized levels
items.quote: On working capital, the position improved sequentially in Q3 with better collection during this quarter. While we continue to hold selective strategic inventory for key raw materials, overall, the working capital is moving back towards the normalized levels.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven almost entirely by volume (~10%-12% YoY); pricing net neutral
items.quote: As I was saying, most of the growth that we have seen on a YoY basis had all come out of the volume growth. Some price increase would have taken, but I think that the increase in one gets knocked off by a decrease in pricing in the other. But on an overall basis, we have seen our volume growth happening close to almost 10%-12%.

items.statement: Added new textile export customers in Turkey, Uzbekistan, Morocco, Philippines, Indonesia; increased stock points
items.quote: The export is driven by new customers. We have added a lot of new geographies like Turkey, Uzbekistan, Morocco, Philippines, Indonesia., These are all the new countries where we have started adding customers. We also increased the number of stock points.

items.statement: AHN growth driven by key account focus and export expansion to Nepal, Bangladesh, Egypt, Nigeria, Thailand, South America, Central Europe
items.quote: Also now in AHN, we are focusing to drive sales through key accounts. Some of that is playing out now. Hopefully, we should see that coming up also going forward. Again, our export initiative in AHN is also now laid out. We have seen some of it happening in this quarter. There are a lot of countries we are adding. Some of them being Nepal, Bangladesh. We have also done some business in Egypt, Nige

items.statement: Major capacity enhancement capex done; next 2-3 years focused on utilization, new product development, piloting, R&D
items.quote: Most of the capacity enhancement capexes have been done. For the next 2-3 years, we may have some CAPEX towards new product development, piloting, R&D, etcetera. But capacity enhancement capex are done and the aim would be now for the next 2-3 years to optimally utilize these capacities, bring in newer products and fill up the plants in India.

items.statement: EO availability may become issue again during ramp-up next year before supplier expansion in Q3 FY27
items.quote: The EO challenge, currently, because of the overall subdued market, we are not facing any issues in terms of EO availability. But as the ramp-up starts happening in the next year, there could be a few months where EO could be an issue.

items.statement: Target 25% ROCE by end of next year
items.quote: And I believe we are on track to achieving 25% ROCE by the end of next year.

items.statement: Target INR 350 crores free cash flow for next year
items.quote: For the next year, we -- our target was INR350 crores. I think that is still intact.

items.statement: Volume growth target 35-40% for FY26
items.quote: Our target for this year was a growth of about 30%, which we revised to maybe towards 40% within this year.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton target to reach 8-9 over next 1-2 years
items.quote: gradually, the target, of course, is to increase this to 8, 8.5 or 9 over the next 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: Target 90% capacity utilization
items.quote: our target is always to achieve 90% kind of a capacity utilization.

items.statement: Target 10% market share in next 2-3 years
items.quote: in the very near future in the next 2 to 3 years, I think we should be able to go to a 10% kind of a market share.

items.statement: 60,000 tons brownfield expansion at Dadri commissioning in 3-4 days
items.quote: for the 60,000 ton capex for Dadri, I think now we have -- I think we will be commissioning it in another 3, 4 days.

items.statement: 90,000 tons Greenfield expansion at Sanand by Q3/Q4 next fiscal
items.quote: For 90,000 tons , I think the time lines are still intact by end of next year is when we are expecting that to happen.

items.statement: IHT capacity 9,000 tons expanding to 15,000 tons combined with OHT in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: the capacity was 9,000 tons , which we are now expanding to 15,000 tons. This should be done in the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: LRPC capacity 18,000 tons at Dadri facility
items.quote: LRPC, which was launched at our Dadri facility with a capacity of 18,000 tons.

items.statement: Strong demand across automotive, infrastructure, general engineering; highest monthly sale 45,000 tons in December
items.quote: we picked up in December, achieving our highest ever monthly sale of 45,000 tons.

items.statement: Specialty wires 4-5% of volume but targeting 15-20% of EBITDA contribution
items.quote: in terms of contribution towards EBITDA, I think this can be contributing about 15% to 20% of the total EBITDA going forward.

items.statement: Low carbon 55-60% of capacity, stainless 20%, high carbon rest; targeting 60-62% low carbon
items.quote: 620,000 tons, I would say about 55%, 60% is low carbon, 20% would be stainless steel and the rest will be high carbon. And I think going forward also, we are looking at similar numbers. The only difference could be in low carbon where we expect at least 60%, 62% of the total capacity

items.statement: Steel cord lab approvals expected in 10-15 days, field trials after plant restart in 1-1.5 months, supply start Q2/Q3 next year
items.quote: the last company that we are expecting lab approval from should also come in, in the next 10, 15 days. After that, we go to field trial once we have our plant up and running, which will take about 1 month, 1.5 months. So Q2, Q3 is our target still for starting supplies of steel cord.

items.statement: Generated INR 240 crores free cash from operations in 9 months, nearly full year target
items.quote: we have generated almost INR240 crores of free cash from operations, which was almost a full year's target.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR 233 crores for 9 months, INR 85 crores for Q3
items.quote: The operating cash flow generated during the 9 months period, INR233 crores and the company generated cash flow from the operation during this quarter that is INR85 crores.

items.statement: Fire in specialty wire shed caused INR 1.5 crores exceptional loss in Q3, no further material impact expected
items.quote: we have already posted an exceptional loss of INR 1.5 crores. That was due to the inventory loss in the fire, which we've estimated. Everything else was insured.

items.statement: Q3 volume 121,000 tons (32% YoY, 6% QoQ); 9M volume 340,000 tons (38% YoY)
items.quote: During the quarter, company delivered a record sales volume of 121,000 metric tons , representing a strong 32% year -on-year growth and 6% sequential growth over quarter 2 financial '26.

items.statement: 9M revenue INR 3,023 crores (18% YoY), EBITDA INR 243 crores (19% YoY), PAT INR 121 crores (7% YoY)
items.quote: For the 9 months period ended financial '26, revenue grew by 18% year -on-year to INR3,023 crores, while the EBITDA came in INR 243 crores, reflecting an increase of 19% year -on-year. Net profit of 9 months for financial '26 stood at INR121 crores, higher by 7% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: No price reduction to gain market share; blended EBITDA per ton decline due to product mix only
items.quote: The strategy of gaining market share by reducing prices did not really happen. We have not actually increased EBITDA per ton on any of our product. So only difference right now that you see in the blended EBITDA is because of product mix and not because of any reduction in margin.

items.statement: B2C sales in low carbon increased from 5% in Q2 to 7% in Q3, targeting 12-15% next year
items.quote: In the second quarter, we were at about 5% B2C sales. In the third quarter itself, we have already crossed 7% B2C sales. And our target for next year is to achieve a 12% to 15% kind of a number.

items.statement: Signed term sheet to acquire Ricardo Elevators, a D2C home elevator brand, via merger; Ricardo promoters to receive low single-digit equity (2-3% dilution) locked for 3-4 years with annual unlocking.

Elevator, so we are talking between 2-3% dilution for L.T. Elevator shareholders.

items.quote: the exact timing will do after March 2026 numbers; however, indicatively, what we have agreed in-principle is, equity in the low single digit in L.T. Elevator, so we are talking between 2-3% dilution for L.T. Elevator shareholders.

items.statement: Ricardo team continues to run business development, marketing, and sales; L.T. Elevator runs backend operations, manufacturing, and engineering.
items.quote: So, the team at Ricardo continues to run the business development, marketing, sales side of it, we completely run the backend operation, manufacturing engineering all of it, and so both companies are together.

items.statement: Ricardo currently procuring 50-60 orders per month, growing 15-20% month-over-month; was 20-25 orders per month a year ago.
items.quote: they are able to procure between 50 to 60 orders per month and that number has been growing almost 15-20% month-over-month. So, at the same time last year they would have been procuring roughly maybe 20-25 orders per month and now they are at 60 orders per month.

items.statement: Ricardo's current order book rendered is Rs.46 crores; digital ad spend is Rs.10-12 lakhs.
items.quote: now the Rs.46 crores order is rendered, their digital spend at this point in time is between Rs.10-12 lakhs so which I found incredible because that is just crazy return on ad spend

items.statement: Parking and traditional elevator businesses have similar net margin profile of 13-16%.
items.quote: parking and elevators are in a very similar industry, very similar margin profile. So, both businesses between 13% to 15%, 16% is the net margin one should expect and both businesses are quite similar.

items.statement: Ricardo expected to deliver 8-10% net margin in FY26 due to high operating costs (18 branches, outsourced manufacturing); long-term potential for 5% higher margin than B2B if premium brand built and selling cost kept within 12.5%.
items.quote: I think FY26 it seems that they will have maybe 8% to 10% net margin, but that is also because on the expense side, they have a lot of people and 18 branches, it is not cheap to operate those

items.quote: The average selling price is between Rs.10 lakhs to Rs.11 lakhs. Typically, in B2C the transportation is extra. The COGS which include installation is roughly Rs.6 lakhs. The marketing expenditure which is ads is between 2-5%. The cost to run all of these experience centers as well as all the people in those experience centers which is the sales teams and all of that, that is roughly 10% as things

items.statement: Plan to raise funds via preferential allotment once market conditions improve to fund expanded capacity for Ricardo-driven growth.
items.quote: Yes, we would probably look to do a preferential once the markets are slightly better because right now the way the markets are it would be difficult to raise the money we want to.

items.statement: B2C model collects 95-100% payment before shipment, significantly improving working capital vs B2G receivables; target 50-60% B2C mix by FY28 to balance.
items.quote: Our working capital will greatly improve because on the B2C side pretty much 95% to 100% of the payment is received before anything is shipped from the factory.

items.statement: Ricardo generates 2,000-2,500 enquiries monthly via Meta ads (100% digital leads); conversion process involves call screening, site visit by BDM, technical-commercial discussion, and closure in 3 meetings.
items.quote: they have already gotten to a point where they are generating 2,000 to 2,500 enquiries every month from individual house owners who want to put up an elevator, and therefore this brand which has built a good social media presence has a fairly decent number of enquiries coming through digital ads.

items.statement: Home elevator market size ~Rs.2,000 crores; early mover advantage in digital D2C channel; incumbents (MNCs) not yet focused on this channel.
items.quote: The home elevator market roughly is around Rs.2,000 crores is a big enough market at this point with not many brands built yet, so it gives us sort of an early-mover advantage in this space. The incumbents which are the large companies like they were sleeping on the digital opportunity

items.statement: Ricardo has 18 experience centers/branches with sales and maintenance teams; team retained post-merger to run consumer-facing operations.
items.quote: they have a lot of people and 18 branches, it is not cheap to operate those, and even though the order book is growing quite fast, but deliveries are getting stuck

items.statement: Ricardo currently 100% outsourced manufacturing causing fulfillment delays and high procurement costs; in-house manufacturing expected to resolve inefficiencies.
items.quote: right now for Ricardo 100% is outsourced. These are the numbers if we were doing the manufacturing, right now it is a little scattered, there are multiple vendors for the same products and all of that.

items.statement: B2C brand building uncertain; 5% margin premium depends on achieving premium brand recall similar to other digital-native Indian brands (Mamaearth, Boat, etc.).
items.quote: it does feel that if we can create a premium brand which it seems is possible as has been true for almost every other consumer category, then it seems possible to have a 5% extra margin from that business, but like there are (Inaudible) 44:27 in that, right? You have to have a premium brand and all of that.

items.statement: Post-merger, L.T. Elevator will operate single B2C brand (Ricardo) nationally; L.T. brand retained for B2B/B2G; 50%+ of elevator orders already from outside East India, rising to 70-80% with Ricardo.
items.quote: now 50% or more of our elevator orders already come from outside East India, right, with Ricardo, the orders coming from outside East India is of the overall mix is probably closer to 70%, 80%.

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth guidance 18%-20%
items.quote: Given the strong traction seen in Q3 in book growth and remaining conscious about the prepayment pressure, we are on track to meet our FY '26 guidance of 18%-20% AUM growth.

items.statement: FY26 credit cost guidance on track
items.quote: Overall, asset quality remains robust, coverage levels are strong and credit costs continue to trend downwards, underscoring the resilience of our portfolio and keeping us well on track to meet our FY '26 guidance on credit costs.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio guidance 38%-39%
items.quote: For FY '26, we remain confident of closing the year with a cost-to-income ratio in the range of 38% to 39%, as we had communicated earlier.

items.statement: AUM growth target 23%-25% CAGR March 2025 to March 2028
items.quote: We have stated that over the next couple of years till March'28, between March'25 to 28, we have said that we will grow at about 23% to 25%.

items.statement: Motor Finance proportion to decline to 7%-8% by FY28
items.quote: That proportion may come down to about 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Motor Finance growth to resume from H1 FY27
items.quote: With these actions in place, we expect growth to resume from the first half of FY '27.

items.statement: Credit cost target around 1%
items.quote: When we look ahead, our stated objective is to be at around 1% on our credit cost.

items.statement: Ex-Motor Finance AUM INR 2.34 lakh crore, up 26% YoY, 9% QoQ
items.quote: Excluding Motor Finance business, our AUM stood at INR2.34 lakh crores, reflecting a 26% Y-o-Y growth and a 9% sequential growth.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM INR 2.61 lakh crore, up 7% QoQ
items.quote: Including the Motor Finance business, our AUM stood at INR2.61 lakh crores with 7% sequential growth.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly AUM growth ~INR 16,800 crore
items.quote: I am pleased to report that we recorded our highest ever quarterly AUM growth of ~ INR16,800 crores driven by festive demand and benefits of GST reduction.

items.statement: Housing Finance AUM INR 81,585 crore, up 30% YoY
items.quote: Total AUM stood at INR 81,585 crores.

items.statement: Motor Finance AUM INR 26,584 crore, down 6% QoQ
items.quote: The Motor Finance AUM stood at INR 26,584 crores, reflecting a 6% sequential decline.

items.statement: Motor Finance disbursements up 17% QoQ
items.quote: Importantly, our disbursements increased by 17% in Q3 over Q2 and we are confident that disbursement momentum will build sequentially from here as the business stabilizes and transformation gains traction.

items.statement: Unsecured retail disbursements up 30% YoY, 13% QoQ
items.quote: I am pleased to report that quarter 3 disbursements were 30% higher on a Y-o-Y basis and 13% over quarter 2.

items.statement: Unsecured retail exposure 10.4% of AUM, target 15%
items.quote: With unsecured retail exposure currently at 10.4% of AUM, it leaves us with ample runaway to achieve our stated vision of increasing it to 15% of the AUM.

items.statement: Retail and SME loans 87% of total AUM
items.quote: Overall, retail and SME loans continue to account for 87% of our total AUM.

items.statement: Branch network 1,505 branches across 27 states/UTs

items.statement: Customer base 8.1 million
items.quote: Combined with our comprehensive digital capabilities, this enables us to effectively serve a growing customer base of 8.1 million.

items.quote: We continue to operate in a stable NIM plus other revenue corridor, with NIM for Q3 at 6.6% , up 14 basis points versus Q2, including a 17 basis points contribution attributable to the proceeds from the IPO.

items.statement: Significant portion of rate easing passed to customers, margins stable
items.quote: During the quarter, while we benefited from lower cost of funds, significant portion of the easing was passed on to customers, keeping margins at stable levels.

items.statement: Medium-term margin expansion potential from product mix optimization and fee income
items.quote: Looking ahead, we see potential for margin expansion over the medium term, supported by further optimization of our product mix, with a rising contribution from higher yield segments such as unsecured retail, affordable housing and secured business loans, as well as growth in fee-based businesses and continued benefits of lower funding costs.

items.statement: Housing Finance margins stable despite competitive intensity

items.statement: Cost of funds 7.2%, down 14 bps QoQ on daily average basis
items.quote: For Q3, overall cost of funds stood at 7.2%, down 14 basis points from Q2 on daily average basis.

items.statement: Benefits of policy rate easing flowing through steadily

items.quote: Excluding the Motor Finance business, Stage 3 assets stood at 1.6%, net Stage 3 at 0.6% and provision coverage ratio at 64.5%, broadly in line with Q2 levels.

items.statement: Motor Finance credit cost declining, break-even achieved in Q3
items.quote: Our performance reflects this trend with credit costs declining and business achieving break-even in Q3.

items.quote: In the home loan, Raghav, there has been a very marginal increase of around 2-3 basis points. On the rounding off, it shows an increase. We have not seen any stress in the home loan portfolio.

items.statement: Collection efficiencies improving, missed payment rates better in Q3 vs Q2
items.quote: The other thing which we are also seeing is that the missed payment rates have also improved in Q3 over Q2. So, collection efficiencies are also showing a better trend.

items.statement: Unsecured retail slippages showing significant improving trend
items.quote: If you notice in our presentation on slide 16, we have also shown the slippages in the unsecured retail business and they also show a significant improving trend.

items.statement: Labour code one-time PAT impact INR 33 crore
items.quote: The profit after tax impact of this New Labour Code has been INR 33 crores.

items.quote: We've made deep investments in expansion of our branches and digital assets three years back. We've seen the benefits of that coming into our operating leverage.

items.quote: All our branch expansion in the last one year has been in the affordable and the micro-housing. So, along with prime we are looking at near prime, affordable as well as micro-housing to see that our margins are protected.
