items.quote: Now, if you look at these wins, some of these wins are scaling as we speak. And the way the business model in some of these things is when we are bringing our tool and IP, we are monetizing some amount upfront and some amount is basically through the productivity that get by deploying lesser number of people because we are using the technology.

items.statement: North America revenue +18.6% YoY; Europe +22.0% YoY; India -2.5% YoY; Rest of World +37.9% YoY (smaller base); Constant currency growth 4.1% QoQ
items.quote: In terms of year-on-year growth this quarter in USD terms, - North America revenue grew by 18.6%, - Europe grew by 22.0%, - India declined by 2.5% and - Rest of the World grew by 37.9% although on a smaller base.

items.statement: 1.1M shares allocated to ESOP Trust for past RSU grants; ESOP cost decreasing in FY26 vs FY25, further reduction expected in FY27
items.quote: This is a part and parcel of the stock options of the RSUs that have been granted in the past. And as a result of that, the cost that needs to come in as per the Black-Scholes valuation methodology is being factored in.

items.statement: Earn-out credit of ₹129.8M from recent acquisition boosted Other Income; capability-led acquisitions part of growth strategy alongside dividend payouts
items.quote: Increase in Other Income was primarily due to earn-out credit of ₹129.8 million from one of our recent acquisitions.

items.statement: S&P Global ESG score improved to 86 from 85; recognized as Microsoft Frontier Firm, Kantar BrandZ Top 6, ISG Star of Excellence for AI/Data (CX score 92), Gartner Emerging Leader, Everest Leader
items.quote: This quarter, I'm pleased to announce that our S&P Global ESG score has improved to 86, a step up from last year's score of 85.

items.statement: Medium-term target to scale installed capacity to over 7 lakh metric tonnes per annum by FY2028
items.quote: We expect to cover it up in the upcoming quarters to meet our medium -term target of scaling this up to over 7 lakh metric tonnes per annum by FY 2028, in line with our focus on building a larger and more diversified recycling platform.

items.statement: Total CAPEX of Rs. 1,225 crores earmarked through FY2028
items.quote: We have earmarked a total CAPEX of Rs. 1,225 crores through FY 2028.

items.statement: Targeting volume CAGR over 25%, profitability growth above 35%, ROIC exceeding 25%, non-lead revenue share 30%, renewable energy 30%, energy intensity reduction over 10% by Vision 2029
items.quote: The company is targeting strong growth metrics, including a volume CAGR of over 25%, profitability growth above 35% and ROIC exceeding 25%, alongside increasing the non -lead segment's contribution to 30% of revenue, raising renewable energy usage to 30% and reducing energy intensity by over 10%.

items.statement: Incurred CAPEX of about Rs. 1,255 crores in first nine months of FY2026
items.quote: During the first nine months of 2026, we have already incurred CAPEX of about Rs. 1,255 crores.

items.statement: Expect to cross Rs. 200 crores CAPEX for full FY2026
items.quote: we have already done a CAPEX of around Rs. 125 crores till now. And we are expecting it to cross Rs. 200 crores by Q4. So, we will meet the target that we set for FY 2026 for capacity expansion.

items.statement: Plan to spend approximately Rs. 1,200 crores in next two to three years for CAPEX and Rs. 1,500 crores for working capital
items.value: Rs. 1,200 crores CAPEX, Rs. 1,500 crores working capital
items.quote: But overall on the funding side we plan to spend approximately Rs. 1,200 crores in the next two years to three years for CAPEX and approximately Rs. 1,500 crores will be needed for working capital.

items.statement: Installed capacity now at about 3.40 lakh metric tonnes per annum
items.quote: installed capacity now at about 3.40 lakh metric tonnes per annum.

items.statement: Mundra lead capacity expansion of 80,000 metric tonnes per annum targeted for completion by Q4 FY2026
items.quote: At Mundra, lead capacity expansion of 80,000 metric tonnes per annum is targeted for completion by Q4 FY 2026.

items.statement: Jaipur lead capacity expansion up to 45,000 metric tonnes per annum targeted for completion by Q4 FY2026
items.quote: At Jaipur, lead capacity expansion up to 45,000 metric tonnes per annum is targeted for completion by Q4 FY 2026.

items.statement: Mundra rubber project slated for commissioning in Q1 FY2027, revenues expected from Q2 FY2027
items.quote: The Mundra rubber project is slated for commissioning in Q1 FY 2027, with revenues expected to begin flowing from Q2 FY 2027, aided by stabilization of the Romania operations as well.

items.statement: Lithium-ion consent to operate expected in next couple of days, likely in Q4 FY2026
items.quote: Lithium-ion is not functional right now. It will probably come in this quarter. The consent to operate for lithium -ion is also expected to come in the next couple of days probably, it is in process.

items.statement: Overseas capacity utilization at around 65%, India capacity utilization over 90%
items.quote: currently , if you look at our overseas capacity utilizations, it is at around 65%.

items.statement: Q3 FY2026 volumes: lead 46,269 tonnes, aluminum 3,550 tonnes, plastic 3,160 tonnes, total 52,982 tonnes
items.quote: So, the lead total quantity that we sold in lead is around 46,269 tonnes. We sold around 3,500 tonnes of aluminum, 3,550 tonnes and 3,160 tonnes of plastic scrap. So, total overall numbers are 52,982 tonnes.

items.statement: Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA Rs. 116 crores, up 13% YoY and 4% QoQ, margin 11.41%+
items.quote: In Q3 FY 2025 - 2026, revenue remained flat on both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis at Rs. 1,017 crores. Adjusted EBITDA stood at Rs. 116 crores, up 13% year -on-year and 4% quarter-on-quarter. With margins remaining strong at 11.41% plus

items.statement: Lead, aluminum, plastic EBITDA per metric tonne at Rs. 23,000, Rs. 14,215, Rs. 10,462 respectively in Q3 FY2026
items.quote: Lead, aluminum and plastic EBITDA per metric tonnes stood at Rs. 23,000, Rs. 14,215 and Rs. 10,462 respectively.

items.statement: Guidance maintained at Rs. 19-20 per kg for lead, Rs. 14-15 for aluminum, Rs. 10-12 for plastic; long-term potential Rs. 0.5-0.75 per kg improvement by FY2028
items.value: Rs. 19-20/kg lead, Rs. 14-15/kg aluminum, Rs. 10-12/kg plastic
items.quote: you can expect what we have already mentioned that around Rs. 19 to Rs. 20 in lead, around Rs. 14 to Rs, 15 in aluminum, and plastic would give you around Rs. 10 to Rs. 12.

items.statement: Buy scrap at discount over LME prices; margin between selling and buying price remains intact when prices rise
items.quote: Because we buy scrap at a discount over the LME prices. When the prices increase, also the absolute price of the scrap increases, but the percentage of the scrap remains the same. So, the margin between the selling price and the buying price remains intact, more or less.

items.statement: Plastic segment volumes rose 55% QoQ to 3,160 metric tonnes; aluminum volumes declined due to higher metal prices causing scrap aggregators to withhold material
items.quote: The plastic segment recorded a strong rebound, with volumes rising 55% Q-on-Q to 3,160 metric tonnes. In contrast, aluminum volumes declined on both a year-on-year basis and quarter-on-quarter basis. The decline in aluminum volumes during the quarter was primarily driven by higher metal prices in the market.

items.statement: Plastic capacity utilization around 40% in 9M FY2026; targeting slow growth 8-10% for next couple of quarters then acceleration
items.quote: currently you can expect a slow growth of around 8% - 10% for the next couple of quarters and then probably we can see an increase further.

items.statement: Domestic vs overseas revenue mix in Q3: 25% domestic, 75% imported; normal mix 45% domestic, 55% imported
items.quote: So, quarter it was 25% from domestic and 75% was imported. But overall, we should be back to the normal one which is around 45% from domestic and 55% from the imported one.

items.statement: Revenue split: 72% India, 28% overseas; profit split: 76% India, 24% overseas
items.quote: just for your knowledge around 72% of the profits, revenue came from India and 28% of the profit or the revenue came from overseas. So, as per profits also 76% was from India and 24% was from overseas.

items.statement: Exide Industries not in top 10 customers currently; volumes expected to grow significantly next year
items.quote: It is not in the top 10 customers of Gravita currently.

items.statement: Regulatory environment favorable; stronger enforcement of BWMR and EPR frameworks enhancing accountability and domestic scrap availability
items.quote: The regulatory environment remains favorable for organized recyclers. Stronger enforcement of the BWMR and EPR frameworks has enhanced accountability across producers, recyclers, and collection agencies, leading to more efficient collection channels, reduced l eakages to the unorganized sector, and improved traceability.

items.statement: NITI Aayog recommended strengthening EPR process, linking GSTN data, framing collection and audit rules; expects amendments by April 1, 2026
items.quote: yesterday NITI Aayog has recommended a few recommendations strengthening the EPR process, strengthening the portal and linking of all data from GSTN portal and there are further collection rules are also being framed. So, we are hopeful that by April 1st, 2026 these rules will be amended or modified and SOP will be created for collection site in battery-based management rule and also audit rules a

items.statement: MCX aluminum alloy trading expected by Q1 FY2027; regulatory constraints cleared, now MCX business decision
items.quote: I am hopeful in FY 2026 it should come by Q1 of FY 2026 - 2027.

items.statement: Lead 100% hedged, no bottom-line impact from price fluctuations; aluminum hedging difficult due to ADC-12 not traded on exchanges
items.quote: as far as lead is concerned, we are totally hedged. So, there will be no impact of these fluctuations on lead. Both in, I mean, it may have impact on the top line, but there would be no impact on the bottom line beca use we go 100% hedged in lead. Aluminum, we are looking at some options to hedge . But currently, because we do ADC -12, which is not traded on any of the exchanges, so we find it a l

items.statement: Plan to raise some debt to limited extent; growth fully funded from internal accruals, QIP liquidity, and limited debt
items.quote: And additionally, we may take some debt to a limited extent where we plan to raise some debt up to within some limits. So, we are fully competent of taking this growth, fully funded from internal accruals and liquidity we have.

items.statement: Gravita Netherlands BV approved additional investment in Gravita Europe S.R.L, acquiring 3.5 lakh shares (15% stake), increasing shareholding from 80% to 95%
items.quote: Gravita Netherlands BV, our step -down subsidiary, has approved an additional investment in Gravita Europe S.R.L through the acquisition of 3.5 lakh shares, representing a 15% stake. Post this transaction, GNBV's shareholding in Gravita Europe S.R.L will increase from 80% to 95%, further strengthening our presence in the European market.

items.statement: New labor law impact estimated at Rs. 4.2 crores annually (Rs. 3.5 crores prior years, Rs. 60-70 lakhs for 9M FY2026)
items.quote: In this year, the total impact of this amount was approximately Rs. 4.2 crores, out of which Rs. 3.5 crores was pertaining to previous years and roughly Rs. 60 lakhs to Rs. 70 lakhs was pertaining to these nine months.

items.statement: Capacity expansion delays due to government licensing delays in Gujarat (Vibrant Gujarat event); expect licenses for Phagi and Mundra plants by end January or February
items.quote: there is some delays from the government authorities in giving the license to operate. Because of various reasons in Gujarat, because of this vibrant Gujarat into place, some of the government official s are not regularly attending the offices right now. So, we are expecting this to probably happen in either month end of January or maximum in Feb itself.

items.statement: Aluminum scrap availability temporarily tightened due to price increases causing aggregators to withhold material; expect normalization as prices stabilize
items.quote: In such periods, scrap aggregators typically withhold material in anticipation of further price increases, which temporarily tightens scrap availability. This led to lower procurement and consequentially reduced processing volumes during the quarter. As pr ices stabilize and scrap flow normalizes, procurement is expected to improve, supporting a recovery in aluminum volumes in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Target RoA of 2.8%-3.0% by Q4FY27
items.quote: I would like to reiterate that we continue to work towards achieving our Lakshya 2026 target of 2.8%-3.0% RoA in Q4FY27.

items.statement: Credit cost guided to 2-2.2% corridor by Q4FY27
items.quote: This trajectory of paring of credit cost will culminate in the achievement of the guided 2-2.2% corridor by Q4FY27.

items.statement: NIMs+Fees guidance corridor of 10% to 10.5%
items.quote: our continuous guidance has been that we will put the NIMs and Fees -- we will try to deliver the NIMs and Fees in the corridor of 10% to 10.5%.

items.statement: Secured to unsecured loan mix target of 60:40
items.quote: Our stated objective is to have the secured, unsecured ratio at 60:40. So that is our stated objective.

items.statement: MFI steady state growth targeted at 15-20%
items.quote: We will be happy to -- happy if we hit somewhere between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Gold Loan branches target of 330+ by end of FY26
items.quote: By the end of FY26, we plan on establishing a distribution strength of 330+ gold loan branches.

items.statement: Project Cyclops full roll-out in Personal Loans by end of Q4FY26
items.quote: In line with our earlier guidance Project Cyclops is now implemented in our Personal Loan business and will complete a full roll-out by end of Q4FY26.

items.statement: Project Nostradamus full stack implementation in Two-Wheeler by March 2026 and in Personal Loan and RBF in H1FY27
items.quote: Full stack Project Nostradamus implementation will be completed in the Two-Wheeler business by March 2026 and will be implemented in Personal Loan and Rural Business Finance vertical in H1FY27.

items.statement: Security receipts resolution expected over next 2-3 years
items.quote: About ₹ 5,000 Cr is sitting on our balance sheet right now. And the way we have guided is that it will take us anywhere between the next 2 to 3 years for a full resolution of that, right.

items.statement: Lakshya 31 plans to be announced in April quarter (Q1FY27)
items.quote: We will announce our Lakshya 31 plans in the April quarter. So as part of our April quarterly results, we will also announce the Lakshya 31 plans.

items.statement: Urban consumption accelerated in Q3FY26 due to GST 2.0 reforms and supply side de-bottlenecking
items.quote: Urban consumption demonstrated strong acceleration in Q3FY26 owing to the GST 2.0 reforms and supply side de-bottlenecking was able to cater to the increased demand.

items.statement: Microfinance collection efficiency improved with Karnataka monthly collection efficiency up 38 bps to 99.56% and pan-India 0 DPD up 20 bps to 99.70%
items.quote: The quarter saw a 38 bps improvement in Karnataka monthly collection efficiency, which increased from 99.18% in September'25 to 99.56% in December'25. The pan India '0 DPD' collection efficiency improved 20 bps to 99.70% from 99.50% during the previous quarter.

items.statement: Consol NIMs+Fees improved 19 bps QoQ to 10.41% driven by stable yields, lower cost of borrowings, and lower NPA reversals
items.quote: Consol NIMs + Fees for the quarter improves 19 bps QoQ to 10.41% from 10.22% in Q2FY26. This has been contributed by stable yields & cost of borrowings reduction due to Treasury efficiencies which resulted in the lowest ever Weighted Average Cost of Borrowing (WACB) at 7.25%

items.statement: WACB at lowest ever 7.25% with further rate transmission expected
items.quote: We do believe that the full transmission of the current round of rate cut has still not even been transferred. So there remains a possibility of some more rate transmission this particular quarter, right.

items.statement: Retail disbursements highest ever at ₹22,701 Cr, up 49% YoY and 20% QoQ; Retail book at ₹1,11,990 Cr, up 21% YoY and 7% QoQ
items.quote: This has led to the retail book growing to ₹ 1,11,990 Cr at the end of this quarter, reflecting a growth of 21% YoY and a RoA of 2.37%, 2.31% for Q3FY26 after the impact of exceptional items, reflecting a growth of 10 bps YoY.

items.statement: Gold Loan disbursements ₹1,408 Cr, up 43% QoQ; book at ₹1,738 Cr, up 18% QoQ
items.quote: In the Gold Loan business, quarterly disbursements stood at ₹ 1,408 Cr up by 43% QoQ and the closing book stood at ₹ 1,738 Cr at the end of third quarter, up by 18% QoQ.

items.statement: Personal Loans disbursements ₹3,574 Cr, up 118% YoY and 23% QoQ; book at ₹12,810 Cr, up 64% YoY and 18% QoQ
items.quote: In the Personal Loans business, we achieved a quarterly disbursement of ₹ 3,574 Cr. This translated into a growth of 118% YoY and 23% QoQ with the book size reaching ₹ 12,810 Cr, an increase of 64% YoY and 18% QoQ, attributed to the successful scale-up of big tech partnerships.

items.statement: Farmer Finance disbursements ₹2,783 Cr, up 12% YoY and 68% QoQ; book at ₹16,671 Cr, up 11% YoY and 5% QoQ
items.quote: In the Farmer Finance vertical, quarterly disbursements stood at ₹ 2,783 Cr in third quarter, up 12% YoY and 68% QoQ. The book size reached ₹ 16,671 Cr, reflecting a growth rate of 11% YoY and 5% QoQ.

items.statement: Home Loans & LAP disbursements ₹2,879 Cr, up 16% YoY and 6% QoQ; book at ₹28,682 Cr, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ
items.quote: Moving on to Housing, we achieved quarterly disbursements of ₹ 2,879 Cr, up 16% YoY and a growth of 6% QoQ, with the book size at ₹ 28,682 Cr, an increase of 22% YoY and 5% QoQ.

items.statement: SME Finance disbursements ₹1,550 Cr, up 24% YoY and 6% QoQ; book at ₹7,946 Cr, up 37% YoY and 6% QoQ
items.quote: In the SME business, quarterly disbursements stood at ₹ 1,550 Cr, up 24% YoY and 6% QoQ. The book stood at ₹ 7,946 Cr, up 37% YoY and 6% QoQ.

items.statement: Credit cost moderated to 2.83% (2.74% ex one-time co-borrower provision of ₹23 Cr), down 15 bps QoQ and 8 bps YoY
items.quote: The credit cost this quarter has moderated from 2.98%, before macro-prudential provision utilization, in Q2FY26 to 2.83% in Q3FY26, a reduction of 15 bps QoQ and 8 bps YoY. It is to be noted that this includes a one-time charge of ₹ 23 Cr on certain co-borrower provisions. Excluding this one-time impact the core credit cost from operations came in at 2.74%, a 24 bps reduction on QoQ basis.

items.statement: Two-Wheeler Net Non-Starter down to 0.41% from 2.36% YoY; Farm Net Non-Starter down to ~0.4% from ~1.5% YoY
items.quote: The Net Non-Starter (NNS) for the Two-Wheeler portfolio went down from 2.36% in Dec'24 to 0.41% in Dec'25 and in the Farm business the NNS reduced from ~1.50% in Dec'24 to ~0.4% (Project Cyclops) in Dec'25.

items.statement: Slippages reduced by ~₹160 Cr QoQ in Q2 and further ~₹190-200 Cr QoQ in Q3
items.quote: If you look at the slippages between first and the second quarter, the slippages were lower by about ₹ 160 Cr. Between Q2 and Q3, the slippages have come down further by about ₹ 190 Cr to ₹ 200 Cr.

items.statement: Investing in technology, new branches for Gold Loan, Rural LAP, and Sampoorna network; cost-to-income guided at ~40% range
items.quote: We are invest ing in technology. We are investing in setting up new branches. Gold Loan, we are setting up 1 branch a day. We also are setting up branches to do Rural LAP. We have Sampoorna branches coming into play. So, the investments will continue to happen

items.statement: Yields being optimized upwards across Two-Wheeler, SME, Personal Loans; Mortgage yields pass on rate cuts
items.quote: We are trying to optimize yields upwards for our Two-Wheeler business. We are trying to optimize yield upwards for our SME business. We are trying to optimize yield upwards for our Personal Loans business.

items.statement: High-yielding secured businesses (Gold Loan, Micro LAP, SME) to compensate for lower MFI growth
items.quote: So overall, whatever -- the question on that is that whatever sort of growth -- sort of missing part of the jigsaw that we might get from our MFI business, we will try to cover it up by our high-yield secured businesses as much.

items.statement: Onboarded 7.0 lakh new customers in Q3, up from 5.9 lakh in Q2
items.quote: Leveraging these tailwinds, we successfully onboarded 7.0 lakh new customers up from 5.9 lakh last quarter.

items.statement: 87%+ of Two-Wheeler disbursements in Dec'25 to Prime segment customers vs 53% in Mar'24
items.quote: Notably, 87%+ of Two-Wheeler disbursements in Dec'25 were to customers from the Prime segment as against 53% for the month of March'24.

items.statement: RBI inspection advised provisioning for co-borrower exposures across businesses; led to ₹23 Cr one-time charge
items.quote: post our RBI interaction at the time of inspection, we were advised that we should take into account all such accounts as well. So, the cumulative effect of this has been about ₹ 23-odd Cr.

items.statement: RBI prescribed ECL for banks creating level playing field; will revisit ECL models starting now
items.quote: thankfully, even RBI has prescribed the ECL to be made applicable to banks. Now everyone will be on the same level playing field. And we will also perhaps get some clarity from the regulatory side, how things are applying to banks.

items.statement: Macro-prudential provisions to be rebuilt for overall unsecured assets (not just MFI) using SR resolution gains and CGFMU guarantees
items.quote: This time, when we build it, we will build it for the overall unsecured asset business of L&T Finance, right. So that will be our strategy. So as and when we get that window of opportunity to build those provisions, we will definitely build those provisions.

items.statement: PCR may trend down towards industry levels (50-55%) as portfolio quality improves and crises subside
items.quote: if at all, we have to take a call, it will be on slightly lowering it rather than increasing it from here. On the macro..

items.statement: RoA at 2.31% (2.37% pre-exceptional) without macro-prudential provision usage; RoE at 11.07%
items.quote: Consol RoA after one-time exceptional item stands at 2.31%, up 4 bps YoY and down 10 bps QoQ. Consol RoE at 11.07%, up 86 bps YoY and down 26 bps QoQ.

items.statement: Retailisation at 98% maintained since Q1FY26
items.quote: We achieved a Retailisation of 98% in Q1FY26 which has remained at the same level in Q3FY26.

items.statement: Upgraded sales volume growth guidance to 20% for Q4 FY26 and FY27, with EBITDA guidance of almost INR5,500 per ton
items.quote: Hence, we are upgrading our sales volume growth guidance of 20% for 4QFY26 and FY27, with the EBITDA guidance of almost INR5,500 per ton.

items.statement: Reiterated 20% volume growth for Q4 FY26 and full year FY27 over FY26
items.quote: So just to reiterate that we are seeing 20% volume growth for Q4 FY '26 and for the full year FY '27 over FY '26.

items.statement: Targeting FY26 volume of around 3.55 million tons with Q4 between 10-11 lakh tons
items.quote: So, rightly you can say that this year we will do around 3.55 million tons, which we are targeting in Q4 between 10-11 lakh tons.

items.statement: Targeting INR1,700-1,800 crores EBITDA for FY26, aiming to cross INR1,900 crores
items.quote: The first guideline, which we have given of INR1,700 crores this year and INR1,800 crores, there is no doubt. We are targeting that we should cross INR1,900 crores.

items.statement: Maintaining 20% volume growth rate for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: And as far as the volume growth for FY'28, so the guidance is that we should continue -- 20%, we should maintain 20% growth rate for FY'27 and FY'28.

items.statement: Successfully tested 5 million ton capacity achieving almost 90% utilization in December 2025
items.quote: So we have successfully tested our 5 million ton capacity, achieving almost 90% utilization in December 2025.

items.statement: Aggressively pursuing capacity expansion to 8 million tons from current 5 million tons in next 2 years via 4 greenfield projects and 1 brownfield project
items.quote: And at the same time, we are aggressively pursuing capacity expansion to 8 million tons from current 5 million tons in next 2 years, which is a mix of 4 greenfield projects; 2 being in East India, 1 in South India and 1 in West India, 1 being the brownfield project in Raipur for value-added products.

items.statement: Identified 1 million ton expansion through debottlenecking by replacing existing mills with faster modernized mills
items.quote: And very interestingly, we identified a 1 million ton expansion through debottlenecking, wherein we identified existing mills that could be replaced with much faster, modernized mills, which will expand our ROCE to the next level because the investment there will be very, very minimal.

items.statement: Total investment to expand capacity from 5 to 8 million tons is around INR1,500 crores funded from internal cash flows over next 2 years
items.quote: So total investment to expand our capacity from 5 million to 8 million tons is around INR1,500 crores, and this will be funded from internal cash flows over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Vision of 10 million tons capacity by 2030 with additional 2 million tons in super specialty segment via JVs with Japanese, Korean, European and American companies
items.quote: Now one thing which, obviously, we will be talking much more about over our earnings call is the additional 2 million tons to achieve our vision of 10 million tons of capacity by 2030. This incremental 2 million tons will be in the super specialty segment, wherein we are identifying various targets worldwide for the JVs with Japanese, Korean, and European and American companies to offer products i

items.statement: Greenfield plus brownfield expansion requires INR1,300 crores and debottlenecking expansion requires INR200 crores
items.value: INR1,300 crores greenfield+brownfield; INR200 crores debottlenecking
items.quote: And the greenfield plus brownfield expansion will require INR1,300 crores, and debottlenecking expansion will require INR200 crores.

items.statement: 9-month EBITDA per ton above INR5,000 surpassing Q1 guidance; strategy of pricing premiumization and SG brand launch expanded EBITDA spreads
items.quote: And the 9-month EBITDA per ton is above INR5,000, surpassing our own guidance given on the quarter 1 earnings call. So our strategy of pricing premiumization by leveraging APL Apollo brand has worked excellently to expand our EBITDA spreads, and the launch of SG brand in the base category worked well to compete with the smaller players in the structural steel tube segment and the sponge iron pipe

items.statement: INR3,000-4,000 per ton premium for APL Apollo-branded products is now the new normal
items.quote: It's been 12 months since we increased the selling price for APL Apollo-branded products, which suggests the markets have accepted our brand equity, and the INR3,000 to INR4,000 per ton premium for APL Apollo-branded products is now the new normal for the structural steel tube segment.

items.statement: Apollo brand targeting INR7,000 EBITDA/ton; Dubai plant targeting INR7,000; roofing targeting INR7,000; Scaff and SG Premium at INR1,500-2,000; blended average close to INR6,000/ton at 370,000 tons/month
items.value: INR7,000/ton Apollo; INR7,000 Dubai; INR7,000 roofing; INR1,500-2,000 Scaff/SG; INR6,000 blended
items.quote: In Apollo, we are targeting 7,000, in Dubai, we will easily reach INR7,000 easily. From Q4, we have no problem at all. Even in roofing, we will get a beta of around INR7,000. In Scaff and SG Premium, our EBITDA is around INR1,500 to INR2,000. So, if we calculate the total average, it is close to INR6,000 per ton. In 3,70,000 tons.

items.statement: Inventory days currently 30-plus targeting 20-day range; surplus cash could reach INR1,500 crores in Q4 to match current liabilities and become liability-free
items.value: 30+ days inventory targeting 20 days; INR1,500 crores surplus cash
items.quote: So we are seeing a lot of opportunities to rationalize the inventory days, which right now is 30-plus. It will be in our 20-day range. And with the strong Q4, our surplus cash on the balance sheet could be INR1,500 crores, which was always the target that we would have as much cash on our books to match our current liabilities, so that we can be a liability-free company.

items.statement: Increasing minimum dividend payout policy from 20% to 25%
items.quote: We're going to increase some dividend payout. Surely, no doubt. Like right now, we are -- we achieved our targets, but we are thinking. So right now, we are going with minimum 20% of dividend payout policy. We increased to 25% minimum.

items.statement: Expect tax rate around 20% when Dubai and Raipur plants at peak contribution; Raipur started 2018 under tax benefit scheme
items.quote: So, Darshan, both Dubai and Raipur plants are at a low tax rate because Raipur, we started in 2018 under that scheme when the government gave tax benefits for the new ventures. So eventually, we expect our tax rate to be around 20%, when the contribution from both Dubai and Raipur will be at its peak

items.statement: Safeguard duty in December had no impact except raw material price increase which was fully passed on
items.quote: No impact on Apollo, except the fact that our raw material prices went up, but that is fully passed on. So no impact as such.

items.statement: Revenue split ~30% OEM (large furniture/kitchen/wardrobe makers) and ~70% retail/dealer network; 25,000+ contractors on Sirca Parivar Pro app driving stickiness
items.quote: Our revenue is balanced across OEM segment, which contributes to about 30%, where our key clients includes the large and organized furniture, kitchen, and wardrobe manufacturers. The retail where we are scaling through distribution expansion and the studios.

items.statement: Holds ~15% share in high-quality PU segment, ~4-4.5% in total wood coatings; differentiates via technical product expertise, architect/contractor influence, Italian brand positioning, and service capability
items.quote: We are almost, you know, this year we'll be at 15% market share. But if we talk about the total market size, you know, we are still small and holds about a 4, 4.5% market share, because the total market size of wood coatings includes the NC, the melamine, the 1K, the economical PU, the 2K PU, but currently we exist only in the high-quality wood coatings.

items.statement: Actively evaluating another acquisition in coatings space (metal coatings) to complete product portfolio; Wembley and Welcome acquisitions already integrated
items.quote: And about the acquisition, yes, company has been eyeing another acquisition, which is under discussion for last couple of quarters, but nothing concrete as of now, but we expect to complete this acquisition, which is, again, in the coding space, which will complete our productivity and, you know, help Sirca to even come out stronger and, you know, reach to its long-term goals.

items.statement: Borrowings at Rs 36 cr with no plans to increase; expected to remain constant
items.quote: So, I think we don't have any plans to increase it, it should remain constant.

items.statement: Volume growth exceeded value growth in localized products due to 20% ASP reduction from import substitution (customs duty, freight savings) passed to market
items.quote: the average selling price of those products has gone down by 20%, so the average selling price of those products earlier were 550. After we started producing it in India, we had saved on the custom duties, the freight, even the cost of production was gone down, and even after increasing the gross margins and increasing our marketing budget, we were able to pass on the benefits to the market.

items.statement: Exports growing with strategic initiatives; Sirca Italy partnership until 2041 supports global credibility and product pipeline
items.quote: Its extensive distribution network spans around over 4,000 dealers and 900 -plus OEM clients across India, with strategic initiatives including Wembley integration and a long-term technology partnership with Sirca S.P.A. until 2041, the company is well-positioned to benefit from the India's growing furniture and interior decor market.

items.statement: Hired experienced team from paint/commodity companies for South expansion (4 new branches: Hyderabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Kerala); team onboard 6-8 months, momentum picking up
items.quote: Recently, we have opened 4 branches in the South India and taken over a very experienced team from different, you know, different paint companies also, and other commodity -based companies. So, the team is on board for last 6 to 8 months, the depots from Hyderabad to Bangalore to Chennai to Kerala are now open, and the momentum has started to pick.

items.statement: Near-term headwinds: extended monsoons, GST changes, early festive season impacting retail/project timelines; December quarter tough due to spray paint ban
items.quote: as we progress through the second half of the year, environment has Short-term challenges like extended monsoons, the GST changes, and early festive season impacting retail and project timelines.

items.statement: Order book grew to INR23.5 billion with Q3 intake of INR387 crores and book-to-bill of 1.3x; YTD book-to-bill 1.56x
items.quote: Our order book remains healthy at INR23.5 billion, reflecting a Q-o-Q increase of INR583 million. This marks the third consecutive quarter of positive momentum driven by steady order intake.

items.statement: New order intake of INR387 crores in Q3 with book-to-bill ratio of 1.3x; YTD book-to-bill 1.56x
items.quote: The new wins in this quarter, combined with strong repeat business, resulted in a healthy order intake of INR387 crores. This translates into a book-to-bill ratio of 1.3 for the quarter.

items.statement: Expect positive year-over-year revenue growth in Q4 FY26 and substantial growth in FY27, though no specific guidance given
items.quote: Yes, so we see, as of now today, the plans which we have it, I think we are seeing a positive year-over-year. And I'm confident that we'll be there by end of this Q4, so we'll be seeing a positive growth when compared to year-over-year.

items.statement: FY27 will be far better than FY26 with positive growth; no specific guidance provided yet
items.quote: FY '27 is also going to be a positive growth. I mean on a positive, it is going to be substantial, but we are not giving any guidance right now. But we are working out on the numbers. FY '27 is going to be far, far better than FY '26.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin expanded to 10.2% in Q3 (+207 bps YoY); double-digit margins sustained with further upside expected from operating leverage
items.quote: However, in margin terms, we delivered a healthy 10.2% EBITDA, at 207 basis points higher year-on-year, which is supported by favorable revenue mix and strong operational and supply chain efficiencies.

items.statement: Margins expected to sustain in 10% range in Q4 and improve further in FY27 despite sales team investments
items.quote: Further and more importantly, the margins will sustain in the 10% range. And to Rajendra's point, in spite of the investments that we're making in sales leadership, etcetera, we're still very confident based on not only the order book that we've built it, but also the kind of industries that we're going after, etcetera.

items.statement: Revenue soft in Q3 due to customer-specific issues from year-end holidays and tariff uncertainty; push-outs on track to ship in Q4
items.quote: Our revenue for the quarter has been soft. This is due to some customer-specific issues that were caused by year-end holiday period and the tariff-related uncertainty.

items.statement: Customers in wait-and-watch mode on tariffs; push-outs already on track to ship in current quarter with no prolonged impact expected
items.quote: A number of our customers have been in a wait-and-watch mode to ensure or to understand how the tariff situation settles before they start picking up more inventory. These push-outs already are on track to ship in the current quarter, and we do not expect any prolonged impact.

items.statement: Build-to-spec revenue at 6-7% in FY26, expected to reach double-digit in FY27; both industry mix and B2S to drive margin expansion
items.quote: The build-to-spec revenue is about 6% to 7% in the current year, and we expect to go to double-digit in the next year.

items.statement: Industry mix more balanced with healthy contributions from aerospace, industrial, medical; PCBA dominates but box build and value-added services growing
items.quote: With the large defense order behind us, we are seeing healthy contributions from aerospace, industrial and medical segment. This shift is driven by strong sales effort towards diversification and improved operational capabilities.

items.statement: Added 2 new logos in Q3: medical (battery management systems) and industrial (high-precision electrical motor controls); more strategic opportunities in advanced stages for Q4
items.quote: We added 2 new logos in this quarter. The first one is in the medical sector, focused on battery management systems for medical applications; the second is in the industrial segment, where we are supporting high-precision electrical motor controls.

items.statement: 4 anchor customers involving Cyient DLM in next-gen product development (2 transportation, 1 industrial, 1 defense); revenues expected within 2 years, meaningful contribution from FY28
items.quote: Specific to this quarter, 4 of our anchor customers are currently involving us in developing their next-generation products, 2 from transportation, 1 from industrial and 1 from defense. We expect revenues from these programs to begin within 2 years, supported by healthy gross margins and higher volumes.

items.statement: Regular capex 1-2% of revenue; can deploy additional capex quickly (3-6 months) using existing land/infrastructure; IPO proceeds capex utilization at 15.4% as of Dec 2025
items.quote: In terms of the capex, what we have is a regular capex and maintenance, which we continue to do, which is anywhere between 1% to 2% of the revenues, which we'll do it. And if there are any specific customers who look for further capex or an additional line or any custom-specific requirement, we have enough dry powder, which we talked about, and we can do it in a pretty quick time, okay?

items.statement: 7 PCBA lines globally; capacity utilization at 50-60%; sufficient capacity for growth with operating leverage potential
items.quote: It's suffice to say that we have sufficient capacity. And in terms of our capacity utilization, it's about 50% to 60%. So we have substantial capacity i n what we are delivering it, and we are able to deliver the double -digit

items.statement: Net working capital temporarily elevated due to inventory buildup (DIO up) for Q4 shipments and customer shipment delays; expected to normalize by end of Q4
items.quote: DIO inventory is elevated due to customer-specific shipment delays in Q3 and inventory buildup for Q4 shipments. It is expected to ease out by the year-end.

items.statement: Net cash positive balance sheet; can leverage up to INR350-400 crores additional working capital; dry powder for acquisitions and capex
items.quote: From a balance sheet perspective, we are heavily leveraged. We are net cash positive. So we have ability to go up to, from a pure working capital perspective, another INR350 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: IPO proceeds utilization at 93.2% as of Dec 2025; working capital utilization 97.2%, capex utilization 15.4%
items.quote: As of December 2025, total utilization stands at 93.2%. Working capital utilization stands at 97.2%, while capex utilization is 15.4%, with the balance to be deployed as planned in the coming quarters.

items.statement: M&A evaluation expense of $17.75M for international acquisition that did not close; terms did not fit expectations; continue scouting for organic and inorganic opportunities
items.quote: The first one-off relates to M&A evaluation expenses amounting to $17.75 million. We incurred this expense to evaluate a deal that did not go through, and hence, we have taken the hit in this quarter.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic growth in Europe and for capabilities; acquired Altek ~1.5 years ago; continue scouting for geography and capability acquisitions
items.quote: We are looking for both organic and inorganic growth, and we continue to be scouting for opportunities. We acquired Altek 1.5 years back and -- sorry, a year back. And there are -- continuing work to look at acquisitions more from a geography and capabilities perspective.

items.statement: US tariff impact small in Q3; 4 mitigation options presented to customers; some adopted; no major challenge expected unless tariffs increase further
items.quote: I mean, so in terms of the U.S. tariff impact in the Q3 is not a huge, okay? It is a small number in terms of the number, if you look at it. But when -- and coming to the options, whatever we have, I think the percentage of the revenues, what we are doing it, I think the options which I said earlier, we have closer to 4 options which we have and which we ar e -- which we have already given it to o

items.statement: Strengthening sales team across geographies; key resources onboarded in Q3 with more additions planned in Q4 to complete optimal sales team
items.quote: We are building a stronger sales team across key geographies and reinforcing our cross-functional alignment so that sales, engineering, program management and operations work as one integrated unit.

items.statement: New CFO R.M. Subramanian joined; first investor call as CFO of Cyient DLM
items.quote: I would also take this opportunity to welcome RMS to Cyient and also to state that this is his first investor call as the CFO of Cyient DLM.

items.statement: Book-to-bill ratio above 1 for third consecutive quarter (1.3x in Q3, 1.56x YTD); strong revenue visibility indicator
items.quote: Our book-to-bill ratio for the quarter is above 1 for the third consecutive quarter. This underscores the sustained demand environment and the effectiveness of our commercial strategy.

items.statement: New wage code one-time impact of INR16.3M expensed in Q3; M&A evaluation expense of $17.75M also one-off; both excluded from normalized margins
items.quote: The second one is the wage impact totaling to INR16.3 million, resulting from the new wage code brought in by the Government of India. Both these expenses are exceptional one-off in nature and not reflective of normal business run rate.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty caused customer push-outs in Q3; mitigation options deployed; risk reduces if tariffs don't increase further
items.quote: A number of our customers have been in a wait-and-watch mode to ensure or to understand how the tariff situation settles before they start picking up more inventory.

items.statement: Recognized as Best Performer in Electronic Hardware Exports by STPI for FY24-25; received risk mitigation award from key aerospace customer
items.quote: We were recognized as the Best Performer in Electronic Hardware Exports by the Software Technologies Parks of India for FY '24-'25. This is a strong external valida tion of our quality, delivery and manufacturing maturity

items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue growth guidance lowered to ~15% from earlier 15-18% range
items.quote: On the full year side, what we have initially guided is around 15% to 18%, while 18% is still the target. I think after seeing a quarter 3 performance, we wanted to be giving you a conservative approach of being able to achieve the 15% kind of a number.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 15-20% driven by 5% SSG and 10% store rollout
items.quote: The goal, sir, is to actually have a 5% SSG and a 15% kind of a new store rollout addition. Both put together, it's going to be 20%. That's the goal that we internally have been working with. But to answer your question in short, yes, we should be able to target anything between 15% and 20%.

items.statement: FY27 gross margin target 42-43% and EBITDA margin target 17-18%
items.quote: on the overall front, the gross margin side, I think achieving a 42% to 43% Sai Silks ( in the next full year should be achievable. And on the EBITDA margin side as well, 17% to 18% is something that we are targeting for the next year

items.statement: FY26 PAT growth expected ~35% YoY
items.quote: on the profitability side, I wanted to mention is th at operational leverage will kick in and almost we are expecting a 35% jump in terms of profitability compared to last year's profit

items.statement: FY27 store expansion target 80,000-85,000 sq ft, up from FY26 target of 60,000-65,000 sq ft
items.quote: For the next year, we want to go a little bit more aggressively compared to this year. We have a strong Sai Silks ( store expansion plan, and we wanted to extend the current target from 65,000 to almost like about close to 80,000 to 85,000 square feet

items.statement: Capex per sq ft INR 4,000-5,500 plus working capital INR 8,000-9,000 per sq ft, total ~INR 12,000-15,000 per sq ft
items.quote: If we are implementing, say, around 75,000 to 80,000 square feet then for that, we would be requiring at the rate of INR4,000 to 5500 per capex and about INR8,000 to INR9,000 per working capital, we should be requiring in the range of INR 12,000 to INR 15,000 per square feet, including working capital, which entail approximately INR100 crores plus or minus for the year.

items.statement: Added 20,500 sq ft in Q3 FY26; 9M FY26 added 11 stores totalling 54,500 sq ft; total footprint 7.7 lakh sq ft as of Dec 31
items.quote: During the 9-month period ending December 31, the company added 11 stores with a cumulative retail space added to be 54,500 square feet and are well aligned to meet this year's target plan of opening a desired retail area in stores. As of December 31, the total company's retail footprint stood at 7.7 lakh square feet of total retail area.

items.statement: FY27 expansion to include Maharashtra (Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur) and Kerala; Varamahalakshmi-led with Valli support
items.quote: The markets where we wanted to look at is both on the current 4 states as well as into the newer territories. As we speak, we are exploring newer markets in terms of Maharashtra and Kerala as well. Very soon, we'll start expanding our store presence across the other areas as well. The format that we choose to expand is basically going to be majorly driven through Varamahalakshmi-led expansion stra

items.statement: Q3 FY26 demand moderated due to Dasara shifting to Q2; consumer spending occasion-driven and value-conscious
items.quote: During the quarter 3 FY 2025-26, the Indian ethnic apparel retail market experienced moderated demand, primarily influenced by the shift in the festive calendar. Dasara, which contributed meaningfully towards the footfalls of Q3 in the previous year, occurred earlier and fell into Q2 during the current financial year.

items.statement: FY27 wedding dates up ~10% vs FY26, well distributed from April to July with no breaks
items.quote: Compared to this financial year, next financial year wedding dates are more by 10 percent. So last year to this year, it's already increased. And compared to this year to next financial year, it's even more than the current year. So it's looking very decent. And the good part, again, which is going to continue is that all these dates are not clustered or not confirmed to just any particular month

items.statement: Q3 FY26 gross margin improved 40 bps YoY to 42.2% driven by pricing discipline and product mix
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter 3 improved 40 basis points Y-o-Y, increasing to 42.2% compared to 41.8% corresponding last quarter. This was driven by pricing discipline and improved product mix.

items.statement: 9M FY26 PAT margin 8.77% vs 6.7% YoY, up ~200 bps from operational leverage and cost discipline
items.quote: On the absolute percentage basis as well, this year for the 9 -month YTD, we achieved a PAT margin of about 8.77 percentage compared to the last year's PAT percentage of about 6.7 percentage, which is a 200 basi s point increase, reflecting improved operational leverage, better cost discipline and absorption and enhanced operational efficiencies across the business

items.statement: Advertising & business promotion spend target <4% of sales (advertising alone <2.5%) to continue in FY27
items.quote: On the absolute advertisement expenditure, our internal goal is 2.5%. That's where our goal is. On the ADVT and business promotion expenditure, both put together, we should be able to be under 4%, 4.5% on the maximum side. But the way things are happening, we are aggressively taking a stand to keep it well under 4%.

items.statement: KLM format: sarees strong, men's & kids wear degrew in Q3 (now 12% of mix vs 15% last year); YTD KLM marginally positive SSG
items.quote: Menswear, kids wear on the overall component today stands to be around 12% overall compared to the overall structure, which is 15% last year. So that piece is shrinking. KLM as a business, majority of it still being sarees should not be a problem.

items.statement: Valli format unit economics similar to Kalamandir with lower capex and inventory; 11 stores operational, no new Valli stores in Q4
items.quote: Broadly, if I have to put Valli into perspective and give you numbers, it will be in the same range of how Kalamandir formats are currently working with reduced capex and reduced inventory levels.

items.statement: Online sales ~1-1.5% of business; online margins slightly lower than offline; no plans for third-party marketplaces (Myntra, Ajio) due to high commissions and returns
items.quote: On the online business, we have like 10% lower cost compared to the offline stores. But on the Kalamandir front, again, there's a difference. But online business in the overall aspect, if you see, it's probably 1%, 1.5% of the overall business currently. So it's still relatively a smaller pie compared to the offline section, but there's a slight lower margin, I mean, on the online business compare

items.statement: Inventory INR 770-800 cr; working capital borrowings zero; internal accruals to fund FY27 expansion; no fresh borrowing needed until H2 FY28
items.quote: Broadly, we are holding an inventory of INR770 crores to INR800 crores at this point of time where working capital borrowings are 0. So then when we are deploying these funds, i.e., when we are expanding store foot print and along with that expansion, our working capital is also met through internal resources only. So the expansion for the next year would be easily funded by the internal generatio

items.statement: IPO funds exhausted by FY26 end (funded ~1.9 lakh sq ft expansion); FY27 expansion funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Yes, this IPO money, we will be getting exhausted by this year-end FY '26. So by that time, out of IPO money, we would have completed about 1,90,000 square feet of expansion. However, during the current year and some part of the last year, we have internal generations accrued, which we are holding on in cash righ t now after liquidating the entire working capital borrowings

items.statement: Tamil Nadu Varamahalakshmi stores at INR 37,000-37,500/sq ft, potential to reach INR 45,000 by end FY27
items.quote: Tamil Nadu currently is delivering on an average around INR 37,000 to 37,500 per square feet. There is a potential for it to go up to 45,000 by the end of '27. So on staggered basis, this will deliver another 7,000 to 7,500 in the next 4, 5 quarters to come.

items.statement: New stores (last year) averaging INR 37,000-37,500/sq ft with potential INR 45,000; ~1 lakh sq ft to mature over 4-5 quarters
items.quote: The new stores that have come in last year, they are averaging around 37,000 to 37,500 with the potential of 45,000. So there is a potential of another 7,500 per square feet on approximately 1 lakh square feet. That would come over the next 4 to 5 quarters.

items.statement: Maharashtra rentals significantly higher; negotiating to fit rent-to-revenue ratios; will start with 1-2 stores to test consumer behaviour
items.quote: As a matter of fact, I think from the last quarter, we have been actively scouting for locations. It's just that the rental costs are much, much higher than the average rental that we paid down in any of these 4 states. We are actively negotiating with the landlords to ensure that it fits into our ecosystem of rent-to-revenue ratios.

items.statement: Unutilized IPO funds ~INR 22 cr for 2 warehouses; identification and transaction targeted before March 31
items.quote: Yes, we would. We have a plan to identify and put up the warehouse also because Tamil Nadu expansion is almost complete, but for about 3 to 4 possible stores hence forth. We would be implementing the warehousing implementation also. Maybe there may be a slight delay of 2 or 3 months, but the identification and transaction will be close to before 31st March.

items.statement: FY26 targets: 50% top-line growth and 100% PAT growth over FY25
items.quote: Our nine-month results are in line with or slightly ahead of our annual guidance, and we remain confident of achieving our FY26 targets of 50% of top-line growth and 100% of PAT growth over FY25.

items.statement: 46 approved ANDAs as of Dec 2025, up from 12 a year ago
items.quote: As of December 2025, we are proud to have a portfolio of 46 approved ANDAs.

items.statement: 28 approved ANDAs (100+ strengths) ready for launch; 22 molecules (50+ strengths) under development
items.quote: Apart from the existing portfolio of 18 ANDAs which have already been launched, we have 28 approved ANDAs having 100-plus strengths available for launch, and 22 more molecules involving 50-plus strengths under development.

items.statement: Acquired 75% stake in Apnar Pharma (US FDA-approved facility); remaining 25% by Q2 FY27
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have completed acquisition of 75% stake in Apnar Pharma last week. The balanced 25% is expected to be completed by Q2 of FY '27.

items.statement: Apnar Pharma expected to contribute INR120-150 crore revenue in FY27
items.quote: we are expecting about INR120 crores to INR150 crores kind of revenue from Apnar in FY '27 as we speak.

items.statement: Branded generics India: INR40-50 crore FY26; INR80+ crore FY27
items.quote: On the branded generics side of the business, we feel that we should be able to conclude this between INR40 crores and INR50 crores. And next year could be another INR80-plus crores is what we are projecting on the branded generic side.

items.statement: Emerging markets revenue target: INR170-180 crore FY27
items.quote: On emerging market side of the business, we feel we should be able to do about INR170 crores to INR180 crores, the revenue next year.

items.statement: Regulated markets mix: 55% own products / 45% CDMO-CMO in 9MFY26; expected 60/40 for FY26, 65/35 for FY27
items.quote: Mix today on the split is largely about 55% on our own product and about 45% on the CDMO, CMO side of the business. And we feel probably full year, we will have about 60% of our own product and about a 40% on the CDMO, CMO side when we conclude this year. For the next year, we feel more or less this mix will continue. Maybe our own product, we may be able to get about 65% and CDMO, CMO contributio

items.statement: US regulated business gross/EBITDA margin ~40%; own products 4-6% higher than CDMO-CMO
items.quote: CDMO, CMO is slightly lower than our own products. I said 4% to 5% or 5% to 6% lower than own products. But overall margin, gross margins , EBITDA margins are at 40% for the US-regulated business.

items.statement: Emerging markets EBITDA margin mid-teens in Q3; targeting 18-22% in FY27, higher later
items.quote: FY'27. So, next year, FY'27, we feel that margin when we get to about 18%, 20% to 22% kind of a number should stabilize and then maybe another three, four quarters, it should improve further couple of basis points.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 29% for 9MFY26; expect ~30% for full FY26
items.quote: FY '26, I think we already at 29%. So we should be a percentage more around 30% by end of the year. Blended total.

items.statement: Capex over next 2-3 years estimated at INR50-100 crore annually; US expansion deferred due to Apnar acquisition
items.quote: So, capex two to three years, I think we need, should be around INR50 crores to INR100 crores in between, depending on the requirement. Because earlier we were planning a capex in the US, but since we have got Apnar now.

items.statement: Atlanta facility expansion to 2 billion tablets likely by next year; Apnar adds immediate capacity
items.quote: So, that capacity expansion, I think it's likely to be done by next year. Now, since we already have Apnar in our fold, so we already have an extended capacity directly now.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle ~90-94 days
items.quote: I think net versus capital cycle is around 90 days, 94 days.

items.statement: Promoter warrants issued for potential INR75-100 crore infusion over 12 months for ANDA acquisitions and working capital
items.quote: Going by the growth trajectory, we worked out a situation where maybe about INR75 crores to INR100 crores could be an additional infusion required over the next 12 months, partly for new product acquisitions in terms of ANDAs or primarily for working capital margin.

items.statement: Small promoter share pledge to consolidate borrowings; no further pledging expected
items.quote: So, Viraj, there was a small pledge that happened that was largely to consolidate some of the borrowings, and it's not likely to go up any pledging whatsoever.

items.statement: Emerging markets per-unit realization ~INR2; improving with mix shift
items.quote: So we are at about close to INR2 per unit today as we speak on our emerging market manufacturing, which we feel will continue to drive up as the product mix will continue to change.

items.statement: Emerging markets: distributor-led direct exports growing; dollar revenue share to expand over 4-6 quarters as 850+ products under registration commercialize
items.quote: Because all the registrations that we are talking about today, which are we have 450 and there are 800 plus is going to come in, they are for direct exports. So our dollar revenue realization will significantly increase in the next four to six quarters.

items.statement: Seeking PIC/S approval for Chhatral facility to access Vietnam, South Africa and other mid-tier markets
items.quote: We are also in the process of obtaining PIC/S approval for our Chhatral manufacturing facility for emerging markets. This approval will enable us to expand our footprint in key mid-tier markets such as Vietnam, South Africa, and others.

items.statement: Solar plant and automation reduced other expenses to INR22 crore in Q3
items.quote: We have put up solar plant in our facility. W just saved us the energy. We have gone for certain automations. We just saved us some labor costs. So, this is the addition of so many measures what we have taken.

items.statement: FY27 PAT growth of 100% unlikely due to higher base; targeting decent top-line and slightly better bottom-line growth
items.quote: Now, once I'm at INR650 crores and maybe a INR100 plus crores kind of a PAT this year, 100 and 105, 115, whatever it comes, to expect that 100% to, you know, it's a little asking too much, but I would say a very decent top line growth and a slightly better bottom line growth is what we are targeting.

items.statement: No inventory write-offs; finished goods inventory max 15 days as production is pre-sold on confirmed purchase orders
items.quote: So, Pujan, we only manufacture basis on a confirmed purchase order that we get from our partners and our manufacturing capacities are pre-sold. So, our finished goods inventory that we carry is very less like in terms of maybe max 15 days in terms of FG inventory that we carry.

items.statement: Expects to maintain historical 40% year-on-year revenue growth for FY26
items.quote: we have been maintaining that there is a 40% growth ratio that Atlanta has always been maintaining historically. And we intend to continue with the same 40% this year. Nothing less than 40% is what we would expect.

items.statement: Order book at all-time high of INR2,451 crores as of 31st December 2025
items.quote: Our order book stands at all-time high of INR2,451 crores, as on 31st December 2025.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 order intake was INR796 crores
items.quote: Order intake during Q3 FY '26 was INR796 crores, providing strongexecution visibility over the next quarter.

items.statement: Expects quarterly order intake of approximately INR600-700 crores going forward
items.quote: Approximately INR700 crores is our quarterly intake. We expect that to be about INR600 crores quarterly intake this quarter also.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 19.4%, up 350 bps year-on-year
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded to 19.4% from 15.8% a 350 basis points improvement.

items.statement: Current margins are sustainable as growth comes from higher kV class transformers
items.quote: The margin has come out from the results. They are more or less fair and sustainable.

items.statement: Backward integration capex for radiators and tanks planned to start by Q1 next year
items.quote: We are also in the process of doing a backward integration capex, which is also disclosed in the DRHP that we filed with SEBI. The backward integration projects are under planning stage as of now, and we intend to start the capex possibly by Q1 of next year.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity expanded from ~16,000 MVA to 63,000 MVA over past 18 months
items.quote: Over the past 18 months, we have invested heavily to expand our manufacturing capacity from approximately 16,000 MVA to 63,000 MVA, nearly a four-fold increase.

items.statement: Vadod facility (Unit 4) at ~30% utilization in Q3, contributed ~INR160 crores revenue
items.quote: Sir, it's close to 30%.

items.statement: Plans to repay remaining INR65 crores long-term debt during current fiscal year

items.quote: Order pipeline is close to INR10,000 crores and we have been witnessing a hit ratio of close to 10% to 15% in this particular year.

items.quote: We have got the assessment dates from the Power Grid for our Vadod facility, which is unit 4. So, we are expecting to finish that assessment audit within this particular month only. items.statement: Strategic decision to not take further 400 kV orders until first prototype executed to avoid market exposure without proven product
items.quote: We have taken a very bold move of not to take further 400 kV class orders till we execute our first order. We do not want to expose ourselves to the market without a proven product prototype first.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 maintained at Rs.1,500-1,550 crores
items.quote: Our annual guidance has always been in the range-bound between Rs.1,500 to 1,550 crores and we stick by it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 10.5%-11.5% for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: Our guidance has always been that the margins would be range-bound between 10.5% to 11.5%, and we continue to stand by this guidance, not only for this year, but also for the next year.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY27 at minimum 20% growth over FY26, around Rs.1,800 crores
items.quote: Our revenue guidance for the next FY27, which we are giving is a minimum 20% of growth over the '26. So, I think it is the same guidance which we have been maintaining throughout during our road shows as well; it will be around Rs.1,800 crores.

items.statement: Finance cost guidance for FY26 at close to 2% of revenue
items.quote: Full year guidance is close to 2%.

items.statement: Renewable sector contributes 25-28% of order book, electronics/semiconductor/electrical ~18%
items.quote: In our pending order book also, we have close to 25% to 28% of our order from the renewable sector, and around 18% is from electronics, semiconductor and electrical.

items.statement: Repeat customers constitute 40-45% of order book
items.quote: Repeat customers for us is around 40-45%.

items.quote: We are doing a Greenfield CAPEX in Ghiloth for sandwich panels. We are doing Rs.101-odd crores there, where we have already started the plan at this location, and it will be operational by the third quarter of the next financial year.

items.statement: Gujarat plant (50,000 tons) planned for FY27 with Rs.55-60 crores capex plus Rs.40 crores land cost
items.quote: The idea is, like to put up a capacity of 50,000 tons to start with, so which needs a CAPEX of around Rs.55 crores to Rs.60 crores. So, that will also be done in the next financial year.

items.statement: Average capacity utilization last three months at 74%+ across all three plants
items.quote: Our average capacity utilization of the last three months across all the three plants put together is 74%-plus.

items.statement: Nine-month capacity utilization at ~69%; target steady-state utilization of 80%
items.quote: See, we would be very happy with the overall capacity utilization of 80%. If we are able to do it on an annualized basis, we would be really, very happy.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 margin 10.1%, nine-month margin 10.8%; employee cost at 12% of revenue in Q3, guided to normalize to 9-9.5%
items.quote: On the margin, last quarter was 10.1%. It is a little down, for sure, but on a nine-month basis, it is 10.8%.

items.statement: Renewable sector margins slightly better but focus on repeat business; able to charge 2-2.5% premium after demonstrating execution capability
items.quote: And now it is the time they have seen our execution, they have seen our quality, and this time we could get some 2%, 2.5% premium from them.

items.statement: Commodity price risk mitigated by 30-45 days raw material inventory, 8-10 weeks mill orders, and weekly order booking at current prices providing natural hedge
items.quote: The first one is the raw material inventory. So, typically we have an inventory of 30-45 days of production. items.statement: Fixed-price contracts with 5-6 month project duration; manufacturing supply completed in 3-4 months; price escalation negotiable for customer-caused delays
items.quote: Our contracts are fixed-price contracts. But we do not order the material on a weekly basis. What I told you is, our order intake happens on a weekly basis on the current prices. So, if today the steel price is 56, it will happen at 56. If next week the steel price is 58, the order booking for us will happen at 58. So, it gives us a natural hedging.

items.statement: Working capital cycle guided at 35 days (~9% of revenue); Q3 at 38 days due to receivables stretch, expected to improve in January
items.quote: Normally, we have given a guidance of 35-days and it will be range-bound within that framework only.

items.statement: Term loan reduced to ~Rs.45 crores, working capital loans ~Rs.80 crores; total debt ~Rs.125-127 crores after Rs.70 crores IPO repayment
items.quote: Today, we have a term loan close to about Rs.45-odd crores, and we have close to Rs.80-odd crores on our working capital loans. So, put together, it is about Rs.125, 127-odd crores of term loan plus WCDL put together that we have.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of Rs.160 crores deployed for Mumbattu and Ghiloth capex; private equity investment in Dec 2024 for Gujarat expansion
items.quote: We got a private equity investment in December 2024, which has remained with us until now, right? So, we have not used that money for anything else. Major part of that money has been lying in fixed deposit to be utilized for the Gujarat expansion.

items.statement: Orders primarily direct from end-users (factory/warehouse owners); minimal contractor/intermediary involvement

items.statement: Nine-month structural steel production at 70,000-74,000 tons
items.quote: In this nine month, we have been able to do around 70,000 tons to 74,000 tons of structural steel.

items.statement: Steady-state ROE target 17-18%, ROC target 22-25% after capex completion; FY27 ROE may see blip due to capex
items.quote: should be able to deliver our ROE close to about 18%. Obviously, you will see a little blip in the ROE in the FY27 because the CAPEX will be happening there. items.quote: We had an additional inventory in finished goods of Rs.35 crores to Rs.40 crores, which could not be built in the month of December, because last six, seven days of December, the payment could not be made by the customers because of Christmas, holidays, and all those things.

items.statement: Strong pipeline from renewable, building materials, glass, cement, automobile sectors; large orders expected in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have further enquiries from the renewable sector also. We have good enquiries from the building materials, glass sector, cement sector, automobile sector. So, going forward, we are seeing a strong tailwind in terms of the CAPEX that are happening in these industries, and for sure, we are on track of booking big orders in this quarter as well.

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved across plants; significant improvement over last year.

items.statement: Inventory slightly elevated vs same quarter last year; collections smooth; cash & liquid balance INR 455 cr as of 31 Dec.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; focus on capital efficiency across fixed and working capital.

items.statement: Global agrochemical market ~$75 bn in 2025, projected ~5.5% CAGR; herbicide largest category.
items.quote: The global agrochemical market particularly crop protection market, valued at approximately $75 billion in 2025, is projected to grow at a CAGR of ~5.5%.

items.statement: Technical procurement from China >40% blended; will continue due to product complexity and lifecycle; not moving away completely.
items.quote: So on a blended basis, still it is more than 40%. And I mean the challenge is not that all of that can be replaced. Not only it is there, it will continue to be there.

items.statement: Export blended margin >20%; CSM blended margin ~30%; domestic institutional mid-teens; seed high-margin; one-off quality provision >INR 10 cr impacted 9M gross margin.

items.statement: No significant capex ahead of market demand; sufficient seeds, plants, equipment to grow; only sustainable maintenance capex planned.

items.statement: ~75% of deposit book repriced; remainder this quarter and ~10% in Q1 FY27; full repricing by Q1 FY27
items.quote: around 75% of my d eposit book has been repriced. I think remaining some portion will get repriced in this quarter and maybe one -tenth of the book will be repriced in the first quarter

items.statement: New labour code impact negligible (<₹25 lakh) due to minimal contractual employees
items.quote: It's very insignificant because we have a very small number of contractual employees. We don't have a large number of contractual employees. It is very insignificant. May not be even ₹25 lakh.

items.statement: Export credit exposure ₹2,000 crore; only 5% (₹100 crore) in countries with tariff issues
items.quote: we have around ₹2,000 crore of export credit exposure and of which only 5% is in respect of countries where some tariff and all these things have happened. So, it is not a major one; around ₹100 crore

items.statement: CASA ratio 38.41%, up 44 bps YoY; maintained 37-38% range for 7-8 quarters; savings +10%, current +23%
items.quote: Our CAS A ratio improved by 44 bps to 38.41 % and we have been able to maintain our CASA in the range of 37 to 38% consistently for last 7, 8 quarters.

items.statement: CD ratio improved to 78.56% from 65% in Mar'23; improving quarterly
items.quote: CD ratio of the bank has been improving on a quarter-on-quarter basis. In March’23 it stood at around 65 %, now in December’25 it has reached to 78.56 %.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 17.43% (Tier-1 15.41%, CET1 15.18%); including 9M profit 18.67%
items.quote: capital adequacy ratio of the bank stood at around 17.43 %, with Tier 1 capital 15.41 % and CET1 at 15.18 %. If we include these 9 months profit al so, then our capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.67 %.

items.statement: International book: overseas deposits +18%, overseas advances +12%; lending selective on pricing
items.quote: deposit if you look, at our deposit growth in the international is around 18% growth as far as overseas deposit is concerned and overseas advances around 12% growth is there.

items.statement: Geopolitical risk limited: strong domestic consumption offsets export impact; minimal exposure to affected countries
items.quote: I believe we have a strong consumption economy. And if there is an impact on the export front, I think domestic is able to support the surplus quantity available of the products.

items.statement: MCLR cut 30 bps so far; further cuts monthly per RBI formula; ALCO meets monthly (next 8-10 Jan)
items.quote: MCLR, I think, 30 basis po ints cut is already in place and expected cut I cannot tell you because it is to be decided by ALCO on a monthly basis.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA per ton guidance Rs 19,000-21,000; nine-month average Rs 21,300; expect to close year around this level
items.quote: whatever guidance we have provided for the year, Rs. 19,000 to 21,000 per metric ton is what we had given. We have delivered in nine months an average of around 21,300 and we believe that this year on an average basis around this number we should be closing.

items.statement: Confident of meeting FY26 volume growth and EBITDA per ton guidance despite geopolitical and QCO issues
items.quote: whatever guidance we had given in terms of volume growth and EBITDA per ton, we are extremely confident of meeting those numbers.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth targets and downstream investment plans to be announced next quarter
items.quote: give us one more quarter, then by Q4, I will come out with, let's say, next 2-3year volume growth target and plans.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance Rs 2,700 crore; Rs 2,200 crore spent in nine months; on track to meet full-year target
items.quote: we had given a guidance of 2,700 crores as a CapEx for the whole financial year FY26. 2,200 crores we have already done and we are on course of completing or ending with around 2,700 crores of CapEx in FY26.

items.statement: Maintenance capex for all plants around Rs 500 crore annually
items.quote: it is around Rs. 500 crores that we have it for all the plants.

items.statement: SMS project in Indonesia and downstream expansion in India progressing well and on track per timeline
items.quote: Our SMS project in Indonesia and aligned downstream capacity expansion in India are progressing well and remain on track as per the timeline.

items.statement: Chromeni utilisation ~75%, Rathi ~80%, target 90-95% this year; RVPL lower due to strategy changes, only finishing lines running
items.quote: Chromeni is around, I would believe, 75% right now. Rat hi is close to 80%. And the target , as always, is to further increase them to atleast 90-95% this year

items.statement: Q3 FY26 deliveries 0.65 million tonnes, up 11% YoY, flat QoQ; 9M FY26 deliveries 1.92 million tonnes, up 11% YoY
items.quote: Our Q3 FY26 deliveries are at 0.65 million tonnes, with an increase of around 11% on year-on-year.

items.statement: Domestic demand sustained across automotive, ornamental pipe and tube, railways, metro, lift and elevator, white goods; export market stable but subdued due to geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: our sales volume in Q3 FY26 grew by 11% year-on-year and remained steady quarter-on-quarter, supported by sustained domestic demand amidst stability in the export market.

items.statement: CRAP share of overall sales ~55% vs ~50% a year ago; HRAP:CRAP ratio improved from 40:60 (Q3 FY24) to 30:70 (Q3 FY26)
items.quote: If we look at our only CRAP percentage of the overall sales, so now it is at around 55%, which was at around 50% a year before. But then if you look only HRAP and CRAP ratio, then I can give you a 3-years trend. So, in Q3 FY24, it was around HRAP : CRAP 40:60, which changed to 35:65. And this financial FY26 Q3, it is 30 :70.

items.statement: Nickel prices fell on average in Q3 but rose in December and January; stainless steel prices move with raw material costs; blended ASP Q3 ~Rs 161,000/t, down 4-4.5% QoQ; current blended realisation ~Rs 190,000-191,000/t
items.quote: nickel in particular, which was otherwise has in fact on an average basis has gone down in Q3, but towards December it started going up and yeah, in the month of January also it is on the higher side.

items.statement: Most nickel-bearing grades sold on back-to-back hedging with 30-45 day pass-through lag; non-nickel grades not fully hedged
items.quote: most things, as you know already, we pass on to the customer with like maybe a lag of 30 to 45 days. So, whatever cost ... And we do in our raw material buying, it's always a back-to-back hedging that we try to ensure.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated EBITDA Rs 1,408 crore, up 17% YoY, 1% QoQ; PAT Rs 828 crore, up 27% YoY, 2% QoQ; 9M FY26 EBITDA Rs 4,106 crore, up 14% YoY; PAT Rs 2,350 crore, up 23% YoY
items.quote: Our Q3 consolidated EBITDA increased by around 17% year-on-year and around 1% on quarter-on-quarter to Rs. 1408 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt Rs 3,451 crore at Dec 31, 2025; net debt/EBITDA 0.67x, net debt/equity 0.18x; FY26 year-end net debt expected around or slightly below Q3 level (guidance was Rs 3,500-3,700 crore)
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, our consolidated net debt has further reduced to Rs. 3451 crores, with a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio at 0.67, comfortably below 1, and a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18.

items.statement: Net debt expected to close FY26 around or slightly below Q3 level of Rs 3,451 crore
items.quote: we believe that this year we should 11 be closing somewhere around where we are already or maybe a bit even lower than what net debt position we have at the end of Quarter 3

items.statement: CBAM verification methodology and authorised verifiers not yet defined by EU; company prepared with high ESG scores (S&P 78/100, top 5% globally, 4th in steel; DJSI top position); expect more clarity this quarter
items.quote: the European Union has come out with threshold levels and calculation methodologies. But what they have not yet come out with the verification methodology and who is going to verify the calculations.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend FY26 of Rs 1 per share (face value Rs 2), aggregate payout ~Rs 82.44 crore; record date Jan 29, 2026
