items.quote: the Board of Directors have approved an interim dividend payment for FY26 of Rs. 1 per share with a face value of Rs. 2 each, aggregating to a payout of nearly Rs. 82.44 crores. The record date for the purpose of payment has been set as January 29, 2026.

items.statement: NPI venture EBITDA guidance $500-1,500 per metric ton of nickel; Q3 achieved ~$900; expect higher end if nickel prices stay elevated; nickel equivalent capacity ~14,000 tonnes at 100% utilisation (49% share of 28,000 t design)
items.quote: we had indicated for our nickel venture, we had given a guidance of around $500 to $1,500 range for metric ton of nickel. And Quarter 3, we have hit somewhere around $900. And we expect, if the nickel prices remain high, so we should be on the higher side of this range.

items.statement: Renewable power utilisation at Jajpur and Hisar reached 56% of total imported power in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our renewable power utilization at Jajpur and Hisar facilities has steadily increased, now 56% of our total imported power in Q326, making a significant step towards cleaner and more sustainable operations.

items.statement: Subsidised inferior imports continue; QCO suspension a setback; without government intervention import share (~22% of production) unlikely to decline
items.quote: Without any government intervention, I don't see these import numbers going down. Because again, what everyone has to understand and what we are trying to push to the government is that globally every country is trying to protect their manufacturers, trying to protect their borders, and India is relatively open.

items.statement: Signed MoUs with four government ITIs in Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra to implement 155-hour stainless steel fabrication course
items.quote: we have signed M OUs with four government industrial training institutes in Odisha, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra to implement a 155 hours stainless steel fabrication course as a part of their curriculum.

items.statement: Achieved S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment score 78/100 for FY25, top 5% in steel sector, 4th globally; secured top position in DJSI-modelled ESG ranking
items.quote: JSL achieved an S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment score of 78 out of 100 for FY25, ranking us among the top 5% in the steel sector and securing 4th position globally.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth target of 25-26% QoQ if gold prices consolidate at current levels
items.quote: If the prices remain at current level. Even if they don't go up from here but they consolidate, then we will see very strong growth in the gold loan portfolio. Vedant Sarda: 25%, 26% growth on Q-o-Q basis? Nirmal Jain: Yes. That should be a very comfortable

items.statement: Housing finance AUM growth target of 15-16% and disbursement growth of 24-25% for FY27
items.quote: So, on the book, we plan to grow by about 15%-16%. And on disbursement, it will be 24%-25%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM growth target of 20-25% for FY27
items.quote: On the whole, you should see about 20%-25% AUM growth next year.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of less than 2% for next financial year, down 50-60 bps from current quarter annualized 2.5%
items.quote: So, another 50-60 basis points decline in the next financial year from the current. Gao Zhixuan: 50. Nirmal Jain: From this quarter level, yes. So, if this quarter annualizes around 250, we should go below 200

items.statement: Target ROE of 18-20% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, our ROE was in the range of 18% to 20% in normal times. So, we would endeavor to reach towards that. So, that is our internal target in the next two to three years.

items.statement: Leverage target of 4-4.5x and capital adequacy target closer to 20% for standalone NBFC
items.quote: Our leverage, we will keep it around 4 -4.5, and capital adequacy, we would like it to be closer to 20.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA improved to 1.6% from 2.14% QoQ, NNPA below 1% at 0.8%, provision coverage 92%
items.quote: Asset quality has improved across the board with a significant reduction in GNPA from 2.14% to 1.6%, and NNPA falling below 1%. Stage-2 and Stage-3 assets are also trending down, indicating further improvement in asset quality going ahead. Our provision coverage stands at 92%, well above regulatory requirements.

items.statement: Housing finance GNPA fell from 2.2% to 0.9% after ARC sale of INR 875 crore portfolio covering BLC and Micro LAP
items.quote: And that is why if you see, our GNPA in housing has fallen from 2.2% to 0.9%. That is the level that we would like it to be.

items.statement: Microfinance collection efficiency at all-time peak of 99.56% in zero bucket, significant improvement in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu at 99.5%+
items.quote: And that indicates the recovery stance, and that is at all-time peak. It is much better now at 99.56%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM grew 9% QoQ and 38% YoY to INR 98,336 crore, core products (home, gold, MSME, microfinance) grew 11% QoQ and 46% YoY to INR 93,767 crore (95% of AUM)
items.quote: For the quarter, the consolidated AUM grew by 38% YoY and 9% quarter -on-quarter at INR 98,336, being at the cusp of INR 100,000 crore, largely driven by gold loan, which crossed the pre-embargo level at INR 43,432 crores, supported by a healthy gross NPA of 0.36%.

items.statement: Assigned loan book up 71% YoY and 15% QoQ to INR 21,373 crore; co-lending assets up 43% YoY and 11% QoQ to INR 13,176 crore; off-book assets at 35% of AUM
items.value: INR 21,373 crore assigned, INR 13,176 crore co-lending
items.quote: With our strategy to partner with banks and down sell our pristine assets, our assigned loan book stands at around INR 21,373 crores, which is up 71% Y-o-Y and 15% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. Besides this, the co-lending assets stand at around INR 13,176 crores, which is up 43% Y-o-Y and 11% quarter-on-quarter, taking the aggregate of books at around 35% of our AUM.

items.statement: Quarterly average cost of borrowing decreased 10% QoQ to 9.28%, increased 13 bps YoY; net interest margin implied 6-7% range
items.quote: On a quarterly average cost of borrowing, increased by around 13 basis points from a Y-o-Y basis and decreased 10% on a quarter-on-quarter basis to 9.28%.

items.statement: Housing finance targeting higher onboarding yields of 11-13% in affordable and emerging segments vs current blended ~10.5-10.6%, portfolio yield to improve over 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Yes, you are right. I think the plan is to ensure that in the next few quarters, the onboarding yield is going to go up because predominantly, our focus is going to be on affordable and emerging, which I spoke about in terms of customer segmentation, prope rty type, and the expected yield

items.statement: No capital raising plan announced; monitoring capital adequacy closely, co-lending engine restart key to sustaining gold loan growth without equity dilution
items.quote: No. At this stage, we haven't announced any capital raising plan. We are monitoring the situation very carefully. But whenever appropriate, we will raise capital.

items.statement: Income tax special audit under Section 142(2A) for block period of 6 assessment years post Section 132 search; scope limited to search findings; appointed auditor to submit report in 60 days; no tax demand, penalty or financial impact ascer
items.quote: The direction under Section 142(2A) is a procedural step in our ongoing income tax assessment following a search conducted under Section 132 of the Income -tax Act. As per law, after a search, there is always a block assessment for six assessment years preceding the year of search, carried out together. This is not a finding, this is not an allegation, and this is not an adjudication.

items.statement: NHB advised restatement of March 2025 NPAs/GNPAs to realization basis from cash receipt basis; December results now follow realized money practice
items.quote: But the important thing is that if you look at our December results, they are in line with the cheques on the realized money and not based on the cheques in receipt but not realized. So, we are now following NHB's guided practice.

items.statement: Raised INR 20,007 crore from term loans, bonds, CP in Q3; liquidity at INR 9,433 crore; net gearing 3.6x; ALM positive across buckets; consolidated capital adequacy 27.7% (NBFC 18.9%, HFC 47.7%, Samasta 30%)
items.value: INR 20,007 crore raised, INR 9,433 crore liquidity
items.quote: We raised around INR 20,007 crore from term loan, bonds, commercial paper during the quarter, and around INR 7,774 crore of our assets were assigned to various banks. And our liquidity stands at around INR 9,433 crore, adequate enough to not just meet our near-term liabilities, but also adequate to support and fund our growth momentum.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 4 per share approved by Board
items.quote: We also declared an interim dividend of INR 4 per share, which was approved by the Board of Directors and will be paid in due course.

items.statement: CISO Sameer Gadve resigned; described as normal churn with competent second line in place
items.quote: No, there is no sudden resignation. It is a normal sort of churn that happens. People find better opportunities. Some people go abroad. So, there is nothing. And then we have a very competent second line and a very competent set of people that take over.

items.statement: Gold loan Stage-3 provision coverage declined from 42% to 19% QoQ due to ECL model recalibration based on negligible historical losses; steady-state gold loan losses typically zero
items.quote: Stage-3 losses are always, again, dependent on gold prices as well as your historical. So, the way ECL is computed is based on empirical data. And what we have seen is that our losses have been negligible. And that is why this number probably was much higher than what it ought to be.

items.statement: Discontinued unsecured MSME and personal loan portfolio down from INR 4,000 crore to INR 3,000 crore in one quarter; running down to lower levels
items.quote: Our discontinued businesses portfolio in one quarter only has come down from roughly 4,000 to 3,000. And that is a short-term three-year loan that we had given through some digital partnership and as personal loan.

items.statement: Housing finance new strategy: focus on affordable (INR 14-15 lakh ticket, 12.8-13% yield) and emerging (INR 20-21 lakh ticket, 11-11.5% yield) segments; exit BLC and Micro LAP
items.quote: Our focus, I think, going forward is going to be in terms of segments broadly on emerging and affordable. Affordable largely will be the priority for us, which can give us yield and emerging to asset mix, which can help us in terms of growth, which will be in line or maybe slightly better than the industry growth rate.

items.statement: Secured MSME loans (INR 50 lakh - 2 crore ticket, 13.6-14% yield) to SMEs in smaller towns under priority sector lending; zero delinquency so far
items.quote: So, these are SMEs, and these are priority sector lending from smaller towns. And in fact, this is a new business, so if you really remember, our historical portfolio had 18% -19% yield. So, we recalibrated our entire business portfolio.

items.statement: OPEX increased INR 50 crore QoQ, half due to one-time INR 22.5 crore charge for new labor code (gratuity/leave revision), rest inflationary
items.quote: No, your point is valid, but this is a one-time charge that we have taken for the new labor code. So, INR 22.5 crore additional cost has come for that revision in measurement of gratuity and leave.

items.statement: Target 1.5 GW capacity addition in H2 FY26; on track with 125 MW added in Q3
items.quote: As we have said earlier, you rightly said that 1.5 GW of fresh capacity addition during H2 of current fiscal, out of which 125 MW we have commissioned during quarter 3. So we are well on track.

items.statement: Expect to reach 30 GW generation capacity by 2030 and 40 GWh storage by 2030
items.quote: We have already locked in about 18.7 GW of incremental capacity in generation and 29.6 GW hour in storage, which will take our installed capacity beyond our stated target of 30 GW in generation while we are confident of achieving our 40 GW hour in storage by 2030.

items.statement: Salboni Phase 1 capex ~₹16,000 crore for 2x800 MW; Phase 2 tariff ₹4.06/kWh fixed
items.quote: whatever we have said in the domain is that the Phase 1 about ₹16,000 crores of investment for 2 *800 MW which we have announced earlier, so we'll be around that number only.

items.statement: Locked-in generation capacity 32.1 GW; secured thermal capacity 10.7 GW; RE contracted 12.6 GW
items.quote: With this, our secured thermal capacity stands at 10.7 GW and locked-in capacity at 32.1 GW, providing ample visibility to our ambitious 2030 target.

items.statement: 4.5 GW RE capacity pending LOA-to-PPA conversion; 27.5 GW operational + under construction
items.quote: with our current operational capacity and the projects under construction, we are already at 27.5 GW. In addition, we have a pipeline of 4.5 GW, and the details of that pipeline are already available.

items.statement: Power demand growth flattish in Q3 due to long monsoon; December 2025 demand up 6.5% YoY; Jan 2026 first 20 days up 6%
items.quote: The third quarter of this fiscal year has witnessed a flattish power demand growth, primarily driven by an unusually long and intense monsoon season and cooler temperature, which reduced the need for cooling and irrigation pump power demand, leading to a muted overall growth.

items.statement: Utkal 400 MW PPA at ₹5.78/kWh single tariff (₹4.04 fixed + ₹1.74 variable) for 25 years from Apr 2026
items.quote: this is the exact tariff is ₹5.78, out of which, the fixed part is ₹4.04 and ₹1.74 variable cost. And if the plant availability is there as per the PPA, my fixed cost is assured.

items.statement: Salboni Phase 1 tariff ₹3.65/kWh fixed, Phase 2 ₹4.06/kWh fixed; fuel pass-through at 2350 heat rate
items.quote: For the first bid the tariff is in the range of ₹3.65, which we have already announced. And the second ₹4.06. This is a fixed charge only. ₹3.6 for Phase 1 and ₹4.06 for Phase 2. Fuel is pass-through.

items.statement: Added 125 MW renewables in Q3; total installed 13.3 GW (up 64% YoY); 5.2 GW added in last 12 months (3.1 GW RE, 2.1 GW thermal)
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 125 MW of new capacity, in renewables, including hybrid projects, taking our total installed capacity to 13.3 GW. Our capacity additions represents a significant year-on-year growth of approximately 64%, up from 8.1 GW in the same period last year.

items.statement: Kutehr hydro fully stabilized, generated 130 MU in Q3; green hydrogen plant (3,800 tpa) commissioned at Vijayanagar
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the Kutehr plant has now fully stabilised and generated about 130 million units during the quarter. We have also continued to remain at the forefront of innovation. During the quarter, we successfully commissioned India's largest green hydrogen plant at our Vijayanagar location, with a capacity of 3,800 tonnes of Green Hydrogen per annum.

items.statement: ~25% of installed capacity (3.3 GW) tied to Group Captive & C&I at blended tariff >₹3.65/kWh; expected to rise to 5.7 GW beyond 30 GW
items.quote: On the capacity front, approximately 3.3 GW which forms around 25% of our current installed capacity is secured with high -quality Group Captive and C&I customers. As we scale beyond 30 GW, this is expected to further increase to approximately 5.7 GW. Importantly, these capacities are contracted at highly remunerative tariffs - with renewables tied up at a high blended average tariff of over ₹3.65

items.statement: Receivables ₹3,000 crore; debtor days 73 vs 96 days YoY
items.quote: Finally, on receivables, total receivables at the end of December stood at approximately ₹3,000 crores, translating to debtor days of 73 days, which is a sharp reduction versus the 96 days which we witnessed in the corresponding quarter of the last fiscal.

items.statement: Promoter preferential allotment ₹3,000 crore (₹500 cr equity + ₹2,500 cr warrants); QIP approval up to ₹10,000 crore
items.quote: Another important milestone during the quarter was the preferential allotment of equity shares to the promoter group, involving a capital infusion of ₹3,000 crore, comprising ₹500 crore through equity and ₹2,500 crore through warrants, which will convert i nto equity over the next 18 months or earlier. In addition, consistent with last year, we have also received Shareholder’s approval for a poten

items.statement: Tidong Hydro and GE Boiler acquisitions progressing; expect GE boiler plant by Jun-Jul 2026; NCLT approval for Raigarh Champa Rail Infra
items.quote: On the inorganic growth front, the acquisitions announced in the previous quarter -Tidong Hydro Power and GE Power India's Boiler Manufacturing division are progressing well. We expect to complete these transactions at the earliest, subject to the completion of customary processes and approvals. Further, we have also received the NCLT approval in relation to the Resolution Plan submitted by the Co

items.statement: CFO Chandrasekaran Prabhakaran joined Jan 2026 from JSW Steel (25+ years exp, Deputy CFO)
items.quote: I'm also delighted to warmly welcome our CFO, Chandrasekaran Prabhakaran, who joined us at the beginning of January from JSW Steel. Prabhakaran brings with him over 25 years of rich and diverse experience across corporate finance, accounting and governance gained through senior leadership roles in large listed conglomerates.

items.statement: Power sales up 65% YoY to 11.1 BU in Q3; 9M generation up 62% to 39.6 BU; LT PPA share 82% of sales
items.quote: Our power sales recorded a strong 65% year -on-year growth in Q3 FY26, increasing from 6.8 billion units to 11.1 billion units. For the nine -month period ended FY26, net generation grew 62% year on year, rising from 24.4 billion units to 39.6 billion units. Notably, long-term PPAs accounted for 82% of total power sales and registered a 63% year -on-year increase in Q3.

items.statement: Solar+wind generation up 149% YoY; thermal up 55%; hydro up 27% vs national 13%
items.quote: Our solar and wind portfolio net generation rose by 149% year on year, led by organic capacity additions and contributions from O2 Power. Thermal generation increased by 55% year o n year, primarily driven by contributions from KSK and capacity additions at our Utkal plant. Further, Hydro generation grew by 27% year on year versus the national average increase of 13 per cent during the quarter

items.statement: KSK tariff reduction ~₹1.25/kWh for 1,000 MW UP PPA in FY27; impact minimal due to operational efficiencies
items.quote: There will be, of course, going forward in FY '27 as per the PPA terms, there will be a tariff reduction of close to about ₹1.25 from one of the DISCOMs, so that will definitely have some impact, but operational efficiencies, as I've said earlier, during the year, we have been building up a lot of operational efficiencies and which have come during the year and kept on coming, so that will give us

items.statement: FDRE IV PPA signed, awaiting regulatory approval in Rajasthan; DSM tightening being addressed industry-wide with Ministry
items.quote: received the letter. We're waiting for regulatory approval. That is the state. There is no further communication to us from Rajasthan on this. Satyadeep Jain: There is no communication on cancellation or anything as of... Sharad Mahendra: PPA has been signed. We are waiting for the regulatory approval. That's all. Nothing

items.statement: BESS containerization & cell assembly plant trial production starting Feb-Mar 2026; approvals expected Mar-Apr; cell import orders placed
items.quote: We have submitted our product for necessary approvals, which we expect by March end or early April the approvals to be in place. But by the t ime, we will start the production sometime in February -- between February

items.statement: Salboni thermal tariffs among lowest in recent 12 GW state bids; state comfortable with blended tariff for 4x800 MW
items.quote: In thermal space, this is one of the most attractive tariffs. So state is absolutely comfortable and regulatory approval also is in place keeping in mind what has prevailed. We need to know what has happened in other bids in Assam, whether it is Bihar or whether it is MP, you see the states. So this is a very good tariff which has been discovered.

items.statement: Avoided 14-15 MT CO2 in 9M FY26 via renewable generation
items.quote: our expanding renewable portfolio enabled us to avoid approximately 14 -15 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions in the first nine months of this fiscal alone, based on the prevailing Indian grid emission factor.

items.statement: Net NPA guidance of below 0.75% achieved at 0.74% in December quarter
items.quote: the net NPA of 0.74%, which is as per our guidance that we should bring it below 0.75% and we have already achieved that guidance in December and we have brought it to 0.74%

items.statement: RAM share target 60% by March 2026 and 70% for FY27
items.quote: we expect that this percentage will gradually go up and by the end of March 26, we should be at 60% and the guidance for FY 26 -27 is 70%

items.statement: Gross NPA target revised to 2.25% by March 2026 from earlier 2.50%
items.quote: I think we are looking at a number of 2.25 % by the end of March

items.statement: ROA target of 1% by March 2027
items.quote: we think that ROA of 1% is surely possible by the end of March ’27

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target 50-55% by March 2027
items.quote: by the end of March 27, we should be nearly around between 50% to 55%

items.statement: NIM expected to bottom out by end of Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: the NIM, will get bottomed out by the end of this quarter or maximum by the end of the next quarter

items.statement: Shift to higher-yielding RAM segments (3-3.5% margin) and shed low-yield corporate loans
items.quote: we price our products and we go into the segments of the asset side where we can really get a margin of 3%-3.5%

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio Rs 4,800 crore (Rs 1,700 crore co-lending, Rs 1,000 crore agri) yielding ~8.85%
items.quote: Regarding the overall Gold Loan portfolio of Rs.4800 Crore, Rs.1700 Crore is through co-lending and out of that Rs.1000 Crore is agriculture and with regard to the yield in gold loan, it is somewhere around 8.85%

items.statement: Four new zones opened, four more planned next FY; FGM offices to increase from 2 to 5; BCs to expand to ~6,000
items.quote: 4 four new zones were opened during the year and another four zones are planned for the next financial year. We have now two FGM offices, we intend to increase it to five, increasing by another three, and also expansion of BCs further to around 6000

items.statement: Recovery from written-off accounts expected Rs 250-300 crore in Q4 FY26
items.quote: in this quarter also we expect around Rs .250 crore to Rs.300 crores of recovery in the Written off accounts

items.statement: Shed Rs 3,000 crore corporate loans due to uncompetitive pricing; cannot compete on AAA corporate with low CASA base
items.quote: we have shed around Rs.3000 crores of corporate loan book just because we didn't want to provide a repricing at a rate which is not convenient to us

items.statement: Tax regime migration under evaluation after accumulated losses covered
items.quote: No, not yet but we have covered all our accumulated losses and now time has come for us to look into this subject and maybe going forward we’ll look into this

items.statement: Targets 20% CAGR loan book growth to INR 7,500 crores by March 2030 and 30% CAGR PBT growth to INR 500 crores in FY30
items.value: INR 7,500 crores loan book; INR 500 crores PBT
items.quote: On the loan book size for the next four years, we look to grow at 20% CAGR to take the book to INR 7,500 crores by March 2030. However, from the profitability perspective, the CAGR is targeted to be around 30% during the same period, so that we achieve Profit Before Tax of INR 500 crores in FY30

items.statement: Targets INR 1,000 crores annual AUM addition; aims to reach INR 4,500 crores by March 2027 from INR 3,500 crores in March 2026
items.quote: Every year, INR 1,000 crores is targeted to be added. Kushal, you are assuming that March '27 continues to be INR 6,000 crores, that's why you're calculating addition of INR 500 crores from thereon, but that's not the case. We have reduced March'27 also. So we are talking about 20% CAGR from March '26 to March '30.

items.statement: Loan book reached all-time high of INR 3,210 crores as of December 31, 2025 with 12% QoQ growth
items.quote: We have achieved an all-time-high loan book of INR 3,210 crores as of December 31, 2025, registering quarter-on-quarter growth of 12%.

items.statement: Supply chain financing contributes around 70% of AUM; factoring license recently granted by RBI
items.quote: Supply chain financing, continues to remain our core strength and focus, which presently contributes to around 70% of our AUM. Recently, RBI has granted us license to commence factoring business, which will further strengthens our supply chain financing

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio below 15%; ROA 4.4% and ROE 10.5% annualized for nine months
items.quote: Operationally, we remain a very highly disciplined NBFC with cost -to-income ratio of less than 15%, nil NPAs. We have delivered return on assets of 4.4% and return on equity of 10.5% on annualized b asis for the first nine

items.statement: Additional equity of INR 338 crores expected by April via share warrants; equity base to reach INR 1,450-1,500 crores by FY27 start
items.value: INR 338 crores; INR 1,450-1,500 crores equity base
items.quote: Additional equity of INR 338 crores is expected by April and with accruals of Q4 put together, I think we are looking to have an equity base of somewhere between INR 1,450 crores to INR 1,500 crores as we begin the new financial year.

items.statement: Board approved exploration of four new subsidiaries: ARC, AIF, Insurance Broking, FinTech; at drawing board stage, no investment planned for 2-3 years
items.quote: Subject to regulatory approvals, today the board has approved our expansion plan to set up four new subsidiaries, which will further augment our fee-based revenue. Currently, it is at the drawing board stage, but the board has approved to explore and evaluate the areas of ARC, AIF, Insurance Broking, and FinTech business.

items.statement: Non-supply chain business (30% of AUM) comprises business loans, LAP, LAS to existing anchor ecosystem customers
items.quote: 30% of our business is non supply chain, more like business loans, cross selling we are doing with our existing customer or their ecosystem. Because when we deal with the anchors, and dealers distributors, may not be direct borrower s, but within their ecosystem, the requirement of non-supply chain base financing comes

items.statement: New ESOP policy approved by Board; requires shareholder approval then remuneration committee decision
items.quote: So, first we will go for the shareholder approval, Kushal. Then we will go to the remuneration committee. Then we will decide. You know, it's away from here.

items.statement: Management acknowledges guidance revisions due to license issues and leadership transition; prioritizes zero NPA over aggressive growth
items.quote: For us, what matters is that growth comes with no accidents, no NPAs. So, if we grow our loan book faster than what we have guided without any NPA, we will go aggressive next year.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of ₹5.5–6.5 per SCM
items.quote: For the entire financial year, we estimate the EBITDA margins to be in the range of ₹5.5 to ₹6.5 per SCM.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR650–700 crores; similar run rate expected for next couple of years
items.quote: for the full financial year, we plan to incur a capital expenditure to the range of INR650 crores to INR700 crores

items.statement: Capex run rate of INR700 crores expected for next couple of years for standalone CGD business
items.quote: For Gujarat Gas, its CGD business, INR700-odd crores is the run rate we should be building in?

items.statement: Morbi industrial volumes expected to reach 3–3.2 MMSCMD in February and March 2026
items.quote: We are expecting close to 3 to 3.2 MMSCMD in Morbi

items.statement: Morbi volumes increased from 1.68 to 2.2 MMSCMD after price cut; further increase expected after Saudi CP announcement
items.quote: If we had not reduced the prices, it would have further reduced. So from 1.68, it has basically increased to 2.2 MMSCMD.

items.statement: CNG sales grew 11% YoY in Q3 FY26; Gujarat up 9%, non-Gujarat up 22%
items.quote: CNG sales rose by 11% year-over-year, with Gujarat recording a 9% increase and areas outside Gujarat delivering a notable 22% growth

items.statement: CNG vehicle base reached 16.94 lakh as of Dec 2025, up 14% YoY
items.quote: As of December '25, the CNG vehicle base across GGL's network reached approximately 16.94 lakh compared to 14.89 lakh a year earlier, reflecting a solid 14% growth.

items.statement: Non-Morbi industrial volumes grew 1% QoQ and 7% YoY to 2.25 MMSCMD in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The non-Morbi volumes of 2.25 MMSCMD for quarter ended 31st December 2025 has grown from 2.22 MMSCMD during the previous quarter. That is an increase of approximately 1%.

items.statement: Morbi industrial price cut by INR4.50/SCM effective Jan 1, 2026; natural gas premium over propane reduced by INR2.40/SCM
items.quote: The recent reduction in spot RLNG prices and crude prices enabled GGL to reduce the prices in Morbi Ceramic segment by INR4.50 per SCM with effect from January 1, 2026.

items.statement: Current Morbi industrial gas price INR41/SCM vs propane INR38.6/SCM; parity expected if propane rises $25–30/ton
items.quote: Currently, the propane price is around INR38.6 against our gas prices of INR41.

items.statement: Gas sourcing mix: 24% APM, 4% New Well, 39% long-term, 33% short-term (IGX + spot)
items.quote: I'll tell you of the 8.5 MMSCMD which we have purchased, of 24% is APM gas, New Well Gas is 4% and long-term contracts are 39% and short term is 33%.

items.statement: Target to increase long-term gas sourcing to 60–70% by end of FY27
items.quote: So I think the objective is to have a stable price, less reliance on spot and maybe on an overall basis, have 60% to 70% volumes tied up on a long term basis.

items.statement: Plan to cross 1,000 CNG stations in 2–3 years from current 833; 78 FDODO agreements signed
items.quote: I think I won't be surprised if we'll enter into 4-digit number in coming 2 to 3 years, that is we may cross 1,000 CNG stations.

items.statement: 10+ FDODO CNG stations to be commissioned in FY26, balance in FY27
items.quote: we will connect more than 10 CNG stations in this financial year and balance in the next financial year.

items.statement: 415 of 833 CNG stations are online (50%); converted 40+ daughter booster stations in last 2 years
items.quote: today, we have around 833 stations. Of that, close to 415 stations are online today. That is almost 50% of the stations are online today.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA per SCM at ₹6.5 vs ₹5.04 YoY; 9M EBITDA ₹1,602 cr vs ₹1,566 cr YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin per SCM stood at ₹6.5 against ₹5.04in corresponding quarter to the previous year.

items.statement: Morbi volume increase of 1 MMSCMD expected to reduce gross margin by ~INR1/SCM due to new trunkline tariffs
items.quote: Approximately INR1 per SCM.

items.statement: Scheme of arrangement final hearing expected mid-February 2026; completion including relisting by next earnings call (~May 2026)
items.quote: We are expecting final hearing from MCA somewhere in the month of February. That will be followed by once we receive a final order from MCA and complete other formalities. So we expect that by the time we get into the next earnings call, I think all formalities will be completed.

items.statement: GSPC identifying propane storage locations; advanced talks to reserve unloading capacity to offer propane as alternate fuel in Morbi
items.quote: our parent company, GSPC, has identified locations for storage and handling of propane. We are currently in advanced talks to reserve unloading capacity, ensuring that we have access to physical infrastructure, to basically capitalize on this opportunity.

items.statement: Propane to be offered as alternate fuel to retain Morbi industrial customers and market share
items.quote: To manage competition, we'll be actively offering propane as an alternate fuel solution, ensuring that we retain our customers, maintain customer relationship and market share in the industrial belt of Morbi and other industrial locations.

items.statement: Priority sector (CNG + domestic PNG) allocation shortfall 51% in Q3; CNG shortfall 64% met via spot/long-term
items.quote: there was a 64% shortfall in the CNG segment, resulting in an overall shortfall of 51% to the priority segment, that is Domestic and CNG.

items.statement: Overall Morbi ceramic cluster capacity ~8 MMSCMD; utilization 7–7.5 MMSCMD (natural gas 1.65, rest propane)
items.quote: The overall volume is close to 7.55. Of that, natural gas volume in the Q3 was around 1.65, rest was with respect to propane.

items.statement: Spot LNG prices spiked due to severe winter in Europe/US; expected to normalize to ~$9 in 2 months; term contracts from mid-2026 to ease supply
items.quote: this sudden increase in spot price is going to be a very short-term phenomenon. Basically, because of the severe winter that has hit Europe and U.S., it has resulted into spot prices going up. But we expect the prices to again come back to initially $9 kind of a level.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions could disrupt supply chains, shipping routes, cause price volatility; project delays (Golden Pass, Qatar NFE) remain a challenge
items.quote: the ongoing geopolitical tension could have a negative impact. It could disrupt the supply chain, impact shipping routes and cause price volatility. Commissioning time lines for some of the projects such as Golden Pass and North Field, NFE of Qatar, they could be delayed.

items.statement: Propane sales to offer credit terms to existing Gujarat Gas customers (security deposits in place) as competitive advantage
items.quote: if they buy propane from any other supplier, they will have to pay in advance, whereas in case of Gujarat Gas, since we already have the financial securities, we'll give them some credit, which is very valuable for these consumers.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 capacity growth guided at around 10% YoY
items.quote: Moving on to the forecast for the fourth quarter of this financial year, we are expecting to add capacity of around 10 percent as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Full year FY26 CASK ex-fuel ex-forex guided at mid-single digit increase YoY
items.quote: We are currently estimating mid-single digit percentage increase in our unit costs excluding fuel and forex for the full financial year 2026 as compared to the full financial year 2025, this revised guidance is based on the revised capacity estimations.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 unit passenger revenue expected to moderate early to mid single digit YoY
items.quote: Further, on the revenue side, basis the trends that we see in January, we are estimating an early to mid single digit moderation in our unit passenger revenue as compared to a high base of the same quarter last year which had a very strong tailwind in the form of the religious congregation for the Maha Kumbh.

items.statement: Served nearly 32 million customers in Q3 FY26 with record festive highs
items.quote: During the quarter, we served nearly 32 million customers, with festive period delivering record highs and our busiest days crossing 3.8 lac customers.

items.statement: Calendar year 2025 served 124 million customers, up 9% YoY
items.quote: For the full calendar year 2025, we had the privilege of serving around 124 million or 12.4 crore customers, a 9 percent increase on a year over year basis.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDAR flat YoY at 60 billion rupees
items.quote: In terms of profitability, EBITDAR came in at 60 billion rupees, broadly similar to EBITDAR during the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 net profit after tax 5.5 billion rupees with over 2% margin
items.quote: We reported a net profit after tax of 5.5 billion rupees, with over 2% profit margin, compared to 24 billion rupees in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 net profit excluding exceptional items and currency depreciation 31.3 billion rupees vs 38.5 billion YoY
items.quote: The net profit excluding the impact of exceptional items and currency depreciation was around 31.3 billion rupees as compared to 38.5 billion rupees during the same period last year.

items.statement: Inducted 36 aircraft gross in Q3 FY26, redelivered 13, closing fleet 440
items.quote: During the quarter, we inducted a total of 24 aircraft from our original orderbook, out of which 18 were inducted through our entity in GIFT city. In addition, we also inducted 12 aircraft in the form of damp leases – thus adding 36 aircraft, on gross basis. We redelivered 13 aircraft during the quarter resulting in a total closing fleet of 440 aircraft at the quarter end.

items.statement: Announced 820 million dollar capital investment in GIFT city entity for aviation assets
items.quote: In the same direction, we had announced a capital investment of 820 million dollars in GIFT city IndiGo Jan 22, 2026 entity to be deployed primarily towards acquisition of aviation assets

items.statement: Prepaid loans on 12 finance-leased aircraft via GIFT city, now 28 owned aircraft
items.quote: We have utilized part of such investment towards prepayment of loans of 12 finance-leased aircraft resulting in ownership of these aircraft. We are building a balance sheet that is not only strong today but capable of supporting the scale and ambition of tomorrow. With this transaction we have a total of 28 owned aircraft at the quarter end and around 20% of aircraft either owned or finance leased

items.statement: Q3 FY26 ASK capacity grew around 11% YoY at upper end of guided range
items.quote: We provided our revised capacity guidance on 10th December, capacity in terms of ASKs grew by around 11% for the quarter, at the upper end of the guided range.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 capacity growth moderated to 10% YoY due to regulatory schedule adjustments
items.quote: This moderation in our capacity growth for the fourth quarter is primarily driven by ad justments related to reduced schedule to align with the regulatory requirements

items.statement: Q3 FY26 passenger unit revenue 4.51 rupees, down 4.5% YoY; yield 5.33 rupees, down 2% YoY; load factor 85%, down 2 points YoY
items.quote: The passenger unit revenue came in at 4.51 rupees, which is 4.5 percent lower on a year-over-year basis, in line with our revised guidance. The yield came in at 5.33 rupees, which is around 2 percent lower compared to the same period last year and a load factor of around 85 percent, which is, again 2 points lower as compared to same period last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 fuel CASK reduced 3% YoY despite 2% increase in Singapore Jet fuel prices
items.quote: On the cost side, our fuel CASK has reduced by 3 percent compared to an increase of around 2 percent in benchmark Singapore Jet fuel prices, primarily driven by benefit of our negotiated rates, change in fleet mix and increased international network.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 CASK ex-fuel ex-forex 2.96 rupees, up 2% YoY due to contractual increases, FX, lower capacity base, partially offset by fewer damp leases
items.quote: On a year-over-year basis, the CASK ex fuel ex forex came in at 2.96 rupees, around 2 percent higher due to Annual contractual increases across line items, Inflated dollar-denominated costs due to depreciation of Indian rupee by 5%, Moderation in capacity growth leading to fixed costs being spread over a slightly lower base of ASKs And it was partially offset by a lower number of damp leases

items.statement: Rupee depreciated over 1% in Q3 vs Q2, 5% over 12 months; net forex loss 10.4 billion rupees on $10B dollar obligations
items.quote: Rupee depreciated by more than 1% at the third quarter end as compared to the second quarter end leading to a forex loss net of hedging of 10.4 billion rupees, on our dollar-based net future obligations of around 10 billion dollars.

items.statement: New Labour Codes implementation led to 9.7 billion rupees provision in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Based on our current estimates, we have recognized an estimated provision of around 9.7 billion rupees towards the implementation of these new labor laws.

items.statement: DGCA imposed 222 million rupees penalty for December operational disruptions
items.quote: On 17 January 2026, the Company received an order from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) imposing a penalty of 222 million rupees in connection with the operational disruptions.

items.statement: Regulator mandated domestic capacity cuts leading to 10% Q4 growth guidance
items.quote: There was a filed schedule, and the regulator has told us to cut down on the domestic network on that file schedule, which we have done.

items.statement: Preparing for revised FDTL norms transition in February
items.quote: Additionally, we have strengthened some of our internal processes and are preparing thoroughly for the transition to the revised FDTL norms in February.

items.statement: December quarter capitalized operating lease liability 524.8 billion rupees, total debt including lease liability 768.6 billion rupees
items.quote: We ended the December quarter with a capitalized operating lease liability of 524.8 billion rupees and a total debt, including the capitalized operating lease liability of around 768.6 billion rupees.

items.statement: Free cash 369.4 billion rupees, restricted cash 146.6 billion rupees at quarter end
items.quote: We continue to maintain strong liquidity as we ended the December quarter with free cash of 369.4 billion rupees and a restricted cash of 146.6 billion rupees.

items.statement: Scaled hedging program from $1B to $3B, extended tenure; international expansion creates natural FX hedge
items.quote: We had a $1 billion hedge program that was in play. We scaled that up to now $3 billion. So, we'll now start hedging ourselves. We were hedging for the next 12 months. We'll extend the tenure so that we are able to hedge up to $3 billion.

items.statement: Launched India's first Airbus A321 XLR with dual-class cabin, hot meals, charging points; Mumbai-Athens operations commence tomorrow
items.quote: recently we proudly introduced India’s very first IndiGo Jan 22, 2026 Airbus A321 XLR, a milestone for IndiGo and for the Indian Aviation industry. The aircraft has a dual-class cabin with 12 IndiGo Stretch seats and 183 economy seats, offering greater seat pitch than our current narrow-body fleet for enhanced comfort on long-haul flights. For the first time, IndiGo customers will enjoy hot meals

items.statement: Stretch business class expanded to 65 aircraft across 8 domestic and 9 international routes
items.quote: Building on the positive response received for our Stretch product, we are expanding it to a total of 65 aircraft en abling wider network options for business and premium customers

items.statement: BluChip loyalty programme reached around 10 million customers
items.quote: Another important milestone this quarter was the rapid scale-up of our BluChip loyalty programme, which has now reached around 10 million customers.

items.statement: December operational disruptions caused 2,500+ flight cancellations, 5.8 billion rupees provision for compensation and vouchers
items.quote: Additionally, the operational disruptions we faced in early December led to significant cancellations and delays leading to customer inconvenience. The Company, in accordance with the applicable regulation, is compensating the affected customers and in addition as a Gesture of Care also extending travel vouchers to the severely impacted customers. Additionally, On 17 January 2026, the Company rece

items.statement: Employ over 68,000 professionals; pilot hiring continuous process aligned with fleet growth
items.quote: Today, IndiGo employs more than 68,000 dedicated professionals and has served over 850 million customers since inception – all while maintaining robust operational performance.

items.statement: Calendar year 2025 operated nearly 800,000 flights, ranking 7th or 8th globally; OTP among top 3-4 globally including December
items.quote: We operated last year, calendar year '25, we operated a little short of 8 lakh flights in a single year. That's a number which brings us to number 7 or number 8 in the world. With an on-time performance number, which is also somewhere in the top 3 to 4 in the world, depending a little bit on the metric you use, including even the December number.

items.statement: Expect gross margins around 60% for coming quarter and next financial year
items.quote: we expect to maintain gross margins of around 60% for the coming quarter and also next financial year.

items.statement: CDMO full-year FY26 growth projection maintained; Q4 FY26 expected to exceed Q4 FY25
items.quote: on annual basis we are still committing to our earlier projection for the CDMO for full year.

items.statement: Overall CAPEX about Rs 1,000 crore in FY26 and over Rs 1,000 crore in FY27
items.quote: The overall CAPEX this year will be about Rs. 1,000 crores and FY '26 based on the current estimate, we do feel it will be over Rs. 1,000 crores next year also.

items.statement: ROCE expected to improve from current 18.5% but no commitment to reach 25% in next 12 months
items.quote: we are confident that the ROCE percentage will go up from the current 18%.

items.statement: Asset turnover targeting 1.1 over time; peak was 1.4
items.quote: maybe 0.9 to 1.1 we will reach , but our peak asset turn was 1.4 . We are not anticipating 1.4 at this moment but we are targeting 1.1 over a period of time.

items.statement: ADC GMP facility allocated $25 million; Phase-1 Krka JV completion by mid-2027
items.quote: ADC is still at the nascent stage right now. W e have allocated $25 million to the GMP facility which is under construction right now.

items.statement: Peptide commercial manufacturing qualification expected this calendar year
items.quote: we expect qualification during this calendar year and we will give you more details as and when we are in position to give feedback to you.

items.statement: Bio fermentation facility Phase-1 capacity over 400 kiloliters operational by end of 2026
items.quote: Construction work for the commercial-scale fermentation facility at Vizag is progressing in line with the plan and we expect a Phase-1 capacity of a little over 400 kiloliters to be operational towards the end of 2026.

items.statement: Greenfield 500-acre Atchutapuram site land allotment in Q4 FY26; CAPEX start second half FY27; qualification in two years
items.quote: We are expecting the land allotment and handover will happen in the Q4 this year, financial year. And CAPEX will start from maybe second part of FY '27 and we expect to qualification and validations only two years from now.

items.statement: Oral solid facility expansion significant part operational in Q3, undergoing ramp-up
items.quote: The oral solid facility expansion is progressing well. A significant part of the plant capacit y became operational during the quarter and is currently undergoing ramp-up activities in line with the plan.

items.statement: Krka JV Phase-1: 3 billion solid oral and 100 million potent tablet capacity by mid-2027; Phase-2 adds 5 billion tablets
items.quote: In the Phase-1, we are creating 3 billion solid oral capacity and 100 million solid oral capacity for potent molecules. In the Phase-2, we will create another 5 billion tablet capacity in the solid oral space.

items.statement: CDMO 9-month growth over 50%; strong recurring business from long-term customers
items.quote: Our cumulative 9 -month performance has been very healthy, clocking more than 50% growth. This has been supported by strong recurring business from our existing long-term customer relationships across various scales.

items.statement: Three commercial NCEs supplied in last 18 months; majority of FY27 CDMO revenue from commercial supplies
items.quote: Majority of FY'27 revenues in our CDMO division will be commercial supplies and I think that much I can make a statement.

items.statement: Generic division 9-month sales Rs 3,510 crore, up 26%; Q3 sales Rs 1,327 crore, up 37%
items.quote: The revenues from the generic division have continued to perform well, re porting growth of 37% to Rs. 1,327 crores for Q3. And for the 9-month period, we achieved sales of Rs. 3,510 crores, reflecting growth of 26%.

items.statement: ARV revenues 9M: formulations Rs 865 crore, API Rs 1,259 crore; Q3 total ARV Rs 744 crore
items.quote: In the 9 months, the formulation is Rs. 865 crores ARV. And the API is Rs. 1,259 crores.

items.statement: ARV run rate now Rs 2,600 crore +/- 200 crore vs earlier guidance of Rs 2,500 crore +/- 200 crore
items.quote: if I have to restate that currently we are at 2 ,600 plus or minus 200 , I will put it that way . But fundamentally hasn't changed much.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin 60.9%, 9M gross margin 60.1%; Q3 EBITDA margin 27%, 9M EBITDA margin 26.1%
items.quote: Gross margin maintained healthy way, for 9 months at 60.1% and for Quarter 3 it is at 60.9% mainly due to better product and division mix and continued process improvement efforts.

items.statement: Gross margin order: CDMO highest, then formulations, then API lowest
items.quote: API on the lower side, formulation on the higher side and CDMO is on the top.

items.statement: Currency benefit on gross margin positive but not significant
items.quote: Definitely we will get a benefit because we are a net exporter , but I am saying that it is not a very significant impact or positive impact.

items.statement: 9M operating cash flow conversion 113% vs 10-year average 63%; helped by customer advances and revenue growth
items.quote: this kind of a help happened because of some of the customer advances which helped this year, number one. But, of course, if you look at the absolute number of the NWC is close to the similar number for the March and December, but the revenue has increased, that's really helped.

items.statement: Customer advances expected to be ongoing; 5-year cash conversion should be better than last 10 years
items.quote: Yes, that's a fair assumption.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 2,092 crore, similar to September quarter; debt/EBITDA decreased to ~1.2x
items.quote: Our net debt stood at Rs. 2,092 crore which is similar range of quarter ended September and debt to EBITDA has further decreased to aroun d 1.2x

items.statement: Debt may increase slightly to fund CAPEX but debt/EBITDA will remain comfortable
items.quote: See, debt may be increased slightly , it is needed. But your debt by EBITDA will be there in a better way.

items.statement: Underwent ~110 quality audits in 9M FY26; passed all without critical points
items.quote: The nine months the Company underwent close to 110 quality audits by multiple regulatory agencies and several customers. Company has successfully passed audit inspections without any critical points.

items.statement: 92 DMFs filed to date; 4 formulation dossiers filed and 5 approvals received in 9M FY26; 91 products filed cumulatively
items.quote: Relatively, 92 DMFs have been filed to date. In developed markets, 4 formulation dossiers have been filed and 5 approvals received during the 9 -month period. Overall, 91 products have been filed cumulatively to date.

items.statement: CDMO pipeline well-balanced across big pharma and mid/small biotechs; majority programs use advanced tech platforms
items.quote: Pipeline momentum has remained very healthy with well-balanced mix of big pharma clientele and also mi d- and small-size biotechs. Majority of the pipeline programs under execution utilize several advanced technology platforms.

items.statement: Decided not to enter large-scale MAB manufacturing and sterile manufacturing despite opportunities
items.quote: Right now, we decide not to enter into large-scale MAB manufacturing, we don't want to do that. That's the area we decide not to get in. And the other area we decide not to enter right now is also sterile manufacturing.

items.statement: R&D spend 4.1% of sales for 9M FY26, up 8% YoY; in line with full-year target
items.quote: overall R&D spend was at 4.1% of our sales for the 9 months FY'26 increased by 8% year-on-year including our spend on the Cell and Gene lab space. This R&D spend is in line with our full year target

items.statement: CDMO revenue lumpy quarter-to-quarter; some commercial supplies only once or twice per year
items.quote: some of these supplies are once or twice per year , in some cases . So, there's not necessarily a supply going out every month . It comes down to their internal manufacturing capacity and demand requirements.

items.statement: ESG score 81/100 from S&P Global, up 10 percentage points
items.quote: one of the leading agency S&P Global has published its 202 5 ESG score in which Laurus reported an impressive 10 percentage point in this, the score achieving 81 out of 100 points.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.6%-1.7% by end of FY27
items.quote: Our guidance is at the end of FY27, we are still hopeful that we will probably be achieving 1.6%-1.7% of credit cost.

items.statement: Advances CAGR guidance of 15%-17% over next 2-3 years with deposit growth higher
items.quote: Also, I think just to reiterate our overall guidance that we have given is a 15% to 17% CAGR on advances and deposit growth to be higher than that.

items.statement: Gross NPA ratio improved to 3.3% and Net NPA to 1.0% after ARC sale
items.quote: Following this sale, our Gross NPA ratio improved sharply to 3.3%, and Net NPA declined to 1%.

items.statement: Bank-wide gross slippages declined to Rs 1,314 crores in Q3 from Rs 1,590 crores in Q2
items.quote: Bank-wide gross slippages declined to Rs 1,314 crores in Q3FY26 from Rs 1,590 crores in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: EEB slippages moderated to Rs 942 crores from Rs 1,118 crores in Q2
items.quote: The largest contribution to this improvement came from the EEB segment, where slippages moderated to Rs 942 crores, compared with Rs 1,118 crores in Q2FY26.

items.statement: EEB collection efficiency improved to 98.2% for Q3 and 98% for December
items.quote: Within the EEB portfolio, full-quarter collection efficiency for Q3 stood at 98.2%, and for the month of December specifically, it was 98%, up from 97.5% in September.

items.statement: EEB 0-90 DPD pool reduced to Rs 2,310 crores (4.6% of advances) from Rs 2,497 crores (4.8%)
items.quote: In the EEB portfolio, the combined 0–90 DPD pool (SMA0, SMA1, SMA2) reduced to Rs 2,310 crores, or 4.6% of EEB advances, from Rs 2,497 crores, or 4.8%, in the prior quarter.

items.statement: NIM improved sequentially to 5.9% from 5.8% driven by 20 bps reduction in cost of deposits
items.quote: NIM for the quarter improved to 5.9%, compared with 5.8% in Q2, supported by a nearly 20-bps reduction in the cost of deposits.

items.statement: Expect 35-50 bps NIM improvement from cost of funds over next 2-3 quarters, offset by 11 bps repo rate impact
items.quote: We expect this cost of funds improvement to continue over the next two to three quarters and the NIM trajectory it will improve from. So, there are about 4 components. One is the cost of funds where we are confident because of the term deposits coming for renewal in Q4 as well as in Q1 and Q2 that we should see anywhere between a 35 basis points to a 50 basis points improvement in the NIMs because

items.statement: Confident Q2 was NIM bottom for FY26, expect further improvement from current levels
items.quote: We are confident that in Q2, we saw a bottom of the NIMs, at least for this financial year, and therefore, some further improvement should be expected from these levels.

items.statement: Total deposits grew 11% YoY to Rs 1.57 lakh crores; retail deposits grew 17% YoY
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, our total deposits stood at Rs 1.57 lakh crores, compared to Rs 1.41 lakh crores a year ago — reflecting a growth of 11% YoY.

items.statement: Bulk deposits declined 6% QoQ, share reduced to 28% from 29% in Q2 and 31% a year ago
items.quote: Bulk deposits declined by 6% QoQ, and their share in total deposits reduced further to about 28%, compared with 29% in the previous quarter and 31% a year earlier.

items.statement: CASA declined 4% YoY to Rs 42,730 crores due to savings rate cuts; core granular savings deposits gaining traction
items.quote: CASA deposits stood at Rs 42,730 crores, showing a 4% YoY decline. This was primarily the result of the savings rate reductions undertaken in Q1 and subsequently in Q2 and Q3.

items.statement: Retail deposit mix (CASA + retail term deposits) improved to 72% of total deposits
items.quote: CASA now stands at 27% of total deposits, and the overall retail mix — including CASA and retail term deposits — improved further to 72%, signalling continued strengthening of deposit granularity and stability

items.statement: Gross advances grew 10% YoY to Rs 1.45 lakh crores; underlying growth 12% YoY adjusting for NPA sale
items.quote: As of 31st December 2025, Gross Advances stood at Rs 1.45 lakh crores, representing 10% YoY growth and on a sequential basis, growth was healthy at 4%.

items.statement: EEB book at Rs 50,076 crores, down 11% YoY but would have grown 2% QoQ adjusting for NPA sale
items.quote: The EEB book stood at Rs 50,076 crores, showing a 11% YoY and 3% sequential decline. However, when normalised for the NPA sale to ARC of Rs 2,759 crores undertaken during the quarter, the portfolio would have recorded a growth of 2% QoQ.

items.statement: Non-EEB portfolio grew 25% YoY, now 65% of total advances; Retail Assets up 57% YoY, Wholesale Banking up 32% YoY
items.quote: Our non-EEB portfolio continues to demonstrate strong, broad-based growth at 25% YoY driven by sustained momentum across both Retail Assets and Wholesale Banking, now accounts for nearly 65% of total advances

items.statement: Secured book grew 27% YoY to 57% of advances; EEB 22%, SBAL 12%, Wholesale 31%, Housing 23%, Retail 10%
items.quote: The secured book grew 27% YoY and now accounts for 57% of total advances, The shift towards secured lending remains a key strategic lever for enhancing asset quality and improving the long-term risk profile.

items.statement: Added 20 new branches and converted 57 housing centres to full branches; total branches 1,831
items.quote: We also continued to expand our distribution footprint, taking the branch network to 1,831 branches, with 20 new branches added during the quarter and the conversion of 57 housing centres into full-fledged banking branches.

items.statement: Created Rs 120 crores incremental gratuity provision due to new labour codes notified on 21 Nov 2025
items.quote: As a result of this assessment, we have created an incremental provision of Rs 120 crores towards gratuity during the quarter.

items.statement: Operating expenses rose 6% QoQ to Rs 1,934 crores due to Rs 120 crores labour code provision; opex-to-assets at 3.9%
items.quote: Operating expenses for the quarter were Rs 1,934 crores, rising 6% sequentially. This increase was largely due to the Rs 120 crores provision for gratuity following the implementation of the new labour codes.

items.statement: Sold Rs 3,707 crores written-off portfolio at ~9% valuation (Rs 126 crores cash to other income) and Rs 3,165 crores NPAs at ~18% (Rs 303 crores cash offset provisions)
items.quote: We sold Rs 3,707 crores of written-off portfolio, which was realized at a valuation of roughly 9%. Out of the total Security Receipts (SRs) issued for this portfolio, our share stood at about 62%. On the cash side, we received Rs 126 crores, and this inflow has been recorded under ‘Other Income’. In addition to this, we also sold Rs 3,165 crores of NPAs, unsecured loan in EEB and ABG book, at a va

items.statement: RBI supervision completed with no material PSL classification qualifications
items.quote: So, this year, the RBI supervision has been completed. We don't have any -- I would say, any remarkable qualification because we are very prudent in classifying the PSL and taking steps. So, nothing material, I would say, has been pointed out.

items.statement: Senior executive exits attributed to personal reasons; team stable with no indication of further departures
items.quote: Let me tell you, there is no other issues and it was absolutely because of his family residing in Bombay, and also, he has got some other more, I would say, compulsions for that year. So he came up very clearly to me and stated that in normal circumstances, actually, he would not have opted for his resignation.

items.statement: West Bengal (42% of MFI) collection efficiency unaffected by reported disturbances; maintaining >99% regular collections in affected districts
items.quote: I can give one simple statistic. So, the districts where these have been reported, our collection efficiency has not been affected. So, we are still doing more than 99% collection in those areas on regular loans.

items.statement: RoA 0.4% and RoE 3% for Q3; 9M RoA 0.5% and RoE 4%
items.quote: Profitability ratios for Q3 — RoA at 0.4% and RoE at 3% — reflect the combined impact of one-off items and the cost of reducing NPAs measures undertaken during the quarter.

items.statement: Capital Adequacy Ratio at 17.8% and Tier I at 17.0% including 9M profits
items.quote: Our capital position remains robust. Including 9MFY26 profit, the Capital Adequacy Ratio stands at 17.8% and Tier I capital at 17.0%, providing ample headroom to support future growth

items.statement: Management confident of achieving 20% YoY revenue growth in FY26 and expects to beat target in Q4
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving 20% year -on-year revenue growth in FY '26. Particularly, Agentic AI and GenAI is increasingly becoming embedded within larger transformation, mandates rather than being pursued as a stand-alone initiative.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin outlook maintained at around 30%
items.quote: We continue to maintain a medium-term EBITDA margin outlook of around 30%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 32.4%, up 194 bps QoQ; 9M FY26 margin declined to 29.9% from 37.8% due to strategic investments
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 32.4%, expanding by 194 basis points sequentially. This improvement was driven by operating leverage from revenue growth, better execution efficiency and the benefits of investments made in earlier quarters.

items.statement: No more large event spending planned; margins expected to normalize as overseas initiatives scale
items.quote: No, no planned event. Nothing. This is very small. Now, even in future, –at least for next 2, 3 years, you will not see those kinds of events which we have attended in last 2, 3 quarters, and which has impacted on EBITDA.

items.statement: Demand healthy across core services (ERP, cloud, data engineering, AI, Salesforce, enterprise transformation); strong pipeline in US, UAE, Australia
items.quote: From a business standpoint, demand across our core services offering remains healthy, particularly in ERP, cloud, data engineering, AI, Salesforce and enterprise transformation programs. Our pipeline remains healthy and strong demand visibility, especially in the U.S., UAE and Australia.

items.statement: US tariff/volatility not affecting business as model is offshore; demand not a problem, supply of talent is
items.quote: See, I'm listening this question, I think, for the last 7 to 8 quarters . And again, I will repeat, we are working on the niche technology. So, demand is not problem for us. Problem is supply. Good resources, finding good resources.

items.statement: Active pipeline gives good visibility for next 2 quarters supported by new deal wins and deeper engagement with existing accounts
items.quote: The active pipeline give us good visibility for the next 2 quarters, supported by both new deal wins and deeper engagement with existing accounts.

items.statement: Top 5 clients contribute 40%, top 10 contribute 54% of 9M FY26 revenue; 78% revenue from overseas customers
items.quote: Now, from a client concentration perspective, our top 5 clients and top 10 clients contributed 40% and 54% of our revenues, respectively, in 9 months FY '26. Approximately 78% of our revenues were derived from overseas customers, underscoring the increasin g contribution of global markets.

items.statement: Cross-sell and upsell very significant; 15-20 large enterprise clients contribute over 60% of revenue
items.quote: I would say, 15, 20 customers, which contribute around over 60% of our revenue. And these customers are mostly large enterprise clients only.

items.statement: IT Services 97.4% of 9M FY26 revenue; Product segment 2.6% but strategically important and scaling disciplined
items.quote: In terms of revenue by business, our IT Services segment contributed 97.4% to our revenue in the 9-month FY '26, while our Product segment contributed 2.6% to our revenue for the same period.

items.statement: Odoo practice >20% of total revenue; 80-85% of Odoo revenue from overseas; recurring revenue 10-15% annually
items.quote: Out of the total Odoo revenue, 80%, 85% comes from out of India, remaining 10%, 15% comes from India for Odoo. And we are not breaking it technology-wise. If you ask that how much revenue we have done in Odoo, so it's more than 20% of our total revenue.

items.statement: DFM (Data Flow Manager) has 2 customers onboarded, 1 in trial, 3 in NDA process; all multi-million/billion dollar companies
items.quote: We have two customers onboarded. Third is taking the trial. And three customers are in process to sign the NDA. All these customers are multimillion or billion company.

items.statement: DFM revenue model recurring; first customer $50k, second $10-20k; customization to be charged later
items.quote: For first customer, we have charged $50,000, and that is the recurring. For second customer, we have charged approximately $10,000 to $20,000, between. I do not remember the exact number. It will be recurring.

items.statement: DFM 2.0 launched with Agentic AI developed in-house; claims 7-8x cheaper than peer Cloudera with more features
items.quote: Manish, if I say 7x to 8x, they are costly, and they have very less feature as compared to us, so is this the correct statement? Manish Gurnani: Easily.

items.statement: Board approved wholly owned subsidiary in Australia to support growth and scale in that region
items.quote: Further, considering the growth potential we see in Australia, the Board has approved the initiation of a wholly owned subsidiary to support growth and scale in that region.

items.statement: Cash generation strong; cash and equivalents INR13 crores; net debt-free
items.quote: Cash generation remains strong, and our balance sheet continues to be healthy with cash and cash equivalents of INR13 crores. We still remain a net debt -free company.

items.statement: Third interim dividend of INR5/share declared in Q3; total FY26 dividend INR11/share; committed to balance growth and shareholder returns
items.quote: During the quarter, Board declared a third interim dividend of INR5 per share, taking the total dividend for the FY26 to INR11 per share.

items.statement: No buyback or promoter buying planned despite stock price decline
items.quote: No plan. I think we have given good numbers for the confidence. If it is not giving the confidence, then what I can do.

items.statement: Certified Great Place to Work Jan 2026-Jan 2027; using AI internally for productivity and delivery efficiency
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that our organization has been certified as a Great Place to Work effectively January 2026 to January 2027. This reflects the trust of our employees and the strong culture we continue to build, which support our growth and long-term success.

items.statement: New labour code implementation to increase gratuity expense in Q4; impact not material and no change to EBITDA margin guidance
items.quote: Additionally, pursuant to the implementation of new labo ur code, gratuity expense is expected to increase. The impact is not material and will be recognized in Q4 without any changes to our EBITDA margin guidance.

items.statement: No pricing pressure from clients; clients focused on output acceleration with AI rather than rate negotiation
items.quote: While we continue to optimize its usage, we have not seen pricing pressure from clients. Instead clients are focused on improving output and accelerating ERP, cloud, data engineering and transformation programs with AI rather than negotiating lower rates.

items.statement: Shift toward fixed-cost/structured T&M engagements to control resources and benefit from productivity gains
items.quote: Shift towards fixed cost are structured T&M engagements where we control resources and benefit directly from productivity gains. As seen during the Q4 FY '25 transition from T&M to fixed cost project, we will continue to prioritize these models as they support pricing discipline and long-term client value.

items.statement: PAT Q3 FY26 INR9.8 crores, margin 23.2%; EPS INR4.13 vs INR3.5 in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Profit after tax for Q3 stood at INR9.8 crores, translating into PAT margin of 23.2%. Earnings per share for the quarter was INR4.13 compared to INR3.5 per share in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: DFM product success depends heavily on luck, long sales cycles to reach decision-makers, and word-of-mouth adoption
items.quote: Product is something that many people develop, and many times, good product, excellent idea . But building a product is 10%, 90% is your luck and sales. So, if things will work, then it will be big. If it will not -- that's why I did not mention anything about DFM in the PPT because we are still talking to the customers, and customer cycle is very long, cumbersome cycle because they are the decisi

items.statement: AI efficiency gains may slightly impact time-and-material engagements but aligns with strategy
items.quote: While this improved efficiency, may slightly impact on time and material engagements, it aligns with our strategy. Shift towards fixed cost are structured T&M engagements where we control resources and benefit directly from productivity gains.

items.statement: No fundamental change in strategy for next 2-3 years; priorities: scale core services, deepen global client relationships, increase large long-tenure engagements, selectively scale products
items.quote: There is no fundamental change in our strategy direction for the next 2 -3 years. Our priorities remain consistent and well defined. We will continue to scale our core services business, deepen relationship with global clients and increase the share of large, long tenure engagements. At the same time, we will selectively scale our product in a calibrated manner.

items.statement: Qualified deal pipeline at USD 61 million across 50 enterprise opportunities, 78% from non-SCF products
items.quote: It is now at USD 61 million across 50 enterprise opportunities. USD 61 million across 50 enterprise opportunities. And the heartening part is nearly 78% of this pipeline, which you are se eing, is coming from non -supply chain finance products

items.statement: Pipeline diversified: India/South Asia 42%, Southeast Asia 36%, GCC and Africa remainder
items.quote: From a geographic standpoint, the pipeline you will again see is very well diversified, led by India and South Asia at around 42%, Southeast Asia at 36%, and we have seen growing traction in GCC and Africa, which contributes to the remainder.

items.statement: PSB Xchange: 3 lender integrations live, 3 in progress, 15 agreements under process; 5 sourcing partner integrations live, 8 in progress, 23 agreements under process
items.quote: On the lender side, we have three real integrations live, three in progress. On the sourcing side, we have five integrations live and eight are in progress.

items.statement: PSB Xchange transaction activity: 80 corporate deals initiated, Rs 12,000 crores limit requests, Rs 4,000 crores approved across 19 anchor corporates
items.quote: Approximately Rs. 12,000 crores of limits requests have been requested on the platform. So, these 80 corporates, they have requested around Rs. 12,000 crores of limits. Out of this, Rs. 4,000 crores of limits have already been approved by the banks.

items.statement: PSB Xchange operational in 26 locations across India with dedicated field credit and technology teams
items.quote: So, we have moved from being just a pure tech company in PSB Xchange. Now we have 22 locations beyond Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai. That means a total of 26 locations across the country where we have dedicated field staff available for PSB Xchange.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 52% YTD nine months, PAT margin 27%; Consolidated EBITDA 19.95%, PAT 7.75% due to service business mix
items.quote: At the standalone level, our core product business continues to operate at EBITDA margin of 52% on a Y-T-D basis, that is for nine months, and a PAT margin of 27%. On a consolidated level, our EBITDA margins are 19.95% and PAT margins are 7.75%

items.statement: Product portfolio (SCF, PSB Xchange, cash management, trade finance) EBITDA margin 43.4% for nine months; SCF alone 52%, other products 40-45% steady state, PSB Xchange 28-33%
items.quote: So, total EBITDA margin for all these products is currently 43.4%. And with respect to the future growth, I think Raja can explain. Raja Debnath: So, just to reiterate, standing on just SCF, if you look at just SCF numbers, ther e our EBITDA margin is 52

items.statement: Management sticks to previous H1 guidance, expects to meet or surpass it; no new FY27 guidance given
items.quote: Whatever guidance we had given during H1, we are in line to meet those. So, no change in the guidance. So, we stick to that.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated revenue Rs 104 crores, nine months Rs 214 crores; product revenue Rs 82.4 crores (Rs 53.85 crores from Veefin + organic products), services Rs 131.3 crores
items.quote: The Quarter 3 revenue was Rs. 104 crores and the nine - month revenue was Rs. 214 crores on a consolidated level, which is driven mainly by a combination of organic growth or organic scale and full impact of our consolidation.

items.statement: PSB Xchange revenue model: 30 bps sourcing fee, 20 bps technology (graded), 15 bps onboarding services; total 30-65 bps on AUM; partner share 10-20 bps if sourced via partner
items.quote: There is the sourcing of business angle from where we get fees, that 30 basis points. Then we have the technology , where it is 20 basis points in a graded manner. Then you have the onboarding services which we provide to banks for getting the channel partners signed up onto the platform for the bank, specific bank. There is another 15 basis points.

items.statement: Preferential round Rs 94.3 crores fully received; utilization: international expansion Rs 10 cr, product development Rs 49.33 cr, sales & marketing Rs 12 cr, general corporate Rs 23 cr over 12-18 months
items.quote: Out of the entire Rs. 94.3 crores, international expansion is Rs. 10 crores, product development is Rs. 49.33 crores, sales and marketing is Rs. 12 crores, and general corporate purpose is Rs. 23 crores. That is the breakup.

items.statement: Senior management on ESOPs with 4-year vesting linked to revenue and bottom line; new senior leaders joined last quarter for PSB Xchange operations
items.quote: Everybody who joins Veefin is on ESOPs, and ESOPs of senior management are always linked with the revenues and the bottom line of the company. So, the reward structure for senior management is always aligned with how well the company will do in the long-term. And all are on four year vesting periods in terms of ESOPs.

items.statement: Client agreements typically 5-7 year lock-in including major banks like HSBC; recurring revenue model provides predictability
items.quote: Yes, all our agreements that we do, they usually come with five year - seven year lock-in period, including the names that you mentioned. So, that is one.

items.statement: No new products in development; focus on monetizing existing 6 products (SCF, cash management, trade finance, internet banking, LMS, LOS) and PSB Xchange
items.quote: There are always products on the horizon but nothing that we are developing right now. Because these products that we have ended up building, these are massive products. So, all the investments that we have done, now is the time to actually juice out the

items.statement: Total addressable market across all transaction banking products estimated at USD 40-65 billion annually
items.quote: The total TAM across all of these products is between USD 40 billion to USD 65 billion annually.

items.statement: Revenue recognition lag of 9-18 months post deal signing due to integration and implementation; pipeline conversion not linear for near-term modeling
items.quote: First is that even after you sign a deal, the revenue starts hitting your account 9 months to 18 months down the line. Because once you sign a deal, post that there is an integration effort, there is an implementation effort.

items.statement: Partner-led implementation strategy with system integrators globally; no focus on building services revenue or associated hiring
items.quote: We are going for a partner-led strategy. Where we are partnering with system integrators globally. In terms of helping us on the implementation. So, we are not focusing right now on the service side of the revenue.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected flattish or marginal growth; AC segment degrowth 10-15% offset by SDA, LDA, components
items.quote: at best, currently, we are estimating a flattish kind of revenue for the current financial year FY '25 '26 marginal growth

items.statement: Medium-term revenue mix target: AC 55%, SDA/LDA 25%, Components 20-25% by FY28-29
items.quote: So that's the over all guidance that AC contributing 55% of the overall revenue and our SDA/LDA growing to 25% and component another 20%, 25%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 7.5-8% in medium to longer-term horizon
items.quote: overall, the company is confident that we will maintain margin -- EBITDA margin of 7.5% to 8% in medium - to longer-term horizon.

items.statement: Capex guidance INR450 crores over next 12-18 months; INR218 crores incurred in 9M FY26, INR225 crores more in next 6-9 months
items.quote: In our opening for this financial year, we have given a guidance that the company is looking at an investment of around INR450 crores over next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 capex INR44 crores for washing machine lines, component segment at Sricity plant
