items.quote: By the end of Q3 FY '26, we made steady progress across multiple key locations. We have incurred INR44 crores of capex in Q3 FY '26, primarily directed towards capacity expansion and equipment installation for washing machine lines, component segment at our new Sricity plant.

items.statement: Hisense JV facility construction complete, trial production on track, to commence production in Q4 FY26 for RACs, later front-load washing machines and TVs
items.quote: The newly formed JV facility, which was under construction has now completed the construction and trial production is on track and have progressed very well. With all key milestones achieved, the facility is now ready to commence production in the current quarter, which is Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Bhiwadi greenfield plant (Epavo) trial production started end of Q2, ramp-up in Q3, client approvals received, targeting profitability in FY27
items.quote: the new greenfield facility in Bhiwad i commenced production -- trial production in end of Q2. Q3, we have seen the ramp -up happening. And as in Q3, the AC market has recovered. There has been some sales, which has happened. But more importantly for us, the approvals from all the key clients has happened. And Q4 onwards, we are looking at reducing first the loss year-on-year. And definitely, FY '

items.statement: Order book for SDA and LDA extremely encouraging based on customer projections (not confirmed POs)
items.quote: So in terms of order book for both SDA and LDA, it is extremely encouraging to see the growth in SDA, LDA categories both.

items.statement: AC industry secondary sales degrowth narrowed to 10-12% in Q3 from 15% in H1; brands planning 15-20% growth over FY24-25 for calendar 2026 season
items.quote: most of the brands are planning anywhere between 15% to 20% kind of growth over FY '24, '25 numbers. And based on it, the current order book is very robust for us.

items.statement: Channel inventory estimated at 4-4.5 million units (old BEE rated), allowed to be sold till June FY26, expected to normalize post Q4
items.quote: Our estimate is currently and the trade inventory put together, the overall inventory level in the market is approximately at 4 million to 4.5 million is the kind of inventory currently in the trade

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 7.41% vs 6.39% YoY; improvement driven by better product mix (SDA, LDA, components at 16-18% gross margin vs AC 14-15%)
items.quote: The EBITDA margin reported at 7.41% as against 6.39% on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: New BEE norms and commodity impact driving 8-10% price increase in Q4 production; 50% from BEE re-rating, 50% from Oct-Dec commodity inflation
items.quote: both BEE as well as the commodi ty impact currently seems around 8% to 10%, especially for the production, ongoing production in Q4

items.statement: Commodity pass-through model protects EPACK margins; further commodity increases may require second price hike in April-June
items.quote: under the current circumstances, the second price increase is something which is imminent.

items.statement: Product business contributed 75% of operating revenue in Q3; AC segment declined 1% YoY, SDA grew 30%, Components 61%, LDA 74%
items.quote: Notably, our product business contributed 75% of total operating revenue during the quarter, reaffirming strong customer confidence in our core offerings and highlighting healthy market adoption across categories.

items.statement: Added 2 new customers in Q3; total customer base 67 in 9M FY26; top 2 customers now 35-40% of revenue (down from 70%+ three years ago), target ~30% medium-term
items.quote: Mr. Balasubramanian, I think we have now reached a very ideal situation wherein the top 2 customers contribute to 35% to 40% kind of revenue.

items.statement: Normalized payable days 90-100 days; Q3 reduction due to consumption of paid inventory with no new procurement
items.quote: Normalized payable days are between 90 to 100 days.

items.statement: Interest cost similar to last quarter (INR13 crores); working capital improvement ongoing to reduce interest cost
items.quote: I think there is some error. The cost is similar to the last quarter. So definitely, we are consistently improving our inventory level and working capital, and we are geared up to reduce the interest cost, but it is the same as last quarter.

items.statement: AC industry long-term demand projected at 28-30 million units by 2030; seasonal risks reducing with uniform demand across quarters
items.quote: by almost 2030, the industry is looking at a demand of anywhere up to 28 million to 30 million is the kind of numbers what everybody is projecting.

items.statement: Key risk: sustained high commodity prices could pressure demand despite pass-through; seasonal demand variability remains
items.quote: that definitely remains the concern, considering the market demand outlook if the commodities continue to grow at such significant high levels.

items.statement: Front-load washing machine outsourcing minimal in India; EPACK-Hisense JV to pioneer front-load manufacturing with Hisense as key customer
items.quote: currently, there's no meaningful outsourcing happening for th e front load. But at the same time, there are no established manufacturers also in India for the front load

items.statement: New BEE star rating norms effective Jan 1 2026; old rated production ended Dec 31 2025; old inventory sell-through allowed till June FY26
items.quote: the last date of production for the same was 31st of December. Our estimate is currently and the trade inventory put together, the overall inventory level in the market is approximately at 4 million to 4.5 million is the kind of inventory currently in the trade

items.statement: Hisense JV to initially manufacture RACs for domestic market, then expand to exports focused on Middle East, GCC, Africa
items.quote: The plant will initially manufacture RACs for domest ic market and will gradually expand to export market, particularly focused on Middle East, GCC and Africa

items.statement: Epavo (motor subsidiary) targeting profitability in FY27 after loss reduction in FY26; client approvals secured for BLDC motors for AC, washing machines, fans
items.quote: And definitely, FY '27, we will see this company trending into green from red.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 25-30%
items.quote: For the current year, we're looking at around 25% to 30% growth. We believe we can sustain a similar growth rate next year as well.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 25-30%
items.quote: We believe we can sustain a similar growth rate next year as well. This level of growth should remain the minimum, and as we continue to add more stores, there is potential for upside beyond this.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue expected to nearly double QoQ
items.quote: So, yes, sales growth in Q4 will be significantly higher almost doubling and based on that, we believe these numbers are achievable.

items.statement: Store expansion plan of 20 new stores by end of FY29
items.quote: Over the next two to three years, we are planning to open around 20 additional stores. If we look at a three-year horizon, by the end of FY '29, we expect to add about 20 new stores across our surrounding geographies.

items.statement: Near-term store opening plan: 1-2 stores before Akshaya Tritiya, 4-6 by Diwali
items.quote: In the current financial year, we are trying to open at least one store. Before Akshaya Tritiya, we are planning to open another one or two stores. And leading up to Diwali, we are planning around four to six store openings.

items.statement: Capex per store: INR 2.5-3 cr for 3,000-5,000 sq ft; INR 5-7 cr for 8,000-10,000 sq ft
items.quote: So, in general, see depend on the store size, the capex remains between INR2.5 crores to INR3 crores for the decent size of 3,000 to 5,000 square feet and for the 8,000 to 10,000 square feet, it remains between the INR5 crores to INR7 crores.

items.statement: Store payback period of approximately 9 months
items.quote: And so far as payback period is concerned, I think what our past experience is saying that within a period of nine months, in general, we get all our capex recovered.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 demand very strong due to high wedding count in Jan-Feb
items.quote: Demand in Q4 is very strong. The wedding season has started, and there are a large number of weddings in January and February. In fact, after the 30th of January, there are even more weddings scheduled.

items.statement: Consumer shift to lightweight and lower-carat (18K, 14K) jewellery due to high gold prices
items.quote: With the increase in gold prices, we’ve seen a clear shift in consumer preferences. Earlier, 22-carat gold was the first choice and there was strong demand for heavy -weight jewellery. However, as gold prices have continued to rise, custo mers are now increasingly preferring lightweight

items.statement: Silver demand strong due to affordability and design innovation
items.quote: In addition, silver jewellery is also seeing strong demand. There has been a lot of innovation and attractive design development in silver jewellery, and customers are a ctively buying in this category as well

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 8.64% in Q3 FY26 (up from ~5% YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR105.6 crore, up 39% QoQ and 89% YoY, with EBITDA margins expanding to 8.64%, reflecting operating leverage and better cost absorption.

items.statement: Inventory gains contributed ~INR 20 cr to Q3 FY26 gross profit
items.quote: Broadly speaking, if we look at it, the inventory gain is approximately INR20 crores.

items.statement: Inventory gains account for 25-28% of margin improvement
items.quote: Secondly, because gold prices have risen meaningfully, we have also benefited from inventory gains, which account for roughly 25% to 28% of the margin increase.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by mix shift to higher-margin diamond, silver, and value-added products
items.quote: Along with gold jewellery, diamond jewellery carries higher making charges, and over the last few years, our diamon d contribution has increased. In addition, silver jewellery and newer product categories which we have consciously introduced, carry meaningfully higher margin profiles compared to plain gold

items.statement: Silver and diamond margins higher than gold; combined share ~10-12% of sales
items.quote: Silver and diamond, if we speak broadly, contribute around 10-12%. The share of silver is about 4-5%, and the diamond share is also around 4-5%.

items.statement: Margins sustainable due to continuing inventory gains and mix shift
items.quote: The margins are sustainable because there are inventory gains. And this may continue because inventory gains are still increasing, and due to that, our business margins remain sustainable.

items.statement: Margins to continue expanding even if gold prices stabilize, driven by mix shift
items.quote: Margins will continue to expand we're seeing that trend already. In a stable or softer gold price environment, our mix shift really helps. We're broadening the portfolio and focusing more on lower ticket and new products, especially in silver, diamonds, and polki, where we have structurally higher margins.

items.statement: Launched lightweight jewellery brand Amoura across all stores; plans separate expansion
items.quote: Yes. So, we have already started our lightweight jewellery segment. We have a brand called Amoura. Currently, we have launched it across all our existing stores, and going forward, we definitely plan to expand it separately as a distinct segment.

items.statement: Plans to introduce 9-karat collections
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect lower-karat categories to continue growing, and we're working on expanding our offerings, including introducing 9-karat collections.

items.statement: Customer walk-ins 1,75,351 in 9M FY26 with 82% conversion ratio
items.quote: From an operating standpoint, customer walk-ins over the nine-month period stood at 1,75,351, with a healthy overall conversion ratio of 82%, indicating sustained purchase intent despite elevated prices.

items.statement: Weighted average gold cost ~INR 1,10,000 per 10g
items.quote: The current weighted average gold price is around INR 1,10,000.

items.statement: Long-term gold price CAGR of 9-10%; short-term may stabilize or decline
items.quote: One thing I can say with confidence is that, over the long term, gold prices tend to grow at around 9% to 10% CAGR. That kind of long-term growth is structural. In the short term over the next one- or two-years prices may stabilize or even decline.

items.statement: FY27 gold price outlook: potentially USD 6,000-6,500 if geopolitics persist
items.quote: For FY '27, gold prices have been continuously rising. Currently, we are already seeing levels around USD 5,000. If the geopolitical situation remains similar, gold prices could potentially move towards USD 6,000 to USD 6,500 though it may or may not happen.

items.statement: Initiated hedging for gold and silver purchases including through GML
items.quote: We have started some amount of hedging. We have initiated hedging, including through GML. So yes, hedging has begun.

items.statement: QIP process ongoing; update expected shortly
items.quote: Yes. The QIP process is ongoing. We are actively working on it and making efforts on that front. Hopefully, you should hear an update shortly.

items.statement: Granted 62,300 stock options (1,200 forfeited) to key managerial, senior, and long-serving employees
items.quote: Separately, on 4th November 2025, the Company granted 62,300 stock options under the Employees Stock Option Scheme, of which 1,200 options were forfeited on 17t h December 2025

items.statement: Employee and other operating expenses expected to grow 10-12% YoY
items.quote: Yes. Overall, you can assume a range of around 10% to 12% on a year-on-year basis. That is broadly the band.

items.statement: Commissioned 5 GW advanced module facility at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, taking total installed module capacity to 9.5 GW
items.quote: We successfully commissioned and stabilized our 5GW advanced module manufacturing facility at Vallam in Tamil Nadu. This takes our total installed module capacity to 9.5 GW.

items.statement: Gangaikondan project with 6 GW modules and 12 GW cells progressing as planned; module plant on track for Q1 FY27 commissioning, first cell out by December 2026
items.quote: Construction activities at the module plant are underway, with structural works and roofing in progress, and the facility remains on track for commissioning in Q1 FY '27. At the cell plant, construction activities, including foundation and sub-structure works, are underway, with critical long-lead items of utility packages under finalization. We are thus on track for a phased commissioning with th

items.statement: Total capex of INR 6,400 crores for 6 GW module and 12 GW cell plant at Gangaikondan, funded by INR 3,800 crores debt and balance equity including INR 1,500 crores from IPO
items.quote: So both this unit collectively, which is a 6 GW module and a 12GW cell, the overall funding would be for INR6,400 crores, which would require a debt of 3,800. Balance to come in the form of equity, of which part of the funds about 1,500 has come in from the IPO.

items.statement: BESS capex of INR 4,300 crores for 7.5 GWh integrated cell and battery pack facility, debt-equity 65:35, financial closure underway
items.quote: On the BES S front, the overall capex is at INR4,300 crores, which on a debt equity of 65:35, the financial closure for which is underway, would fetch some INR2,800 crores on the debt part, balance INR1,300 crores over the next 30 months as of now is planned to be funded from the internal accruals of the company

items.statement: Order book at 10.58 GW as of 9M FY26, up 28% YoY; diversified with IPPs 55%, C&I 21%, government/EPC 11%, distribution 13%
items.quote: Turning to our order book, as on 9M FY '26, it stood at 10.58 GW compared to 8.2 GW in the same period last year, representing a year-on-year growth of 28 %. The order book continues to be well diversified, with IPPs accounting for a significant share of approximately 55%, followed by a steadily increasing contribution from the C&I segment at around 21 %.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA INR 682 crores at 20.3% margin, up 154% YoY; Q3 FY26 EBITDA INR 205 crores at 18.5% margin vs 8% YoY
items.quote: The company reported a healthy 9MFY26 EBITDA of INR 682 crores at 20.3% EBITDA margin, recording a 154% jump from the same period last fiscal.

items.statement: Expect Non-DCR business to deliver 18-20% EBITDA margin on sustained basis going forward
items.quote: And going forward, we expect the Non-DCR business to deliver 18% to 20% on a sustained basis.

items.statement: Non-DCR realization expected at INR 14-14.5 per watt peak with current cell cost increase; DCR realization remains at INR 23-24 per watt peak
items.quote: So, with the current increase in cell cost, we expect the Non-DCR to deliver a realization of INR14 to INR14.5 per watt peak. And on DCR front, this change will not impact the DCR module price to go up. They still continue to remain at INR23-24.

items.statement: Sourcing cells from Southeast Asian countries to reduce China dependence; Chinese cells attract 27.5% duty while non-Chinese Southeast Asian cells land at similar pricing
items.quote: The company has started sourcing cells from Southeast Asian countries, thereby reducing China dependence. Furthermore, surging silver prices are placing pressure on the N-type cell input cost.

items.statement: Exploring LECO process, rear-side silver-coated copper pastes, and electroplating with copper-nickel barrier to reduce silver consumption per watt in cell manufacturing
items.quote: new process innovations in cell manufacturing, like LECO, rear-side usage of silver-coated copper pastes, and other such initiatives are being explored in order to reduce t he silver consumption per watt

items.statement: Module supply contracts designed as cost-plus with pass-through for cell price (88% of order book) and change-in-law provisions; BORM costs absorbed in P&L
items.quote: On the pass-through concept, the pass -through actually is only for the cell, not the BO RM always. And if we have a revisit of the order book, as of 31st December, about 88% of the order book does have the pass-through benefit for the cell price only

items.statement: Expect 30-35 GW+ utility-scale DCR demand in FY28; addressable tendered capacity of ~104 GW non-DCR and ~15 GW DCR for next two fiscals
items.quote: We believe that about 30-35 GW plus kind of a utility scale DCR demand will come through in Fiscal '28. We are expecting a healthy pipeline of more RFSs' to be announced in the coming quarters that will be adding to the utility scale demand.

items.statement: India added ~8.5 GW solar in Q3; cumulative 9M installations ~30 GW taking total to 136 GW; renewables now 50% of 510 GW total installed capacity
items.quote: During the last quarter, India added approximately 8.5 GW of solar capacity. On a cumulative basis, solar installations during the last nine months reached around 30 GW, taking the total installed solar capacity to 136 GW as of 31st December, 2025.

items.statement: MNRE raising minimum module efficiency threshold to 21.5% by FY28 for utility-scale and 21% for rooftop; ALMM List-II for cells and proposed List-III for wafers from June 2028
items.quote: The minimum efficiency threshold is increasing from 20% to 21.5% by FY '28 for utility-scale projects and the same for rooftop would increase to 21%. It is an intentional move by the Ministry to weed out unnecessary build-out of less efficient legacy systems.

items.statement: DGTR recommended 23-30% anti-dumping duty on Chinese cells; 90-day period for Ministry of Finance notification lapsed Dec 29, 2025 with no development
items.quote: The DGTR on 29th September, 2025 recommended to the Ministry of Finance a levy of anti-dumping duty on the cells imported from China in the range of 23% to 30% citing injury to the domestic cell manufacturers, on which the Ministry of Finance had to act within 90 days of such recommendation. However, the 90-day period for the Ministry of Finance to pass the notification has lapsed on 29 December,

items.statement: 16% of order book from exports; using UFLPA/FEOC compliant Southeast Asian cell supply chain for US exports; India's reciprocal tariffs make Indian cells unviable for exports
items.quote: Nidhi, 16% of our order book is from exports. Indian cells are unviable to use for exports because of the reciprocal tariff imposed on India as a country. And hence, a UFLPA compliant and FEOC compliant supply chain from other Southeast Asian countries needs to be worked out and have a pre-approval from the CBP for us to be able to export to the US.

items.statement: China's removal of 9% VAT export rebate from April 2026 seen as constructive, may moderate state-supported pricing and improve competitiveness in Europe and MENA markets
items.quote: Recent changes in China's VAT export rebate could meaningfully alter price dynamics in selected markets. We view this as a constructive development that may moderate the extent of state-supported pricing and encourage greater cost discipline across the value chain.

items.statement: Weighted average finance cost of debt declined to 6.5% in 9M FY26 from 7% in H1 FY26; supported by disciplined cash flow, improved credit profile, low-cost working capital facilities
items.quote: The company has continued to maintain a strong focus on optimizing its finance cost. Consequently, the weighted average finance cost of debt declined to 6.5% during 9MFY '26, from 7% in H1 FY '26.

items.statement: India Ratings upgraded long-term rating from Ind A to Ind A+ and short-term from Ind A1 to Ind A1+ with stable outlook
items.quote: I am pleased to share that during the quarter, India Ratings upgraded our long-term bank facilities rating from Ind A to Ind A+, with a stable outlook, and also upgraded our short-term rating from Ind A1 to Ind A1+.

items.statement: Headcount increased from 1,587 in Dec 2024 to 2,413 in Dec 2025 for new facility commissioning
items.quote: Our headcount has increased from 1,587 employees in December 2024 to 2,413 in December 2025, reflecting the addition of skilled professionals across manufacturing, operations, and project execution to ensure smooth commissioning of our new facilities.

items.statement: Entire 9.5 GW module capacity now TOPCon; all future additions including 6 GW at Gangaikondan will be TOPCon
items.quote: But I'm glad to inform that the entire 9.5 GW is TOPCon. And all our additions going forward, including the 6 GW, would be TOPCon.

items.statement: Vallam 5 GW facility leased for ~INR 400 crores at 8.5% over 5 years; annual lease payment ~INR 108 crores
items.quote: So, we have taken this for a ~INR400 crores debt financing. It is at 8.5% lease and it would be apportioned over a period of 5 years starting from this quarter. And on an annual basis, it will be ~INR108 crores which takes care of the interest on the liability also.

items.statement: Effective capacity utilization at 90% for Q3 FY26 and 88% for 9M FY26
items.quote: The effective capacity utilization for Q3 and 9MFY '26 stood at 90% and 88% respectively.

items.statement: China's VAT export rebate removal from April 2026 and surging silver prices creating input cost pressure; mitigated by cost-plus contracts and technology innovations
items.quote: In the short term, we are navigating a tightening input cost environment driven by shifts in the Chinese supply chain, including polysilicon production controls compounded by removal of 9% VAT export rebate from April 2026, which effectively shall raise the raw material cost.

items.statement: Top 10 customers include 7 repeat customers; order book diversified across IPPs, C&I, government/EPC, and distribution segments
items.quote: We do not believe that in the customer circle, where top 10 of our customers, about 7 out of 10 are repeat customers and are repeatedly granting their patronage to a credible name like Vikram Solar.

items.quote: And most of your overcrowding exists in the lesser efficient legacy systems. If you see the PowerPoint in the slide, we mentioned that the top 15 manufacturers control about 100 GW of supply. And then there are 95 other manufacturers that control the remaining capacity of 45.

items.quote: Out of the BOM, bill of material, let us say bill of material is 100. So, in that 100, around 20% to 30% typically will be semiconductor chips typically. Because remaining are some assembly, some other components, mechanical components, and testing.

items.quote: aim is minimum INR ( +1,000 ) crore next year onwards from data center type of business . So, that is our aim and a few hundred crores is not sufficient for us

items.quote: We are not anticipating much because of these metals . B ecause firstly , ours is a semiconductor or electronics company , where material , these variety does not impact us that much . M aybe overall in our materials , maybe 5% or so , maybe coming from so - called materials for

items.quote: is more or less 50 - 50 because we told 50 - 50 is the overall investment , 50 - 50 will be the more or less work share between both the lead bidders . So L&T and BEL, it is more or less 50 - 50 because investments and everything has to go together only

items.quote: we are not anticipating much change in the manpower expenses, which is around 14% typically of our turnover. We will have more or less similar figures only.

items.statement: EU defense cooperation opening new market; joint research opportunities with EU research fund. Quantification by April 2026
items.quote: It is too early to tell that right now. But definitely it is opening up a new market for us. And there is 1 more thing, new joint research opportunit ies also. Because I think they have told that there is a big r esearch fund also available with EU , where they want to have some joint development

items.statement: Airborne systems indigenization ~70-80%; some foreign subsystems retained due to proven testing. Module-level indigenization ongoing with DRDO/partners
items.quote: I can tell you more than 70 % - 80 % of airborne sensors are now of indigenous origin , but definitely a few are still of foreign origin because they are already te sted somewhere in some other platforms

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR 17,302 crore (+19% YoY); PBT INR 5,171 crore (+22%); PAT INR 3,845 crore (+21%); EBITDA margin 30% (vs 28%); EPS INR 5.26 (vs 4.36)
items.quote: till Q3, we have achieved revenue from operations of INR 17,302 crores as compared to INR 14,538 crores, which was up to Q3 of last year with the overall growth of 19%. The profit before tax increased to INR 5,171 crores up to Q3 as compared to INR 4,242 crores up to Q3 last year with a growth of 22%.

items.statement: FY26 sales guidance INR1,800-1,850 crores, PBT INR345-360 crores, 12-14% top-line growth, 20%+ bottom-line growth
items.quote: We expect to close the year with a sales of about INR1,800 crores to INR1,850 crores and a PBT of about INR345 crores to INR360 crores, a growth of about 12% to 14% on the top line and about 20% plus on the bottom line.

items.statement: Targets 20% top-line growth and 20% EBIT margin going forward from FY27
items.quote: We expect that we will get back to our targeted growth rate of 20% on the top line and an EBIT margin of 20% going forward.

items.statement: Order book INR1,939 crores as of 1 Jan 2026, up 19% from start of year, no large package orders this year vs INR600 crores last year
items.quote: As on 1st January '26, we have an orders on hand of INR1,939 crores, which is about INR60 crores higher than the same period last year. But there is one big difference. Last year, we had nearly INR600 crores of large package orders in this. This year, however, we have no large package orders in the INR1,939 crores.

items.statement: Q3 raw material to sales ratio improved to 48.1% from 51.8% YoY; YTD improvement 1.4% due to better mix and service margins
items.quote: The raw material to sales ratio for the Q3 FY '26 was better by 3.7% compared to Q3 FY '25. In terms of percentage, it was 48.1% in Q3 FY '26 against 51.80% in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Expect further 1-2% reduction in raw material cost percentage going forward from manufacturing capability development
items.quote: And this manufacturing capability to bringing raw material at the lowest price or the price which we want to build our sales for the compressor. So both put together, roughly we are expecting to reduce 1% to 2% further going forward.

items.statement: Capex spend INR54 crores YTD, expect total INR90 crores for FY26; additional INR200 crores for PLI project over next 1.5 years
items.quote: capex spend was INR54 crores. We expect a total capex spend of about INR90 crores for the year.

items.statement: Invested in new CNC machines from Japan and Germany to double centrifugal compressor capacity, available from Q1 FY27
items.quote: We have invested in a couple of new CNC machines from Japan and Germany to double the capacity in this line to meet the growing demand. The additional capacity will be available from Q1 next year.

items.statement: Zephyros ammonia-based refrigeration system commissioned as technology demonstrator; PLI clearance expected this quarter; Khione package sales picked up; Tyche semi-hermetic compressor sales commenced and scaling
items.quote: We also commissioned two Zephyros plants as a technology demonstrator, and these plants have been commissioned within our plant to see their performance. Learnings will be used to fine-tune the product for bulk manufacture under the PLI program. We expect to have this clearance during this quarter.

items.statement: Air conditioning and general capex commitment across segments remains slow; cold chain, ice plants, dairies, food processing continue to invest; oil & gas project finalizations picking up slowly
items.quote: Air conditioning is still running slow. General capex commitment across most segments is slow. That has not changed. What we meant in particular was the whole of the year '25, that is calendar year '25, no major project orders in the oil and gas sector, in the petrochemical sector was finalized.

items.statement: Process gas segment flat for the year; export sales expected INR140 crores vs INR124 crores last year, mostly MENA region
items.quote: Export order booking was on plan. We should be doing a sale of about INR140 crores this year compared to INR124 crores in the previous year. Most of the exports have been for process gas business and a significant part of it is into the MENA region.

items.statement: Net working capital INR276 crores, lower than INR288 crores YoY due to strong receivable management and customer advances; inventory remains a challenge
items.quote: The net working capital was at INR276 crores. This is lower than the INR288 crores in the same period last year. This is behind the back of strong receivable management and significant advances from the customers. Inventories, as I mentioned, is still a challenge.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with net cash position of INR395 crores as of 1 Jan 2026
items.quote: Company has maintained the status as a debt-free company and we, the company still has a net cash position of INR395 crores as on 1st January 2026.

items.statement: New labor code effective 21 Nov 2025 increases estimated gratuity provision by INR18.3 crores (one-time); leave encashment impact ~INR1 crore; ongoing impact 0.8-1% of total cost annually
items.quote: Based on our current assessment, the estimated gratuity provision has increased by INR18.3 crores. The amount is an estimate and may vary by end of FY '26. We are currently awaiting clearer guidance and further regulatory directions to finalize the specific requirement and impact on our year ending reporting.

items.statement: Interim dividend approved at 175% of face value (INR2), i.e., INR3.50 per share
items.quote: In line with our dividend policy, the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend at the rate of 175% on the face value of INR2 per share, that is INR3.50 per share dividend to be paid as per the regular practice.

items.statement: MD K. Srinivasan retiring after ~5 years; succession to Aman (promoter family) planned and structured; employee engagement score 86 vs industry 82-83; attrition below 10%

So, to answer your question, I mean, net-net, we expect very minimal, if any, impact on profitability because of increases in any of these material costs.

There is no effect of silver contribution on our non-DCR. On DCR orders, as I shared with Nitin, who asked the last question, that, you know, we are working on reduction of silver consumption.

items.quote: Similarly, we are working on improving efficiency from current levels of 25.2% to 25.8% by the end of this year using latest process technologies and know-how. This experience will extremely be useful in launching operations of our new 7 gigawatt TOPCon cell line. We are now excited and focused on commissioning and ramping up of our new cell and module lines progressively over the next four quarte

items.statement: Transformer business (Transcon) capacity to reach 16.75 GVA by Jul 2026; shifting mix to higher-margin MVHV and EHV segments; targeting INR 1,000+ cr revenue by FY28
items.quote: Transcon is performing very well as seen in the YTD numbers, with total capacity expected to increase to 16.75 GVA by July 2026, and change in product mix towards more lucrative MVHV and EHV segments. This business is expected to become a key growth contributor for us.

items.statement: Inventory piled up at Sep 30 due to GST issue fully liquidated in Q3; higher non-DCR sales in quarter due to customer receivables/site readiness delays
items.quote: Yes, so the inventory which was carried forward in September 30th has been fully liquidated. And as I said earlier, that is not showing in the revenue number this quarter because this quarter we had slightly higher non-DCR sales compared to DCR sales. And that was because of various issues with the customers in terms of their receivables and their delay in pickup which has now become very positive

items.statement: Depreciation normalized after accelerated depreciation on Mono PERC lines ended; new lines on standard 5-year schedule; sustainable consistent trend going forward

So going forward, you will see a more, I would say, a sustainable and consistent depreciation trend in line with our new assets coming online this year. And the variability will be very less going forward.

items.statement: Module utilization consistently 75-80%, cell ~90% (except new line ramp); best-in-class industry utilization; no client delays, only 1-2 week mix shifts
items.quote: On module utilization, we have consistently been between 75% to 80%. And on cell, we have consistently been about close to 90%, except for when our 1.2 gigawatts TCon cell line got commissioned. Now, these are best in class numbers in industry. When you compare on utilization, we are already at peak of utilization.

items.statement: FY26 total market demand (DCR+non-DCR) >50 GW annualized; FY28 demand expected 60-65 GW; actual cell capacity additions far below nameplate announcements due to financial discipline and execution timelines
items.quote: On the demand side, we are saying that FY26 should end with a total market demand, including the DCR and the non-DCR components of more than 50 gigawatts annualized. And by FY28 we would expect that demand to grow to about 60 to 65 gigawatts.

And then, 7 GW are coming up in June and September, you would just get about one quarter of r

This business is expected to become a key growth contributor for us. Our KSolare acquisition is also planned to be closed in the next one month

items.statement: FY26 cell production expected at ~20 GW annualized from current 1.6 GW run rate; FY27 production depends on new line commissioning and ramp-up
items.quote: So in the current year – the current run rate of production are about 1600 megawatts which equates to about 20 gigawatts of production for the full year. And for next year, it remains to be seen which lines actually come up.

items.statement: FY27 cell demand expected ~30 GW+ vs 15-18 GW in FY26; no oversupply expected given capacity addition pace
items.quote: That's correct. Like I said earlier, the total demand in the year is expected to increase to about 30 gigawatts plus, which compares with something like 15 to 18 gigawatts this year.

items.statement: Operational cell capacity by end FY26 expected at 27-30 GW vs earlier 54 GW expectation; nameplate announcements total ~200 GW but financial discipline limits actual build
items.quote: Chiranjeev already mentioned that last year there was an expectation that by the end of FY26 there would be operational capacity of 54 gigawatts, which the reality is that it will be somewhere between 27 to 30 gigawatts.

items.statement: New 7 GW G12R cell line due for completion between June and September; new lines take 6-18 months to fully stabilize
items.quote: Obviously, our lines are due for completion between June and September. But bear in mind that all new lines do take from 6 months to as long as 18 months to fully stabilize and start running.

items.statement: Effective capacity utilization target 90% of nameplate; 10 GW expansion will yield ~9 GW actual production after ramp-up
items.quote: The actual usable would be 90% of 10, that is 9 gigawatts.

items.statement: Accelerated implementation of 7 GW cell line due to favorable demand-supply outlook and opportunity to sell cells at attractive prices
items.quote: So, given our view was that the demand supply landscape is expected to remain favorable, we saw an opportunity, and that is why we decided to accelerate the implementation of a 7 gigawatt cell line.

items.statement: Majority of next year's production already sold out; order book changes are lumpy but discussion pipeline remains strong
items.quote: Like we've been saying, a lot of our production over the next year is already sold out. Changes in the order book do tend to be lumpy. So, it is very natural to see big orders in one quarter followed by slight decrease in the next quarter.

items.statement: Order book excludes retail sales (~0.5 GW/year, ~INR1,000 cr revenue); includes spot and short-term delivery orders
items.quote: And the order book which we show, we do not take into account our own retail sales, which is close to about half a gigawatt every year. It's about INR1,000 crores of revenue, which we do not take in our order book because this is a retail market.

items.statement: Non-DCR module pricing ~INR1.4-1.5 cr/MW; DCR module pricing ~INR2.2-2.3 cr/MW; mix shift of 3-4% impacts revenue but not margins
items.quote: When we sell a non-DCR module to a customer, when you look at the prevailing pricing levels, it is approximately around INR1.4 crores to INR1.5 crores per megawatt at which we sell these modules. When we sell a DCR module, the pricing is around INR2.2 crores to INR2.3 crores per megawatt.

items.statement: Non-DCR cell prices increased from sub-INR0.04 to ~INR0.06 per watt; silver cost share rose from INR0.01 to INR0.025 per watt
items.quote: So, it has gone up from levels of about sub INR0.04 to about INR0.06 now, as we speak.

items.statement: DCR cell prices stable above INR13 despite market talk of drop; industry not pushing price increases yet due to 6-month supply visibility and silver hedge rollover
items.quote: In fact, you know, as per market estimates, there was a talk that DCR prices would fall to as low as INR13, but we have not seen this drop. We are still seeing price elevation over INR13.

items.statement: 80-85% of order book dollar-based (cell and module, DCR and non-DCR); rupee orders mostly short-term
items.quote: So about majority, about 80%-85% of our order book is dollar-based. There are very few orders which we take on rupee-based. Those are mostly short-term orders. Cell and module both, be it DCR, non-DCR or be it cells, is all dollar based.

items.statement: Non-DCR margins maintained at attractive levels despite competition; dollar-term spreads unchanged as cost increases passed through
items.quote: So, our margin in dollar terms, we have been at pains to elaborate, that does remain unchanged. Because we've discussed the silver price cost increase, we've discussed increases or changes in other commodities.

items.statement: DCR orders executed in quarter were earlier contracts with higher margins; non-DCR margin compression seen last quarter but prices now increasing
items.quote: Maybe last quarter we had seen a slight compression, but it's now kind of started increasing. Prices have started increasing.

items.statement: 7 GW expansion and TOPCon line are G12R technology; M10 uneconomical; industry moving to G12R/G12; existing players must upgrade causing production dips
items.quote: And our 7 gigawatt line is a G12R line and even the TOPCon which is operational is G12R.

items.statement: ALMM-2 shifts profit pool from module to cell; ALMM-3 will shift focus to ingot/wafer upstream over next 3 years
items.quote: And finally, we have always maintained that with the implementation of ALMM-2, all the focus of the market and the profit pool is basically shifting from the module to the cell business. And with the implementation of ALMM-3, the same effect will basically move from cell to the upstream ingot and wafer business

items.statement: ALMM-2 effective June 2026 for C&I immediately; IPP projects phased in after grandfathered projects; by FY28 India market expected 100% DCR
items.quote: As ALMM fully implemented, you would see that by FY28 India market, I think 100% would be DCR. It starts off in 2026 June, but then it is a gradual phased implementation.

items.statement: ~90%+ of current 61 GW solar + 20 GW hybrid pipeline is ALMM-1; auction slowdown since ALMM-2 effective
items.quote: So, I would expect as much as, you know, I am taking a very broad guess, but as much as 90% plus of the current pipeline would be ALMM-1.

items.statement: Silver cost share increased from INR0.01 to INR0.025 per watt; expected to decline with silver reduction proposals
items.value: INR0.01 a watt to about INR0.025 a watt
items.quote: The cost of silver, the share of silver has basically gone up from about INR0.01 a watt to about INR0.025 a watt. And we would expect that number to actually start going down with the proposal for reducing silver consumption.

items.statement: Only 6-8 players expected to successfully backward integrate with ALMM-3; scale, technology, integration key competitive advantages
items.quote: So, I think given that and if you look at how many companies will be able to also successfully integrate backwards in this short space of time, we do believe that it will be only about, I would say, six to eight players who will be successful in doing so.

items.statement: Industry consolidation expected over next 2 years as execution challenges increase; Goldi Solar acquiring small cell company cited as example
items.quote: We feel that many companies will find that actual execution and operations is far more challenging, and particularly with complexities around technology, scale, backward integration, etcetera. So, we will see more consolidation opportunities over a period of time.

items.statement: Green hydrogen: ~15-20 GW solar module demand per million tons H2; 5M ton target implies ~100 GW module demand
items.quote: But I think based on broad industry trends, we expect about 15-20 gigawatts of solar module demand for every million tons of hydrogen capacity. So, if the government target is 5 million tons, the total solar module demand could be about 100 gigawatts.

items.statement: Green hydrogen technical/economic viability expected to take 3-4 years; actual implementation very slow; tracking market closely
items.quote: But I think the truth is that the technical and economic viability of green hydrogen business is expected to take another 3 to 4 years. That is why you see the actual implementation on the ground to be very, very slow.

items.statement: Demand growth driven by residential rooftop (PM-Surya Ghar) and ALMM-2 implementation for private rooftop/open access; growth to surprise on upside
items.quote: We believe that growth and demand, you know, growth will surprise us on the upside. Now with the new capacities coming up and the increase in scale of our operations, particularly over the next two to four quarters, we are poised for a tremendous growth in our business.

items.statement: Proposed forays into storage inverters and transformers for scale and diversification benefits
items.quote: And combined with proposed forays into storage inverters and transformers, we are set to see an exciting growth journey with combined benefits of scale and diversification.

items.statement: Management sees clear visibility of surpassing EBITDA guidance of Rs. 5,500 to Rs. 6,000 crores for FY2026
items.quote: Ladies and gentlemen, we see a clear visibility of surpassing our EBITDA guidance of Rs. 5,500 to Rs. 6,000 crores for FY2026.

items.statement: Order book stands at ~Rs. 60,000 crores with a healthy order pipeline exceeding 100 gigawatts
items.quote: This is supported by a solid order book of ~Rs. 60,000 crores, a healthy order pipeline e xceeding 100 gigawatts

items.quote: Our module production increased by 94% on a year-on-year basis, and the cell production increased by 35% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Setting up 1 GW electrolyser facility with planned CAPEX of ~Rs. 676 crores; expected operational by FY27 with PLI of Rs. 444 crores
items.quote: We are taking early steps in green hydrogen market through setting up a 1 gigawatt electrolyser facility with planned CAPEx of ~Rs. 676 crores. The capacity is expected to be operationalized by FY27. And for that, we have a PLI of Rs. 444 crores.

items.statement: Inverter facility Phase 1 (3 GW) commissioned at Sarodhi, Gujarat; Phase 2 (1 GW addition) to be operational by FY27
items.quote: Waaree has already commissioned phase one of its three-gigawatt inverter facility at Sarodhi, Gujarat, with phase two comprising of 1 gigawatt addition to be operational by FY27.

items.statement: Expect to operationalize all module, cell, and ingot & wafer plants by FY27
items.quote: We continue to expand on stated timelines for our modules, cells, and ingots & wafers plant. We expect to operationalize all of these by FY27.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin expanded to almost 24% for 9M FY26 vs 17% last year; Q3 EBITDA margin beyond 25%
items.quote: And the margin, of course, has expanded to almost 24% versus 17% last year in the same period.

items.statement: Silver impact less than 9% on module basis; back-to-back cell tying for order book; wafer and silver costs managed with market pricing
items.quote: And as far as commodity price is concerned or s ilver impact is concerned, it's less than 9% on a module basis

items.quote: If you break that up, it will be in India, non-DCR would be about Rs. 14 to Rs. 15 and the US will be roughly around Rs. 24-25 and some orders are even above that.

items.quote: Furthermore, we have also secured no n-Chinese fully traceable polysilicon supply chain through our strategic investment in United Solar Holdings based out of

items.quote: Yes. It's ranging between around ¢7 as of now. And, of course, the scale benefit will also kick in once we continue to ramp up our operation

items.statement: India solar requirement increasing exponentially; retail demand just kicking in, expected to grow in multiples; C&I sector to jump significantly
items.quote: The requirement in India is actually only going to increase, and e xponentially so. We have actually just skimmed on the surface as far as the retail demand is

items.statement: Provisioned Rs. 294 crores for US investigation based on legal advice; no demand received yet but acting as responsible corporation
items.quote: However, we did consult our lawyers. And we are acting on the basis of the advice that we got from our lawyers in the US. And that's why we have provisioned the amount that we have talked about, around Rs. 294 odd crores.

items.statement: Chinese export rebates tapering off, cell prices rising from 4-4.5 cents to ~6 cents/Wp, making India a viable global supply chain alternative
items.quote: The export rebates are tapering off as you know. And that is actually, in a sense, I would say it's a good news. We are seeing that the cell prices from ¢4 to ¢4.5 are now jumping to roughly around ¢6 per watt -peak as a direct result of some of the actions taken by the Chinese government

items.statement: Orders considered firm with advances; retail ships on full payment; advances range 5-15% contract to contract
items.quote: It's generally contract to contract and ranges anywhere between 5% to even 15%.

items.statement: Acquired Meyer Burger assets (HJT manufacturing) in US; expanding Texas facility; actively considering cell manufacturing in US at right time
items.quote: As you have seen, we have gone ahead and acquired M eyer Burger. It's an HJT manufacturing play at this point in time that they had. We are expanding our facility in Texas as well

items.statement: Cell efficiency hovering at 24-24.5%; 5.4 GW cell capacity quoted at total watt peak output
items.quote: Directionally, it is in the region of around 24%-24.5% from a cell efficiency perspective. That's where we are hovering.

items.statement: New 10 GW cell capacity ramp-up estimated at 4 months per line (vs 6 months for first lines) leveraging 5.4 GW learning
items.quote: So, all of that taken together, we will actually start leaning more towards 4 months is what my estimation will be for the new 10 gigawatts of facility.

items.statement: Order book split 65% overseas, 35% domestic; domestic mix 80-85% non-DCR; cells consumed captively for module production
items.quote: So, that's roughly 35-65 split with 65 overseas and 35 is domestic. And we consume almost all of the cells that we use. And so, therefore, they go into our own module production.

items.statement: PPAs stuck due to combination of demand, bureaucratic, transmission capacity, transformer, bay, and land availability issues
items.quote: I think it's all of the above and also the fact that there are some real technical and geographical limitations in terms of just the necessary transmission capacity not being available, transformers not being available, bays not being available. So, I guess it's a combination of many reasons. Land not being available.

items.statement: Signed PPA worth 713 MW with creditworthy utilities and global C&Is; secured 6.1 GW connectivity, ~3,500 acres secured, 13,500 acres tied up
items.quote: We have already signed PPA worth 713 megawatts, with credit worthiness of utilities backing us up, global C&Is, and have already secured connectivity of 6.1 gigawatts, with land of ~3,500 secured acres and 13,500 acres tied up under acquisition.

items.statement: Progressing towards net zero Scope 1 & 2 by 2030, Scope 3 by 2040; first Indian module manufacturer with EPD certification; EcoVadis gold medal
items.quote: Waaree is progressing towards net zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2030, and Scope 3 by 2040. We are proud to be the first Indian module manufacturer to receive EPD certification and have secured gold medal in EcoVadis Sustainability Rating.

items.quote: And let's say if that continues, this Q4 will land somewhere between Rs. 620 crores to Rs. 630 crores.

items.quote: So, this year, I think we will be in that 65, 70 kind of range, right? We closed at 323 stores, so Y-o-Y in that 70 kind of handle versus March '25.

items.quote: More importantly, on a YTD basis, we are at Rs. 129.6 crores of pre-IndAS EBITDA versus Rs. 7.4 crores last year YTD. This reflects a margin of 7.4% YTD as compared to less than 1% in same period last year.

items.statement: Contribution margin (ex-inventory gain) improved 333 bps YoY to 33.3% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Contribution margin, which is a key product margin metric that we look at, excluding inventory gain, stood at 33.3%, an improvement of 333 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Store-level pre-IndAS EBITDA margins at 22-24% for stores at Rs. 10-12 cr annual productivity
items.quote: So, I think the way to think about it is that at Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 12 crores kind of productivity, the store level pre-IndAS margins are at about 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Baseline operating EBITDA margin expected in low-teens as cohorts mature to Rs. 10-11 cr productivity with 6% A&P
items.quote: broader cohort productivity gets to that Rs. 10 crores, Rs. 11 crores kind of numbers, the baseline margin for the business is going to be in, like, low teens at the minimum , with significant investment continuing on the A&P

items.statement: Same-store sales growth 12% YoY for 9M FY26; December exit rate in mid-teens
items.quote: Our customer b ase grew 25% year - on - year to 903,000 customers and same store sale growth of 12% year - on - year. Again, I would like to reemphasize that December same - store - sale s - growth exit rates were in mid - teens

items.statement: Festive demand strong in October, moderated in November, rebounded sharply in December
items.quote: Festive demand in October was strong, moderated in November, and then rebounded sharply in December.

items.statement: 323 stores across 130 cities as of Dec-end; added 12 stores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: As of December-end, we had 323 stores across 130 cities, having added 12 new stores during the quarter.

items.statement: Studded mix 61% YoY in 9M FY26 (lower YoY); offset by scale benefits, improved mix within studded, manufacturing efficiencies
items.quote: This is despite lower studded mix on a Y - o - Y basis of 61%. Thi s was offset by scale benefits, improved product mix within studded products, and manufacturing efficiencies

items.statement: Gross debt Rs. 650 crores; net debt Rs. 222 crores as of Dec-end
items.quote: So, gross debt is about Rs. 650 crores , n et debt is about Rs. 222 crores

items.statement: Ethereal (lab-grown diamond brand, 74% owned) in early discovery phase; seeing good traction, investing more capital
items.quote: We are seeing some good traction in lab - grown brand Ethereal. They have very few stores , and it i s kind of a discovery phase and it seems to be doing well. And hence we have decided to put in some more money

items.statement: Entry price points (sub-Rs. 20k/30k) vacated due to gold price rise; repopulated in November-December; no margin impact from price-point mix shift
items.quote: In our data we do not see that. It's not that, let's say, sub Rs. 20,000 or sub Rs. 30,000 product have lower gross margins or lower contribution margins, that kind of a trend is not there in the data.

items.statement: A&P spend at 5.7% of sales in Q3 FY26, down 129 bps YoY; driven by scale and high repeat mix (57.8%)

items.statement: Manufacturing cost efficiencies: absolute other expenses (ex-A&P) fell Rs. 11 cr YoY due to factory process improvements, capacity utilization, consolidation across 3 factories
items.quote: So, if the productivity at a factory level is X, which is a new factory ; o ver time, as people build more process efficiency, the amount of people, time, material etc. that you need to spend on, that goes down. items.statement: First quarter of reported net profit: PAT Rs. 71.5 crores vs loss of Rs. 26.9 crores in Q3 FY25; cash profit ~Rs. 122 crores
items.quote: As Gaurav highlighted earlier, this was our first quarter of reported PAT of Rs. 71.5 crores as compared to a loss of Rs. 26.9 crores in the same quarter last year. Importantly, the business generated a solid cash profit of about Rs. 122 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: FOCO-to-COCO store conversion continuing; PAT-accretive and economically sensible given cost of capital
items.quote: So, the consolidation is happening from FOCO to COCO, and that I think will continue because that is a very expensive capital structure that we are running related to what our cost of capital is. So, that consolidation obviously makes economic sense and is PAT accretive.

items.statement: Expects one NFO launch in next 2-3 months, possibly in Q4 FY26
items.quote: On the NFO, we are in the process of the regulatory approvals. We are, you know, quite close to launching one. So I think over the next two to three months, we will have an NFO out as well.
