items.statement: Targets dividend payout of 40-50% of PAT over next couple of years
items.quote: something between the range of 40% to 50% of our PAT is what we're looking at over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Sees industry-wide SIP discontinuation trend due to market volatility and digital investor behavior
items.quote: We are still analyzing data. But from what we can see from a preliminary investigation of the data that we find that people are discontinuing SIPs a lot more. And I guess it's got to do with the volatility in the market.

items.statement: Equity yields 35-36 bps, fixed income 28-29 bps, liquid/overnight 2-3 bps, overall 33-34 bps
items.quote: On the yields front, equity yields in the region of about 35 to 36 basis points, fixed income yields are around 26 -- 28 to 29 basis points, a liquid and overnight funds is in the region of 2 to 3 basis points. On an overall basis, our yields are in the region of 33 to 34 basis points.

items.statement: Closing AUM INR1.2 lakh crore, up 12% YoY; QAAUM INR1.22 lakh crore, up 13% YoY
items.quote: our closing AUM stands close to INR1.2 lakh crores, up by almost 12% year-on-year, supported by a base of over 50 lakh investor folios across India. Our quarterly average AUM also grew approximately 13% year-on-year to close at INR1.22 lakh

items.statement: 21 lakh active SIP accounts with monthly SIP+STP contributions of INR755 crore
items.quote: SIP continues to be a key strength, with over 21 lakh active SIP accounts, with monthly contributions from SIP and STP combined of INR755 crores.

items.statement: B30 monthly average AUM increased to INR289 crore from INR261 crore YoY
items.quote: our monthly average AUM from beyond the top 30 cities accounting for INR289 crores as of December 2025, increasing from INR261 crores in December 2024

items.statement: Opening 3-5 new branches per year to support distribution franchise
items.quote: Over the last 2 years, we have roughly opened about 5 new branches per year. And that's the rate we see ourselves growing, 3 to 5 branches a year from here on as well.

items.statement: Equity-debt mix 90:10; individual investors 87%, institutional 13%
items.quote: Our growth has been well-rounded, driven by a healthy equity-to-debt mix of 90% equity and 10% debt, and a balanced investor base, with individual investors contributing 87% and institutional investors contributing 13% of our assets.

items.statement: Focus remains on mutual funds; evaluating AIFs, GIFT City, passives for next 6-12 months
items.quote: But going forward, we will continue to focus on mutual fund because we believe that is still very underpenetrated and that's the core of our business. So we do not want to lose sight of the core. But we will clearly evaluate what should be the next steps in the next 6-12 months as to whether we should do AIFs, whether we should get into, say, GIFT City or passives.

items.statement: Works with 59,171 distributors; aims to increase wallet share with meaningful partners
items.quote: We work with 59,171 distributors. So, clearly, we have a distribution franchise. We have over 50 lakh folios. So, there are 50 lakh investors with us.

items.statement: New labor codes from November 2025 caused one-time INR10.15 crore employee benefit expense
items.quote: the company has accounted for a one-time employee benefit expenditure to the tune of INR10.15 crores, largely on account of new labor laws and IPO-related expenses.

items.statement: SEBI TER restructuring effective April 1 mainly segregates GST from TER and addresses exit loads
items.quote: These changes come into effect from April 1. By and large, the changes are more to what I can see to do with segregating the GST from the TER. So there is more clarity as well in case the GST is going to change over time that doesn't impact the industry going forward.

items.statement: Industry AUM INR80.2 lakh crore, QAAUM INR81 lakh crore, up 18.1% YoY and 5% QoQ
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, the industry AUM stood at INR80.2 lakh crores, while Q3 FY26 quarterly average AUM was approximately INR81 lakh crores, reflecting an 18.1% year-on-year growth and 5% quarter-on-quarter growth.

items.statement: Equity market share approximately 2.4% of total equity AUM
items.quote: Just off the cuff, it's about 2.4%.

items.statement: One-time labor code impact on gratuity (now 50% of basic) felt across industry
items.quote: the labor code basically has to do with gratuity. So the gratuity is now basically on 50% of your basic. So companies that were calculating it for lower than that need to recalibrate. So that one-time impact for that has already been taken into our books for the December quarter, and that's what Ashwin alluded to. But it will be felt across all companies. It's not only us, but it's going to be the

items.statement: Investing in sales team expansion and research capabilities on investment side
items.quote: We continue to invest within the sales team as well as part of expanding it. Also, we continue to invest in our research capabilities on the investment side.

items.statement: Will link dividend payout to PAT; currently targeting 40-50% payout ratio
items.quote: From what I see in the industry, the payout seems to be linked to your PAT. We will continue to do, we will move to that as well and link it to that over time.

items.statement: 9-month revenue INR310.7 crore (+18% YoY), PBT INR216.4 crore (+9% YoY), adjusted PBT INR226.5 crore (+14% YoY)
items.quote: In 9 months 2026, our total revenue stood at INR310.7 crores compared to INR263.3 crores. In 9 months 25, it is representing a growth of 18% on a Y-o-Y basis. In 9 months 2026, our PBT stood at INR216.4 crores compared to INR199.33 crores. In 9 months, representing a growth of 9% on a Year-to-Year basis.

items.statement: Guided for mid-to-high single digit revenue growth for India Tea business
items.quote: we have always guided for a mid-to-high single digit growth for the tea business

items.statement: Guided for Salt business mid-to-high single digit revenue growth with 4-5% volume growth
items.quote: we have always guided for Salt being again in the mid to high single digit growth on revenue, volume being about 4-5% and rest being value price mix movements

items.statement: Guided for growth businesses to grow at roughly 30%
items.quote: our guidance is for roughly 30% growth, and we will remain guided by that

items.statement: Expect to exit Q4 FY26 at 14.5-15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: when we exit Q4, we should be in the ballpark of 14.5 %-15% EBITDA margin

items.statement: Longer term target for India foods business is 17%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: a good foods business in India should be a 17% plus. We are targeted towards that in the longer term

items.statement: India branded business posted 15% underlying volume growth in Q3 FY26
items.quote: India branded business posted underlying volume growth of 15 %

items.statement: Growth businesses grew 29% and contributed 30% of India revenue, surpassing Rs 1,000 crore quarterly revenue
items.quote: Growth businesses, which you always guided for being 30 % of our business growing at 30%, we were quite in the ballpark, growing 2 9% and contributing 30% to our revenue, surpassing Rs. 1,000 crores in quarterly revenue

items.statement: Tata Sampann grew 45% all volume driven in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Tata Sampan n had a strong quarter, 45 % growth, all volume driven

items.statement: RTD grew 26% all volume driven in Q3 FY26
items.quote: RTD delivered strong performance, 26 %, again, all volume driven

items.statement: International business grew 11% constant currency revenue growth led by US coffee volume growth
items.quote: International business maintained a strong trajectory, 11 % constant currency re venue growth, primarily led by US coffee, which had strong volume growth as well

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA up 26%, margins expanded 60 bps QoQ and 120 bps YoY to 14.2%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA up 26 %, so EBITDA has grown roughly 2x of revenue. Margins expanded 60 bps quarter -on-quarter, 120 bps year -on-year to 14.2 %

items.statement: India Tea gross margins expanded handsomely as tea prices normalized
items.quote: Marginal movement in market share , albeit, gross margins expanded handsomely out here as Tea prices came back to normal

items.statement: Sampann MAPE positive and improving quarter-on-quarter, targeting double-digit EBITDA margin near to medium term
items.quote: we have hit double-digit. We remain confident of edging up the total business to close to a 15 % sort of number in the medium term, near to medium

items.statement: International margins not yet at normative levels, about a quarter away from normalized pricing
items.quote: international margins are not at the normative level, simply because the entire impact of the coffee cost increases have not passed through. We have had one more round of price increase in the US in the month of January, post which we would have broadly passed on the current cost increases. But that takes some time to translate into the P&L. So, I would say we are about a quarter away from seeing

items.statement: Tata Starbucks at 504 stores across 81 cities, opened 12 stores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: We opened 12 new stores during the quarter. We are now at 504. We opened our second reserve store in Gurgaon, and now we are present in 81 cities, with Jabalpur being the latest city to be opened

items.statement: National rollout of new go-to-market model 82% complete, will be 100% by first week of February
items.quote: We are about 82% done on the national rollout. By first week of February, we will be 100% done

items.statement: Added 160 distributors and transitioned 270 distributors to new go-to-market model
items.quote: 270 odd distributors have been transitioned to the new go-to-market model. And we have added 160 more distributors

items.statement: Passed on most tea price cuts to consumers in Q3, volume equal to value growth
items.quote: we have already passed on most of the increases in this quarter. And that is why you saw volume equal to value growth for the quarter

items.statement: Took another round of price increase in US coffee in January 2025
items.quote: We have had one more round of price increase in the US in the month of January, post which we would have broadly passed on the current cost increases

items.statement: Launched 15 new products in Q3 FY26, 55 year-to-date, innovation-to-sales at 4.8% approaching 5% target
items.quote: We have launched 15 products this quarter. Year -to-date is 55. And we have publicly said that we want to be around the 5% plus mark on innovation to sales, defined as revenue from products launched in the last 3 years. We are at a 4.8% at the end of last quarter

items.statement: Quick commerce now 15% of India business, e-commerce 4-5%, modern trade 14-15%, institutions 5%, GT 62%
items.quote: quick commerce is about 15%. The balance about 4-5% would be e-commerce

items.statement: Salt market share up 40 bps, Tea market share down 70 bps per Nielsen (covers 57-60% of business)
items.quote: Salt market share, we had volume growth. On top of that, we had market share growth as well of 40 bps. Market share of tea, as I mentioned, this only tracks about 57%-60% of our business, down 70 bps

items.statement: Tea prices broadly at 2024 levels with slight uptick end of Q3, coffee at 370-390 expected to come down but volatile
items.quote: Tea prices are coming down broadly to the 2024 levels, albeit in the fag end of Q3, we did see a little bit of an uptick on Tea prices, keeping a close watch on that. Coffee has started to come down, except after the Venezuela action, there was a bit of uptick on coffee. The forecast is that from the current , about 370-390, it should start coming

items.statement: Cash balance of Rs 1,272 crore as of Q3 FY26
items.quote: And we are now sitting with Rs. 1,272 crores of cash

items.statement: Tata Starbucks second successive quarter of 3% same-store sales growth, average daily traffic stabilized
items.quote: Tata Starbucks, second successive quarter of same store sales growth of 3%. Average daily traffic, which was the issue, is now more or less stabilized and ticket is holding

items.statement: Management says it is too early to give specific FY27 advertising growth or EBITDA margin guidance but remains optimistic about an inflection point in coming quarters.
items.quote: we remain still optimistic certainly for FY '27 outlook, but it will be too early for us to kind of give a specific number guidance at this stag e. However, we stay absolutely optimistic given where we have seen in FY '26, we should start to kind of see an inflection point over the next few quarters

items.statement: Management aims to improve EBITDA margins from FY26 exit levels as a top priority.
items.quote: Our endeavour is to improve margins from where we will end in FY '26, and that certainly stays as the top priority.

items.statement: Advertising revenue grew 6% quarter-on-quarter but declined 9% year-on-year due to soft FMCG spending; gradual recovery expected.
items.quote: advertising revenues were up 6% quarter -on-quarter and though they are down 9% year -on-year, reflecting a slow but steady pace of recovery.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 73% year-on-year to INR 4,180 million, the highest quarterly digital revenue so far.
items.quote: has resulted in a 73% year -on-year increase in our digital revenue to INR 4,180 million. This marks our highest quarterly revenue so far in the digital business.

items.statement: Digital business posted first-ever positive quarterly EBITDA of INR 564 million versus a loss of INR 1,362 million a year ago.
items.quote: it has resulted us to post an EBITDA of INR 564 million compared to a loss of INR 1,362 million in the same quarter last year. This marks the first quarter in which our digital business has delivered a positive EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 310 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 10.5% on 15% operating revenue growth and tight fixed cost management.
items.quote: With a 15% increase in operating revenue and tight management of fixed costs, our EBITDA margin improved by 310 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 10.5%.

items.statement: ZEE5 annual recurring revenue (ARR) crossed INR 1,000 crores this year.
items.quote: this year, we have reached an ARR business in ZEE5 of north of INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Released 39 shows and movies including 11 original series across 7 languages on ZEE5; launched Kids segment KidZ on ZEE5 and micro-drama app Bullet.
items.quote: We released 39 shows and movies, including 11 original series. This enhanced content offering across 7 languages, coupled with a revised pricing strategy on our digital entertainment platform, ZEE5, has resulted in a 73% year -on-year increase in our digital revenue to INR 4,180 million.

items.statement: Studio business released 8 movies (3 own productions, 5 distribution deals) and acquired theatrical and satellite rights for Kantara Chapter 1 and Akhanda 2.
items.quote: During the quarter, we released 8 movies, 1 in Hindi and 7 in regional languages, of which 3 were our own productions and 5 were distribution deals. We also acquired theatrical and satellite rights for Kantara Chapter 1 and Akhanda 2 during this quarter.

items.statement: Network viewership share gained 60 basis points year-on-year to 17.5%; weekly impressions above 28 billion and weekly reach exceeding 730 million.
items.quote: As we look at the viewership share for quarter 3, we gained 60 basis points year -on-year, taking our network share to 17.5%.

items.statement: Zee Marathi achieved 33.6% market share; South network share at 17.7%; Zee Bangla regained leadership in East.
items.quote: For Zee Marathi, the new content slate has resonated strongly with the consumers across Maharashtra, enabling us to achieve a market share of 33.6%.

items.statement: Content inventory advances and deposits declined by INR 1.2 billion over the last 9 months to INR 69.3 billion as of December 2025.
items.quote: Overall, our content inventory advances and deposits stood at INR 69.3 billion, down by INR 1.2 billion over the last 9 months.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments stood at INR 21.8 billion as of December 2025, comprising cash, fixed deposits, and liquid mutual funds.
items.quote: Cash and treasury investments as of December 2025 stood at INR 21.8 billion, comprising of cash of INR 5.0 billion, fixed deposits of INR 7.0 billion and investments in liquid mutual funds of INR 9.8 billion.

items.statement: Deferred further FCCB drawdowns; will not raise more until full visibility on deployment of proceeds.
items.quote: We have deferred the next drawdowns. And we have said it very clearly before also unless we have full visibility on the deployment of those proceeds, we are not going to go for any drawdowns.

items.statement: Headcount rationalization done across the company to remove overlaps between linear and digital businesses; operating at optimized cost structure.
items.quote: There were certain overlaps in linear and digital businesses, which made certain positions redundant. So that was the genesis of the restructuring.

items.statement: Star arbitration hearing adjourned to July 2026; verdict timing uncertain.
items.quote: the next hearing will be somewhere in July. So, I think that's all we can express on this call right now.

items.statement: Revised pricing agreement with a telco player and syndication revenues aided digital revenue growth this quarter.
items.quote: The revenue growth was aided by syndication revenues and revised pricing agreement with a telco player during this quarter, along with improved advertising revenues.

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization declining due to low capitalization in recent years and amortization of past tech centre investments in Bengaluru.
items.quote: This has been because in the last few years, our capitalization has not been very high. So, it is just a normal amortization as per the policy. And it is just that the rate of our addition to fixed assets has not been very high.

items.statement: Advertising recovery dependent on FMCG spending pickup and GST cut benefits, which are not yet fully visible.
items.quote: we are yet to see the full benefits of GST cut and a sustained pickup in FMCG advertising spend towards brand building.

items.statement: ESG score of 51 out of 100 in Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment, ranking Zee among top 5% of global media and entertainment players.
items.quote: progress we have made in our ESG journey, which is also reflected in our score of 51 out of 100 in the Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment in the media and entertainment sector. This ranks Zee amongst the top 5% of global players in this sector.

items.statement: Targets Rs 6,000 crore revenue in FY27 from existing assets; Rs 6,500 crore if US tariffs resolve
items.quote: So, in a nutshell, we can hit Rs. 6,500 crores next year. But Rs. 6,000 crores is very visible and with better margins.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 revenue around Rs 1,475 crore, ~14-15% sequential growth
items.quote: I think going forward, January to March looks like again a 20% turnover growth increase from the previous quarter. I think we are looking at 14%, 15%.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA per wheel of Rs 270 in Q4 FY26; aims for Rs 300 eventually
items.quote: So, I think Rs. 270 should not be far. We are hoping that in the fourth quarter we will hit Rs. 270.

items.statement: FY26 capex Rs 225-250 crore, part of multi-year Bhuj project
items.quote: FY 2026 will be around Rs. 225 crores to Rs. 250 crores. Part of CAPEX spend will share for the next year.

items.statement: Aluminum wheel capacity to reach 5 million annualized by March 2026; Bhuj adds 1.2M wheels and 0.6M knuckles by Diwali 2026
items.quote: So, it will be 6.2 for aluminum wheels. And it will be 1.1 for knuckles.

items.statement: CV and tractor OTR segments at 100% utilization; aluminum wheels at ~4.6-4.7M annualized, targeting 5M by March
items.quote: We are totally sold out in the CV segment. We are totally sold out in the tractor OTR segment. We are completely 100% running there.

items.statement: Aluminum order book sold out for next two years; strong domestic order visibility across tractor, aluminum wheels, CV
items.quote: Our entire order book for aluminum is sold out for the next two years.

items.statement: EBITDA per wheel rose to Rs 260 in Q3 from Rs 240 previous quarter; driven by higher utilization and value-added mix
items.quote: And the margin per wheel has gone up, from Rs. 240 in the last quarter, it has gone to Rs.260 this quarter, right?

items.statement: Expects margin improvement in Q4 as conversion costs decline with higher utilization
items.quote: With the higher utilization, our conversion costs are coming down, our fixed costs are coming down. So you will naturally see an increase in margins in the month of January to March.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across CV (16% YoY), tractor (12-13%), aluminum wheels, two-wheelers; export demand subdued due to US tariffs
items.quote: Despite sluggish demand in the export market, we delivered strong performance supported by healthy domestic demand.

items.statement: Europe now 58% of export revenue; expects European OEM business to double in FY27
items.quote: Europe has emerged as a key growth market for us and now accounts for over 58% of our export revenue. We expect this diversified mix to remain intact throughout this year.

items.statement: US steel wheel exports down Rs 300-400 crore annually; could recover Rs 500 crore if tariffs resolve and competitors face duties
items.quote: Our steel business of exports has been compromised to the extent of Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 400 crores from the American market.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through is absolute for aluminum (quarterly) and steel (quarterly); no margin impact
items.quote: Once for all, I want to clarify that raw material is a pass-through. So every three months there is a change in aluminum prices that is set up by the customer based on the previous three months rates.

items.statement: Negotiated price increases with two key passenger car customers; effective next year
items.quote: We have negotiated with two important customers of ours. And they have given us a price increase, and it is getting reflected slowly every year. Next year is going to be more effective.

items.statement: Alloy wheels 37% of revenue, 20% of volume in 9M FY26; aluminum knuckle revenue ~Rs 54 crore, targeting Rs 80-90 crore by year-end
items.quote: Alloy wheels have been a key driver, contributing approximately 37% to the total revenue and 20% in the volume terms.

items.statement: Expanding aluminum knuckle customer base beyond EVs into ICE; onboarding new OEMs in Europe for knuckles and wheels
items.quote: Our focus remains on broadening the customer base by onboarding additional OEMs where we are seeing encouraging progress.

items.statement: Thailand and Vietnam aluminum wheel exports under US investigation for circumvention; could benefit India if duties imposed
items.quote: Our competition in Thailand and in Vietnam is coming under investigation for circumventing duties. So if these two things happen, that those guys get caught up in that trap and suddenly tariffs with India open up, then we can hit Rs. 500 crores additional revenue from America.

items.statement: Bhuj capex funded by mix of debt and internal accruals; robust EBITDA accretion expected
items.quote: It will be a mix of debt as well as our internal accruals. So we foresee a very robust EBITDA accretion going with this fourth quarter and the whole next year.

items.statement: Tractor industry growth 12-13% YoY; company fully sold out in tractor OTR segment
items.quote: Tractors again have been showing us a 12% to 13% growth rate.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty persists; resolution expected in 3-6 months; export revenue at risk until resolved
items.quote: We are hoping by end of March, things should happen. And so next financial year is a clear home run for us once these tariffs are removed.

items.statement: Aluminum wheel greenfield capex cost high industry-wide; payback ~7 years on conservative assumptions
items.quote: We are getting our payback in seven years. Seven years we are getting our money back.

items.statement: Investing in digitalization and AI to be future-ready within one year
items.quote: We are investing money in digitalization. We are investing money in AI, and we will be very future-ready in the next one year.

items.statement: Government infrastructure focus creating robust multi-year project pipeline across all regions driving sustained cement demand
items.quote: Government's focus on infrastructure is translating into a robust pipeline of new projects nationwide with several marquee investments announced across every region, translating into solid demand.

items.statement: All-India cement demand growth expected at 9-10% for Q3 FY26 and 6.5-7% for 9M FY26
items.quote: Don't hold me to it, but we would expect anywhere between 9% to 10% all-India demand.

items.statement: 8-9 million tons capacity addition in Q4 FY26, 12 million tons in FY27, balance in FY28 for 22 million ton expansion phase
items.quote: So, we should have approximately 8 to 9 million tons more coming in this quarter. And the balance,12 million tons in fiscal '27 and then balance remaining will be in '28.

items.statement: 9-month capex at INR7,000-7,200 crores, Q4 FY26 capex INR2,000-2,500 crores, full year FY26 around INR9,500-10,000 crores
items.quote: INR7,000 crores to INR7,200 crores is 9 months and yes INR2,000 crores to INR2,500 crores will get spent in this quarter. So anywhere around INR9,500 crores, INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: Kesoram efficiency capex INR263 crores spent of INR382 crores committed; India Cements INR144 crores spent of INR601 crores committed; benefits from January-March 2027
items.quote: At Kesoram, we have already spent INR263 crores, out of the commitment of about INR382 crores. At India Cements, we have committed already INR601 crores and spent INR144 crores on the program.

items.statement: Cables and wires project INR500 crores orders placed, INR197 crores spent, 30% team onboard, civil work started, launch targeted October-December 2026 quarter
items.quote: About INR500 crores worth of orders have already been placed. We have spent INR197 crores. 30% of the planned team is already onboard, civil work has started, and we are on schedule to see the launch of our product in the October-December '26 quarter.

items.statement: Efficiency improvement program delivered INR86/ton last year, expected to cross INR100/ton this fiscal year; lead distance improved to 363 km from 400 km target, clinker factor 1.49 vs 1.54 target
items.quote: Last year, full year, on those quantified measurable targets, we have delivered INR86 per ton. My guess is we should be crossing INR100 mark on those efficiency improvement programs in this financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA per ton expected to be significantly better than Q3's INR916; employee cost increase due to annual increments and new plant additions
items.quote: To your second question, we will do much better than what we did this quarter. I don't want to get into any specific number.

items.statement: Cement prices improving across all segments with growing demand; INR3-4/ton naked realization increase and INR6-8/ton price increase vs Q3 average; cost pass-through expected for pet coke, coal, labor code, rupee depreciation
items.quote: I think we are roughly INR3 to INR4 on a naked cement realization basis up. If naked cement realization is up INR3 to INR4, prices are up , it's somewhere around INR6 to INR8.

items.statement: FY26 capacity 198-199 million tons, FY27 adds 12 million tons, FY28 reaches 235 million tons
items.quote: '26 should be 198, 199 and then 12 more million tons in towards '27, yes.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 capacity utilization expected above 90% of existing installed capacity
items.quote: January-March quarter, God willing, we will operate at more than 90% of our existing installed capacity.

items.statement: Kesoram brand conversion at 69% (crossed 70% currently), India Cements at 58% (crossed 55% currently); full rebranding targeted by June 2026
items.quote: Brand conversion at Kesoram having reached 69% in December '25. And today, if we speak, it must have crossed further. India Cements has already crossed 58% at the end of December '25.

items.statement: India Cements EBITDA/ton at INR600 in Q3 vs INR755 in Q2; target INR1,000 exit Q4 FY27 through brand conversion, price improvement, efficiency capex and capacity utilization
items.quote: Balance almost 40% or 45% of brand conversion has to be completed and prices are going up in the southern markets as well. Further, as I called out, the capex program has begun for efficiency improvement.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt/EBITDA at 1.08x; target 0.8-0.9x by end FY26; all growth funded through internal accruals
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we are at 1.08x net debt EBITDA. I believe and I'm very confident that we'll reach the mark of 1x and be in 0.8, 0.9x net debt EBITDA by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: India Cements non-core land parcels sale expected to generate minimum INR500 crores; INR200-250 crores realized so far; Indonesian coal mining company sold
items.quote: I would expect further generation of up to INR500 crores minimum, which we should be able to get.

items.statement: Clinker conversion factor target 1.54 by mid FY27-FY28, currently at 1.49; green power share target 60% by FY27 or H1 FY28 from current 41%
items.quote: We have taken a target of clinker conversion factor of 1.54. We are moving on that direction. In 1.54, we have reached INR1.49.

items.statement: Lead distance reduced to 363 km vs 375 km target (25 km reduction from 400 km base)
items.quote: We have already reached 363 kilometers.

items.statement: Industry capacity additions will be absorbed by strong demand; no pricing pressure expected if demand remains robust
items.quote: The reason I talked about all the demand footprint and demand new initiatives, I think cement will easily get absorbed. And if the demand remains strong, we will not see any problem in prices.

items.statement: South India witnessing large institutional demand from Amaravati city project, IT complexes, data centers, highways; young IT population driving housing and social infrastructure demand
items.quote: South is witnessing large institutional demand, the Am ravati City project, which is going at its breakneck pace, the IT complexes. Complexes which are coming up, data centers which are coming up.

items.statement: Input cost risks from pet coke/coal prices, new labor code impact, rupee depreciation; dollar movement uncertainty affects Q4 cost outlook
items.quote: There have been cost increases in the cost of pet coke and coal, new labor code will have its own impact, rupee depreciation. All these will have an impact on the cement industry.

items.statement: Acquisition opportunities highly opportunistic; would examine if they come to table; nothing currently in progress
items.quote: It's highly opportunistic. We would love to examine opportunities if they come to the table.

items.statement: Industry demand growth guidance 7-8% for next 4-5 years remains intact; Q4 FY26 demand robust but 9-10% may be optimistic due to high base
items.quote: That remains. That remains, Shravan.

items.statement: Other operating income increased INR88 crores sequentially due to incentive transitions (Dhar line 1 exhausted, Dhar line 2 kicked in) and volume-market mix changes
items.quote: Case in point, our Dhar line 1 got exhausted, whatever was the balancing quantum of money left and Dhar 2 kicked in.

items.statement: Early-stage construction products like cement and steel performed well in Q2 and expected to perform strongly in Q3, increasing project pipeline for tiling
items.quote: Early-stage products like cement and steel did well in quarter 2 and are expected to perform strongly in quarter 3 also. This is good news for us as it increases the project pipeline for tiling.

items.statement: Industry exports estimated to grow 8% over last year for 8 months FY26 till November 2025, helping divert capacities from domestic to international markets
items.quote: Data till November '25 suggests that for 8 months FY '26, exports are estimated to grow by 8% over last year. This should help by diverting capacities from domestic to international markets.

items.statement: Full impact of cement and steel demand on tile demand expected to start coming in second half of calendar year 2026, progressively improving quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: I think it would take, say 3, 4 quarters for it to start playing up. So I think middle of this calendar year -- and it will progressively keep improving quarter-on-quarter, but I think the full impact should start coming in, in the second half of this calendar year.

items.statement: Manufacturing cost reduced 4.5% on like-for-like basis after normalizing for product mix and energy prices; gross margins sustained at mid to high 30s
items.quote: A sharp focus on operational efficiency has led to a 4.5% reduction in the manufacturing cost on a like-for-like basis after normalizing for product mix and energy prices.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA increased 35% year-on-year to INR10.8 crores; PBT rose to INR4.7 crores from INR1.4 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, Q3 FY '26 EBITDA increased by a robust 35% year-on-year to INR10.8 crores. Profit before tax rose to INR4.7 crores compared to INR1.4 crores in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA stood at INR26.1 crores, up 25% year-on-year; PBT improved to INR8 crores from INR0.2 crores in corresponding period last year
items.quote: For the 9 months ended FY '26, EBITDA stood at INR26.1 crores, marking a 25% increase year-on-year basis. PBT improved significantly to INR8 crores from INR0.2 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Working capital cycle remains healthy at 31 days, in line with December 2024 levels
items.quote: The working capital cycle remains healthy at 31 days, in line with December '24 levels.

items.statement: Company is virtually debt-free on a net basis with net debt of just INR0.1 crores, reflecting strong liquidity and cash flow
items.quote: Importantly, the company is now virtually debt-free on a net basis with a net debt of just INR0.1 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization in the 65%-odd range, similar to last quarter
items.quote: So current utilizations are similar to the last quarter. It's in the 65%-odd range only.

items.statement: 61% of sales from vitrified segment; GVT alone contributes 44% of sales during Q3, higher than previously
items.quote: 61% of our sales today comes from vitrified segment, which is higher than what it was previously, while GVT alone contributes 44% of our sales during Q3.

items.statement: Focus shifting to high-end GVT with more surface finishes; entry-level GVT facing price competition; ceramics declining as GVT manufacturing capacity increased
items.quote: within GVT, now our focus is our high-end GVT. The entry level GVT product is now facing a lot of price competition. So we are moving into the higher end of GVT products, more surface finishes and all

items.statement: Dealer inventory destocking trend played out over last 1.5-2 years; dealers now at comfortable stock levels; primary and secondary sales expected to be in tandem going forward
items.quote: I think over the last 1.5, 2 years, they have brought down their stocks to a level that they are comfortable with. So going forward, I think primary and secondary should be in tandem.

items.statement: Sales team carries target for secondary sale orders generated for dealers; digitized process capturing this on apps; number steadily building up
items.quote: Especially for us for the last 9 months or 1 year, Ashvath, we have been very aggressively pushing our team towards demand generation. So our sales team today carries a target for what is the total secondary sale orders that you have generated for the dealers and given to them, and we have a clear digitized process for capturing that on our apps and all. And that number has been steadily building

items.statement: OBTBs contribute 42% of sales; conscious shift to quality over quantity; closed large number of underperforming OBTBs; focusing on renovating and expanding existing 300+ OBTBs
items.quote: Even today, more than 40% of our sales is coming in from OBTBs -- actually 42% odd. Now your query about number of OBTBs 3 years back and now, so we have made a very conscious shift to start chasing quality versus quantity.

items.statement: No major capacity-enhancing investment planned; company has 42-43 million sqm capacity with associate company; enough spare capacity for next 2-3 years; focus on market building, distribution, brand awareness
items.quote: We have -- I'll just mention another thing that might help you. Anuj had talked about capacity utilization. So we did go through over the last 4 years, a big capacity expansion -- multiple capacity expansion projects. As a company, we now have almost 42 million, 43 million square meters capacity along with are associate company. So we don't -- we do not see any major capacity enhancing investment.

items.statement: Will spend aggressively on TV advertising in FY27, expanding to new regions like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana; also spending on distribution and displays
items.quote: We are going to spend much more aggressively on TV in FY '27 and of course, spend on adding up distribution and displays.

items.statement: Gas prices stable; weighted average basis up only INR0.50 compared to last quarter; no 30% increase as rumored
items.quote: No. So gas prices are pretty much stable. I think on a weighted average basis compared to the last quarter, gas prices are up by INR0.50 only.

items.statement: Morbi pricing declining; company's manufacturing ASPs maintained but Morbi ASPs declined; purchase price from Morbi also declined, benefit passed to dealers
items.quote: And so I think Morbi pricing has been going down as always. I think that's really the norm. And for us also to share our own manufacturing ASPs have been maintained, but our Morbi ASPs have actually declined.

items.statement: Q3 top line increased 3.4% year-on-year; 9M revenue INR474 crores, up 1.1% from last year; growth entirely volume-led from Q2 onwards
items.quote: On the revenue front, quarter 3 top line has increased by 3.4% over last year. For the 9-month period, these figures are INR474 crores, up 1.1% from last year.

items.statement: Volume growth led by core markets North and East; West leading in growth; South growing but muted with some states doing well
items.quote: So the core markets of North and East have continued to do well. We are doing very nicely in Western India also. Actually, that is leading in growth. And South also has -- South, some geographies have started picking up for us nicely.

items.statement: No major capacity addition expected in 2026; only 8-10 plants known to come online through 2026; capacity to remain similar to last 1-2 years
items.quote: Another thing which I spoke about briefly is that we don't see any major capacity addition in 2026. There are hardly another 8, 10 plants which we know of, which will come into play through 2026.

items.statement: Chinese export incentives likely to be removed effective April 1, 2026; should help Indian domestic market compete better with Chinese players
items.quote: Also, one more change, which is anticipated from 1st of April is that there were some export benefits, which Chinese government used to pass on to the exporters. Likely, some of those incentives effective 1st of April will not be there.

items.statement: Tile adhesives moved beyond pilot phase; selling commercially in selected North India markets; national rollout planned next financial year
items.quote: No, no, we are selling now. It's moved beyond the pilot phase. We are selling it commercially.

items.statement: Slab market has 28-odd manufacturers in Morbi; 3-4 under shutdown; 6-7 new plants expected in CY2026; significant erosion in slab rates; 15mm thickness emerging as granite substitute
items.quote: So there are 28-odd vendors in Morbi doing slabs. A few of them -- I think 3, 4 of them are under shutdown. We expect another 6 or 7 new plants to come in, in calendar year '26 on slabs.

items.statement: No plans to enter slab manufacturing; capex and capacity utilization equation not attractive; already in market as trader
items.quote: Not as a manufacturer. We are already in the market. We don't have plans to get into it as a manufacturer. The kind of capex it takes and the capacity utilization you need to make money, that equation doesn't look very attractive as of now.

items.statement: Digital tools a key differentiator; 9 out of 10 prospective sales hires from tile industry identify Orient Bell as a tech company; 500+ dealers using voice-enabled visualization tool launched May 2019
items.quote: Today, there is a voice-enabled tool, and we have 500-odd dealers who are using it. So all of this helps because these are things which a customer is not able to get from any of the competing brands.

items.statement: Demand conditions stable with building blocks for gradual consumption recovery supported by moderating inflation, GST rationalization, higher MSPs, and healthy crop sowing.
items.quote: We continued to see the building blocks for a gradual recovery in consumption, supported by moderating inflation, improved affordability following the recent GST rate rationalization, which has been transformative, higher MSPs, and a healthy crop sowing season.

items.statement: Expect improved volume growth trajectory in core portfolio while pricing growth moderates; progressive improvement in operating profit growth rates.
items.quote: We aim to sustain the volume growth momentum even as pricing growth is likely to moderate over the course of the next few quarters. With input cost easing and margin pressure subsiding, we expect progressive improvement in operating profit growth rates over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Target mid-teens operating profit growth and 150-200 bps operating margin expansion.
items.quote: We could try for more, and at least we would strive for improving the operating margin by about 150-200 basis points.

items.statement: Copra prices down 25-30% from peak; Parachute will pass benefit to consumers in coming months via single price cut after March-April visibility.
items.quote: With correction having set in and copra prices down by around 25% to 30% from peak levels, the brand will be passing on the benefit to the consumer in the coming months, as and when we believe it is the right time to do it.

items.statement: No immediate Parachute price cut; will take one correction after March-April when copra trajectory firms up; may use consumer offers interim.
items.quote: We are still awaiting to get a firm handle on how the copra price trajectory will move, which we will get by March-April, and then take correction in one go, rather than taking in multiple steps, because if you take pricing correction in multiple steps, it disturbs the trade rhythm.

items.statement: VAHO value share at all-time high ~30% MAT; double-digit growth trajectory expected near-to-medium term.
items.quote: Our value share on MAT basis stands at an all-time high of nearly 30%, showing considerable progress towards premiumization of the mix and bridging the gap between volume and value share, along with our intended lines and long-term aspirations.

items.statement: Foods portfolio paused growth to rectify low-profitability SKUs; confident of resuming accelerated organic growth in next two quarters.
items.quote: We remain very bullish on value-added foods and nutra opportunity in India, and our strategy to invest in fewer, bigger, better plays in terms of our portfolio approach. That being said, we are confident of resuming the accelerated growth trajectory in our organic food business over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Strategic investment in 4700BC at INR 140 cr ARR; target 3x ARR in three years; synergies with True Elements for cost and GTM.
items.quote: It is clocking at about INR 140 crores ARR in the last three months. We see tremendous potential for the brand to scale its ARR to 3x in the next three years.

items.statement: Premium Personal Care portfolio to exit FY26 at ARR INR 350+ cr; Digital-First portfolio to exit FY26 at ARR INR 1,000+ cr; target 2.5x FY24 ARR next year.
items.quote: In Premium Personal Care, the portfolio comprising Serums, Male Grooming, and Skincare grew in double digits and is expected to exit the year at an ARR of INR 350+ crores. In addition, the Digital-First portfolio is expected to exit FY '26 with an ARR of INR +1,000 crores.

items.statement: Digital-First portfolio target double-digit EBITDA margin by end of FY27.
items.quote: We are on track to reach 2.5x of FY '24 ARR next year, and we are making concerted efforts to move to double-digit EBITDA margin in the Digital-First portfolio by end of FY '27.

items.statement: Project SETU ~30% complete; 3-5 year project to deepen rural coverage and expand urban channels (chemist, cosmetic, specialty food).
items.quote: Project SETU has continued to strengthen our distribution fundamentals, execution capabilities, and the coverage expansion remains firmly on track, led by deeper presence in upgraded towns and pan-India rural scale-up. We will now commence our initiatives on targeted expansion in urban channels, such as chemist, cosmetic, and specialty food outlets.

items.statement: E-commerce and quick commerce leading growth; traditional trade showing clear improvement from consistent investments.
items.quote: Among channels, while e-commerce and quick commerce were leading growth drivers, we saw a clear improvement in traditional trade, marking the outcome of consistent investments and targeted actions over the last 2 years.

items.statement: At least one competitor in coconut oil now following rational pricing model, avoiding negative gross margins.
items.quote: Number three, which is also gives us hope that at least one of our competitors is being extremely rational on pricing, because we also faced, as you know, irrational pricing from two competitors in the past, and now at least one of them is following a rational pricing model.

items.statement: International business robust broad-based growth; Bangladesh steady core and new franchises; Vietnam and South Africa double-digit constant currency growth; MENA strong; NCD accelerated.
items.quote: Bangladesh led from the front, supported by a steady core business and a scale -up of new franchises like shampoos. Vietnam and South Africa bounced back to deliver do uble-digit constant currency growth, driven by targeted initiatives. MENA continued to deliver strong performance in key franchises across both the Gulf region and Egypt . The NCD business also delivered accelerated growth

items.statement: Bangladesh macro uncertainties monitored; business resilient with 8% growth in Q2 despite grim conditions.
items.quote: Even in Quarter 2, when the issues were quite grim in terms of the, it was in August that this thing happened. That quarter, we grew by 8%. So, we have taken steps out there, and we don't see any reason to be extremely concerned at this moment in time in terms of delivering business.

items.statement: Supply chain efficiencies and AI-based forecasting enable far thinner pipelines; changeover much faster vs 8-12 weeks previously.
items.quote: The big change that has happened is that we work with far, far thinner pipelines because of our supply chain efficiencies and our AI-based forecasting models. So, therefore, we are compared to, say, five years ago and all that, that the changeover, which used to take 8 weeks to 12 weeks, especially in rural, this is going to be much faster.

items.statement: Consolidated high single-digit revenue growth expected for FY26; India business to hold normative EBITDA margins in Q4 FY26; GAUM to deliver double-digit revenue and profit growth for FY26; Indonesia recovery expected from FY27
items.quote: For the year, we remain confident of achieving high single -digit revenue growth at a consolidated level. Our India business is expected to deliver continued growth performance while holding normative EBITDA margins in the coming quarter. GAUM continues to perform well and deliver on its stated objectives of double-digit revenue and profit growth for the year.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin annual range guided at 24-26% for FY26; management expects margins to stay within this range and not exceed it due to negative mix from fast-growing categories
items.quote: I would be surprised if we exceed this 24% to 26% range. This is also an annual range; on a quarter it may go up and down. The annual range of 24% to 26% is roughly where we will be is what I think.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin at 24.8% in Q3 FY26 driven by cost savings (media, supply chain, blend flex), favourable input costs, calibrated pricing and operating leverage; structural savings to persist
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at a healthy 24.8%, supported by favourable input costs, disciplined cost management, calibrated pricing actions, and improved operating leverage. I think the few quarters that we had of margin challenges is probably behind us.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 16% with margins at 21.6% in Q3 FY26; Indonesia profitability improved ~100 bps YoY; GAUM EBITDA grew 18%
items.quote: Revenues grew 9% in INR terms, underpinned by a healthy 7% underlying volume growth. EBITDA expanded by 16%, with margins reaching 21.6%. Our net profit before exceptionals grew by 14% underlying the quality and sustainability of our earnings growth.

items.statement: Indonesia delivered stable 5% underlying volume growth led by shampoo, hair colour, baby care with market share gains across categories; revenue flattish due to distribution changes
items.quote: The gy business delivered a stable UVG of 5% led by shampoo, hair colour, baby care and with market share gains across all categories. Revenue was flattish, adjusting for the one -off changes in distribution adjustment.

items.statement: GAUM (Africa, USA, Middle East) sales grew 19% in INR terms with strong performance in hair fashion and air fresheners; aer pocket launch resonating well
items.quote: Our Africa, U.S.A. and Middle East GAUM business delivered outstanding results, wi th sales growth of 19% in INR terms. EBITDA grew 18%, led by strong performance in hair fashion and air fresheners.

items.statement: Home Care grew 12% value led by air fresheners, fabric care, household insecticides (RNF formulations); Personal Care recovered 7% with soaps improving post-GST cut; incense sticks grew fast with 30% price hike and no volume slowdown
items.quote: delivered 12% value growth led by strong performance in air fresheners and fabric care alongside continued market share gains in household insecticide, driven by our superior RNF based formulations. We continue to expect similar share gains going forward. Personal Care witnessed a meaningful recovery, growing 7% with soaps demonstrating a positive trajectory, supported by improving affordability f

items.statement: Fast-growing categories (air care, laundry liquids, incense sticks, EDP/perfumes) growing at 30%+ with large TAMs; hair colour and non-mosquito HI growing double-digits; soaps expected 4-6% value growth long-term
items.quote: The three big categories that have been growing very fast for us have been air care, laundry liquid, and incense sticks. These are the three that have really and they're now becoming all of them are material size and rapid growth. All of them have very large TAMs. I think that's and there's a fourth one that seems to be emerging by the way, it's still not large enough, which is perfumes, EDP.

items.statement: Muuchstac acquisition completed 10 Nov 2024; business ~INR 70 cr, men's face wash market ~INR 1,000 cr growing 20%; targeting #2 position; Park Avenue (Raymond) acquisition progressing reasonably, EDP segment exploding to ~INR 100 cr
items.quote: I am pleased to confirm that our acquisition of Muuchstac was successfully completed on 10th November, with operations now fully live and performance on plan. This strategic addition strengthens our portfolio in the fast -growing men's face wash segment and positions us well to capture emerging opportunities in this space.

items.statement: Pet food test market in Tamil Nadu showing mixed results; market share lower than hoped; plant ready in Nashik; building capabilities (kennel, manufacturing, sales team, vet program); long-term commitment, slow burn for few years
items.quote: We basically launched a test market in Tamil Nadu and as we speak, we have got a plant ready now in Nashik, which is ready to go. I think in Tamil Nadu, our results have been mixed. We've had some success in terms of consumer traction, distribution, etc. But I don't think we're still at a position where we can say we've got the mix 100% right.

items.statement: Incense sticks: 30% weighted average price increase since launch with no volume slowdown, margins now good; soaps: blend flex savings from vegetable oil vs fossil fuel price shifts; media savings from new agency and better internal planning
items.quote: Yes, in incense sticks, we have taken a weighted average price increase of 30% since we launched, and we are seeing no slowdown in our volume growth. So now our margins are pretty good actually in incense sticks.

items.statement: Cost savings driving margin improvement: significant media savings (new agency, better GRP efficiency), supply chain savings (new factories), blend flex in soaps and detergents; 50% of other expense reduction from savings, rest phasing
items.quote: We've had an unusually high year in terms of cost savings. I think we've had very significant savings in media cost. So actually, while our ATL looks optically lower, the number of GRPs that we are spending in the market is actually higher. And I think , we made a big decision to change to a very large new media house, and that has a significant media savings.

items.statement: Household Insecticides: RNF molecule driving share gains in all 4 segments (incense sticks, electrics, aerosols, coils); overall HI volume growth mid-single digit, inching to high single digit; volatility +/-5% per quarter
items.quote: I think the RNF won't change the volatility of HI results because the volatility of HI results depends on the volatility of seasonality. It will change the mean from a business that was practically not growing. I think it is going to go and as our incense sticks business becomes bigger and bigger, and that business is now quite a profitable business. And we're having good success in market share i

items.statement: Soap volume growth positive in Q3 but below expectations; GST transition and cold winter impacted Oct-Nov; December strong; long-term soap value growth expected 4-6% with low single-digit volume and pricing
items.quote: I think it's a good question. I expect soap value to grow at between 4% and 6% in the long-term basis, low single-digit volume growth and low single-digit pricing as well. That's what I expect in soaps.

items.statement: Margins sensitive to sharp oil price increases (>15%); if oil spikes, margins may take 1-2 quarters to recover as company won't cut media spending; pass-through faster on price drops than hikes
items.quote: I would say that if there is a very sharp increase in oil prices again, and when I say very sharp, it has to be greater than 15 -odd percent, then we will take another quarter or two to recover the margins. We won't react in the short term by cutting media just to cover up some margins optically.

items.statement: Indonesia near-term volatility due to Labaran (Ramzan) date shift; competitive intensity peak behind but market remains competitive; currency fluctuations affect GAUM reported growth
items.quote: This quarter, again, in Indonesia, optically, the results may not great because of the change in dates of Labaran, which is Ramzan for them. But the underlying 4%, 5% volume seems to be back, and it will follow in price soon.

items.statement: GST reduction on soaps improving affordability and supporting volume recovery; transition impacted Oct-Nov stock clearance, benefits visible from December
items.quote: Personal Care witnessed a meaningful recovery, growing 7% with soaps demonstrating a positive trajectory, supported by improving affordability following the GST reduction and stable commodity prices.

items.statement: Indonesia competitive intensity peak (6 months of high pricing competition) appears behind; market remains competitive but stabilizing; GAUM facing currency volatility but structural volume growth strong
items.quote: I think the peak of competitive intensity is indeed behind us. It continues to be competitive like every other part, but there was a period of 6 months of very highly competitive activity on pricing which does seem to be a little bit behind.

items.statement: Other expenses in India down ~6% YoY in Q3; 50% from structural savings (media, supply chain, other cost lines), 50% from phasing between quarters
items.quote: I would say 50% of it would be attributable to savings. There have been savings in other cost lines and part of it has to do with phasing. And then in a quarter, there is some phasing which happens quarter -to-quarter on cost, but we have managed to kind of save on to some of the other expenses.

items.statement: Media function: creative insourced, media buying bolstered in-house with technology, still working with Group M; advertising function internal
items.quote: I think we made a presentation on insourcing the creative function. The media buying, we have actually bolstered our team in -house and there's a lot of use of technology. So, one reason for the reduction in media cost is the agency. Another reason is far better internal planning, but our media function is not an in -house function. We continue to work with Group M, and o ur advertising function i

items.statement: Litigation costs (Strength of Nature class action) ~INR 23 cr in quarter; legal expenses likely to continue for few quarters as suit progresses
items.quote: I mean there is, some of the costs are getting incurred in terms of legal expenses, which are being incurred. We will have to see how the suit progresses. But yes, it's likely to kind of continue for a few quarters.

items.statement: NIM expected to be in the range of 2.45% to 2.50% even if further repo rate cuts happen
items.quote: So, even if further reduction in Repo happens, we presume that our NIM will be in the range of 2.45 to 2.50.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance of 10-11% already surpassed at 13.59% and will be maintained
items.quote: Regarding credit growth, sir, you have told we have given a guidance of 10% to 11%, but already we are crossing 13.59%, and we see that going ahead this will be maintained.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance of 9-10% already surpassed at near 13% and will be maintained in Q4
items.quote: And on the deposit side also, we have given a guidance of 9% to 10%. We are already near 13%, and we see that it will be maintained in the 4th Quarter also.

items.statement: NIM contracted by 2 bps in Q3 due to 6 bps yield compression on advances partly offset by 4 bps deposit cost reduction
items.quote: Regarding margins, our NIM contracted by 2 basis points because the yield on advances… because on 5th, there was a reduction in repo by 25 basis points, and about 49% of our advance is Repo linked. So, immediately that transition was happening in those accounts. So, yield on advances contracted by 6 basis points, although the cost of deposit also reduced by 4 basis points, which had a net impact o

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilize if no further rate cuts occur due to OMO and swap injecting liquidity and cooling deposit costs
items.quote: With the OMO coming up and the swap being announced, liquidity will be injected, and we see the cost of deposits cooling down further. So yes, if the rate cut doesn't happen, we see that it will stabilize.

items.statement: NIM could improve by 15-20 bps once rate cycle effect settles and deposit repricing catches up with RLLR loan repricing
items.quote: Sir, definitely yes, that will happen as the rate cycle effect settles down. Because now there is always a time lag on passing on the RLLR based loans and the deposit repricing. Once that stabilizes, automatically 15-20 basis point will immediately rise across lenders.

items.statement: RAM credit grew 18.70% YoY to Rs 7.04 lakh crore, driven by retail at 31.37% and MSME at 13.74%
items.quote: Now, more than 13% of our credit growth is driven by RAM credit, which stood at 7.04 lakh crores and grew at 18.70%. The retail credit grew at 31.37% and stood at 2.73 lakh crores. The housing loan grew by 17.58% and stood at 1.21 lakh crores. Vehicle loan also shown fantastic growth. The growth was 26.20% and stood at 25,098 crores. MSME has also shown robust growth of 13.74% and stood at 1.60 la

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio at Rs 2.21 lakh crore growing at 30% YoY, with Agri gold at Rs 1.48 lakh crore and Non-Agri at Rs 72,661 crore
items.quote: Sir, our total gold loan portfolio is 2,21,000 crores. Out of that, Agri gold is 1,48,000 crores. And Non-Agri is 72,661 crores. So, very consciously, we have rolled back the products of gold loan in metropolitan and urban centres because that was the RBI observation. Now, we are totally compliant with it. And our gold loan portfolio is improving at 30% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: SMA-2 down from Rs 21,268 cr to Rs 15,454 cr (2% to 1.30%), SMA-1 down from Rs 11,882 cr to Rs 10,593 cr (1.13% to 0.89%)
items.quote: Sir, our SMA in absolute terms has come down from 43,000 crores to 35,604 crores. The SMA-2 has come down from 21,268 crores to 15,454 crores. And SMA-1 has come down from 11,882 crores to 10,593 crores. So, SMA-2 has come down from 2% to 1.30%. SMA-1 has come down from 1.13% to 0.89%.

items.statement: Fresh slippages in Q3: Agriculture Rs 789 cr, MSME Rs 739 cr, Retail Rs 294 cr, Gold Rs 35 cr; no corporate slippages
items.quote: Yes, sir. In Agriculture, the total slippage is 1,857 crores. 789 is from Agriculture sector. 739 is from MSME. Retail 294 and 35 is from gold. No corporate account has slipped.

items.statement: Written-off book at Rs 66,000 cr; recovery run rate of ~Rs 2,000 cr per quarter to continue in FY27
items.quote: Sir, we have taken a conscious call that it has to be more than the 2,000 crore range, and we are continuously trying to achieve that number. If you see last December also it was 2,008 crores, this year 2,051 crores. Although my total NPA book is falling, we are trying to maintain this recovery ratio.

items.statement: Written-off recoveries split ~50-50 between retail and corporate; retail DWO recovery averages Rs 900-1,000 cr per quarter
items.quote: That is yes. From Retail recovery in DWO is around, on an average. In some quarter it may be more, some quarter it may be less. On an average around 1,000 crores, 900 to 1,000 crores

items.statement: Credit cost improved 25 bps YoY to 0.64%
items.quote: Our credit cost was at 0.64% and improved by 25 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: CET-1 improved 40 bps YoY to 12.37%
items.quote: Our CET-1 stood at 12.37%, which improved by 40 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: CASA grew 9.32% YoY; savings individual >10%, current account 14.92% (impacted by one large transaction)
items.quote: Now, coming to the CASA front also, if you see our savings bank is growing at 8.51%. And saving bank individual is growing more than 10%. So, we are performing better than the peers in savings. Even if you see the current account, it is growing at 14.92%. Only due to one single transaction that has happened previous quarter of 26,000 in current account, that is why Q on Q sub dip is there. But CAS

items.statement: Priority sector lending at 45.25% against 40% norm, enabling continued PSLC income
items.quote: Our total priority sector against 40% norms is now at 45.25%. So there is still some space for offloading PSLC in the fourth quarter to supplement what Mr. Majumdar is saying.

items.statement: PSLC income now sustainable across quarters: Rs 1,240 cr in Q1, Rs 900 cr in Q2, Rs 140 cr in Q3, substantial expected in Q4
items.quote: And this quarter, not only we have earned around 1,240 crores, we have earned 900 crores in the 2 nd Quarter. 3rd Quarter, actually, there is no chance for a PSLC. There also we earned 140 crores. And I assure you, we'll earn a substantial amount in the 4 th Quarter also. So it is the industry; if any regulatory thing has happened, it is only helping us. And it is helping us as a renewed avenue of

items.statement: ECL implementation from April 1, 2027; estimated Rs 10,000 cr total impact (Rs 2,500 cr Stage 2, Rs 2,500 cr NFP, Rs 5,000 cr Stage 1 default rate), amortizable over 4 years at Rs 2,000-2,500 cr per year
items.quote: Coming to ECL, the other parameters madam, it is going to be implemented from 1st April 2027. Now, our bank is making… last year it has made a profit of 17,000 crores. This year, going by the same trend, our profit will be in the range of 17,000 to 20,000 crores. So, in the ECL under Stage 2… because Stage 1 and Stage 3 does not have any much material impact because it is almost similar to IRAC no

items.statement: No pre-emptive ECL provisions being made; quarterly profits sufficient to absorb impact when implemented

items.quote: Standard asset provision, one is we had to provide for DCCO extension, that some provision of around 80 crores is there… around 90 crores is there. And other than that, I think these are all routine. There is nothing else.

items.statement: Company on track to become debt-free by FY27
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong, and we are on well track to become debt-free by FY27.

items.statement: A&SP spending guided at 6-8% of IMFL revenue
items.quote: We continue to guide for A&SP spending in the range of 6-8% to sustain strong brand visibility and growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve by 125 bps each year for next two years reaching late teens
items.quote: We are going to improve our margin based on our product profile and premiumization happening, by 125 basis points each for next two years, thereby going to late teen kind of margin.

items.statement: Prestige & Above volume grew 26% YoY in Q3 FY26

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh market share increased from over 15% to 26% in Q3 FY26

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 350 bps YoY to 46.9% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Gross margin during the quarter was 46.9%, representing a 350 bps expansion on year-on-year basis, 290 bps expansion on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Raw material contributed 225 bps of gross margin expansion YoY

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 300 bps YoY to 17.2% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 300 bps on year-on-year basis to 17.2%.

items.statement: ENA and grain prices expected to stay stable to favorable near-term

items.statement: Scotch prices seeing softening due to oversupply in Scotland
items.quote: We are seeing a price decline in fact in the scotch prices. And there is enough of Scotch which is there. So, we are seeing softening of prices.

items.statement: Premiumization and product mix contributed 125 bps to gross margin expansion YoY
items.quote: It is a combination of softer raw material scenario where we have had an improvement in margin of around 225 basis points, and the premiumization and product mix has been 125 basis points margin improvement.

items.statement: Luxury portfolio revenue expected to reach Rs. 500 crores in FY26 vs Rs. 340 crores last year
items.quote: See, last year we got Rs. 340 crores and this year we should be close to about Rs. 500 crores in revenue terms.

items.statement: On-trade channel now contributes 6-7% of total sales
items.quote: On-trade would be about close to 6%-7% of our total sales now.

items.statement: Exports contribute 5% of volume and 8% of revenue with steady growth
items.quote: Well, as a percentage of the overall business, the volume is about 5% and the revenue is about 8%. And we have been having a steady growth in our export business, both in terms of the luxury portfolio as well as the regular portfolio.

items.statement: Ongoing capex directed towards maintenance and essential capacity optimization
items.quote: Our ongoing capex is largely directed towards maintenance capex and essential capacity optimization.

items.statement: Board approved 100% wholly-owned subsidiary in Scotland to secure malt supply chain
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved setting up a 100% wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company in Scotland. This is in line with our strategy of investing in our Malt capabilities.

So, we can look at it, but as of now, nothing is on the cards.

items.statement: Telangana collections improving; old outstanding expected to clear within a month
items.quote: In fact, in the last one to two months, we have got payment out of the old outstanding, and hopefully, the entire old outstanding should be cleared within a month.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by Rs. 209 crores since March 2025
items.quote: Our net debt reduced by Rs. 209 crores since March 2025, driven by improved profitability.

items.statement: Post-debt repayment cash likely to be used for dividend payouts
items.quote: I think depending on the board's decision, but I think mostly it will be used for dividend payouts.

items.statement: On-trade team expanded to 50-70 people over last 1.5 years
items.quote: In fact, in the last one and a half years, we have really beefed up our on-trade team. We have recruited from all the institutions, etc., We have been close to about 50 to 70 people on the on-trade side.

items.statement: Royal Ranthambore Whisky grew over 50% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Royal Ranthambore Whisky delivered an outstanding performance with over 50% growth in Q3, driven by strong demand across both civil and CSD channels.

items.quote: To your second question, we will do much better than what we did this quarter. I don't want to get into any specific number.

items.quote: Credit cost, we'll maintain this level. I think we will be able to maintain. Although I have given guidance of less than 1, but I think at least next quarter, I will be able to maintain.

items.quote: I have already given guidance of less than 2%. We'll maintain that. Net NPA, 0.5%. We can do 0, but then after 0, what to do? So, we will maintain that.

items.quote: My target is, say, my total digital business is 15%. I want to take it up to 50% in next two to three years.

items.quote: Last point, we have a good pipeline of around Rs 50,000 crore in the corporate credit.

items.statement: AUC recovery guidance of Rs 2,000 crore already achieved in nine months
items.quote: AUC recovery, we have guidance of R s 2,000 crore. We have already reached that figure R s 2,000 crore we have already reached

items.statement: NCLT recovery of Rs 338 crore in Q3 FY26
items.quote: NCLT recovery, one good account/ one chunky account has been recovered during this quarter. In that, around R s 300 crore recovery has come, so through recovery through NCLT is Rs 338 crore

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved sequentially from 3.34% to 3.40% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Domestic NIM has improved sequentially from 3.34% to 3.40%.

items.quote: Total SMA book is Rs 31,488 crore. Out of that, SMA 0 is Rs 12,000 crore, SMA 1 is Rs 8,000 crore, SMA 2 is almost Rs 11,000 crore. So, Rs 11,000 crore and Rs 8,000 crore, on Rs 19,000 crore, 10%.

items.quote: Last quarter, I have made provision of 5% on SMA 1. This quarter, I have increased it up to 10%, so additional R s 380 crore provision we have made on SMA 1

items.quote: There are two PSU accounts where state government guarantee is available. So, last quarter, that was in SMA 0. This quarter, it has come to SMA 2. So, I mean, chances of slipping these account are, I mean, very less.

items.statement: IT capex plus opex around Rs 2,000 crore per annum for next 12-24 months
items.quote: Around Rs 2,000 crore per annum. Including both capex and opex. Because majority of IT expenditure is also coming in the shape of opex.

items.quote: Rs 2,000 crore of Tier 1 bond has retired, but we have not gone for raising fresh Tier 1, because we are still well capitalized. CET1 is 14.54%.

items.quote: Even this year, I have kept approval from the Board for QIP, up to Rs 5,000 crore. If you get opportunity, we can, of course. But as a part we don't need as of now.

items.statement: DICGC premium up Rs 128 crore (Rs 82 cr prior years, Rs 46 cr current quarter); Rs 60 cr ongoing quarterly increase

items.quote: AS 15, we have made. If you see, from last quarter, it has gone up by Rs 102 crore. So that is purely based on the actuarial valuation.

items.statement: MD sees credit growth sustaining at 12-13% in FY27, cautious on aggressive growth to avoid risk build-up
items.quote: I think 12% to 13% growth is good, Darshil. Because see, if you pursue very aggressive growth no, then you will start asking why your NPA is going up.

items.statement: Green finance portfolio growing ~60%; strong demand in EV, solar, logistics/warehousing
items.quote: If you see, I give you just one number. My growth in green finance itself is around 60%. So, we have good pipeline of that also.
